The security agencies have asked the Department of Telecom to ensure that traffic originating and terminating in India does not travel outside the country.

Amidst security concerns raised on the use of Blackberry services, India has already assured Canada that commercial interest of RIM, the maker of Blackberry, would be kept in mind while taking any final decision. Both Indian and Canadian governments had exchanged letters to sort out the issue.

On April 17, Canadian High Commissioner David M Malone had written a letter to Communications and IT Minister A Raja, through Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), on the issue of lawful interception of information related to RIM.

MEA in its reply to Malone on April 25 said, "It would be advisable for RIM to recognise that Department of Telecommunications is trying to be helpful in the case and to work together with them. It may not help the RIM cause to make allegations about those who are trying to help them."

There are about four lakh Blackberry subscribers in India and the services are being offered by Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Essar, Reliance Communications and BPL.

The DoT had also convened a meeting of various stakeholders in order to find a solution to the problem including IB officials with technical representative of RIM.

Heading: High-flying JCT ready for Vasco - Indian Express
Content:
Juventus had to fight back for a 2-2 draw at BATE Borisov in Group H. The Italian club had to come from two goals down in Minsk with BATE holding on for their first-ever Champions League point. Vincenzo Iaquinta scored both Juve goals after the Belarus side went two up in 23 minutes through Sergei Kryvets and Igor Stasevich.

"They surprised us. We couldn't hold them in any area of the field. It was a nightmare first half hour," Juve coach Claudio Ranieri said. "We did well not to give up. We have to compliment these lads from Belarus. They ran like there were 22 of them, not 11."

In the other Group H match, Real Madrid kept their 100 per cent record intact with a 2-1 win at Zenit St Petersburg, Ruud van Nistelrooy netting the 31st-minute winner.

Heading: Sourav... to be continued - Indian Express
Content:
Upbeat after defeating defending champions Dempo 2-1, JCT look favourites against Vasco Sports Club when they meet on Thursday in the second round of the ONGC I-League at the Nehru Stadium.

"It was good to begin with a win, especially against Dempo who are in high spirits after qualifying for the semi-finals of the AFC Cup. Our plan — to keep our forte intact and attack on counter — worked well as we got both the goals on counter attack. We cannot play the same strategy against every team. Tomorrow it will be different. We will assess the opponent's strength before going in for the offensive," said Sukhwinder Singh.

'Keeper's heroics

JCT, who were at the receiving end against Dempo, have to thank their keeper Karanjit Singh who did well under the bar bringing up smart saves to deny Dempo on many occasions.

The good news for Vasco is the availability of their three foreigners from Uzbekistan— Yorkin Nazarov, Sherzod Nazarov and Ravshan Teshabaev — will play in the midfielder for the first time, which will come as a boost.

"JCT are a tough side with a solid defence. Our team, which lacks experience, will have to play well if we are to beat them. We have the potential and the presence of the three foreigners should help us to come out triumphant," said Mario D'souza, secretary of the Vasco team.

Heading: Badrinath can’t wait to get going - Indian Express
Content:
As the new selection committee arrived at the BCCI headquarters in Mumbai, the only question hovering over the Cricket Centre — with lots of speculation thrown in the mix — was about Sourav Ganguly's future.

But interestingly, though the meeting lasted for more than two hours, Ganguly's name was discussed for less than 10 minutes. The former India skipper, the subject of much disputation across India over the last few days, gave rise to neither a prolonged debate, nor any serious contradictions. As one of the selectors put it: "It was a unanimous decision. There was no debate regarding Ganguly's inclusion."

The left-hander's exclusion from the Irani Cup earlier was seen as a first step towards the exit of India's so-called 'Fab Five' — and a signal to players to bid adieu before selectors were forced to wield the the axe. Reports floated rampantly of the newly-elected BCCI president Shashank Manohar had had a word with senior players. A VRS scheme to ensure customised exits was talked of, and there were post-meeting speculations that a "deal" had been made with Ganguly. But every BCCI official, selector and player spoken to after the meeting dismissed the reports outrightly.

Notwithstanding his Irani omission, Ganguly's inclusion in the Test side didn't really come as a surprise considering his record over the last two years. Barring the bad series in Sri Lanka, where he managed just 96 runs in six innings, Ganguly's comeback to Indian cricket in late 2006 has seen him score 1571 runs at an average of 50.67. He was also named the best Asian Test player recently.

"You can't leave out such an experienced player just because he has failed in one series," said a selector. But with the squad picked for just two Tests against the Aussies, it will be interesting to see what happens if Ganguly fails to add big runs to his kitty.

Newest future star

Middle-order batsman S Badrinath was called into the squad in place of Rohit Sharma, who travelled for the last series to Sri Lanka but didn't get a game. Projected as the future of Indian cricket just a couple of months ago, the 21-year-old Sharma has now made way for the 28-year-old Badri, perhaps rendering the age criterion unimportant and only taking form into consideration. Even Mohd Kaif couldn't impress the new selection committee despite his consistent scores in domestic cricket.

Though it's early days for this panel to jump to any conclusions, it did prompt some experts to suggest that Sharma is from Dilip Vengsarkar's zone, while Badri from new chairman Srikkanth's.

Reverse gear?

The other surprise inclusion was leggie Amit Mishra — the name that took up more time that any other during Wednesday's meeting. While the earlier committee had stressed on youngsters being offered opportunities to be groomed for the future, Srikkanth & Co seem to have opted to go into reverse gear. The Haryana leggie was last seen in action in 2003 during the Bangladesh tri-series, and has been a regular in the India A side since.

The selection committee debated the 26-year-old Mishra's picking over youngsters Piyush Chawla and Pragyan Ojha. "Mishra made the cut because of his experience and also because is in good form," said a selector.

Heading: Ganguly opts to play for India A - Indian Express
Content:
With the announcement of the squad for the first two Tests against Australia in Mumbai coinciding with the end of the afternoon net session in Hyderabad, the shifty focus of the media and harsh world of professional sports came together as one under the blazing sun. As a sweaty Badrinath wound up his training session, he suddenly got mobbed by an army of cameras. He instantly knew what it was about. "Am I in the Test side?" was his first reaction.

While Badri gave his better-late-than-never sound bytes, several 'former' Test players turned Board President's XI team members stood around, having suddenly turned onlookers in Indian cricket's latest crowning. Among those who gingerly walked towards the dressing room were Yuvraj Singh and Irfan Pathan — two men who know what it feels like to be in the spotlight.

There were two questions quite audible in the group dragging their kitbags: How come Amit Mishra made it? And did Sourav Ganguly's selection have any strings attached?

Change in equations

The change in the selection committee has seen a change in equations as well. Mishra's inclusion made it clear that young Piyush Chawla wasn't quite the heir apparent to the ageing leggie Anil Kumble anymore, and Badrinath has practically replaced Rohit Sharma as the next big thing in Indian cricket, with the middle-order queue outside the playing XI only getting longer. Only Yuvraj didn't see any change in his status.

In a room full of long faces, Badrinath was smiling alone. "This game is the perfect preparation for me," he said of the game against the Australians starting on Thursday. "They have a really good pace attack and I will have a good look at them here. This will give me the confidence going into the Tests," he said.

Preparing for pace

Even before the news trickled through though, Badrinath had been bracing up for the challenge ahead. After playing the Board President's XI pacers Pankaj Singh and MS Gony in the nets, he spent a long time facing the bowling machine in top gear. Still not satisfied, he chose the bounciest synthetic ball and asked for a long throw-down session. Asked about his preparation and he spoke about the 'back foot' play he was working on. "Whatever the kind of pitch, you need to be strong on the back foot against the Aussies," he said.

There are several players in the Board President's XI whose brains he can pick about playing the Australians — Yuvraj Singh, Aakash Chopra, Rohit Sharma, Parthiv Patel, Irfan Pathan, Piyush Chawla and Wasim Jaffer are all familiar with the opposition. Like Badri, Virat Kohli had toured Australia with the India A team, while Pankaj was in the Indian Test squad that went to Australia earlier this year.

Of the above mentioned players, most have enjoyed success against the world champions, but for now, they can only try and make another case over the next four days.

Heading: McGain injury opens old wounds - Indian Express
Content:
Sourav Ganguly will play in India A's second and final four-day match against New Zealand A in Chennai before joining the team for the Australia Test series.

The former India captain is leaving for Chennai to play under Suresh Raina in the match beginning on Thursday.

"Sourav (Ganguly) wanted to play a match before joining the team, so we have arranged him to play in India A's match against New Zealand A. After the four-day match gets over, Ganguly will directly join the Indian Test squad at the National Cricket Academy (NCA) in Bangalore where the players are camping right now," BCCI chief administrative officer Ratnakar Shetty said.

Dalmiya 'happy'

Meanwhile, CAB president Jagmohan Dalmiya, who doesn't share the best of relationships with Ganguly, expressed happiness over the latter's inlucsion in the squad.

"We are all happy for him (Ganguly). I wish him all the best for the two Tests against Australia," Dalmiya said, adding that the left-hander didn't need anybody's backing to earn his place back in the national team.

Dalmiya also pointed out that he had requested Ganguly to lead Bengal in the Ranji Trophy.

Heading: Happy I’m not just an India A veteran anymore: Mishra - Indian Express
Content:
The aggravation of Bryce McGain's shoulder injury sustained last month has opened an old Aussie wound. With the 36-year-old leg-spinner ruled out for the first Test and doubts expressed about his availability for the rest of the series, the visitors now have only one spin option in the form of off-spinner Jason Krejza.

A startling statistic about Aussie off-spinners who have toured India before could be disturbing for the tourists. Names such as Gavin Robertson, Nathan Hauritz and Colin Miller come instantly to the mind and their records in India show that trips to the land of spin-friendly conditions haven't been so memorable for them. Hauritz and Miller never played Tests after their Indian experience while Robertson got one more game in Pakistan before his career folded up.

Krejza is aware of the challenges that bowlers of his kind face in India. "I know it's tough here. Getting the Indian batsmen out isn't easy. But the one word I've repeatedly been told to remember is 'patience'," says the 25-year-old.

At the nets on Wednesday, Krejza got more advice than usual. First McGain, then Greg Chappell and finally skipper Ricky Ponting had long chats with him. While the offie seemed excited about the spotlight, McGain was dejected. Just a day before, things were different as one had caught up with the leggie. A full-time IT worker till a year ago, he had been enjoying his new life with the world champions.

McGain had spoken about his sessions at the nets, and his improving shoulder, which had been injured during his stint with Australia A in Bangalore a few weeks ago. "I had a real hard long session at the nets. I am quite happy with my fitness, though I didn't go all out. I didn't quite rip it this afternoon. I'm looking forward to having a good session before Thursday's game," he had said.

But on Wednesday morning, McGain was ruled out of the practice session, the tour game and even the Test. Aussie coach Tim Nielson said that a decision on his replacement would be taken in the coming days.

Till then, Krejza will be Australia's lone spin hope. Perhaps McGain could share the advice he got from Shane Warne before he left for India. "Warne gave lot of encouragement and reassurance: 'You don't have to bowl like an Indian spinner. You don't need to bowl fast. A good ball in Australia will be a good ball in India too'."

But that's a leggie talking, and not one of the Aussie off-spinners who has toured India.

Heading: Over the next four days, Yuvraj out to prove he belongs - Indian Express
Content:
A month ago, during India A's matches against Australia A, leg-spinner Amit Mishra was joking how he had been labelled a veteran in the A side.

After being picked in the India Test squad on Wednesday, he recalled how he used to be nervous before every selection meeting and sit in front of his television set as the national selectors announced the squad. "As the names of the team flashed, my heart would skip a beat. I used to think I'd get in but it never happened," he said. On Wednesday, as Mishra's fingers were rolling against the New Zealand A side at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, his name was finally on the screen. I'm no longer a veteran India A cricketer," the 26-year-old joked.

"I was always hopeful. The best thing I did was to not leave cricket after I was left out," added the leggie whose three-wicket haul, together with Ashok Dinda's five-for helped India A win by 129 runs.

Dinda shines

Dinda scalped five wickets giving away 60 runs as New Zealand A, needing 355 to win, were dismissed for 225 in 81.4 overs on the final day. Resuming at 41/1, Aaron Redmond (37) James Marshall (47), Peter Fulton (39) and Reece Young (39 not out) tried to build up some resistance but were undone by getting out in quick succession.

Brief scores: India A 248 & 336 bt New Zealand A 230 & 225 (A Dinda 5-60; A Mishra 3-55) by 129 runs

Heading: Singapore’s a circus track: Ferrari - Indian Express
Content:
The gap between his potential and performance remains but Yuvraj Singh is convinced he is ready to prove that he belongs to the longer version of the game.

Leading Board President's XI against Ricky Ponting's Australia for the warm-up match starting on Thursday, Yuvraj admitted he had issues with his batting but claimed he had sorted them out. "This match is a great opportunity for me. There were some flaws in my batting but I have worked those out," Yuvraj said.

Asked if he wanted to send any message to the selectors with a strong performance here, the left-hander said, "I'll rather be proving a point to myself. Every time you go out there you want to show you belong.

"Selection is not in my hands but I'm pretty confident of getting my form back. Hope I have a good game here," he added.

According to him, he has not done too badly in the last two years but it's only in the last four months that things didn't go as he would have liked.

"I just want to set things in order as early as possible. This is a really big match for us and tomorrow the guys will all be geared up for the game," he said.

Heading: F1 Plans Friday jackpot - Indian Express
Content:
Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo has poured scorn on Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix, saying the "circus" track and the use of the safety car had been humiliating for Formula One.

Formula One's first night race drew rave reviews from participants and onlookers, including the sport's delighted supremo Bernie Ecclestone, but was one to forget for the Italian team.

Brazilian title contender Felipe Massa had his race ruined by a bungled pit stop while faltering world champion Kimi Raikkonen crashed near the end.

"When we race on tracks which should be used for the circus, anything can happen including the spectacle of the Safety Car," Montezemolo was quoted as saying in Tuesday's Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper.

"All this is humiliating for F1 and it is an aspect I want to talk about with the other teams in the next few weeks."

Singapore saw two safety car interventions, the first of which turned the race upside down and contributed to Spaniard Fernando Alonso's unexpected victory for Renault.

Montezemolo, appointed this month as the first chairman of the Formula One Teams Association, said before the race that street circuits and the lack of overtaking opportunities were not the right way forward for the sport.

Ferrari's failure to score any points in Singapore meant McLaren's Lewis Hamilton, third behind winner Fernando Alonso, extended his championship lead over Massa to seven points with three races left.

Finn Raikkonen is out of contention but Montezemolo still sounded confident.

"We have the best Ferrari, Massa is the best. I expect... Raikkonen to show he is world champion in the remaining races, to help Massa, to race for the good of the team and to finish in front of the McLarens," he said.

The team president also backed the mechanics who gave Massa the green light during a pit stop despite the fuel hose still being attached to the car as he sped away.

"We have extraordinary mechanics who in other occasions have swung results our way. We must stay close to each other because Ferrari are always world champions and are still in the running to win," Montezemolo added.

Heading: AITA names fresh coaches - Indian Express
Content:
Formula One drivers could compete for a $1 million Friday jackpot as part of a revamp of grand prix weekends, McLaren chief executive Martin Whitmarsh has suggested. "We (the teams) are looking at the whole format of a race weekend," the Briton told the autosport.com website after Sunday's first night-time race in Singapore.

"At the moment we have formulated a Friday testing format, but in reality no one is doing the normal disciplined testing. We are preparing for the race (instead). "So we say, 'Is this good value? Does it help the show?'.

"Or do you perhaps do something where you say 'Let's cut it down to 45 minutes'. Maybe you give a completely different specification of tyres, a really hard tyre, and you create a mini-competition where everyone tries to set the fastest time and you give a million dollars to the winning driver?'

"It means there would be something to write about and it introduces the weekend. It is separate from the race. So there are all those sort of ideas about."

Whitmarsh heads the sporting working group of the newly-created Formula One Teams Association (FOTA) which is working with the governing FIA and commercial rights holders to finds ways of improving the spectacle, cutting costs and increasing revenues. He said he hoped the working group would reach some conclusions during the next two races in Japan and China before submitting recommendations to FOTA and then the FIA.

Heading: Weightlifter gets life ban for second doping offence - Indian Express
Content:
After the furore created by its selection of coaches for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, the All India Tennis Association (AITA) has agreed to do away with that list and form a new panel.

AITA officials met with sports ministry officials on Wednesday and have now come out with a fresh list of five coaches who will oversee preparations for the 2010 Games.

Veteran Davis Cup coach and former India player Jaideep Mukherjea has been named the chief coach and the chairman of the preparation committee for the Games. Present Davis Cup coach Nandan Bal and Fed Cup coach Enrico Piperno have both been named visiting coaches. Both Bal and Piperno have been with the national team for over a decade now. Nitin Kirtane and Radhika Tulpule have also been named in the five-member panel.

Earlier, the AITA had named former Davis Cup player Vishal Uppal as the chief coach, with Arun Kumar, Kawaljit Singh, Nar Singh, Sukhbir Singh and Shalini Thakur as the other coaches. Interestingly, all were from Delhi.

After the ministry launched an enquiry, a top AITA official admitted that the panel has been changed. "Besides these five, there will be one more coach, who is yet to be decided upon. The decision has been taken since Pune is now the main centre for training as the DLTA complex (in New Delhi) will undergo complete renovation soon. We plan to shift training to Pune right after the Commonwealth Youth Games. We have also requested the ministry to reconsider funding for the Games project — right now we have been allotted Rs 20 crores for the two-year period, which also includes tournament fund," the official said. "We are also looking at hiring a foreign coach and a trainer," he added.

Not an excuse

Sources say that the issue of the coaches panel was the main agenda during Wednesday's meeting, with the ministry refusing to accept lack of funds as an excuse to not get top coaches.

"While the AITA has said that there is a lack of funds, the ministry has responded by saying that money cannot be a hindrance in providing proper coaching to the players," a ministry official said.

AITA secretary Anil Khanna had earlier said that the former list was temporary and could change subject to the ministry agreeing to increase funding. "The ministry has decided on a monthly salary of Rs 30,000 per coach. Our maximum expenses are towards paying the coaches, so we'll definitely look at much bigger names," he had said.

Heading: Referee apologises for penalty error - Indian Express
Content:
Weightlifter B Prameelavalli was banned for life on Wednesday after failing a dope test for the second time. The Andhra Pradesh girl, who had returned to competitive weightlifting after serving a ban in March, was tested at the Junior National Championship in Noida last month where smashed three national records in the women's 63kg category.

"The ban is automatic after her 'A' test results," Weightlifting Federation of India secretary-general BR Gulati told The Indian Express. "It can be revoked only if the 'B' sample test proves otherwise," he said but added that the lifter had not asked for a 'B' sample test.

In Noida, her efforts in snatch (87 kg), clean and jerk (116 kg), and aggregate (203 kg) fetched her three gold medals and helped her state win the team title, raising hopes of a good showing at the forthcoming Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune. But a second offence in three years means her career is all but over. Prameelavalli had first tested positive during random WADA tests in Patiala just before the 2006 Melbourne Commonwealth Games and was handed a two-year ban.

UP unit banned

Meanwhile, the WFI has also slapped a one-year ban and Rs 20,000 fine on the UP Weightlifting Association after two of its lifters — Manjit Singh and Pramod Goswami — tested positive for banned substance at the Noida meet. Manjit won gold in the 77kg category while Pramod won silver in the 56kg. P Bhuvana of Puducherry, who won silver in the 53kg, also failed the dope test. The tainted troika faces a two-year ban.

Explaining the decision to ban the state association, Gulati said the WFI had introduced this new clause as a deterrent. "We hope this will serve the purpose as the state units are expected to share the blame and responsibility. Like the WFI which is responsible for the overall weightlifting scene in the country, the state units will have to take care of their lifters and educate them," he said.

As per the new clause, if two or more lifters from a particular state test positive in a calendar year, the state association will have to pay a fine of Rs 20,000 and serve a one-year ban which means, no lifter from that state will be able to participate in any WFI meets.

Heading: Porto see stars in London - Indian Express
Content:
Referee Rob Styles has apologised for the controversial penalty decision that allowed Manchester United to take the lead against Bolton Wanderers in Saturday's Premier League game, which the champions went on to win 2-0.

Styles penalised J-lloyd Samuel for bringing down Cristiano Ronaldo after an hour when TV pictures showed that he played the ball, and not even the Portuguese winger appealed.

"He has written to (referees' chief) Keith Hackett and said that in the video he's made a mistake and he wants to apologise for it," former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher told Sky Sports News. "He's held his hand up, he knows he made a mistake, he was in the perfect position but he thought Ronaldo had nicked the ball away."

Heading: Punjab Palace on Wheels back on track - Indian Express
Content:
Arsenal demolished a feeble Porto side 4-0 in the Champions League at the Emirates on Tuesday with two goals each from Robin van Persie and Emmanuel Adebayor firing them to the top of Group G.

Dutchman van Persie settled some early Arsenal jitters to slot the opener after 31 minutes before Adebayor headed the second shortly before halftime. Porto, who have never won in England, capitulated after the break and van Persie waltzed through to make it 3-0 before Adebayor converted a penalty with 19 minutes remaining.

The visitors had hit the crossbar through Cristian Rodriguez when the score was 0-0 but were outplayed as Arsenal recorded their first win in this season's competition after drawing their opener 1-1 with Dynamo Kiev. Arsenal have four points from two games, one point more than Porto. Dynamo Kiev are third with two points after their 0-0 draw away to Fenerbahce.

Quick response

Manager Arsene Wenger had been critical of his side's attitude after a shock 2-1 home defeat against Hull City on Saturday cost Arsenal top spot in the Premier League. But he had no complaints on Tuesday. "I didn't want to punish the players after the Hull defeat. Sometimes you give a team the chance to respond," he told reporters. "It was what I expected, we could have scored more but we responded in a convincing way."

Dimitar Berbatov's first two goals for Manchester United helped secure a 3-0 win over AaB Aalborg in Group E. The Bulgarian striker pounced twice in the second half after Wayne Rooney had put the holders ahead in the 22n d minute to give United their first win of the campaign.

The sheen was taken somewhat off the win after it emerged that United midfielder Paul Scholes will face a lengthy lay-off because of knee ligament injury.

Villarreal are level at the top of the group with United on four points after a 1-0 win at home to Celtic with a second half goal from midfielder Marcos Senna. Celtic and Aalborg have a point apiece.

Bayern Munich top Group F despite being held 1-1 at home by Olympique Lyon.

Bayern have four points with Lyon and Fiorentina, held 0-0 at home by Steaua Bucharest, two points behind. The Romanians have one point.

Heading: 200 policemen for 4 lakh people - Indian Express
Content:
The plan to introduce a super luxury tourist train for Punjab on the lines of the Palace on Wheels finally got back on track on Wednesday with the Railway Ministry signing a Memorandum of Understanding with the Punjab Government.

The proposal, first mooted almost a year back, had hit a roadblock with the Railways effecting a policy change in deciding to levy haulage charges on luxury train operators for the first three years of operation in addition to seeking a part of the gross revenue earned. For this particular train, the fact that the Railway Ministry was seeking a haulage charge of Rs 20 lakh per trip from the Punjab Government had put a question mark on the project.

In fact, at the signing of the MoU on Wednesday, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and Tourism and Culture Minister Ambika Soni both batted for the waiving off of these haulage charges. Subtly declining to agree, Lalu Prasad Yadav replied by saying that these charges could be deferred till the time the venture becomes financially viable and that the Railways could allow the running of the train on credit. To come up at a cost of Rs 36 crore, this luxury train will cover popular destinations like Amritsar, Anandpur Sahib, Chandigarh, Patiala not just in Punjab but also cities like Dharamshala, Kurukshetra, Agra, Delhi and Jaipur in its seven-day itinerary.

Essentially targeted at premium-end clientele, the coaches will be equipped with five-star facilities and will have saloons, restaurant cars, multiple cuisines, lounge bars, observation cars with a viewing gallery, gym, spa, beauty saloon, library, games room, and an Internet-equipped computer centre.

Railway Board chairman K C Jena said this luxury train was expected to have its maiden voyage in an approximate timeframe of two years. While the Railways will bear the cost of the bare coach shells, the cost of air-conditioning and interior decoration will be borne by the Punjab Government. While the Railways and Punjab Government have pooled in Rs 13.5 crore each for the project, the Tourism Ministry has pitched in with a grant of Rs 7.25 crore.

Heading: Gay pride: laws and outlaws - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Maharashtra Police said it could not rule out the possibility of a Hindu extremist hand in Monday's blast in Malegaon, investigators are revisiting the crude bombs that were planted in auditoriums on the outskirts of Mumbai earlier this year.

The state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) last month charged six members of two Hindu revivalist organisations, the Sanatan Sanstha and the Hindu Janjagruti Samiti (HJS), for the incidents in Thane, Vashi and Panvel, and its members will be questioned in connection with the Malegaon blast, sources in the ATS told 'The Indian Express' on Wednesday.

"The possibility of Hindu extremist groups being involved is being probed along with other possibilities. We will soon question members of the Sanatan Sanstha and the HJS," said a senior ATS official.

On September 11, the ATS had filed a 1,020-page chargesheet against six arrested accused for their alleged involvement in a small explosion that took place at a Panvel theatre screening Bollywood film Jodhaa Akbar on February 20, a crude bomb planted at Vishnudas Bhave auditorium in Vashi on May 31 as well as a bomb that exploded at Gadkari Rangayatan auditorium in Thane on June 4. The Vashi and Thane halls were showing a Marathi play which apparently poked fun at the Mahabharat.

All six are members of the Sanatan Sanstha and the HJS, although the organisations claimed that they had no role and the men may have acted on their own. During interrogation, the six are also said to have said that their activities were not at the behest of the organisations. The ATS chargesheet made no mention of the role of the two organisations.

However, the ATS is now planning to file a supplementary chargesheet after getting new evidence. According to sources, there is a strong possibility that both organisations might find a mention in it. "Our investigations are continuing and we will file a supplementary chargesheet. This time, there might be a mention of the HJS and Sanatan Sanstha," said the officer.

Responding to questions from The Indian Express, Dr Durgesh Samant, the national spokesperson of the HJS, said: "If the police want to question us, they are free to do so. However, we deny any involvement in the Malegaon blast. We are against such acts, and condemn them." Sanatan Sanstha spokesman Abhay Vartak said this was an attempt by the police to misguide people and "appease Muslims".

Incidentally, while a forensic report on the nature of explosives used in Monday's blasts in Malegaon is yet to be given to the ATS, forensic experts say there are obvious differences in the crude bombs used in the attack and the ones used in the September 8, 2006, blasts at Bada Kabdistana and Mushaira Chowk areas of the textile town.

"In the Malegaon blasts two years ago, a deadly cocktail of RDX, ammonium nitrate and fuel oil was used. There was no shrapnel such as ball bearings. In Monday's blast, we have already ascertained that missiles were packed in the bomb," said Dr Rukmini Krishnamurthy, Director of the Kalina Forensic Sciences Laboratory.

Heading: How Chandigarh stubbed the butt - Indian Express
Content:
Over 50 per cent of the 591 lavatories constructed by Assam tea estate owners at the labour lines have been abandoned by plantation workers due to poor hygiene and sanitation and have resulted in a loss of over Rs 30 lakh, a study has revealed.

"The survey that covered 769 families in 16 tea estates in Dibrugarh district in Upper Assam revealed that though 591 toilets were constructed, most are not being used by these families," said Jeero Master, the Unicef representative in Assam.

"Tea estate owners have spent between Rs 8,000 and Rs 14,000 to construct these toilets for the labourers. But, the construction is of very poor quality and appropriate technology for hygienic and scientific sanitation has not been use," she said.

The study was carried out by the Centre for Humanistic Development (CHD), a Guwahati-based NGO on behalf of Unicef in March, the Unicef state representative added.

Master said Unicef has come up with 135 demo toilets — each unit costs Rs 3,000 — in 23 tea estates in Dibrugarh district as part of a pilot project. "Each demo toilet at the pit and plinth level is costing only Rs 1400, and with a bamboo wall and a tin roof, it would hardly come to Rs 3000," she said.

The state chapter of the world body took up the initiative following reports of large number of deaths every year in Assam's tea estates due to lack of sanitation and safe drinking water.

"We are also supporting the gardens with sodium hydrochloride granules for odour-free chlorination of drinking water," she said. Unicef has also launched a collaborative programme with the Assam Branch Indian Tea Association (ABITA) to train hospital staff in tea estates on promoting personal hygiene among the semi-illiterate labourers, she added.

Heading: Sparking the drive - Indian Express
Content:
While the rest of the country thinks up ways to ban smoking in public places from tomorrow, they could take a tip or two from Chandigarh. For, this Union Territory became smoke-free long back — on July 15, 2007 — inspiring even Bahrain to follow in its footsteps.

Today, the city took another step by launching a website — chandigarh.tobaccofreeindia.com — where people can get information about no-smoking laws and lodge their complaints on violations online.

If someone is caught smoking at a public place, he is fined Rs 200. Until now, 2,671 challans have been issued. "We are issuing 20-25 challans a month. Officers of sub-inspector level and above are authorised to challan violators," says Dr Deepak Bakshi, the nodal officer of the no-smoking drive.

Is the challan money being pumped back into the drive? "As of now, not," he adds. "But we may if it is required."

Manjit Singh Bains, director, UT health services, says: "The drive has made a visible impact in hospitals and government offices. We are getting weekly reports from various departments on ban enforcement."

He adds: "The UT Administration has allowed me to use money from my budget for this drive."

Hemant Goswami, chairman of an NGO called Burning Brain Society which was instrumental in making the city smoke-free, says there has been no monetary help from the Centre. "'They released millions of rupees to 11 other states for a similar campaign on the lines of Chandigarh, but not a paisa to the city that introduced the concept."

This, when Goswami was invited by Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss to his home state, Tamil Nadu, last year to help work out a campaign in Chennai as well.

The campaign has not been a smooth sailing. "Awareness level was very high in the initial four-five months," says Vivek Atray, UT tourism director.

However, for A P S Shergill, who is a member of the Chandigarh Tobacco Control Cell, the drive has become a non-issue. "When SSP Gaurav Yadav was here, there was a proactive approach. But now, there is total apathy. While foreigners respect the ban, locals don't," he says.

There is a discernible slackening on the ground. For example, when the drive was launched, a huge hoarding on smoke-free Chandigarh had come up at Sector 17 inter-state bus terminus. It is no longer there. Nor is there any signboard at the Sector 43 bus stand. As a result, many outsiders don't get the message. "We did not know smoking is banned here," says Bunty Thakur, a Nagpur resident. "We came here for a job interview. But cigarettes are not easily available here."

It's not just outsiders, even locals can be seen smoking in public, making the job more difficult for cops. "We lack sufficient strength. Moreover, we have more pressing problems at hand. But we do challan people," says a sub-inspector, requesting anonymity.

Heading: CIC seeks marital status information on Hema Malini, Dharmendra - Indian Express
Content:
Hemant Goswami, chairperson of the Burning Brain Society — an NGO — was instrumental in getting Chandigarh residents to kick the butt, at least in public places. And to stub out the cigarette, he used RTI.

Goswami, who claims to be the great grandson of Swami Ram Tirath, filed around 300 RTI applications with various government departments to know what they were doing to implement provisions of a 2003 legislation. One day, he confronted Chandigarh Administrator O P Verma when he was going to attend a bravery awards function associated with a cigarette brand. He also filed a writ in the High Court, making the governors of Punjab and Haryana and the Chandigarh Administrator a party. That's what he calls the first hardcore sensitisation of officers at a high level. All this before 2006.

When around 1,800 signboards, against the use of tobacco, came up across the city in 2006, the idea of making Chandigarh a smoke-free city took root. With a Master's in marketing management, Goswami met officials in the Union Health Ministry and UT Administration and convinced them that it was doable.

After July 15, 2007 when Chandigarh was officially declared smoke-free, Goswami went out with his team, spotting violators. Then he filed 200 complaints against them.

Goswami, who has tried a puff or two during his college days, hopes the campaign will be successful. "We have seen highs and lows. But from now onwards the drive can only get better," he says, hinting at the October 2 deadline.

"It's an accident that tobacco is a legal drug. It's 10 times more dangerous than heroin," he says. "I'll keep fighting till tobacco becomes illegal."

Heading: Two surrender in German tourist molestation case - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Information Commission (CIC) on Wednesday recommended both Houses of Parliament to make available information on the marital status of MPs Dharmendra and Hema Malini. In a carefully-drafted order to the secretariats of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah delivered a non-binding instruction to provide relevant details on the issue.

The order comes on the basis of an RTI request by Subhash Aggarwal seeking information if the two MPs, both actors-turned-politicians, were married to each other and whether they had shared any information on their marital status.

The RTI applicant had appealed to the CIC to direct Parliament officials to furnish correct details about the them. As per Lok Sabha, wife of BJP MP Dharmendra is Prakash Deol. Whereas Rajya Sabha MP Hema Malini in her submissions has claimed Dharmendra Deol to be her husband. The Rajya Sabha Secretariat said "spouse of Hema Malini is Dharmendra and the information is based on the bio-data submitted by the MP in the House".

Aggarwal, who wanted to know about the discrepancies in the answers, was told by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat that under the RTI Act, the resolution of discrepancies in the information available with the two secretariats is not their mandate. Lok Sabha Secretariat through several letters had mentioned that Dharmendra did not supply any information about his wife to the 'Who's Who Cell'.

Heading: Nepal, India to reconstruct Kosi river embankment - Indian Express
Content:
Two of the five accused who allegedly kidnapped a German national from Hotel Taj GVK and molested her on Sunday, surrendered in the district courts around 4 pm on Wednesday. The two, identified as Sukhwinder Singh alias Sukhi (23) and Maninder Singh Jolly (24), were remanded to police custody for two days by the chief judicial magistrate.

Of the five, 20-year-old Pankaj was arrested on Monday and Harpreet Singh alias Dalli was arrested on Tuesday. Another accused, Sompal, is absconding. He is facing a trial in an attempt to murder case, the police said.

Sukhi and Jolly surfaced in court on Wednesday soon after Harpreet was remanded to police custody for two days. They were sent for medical examination to Government Multi Specialty Hospital, Sector 16.

According to Ambala police, both the accused are drug addicts and have several cases of narcotics possession registered against them. Reportedly, the duo is facing trial in another case of kidnapping in Ambala.

In their statements to the police, Jolly and Sukhi said they came to Chandigarh on Saturday evening along with Sompal, Pankaj and Harpreet. They had drinks at a liquor vend in Kaimbwala village and went to the hotel where they saw a foreigner standing in the parking lot. Jolly was the first one to approach her.

"After a brief conversation, she asked us to let her drive the Scorpio, to which we agreed. Later, she asked us to get her a Bacardi or vodka. She said she wanted to accompany us to Ambala and we took her along," said Sukhi in his statement to the police.

The accused kept mum when asked how the girl sustained injuries all over her body.

Heading: Broadcasters’ body moots PPP model - Indian Express
Content:
Nepal and India on Wednesday agreed to start reconstruction of the damaged Kosi embankment in January after the water level recedes and decided to expedite the work on two major power projects.

Nepal-India Joint Committee on Water Resources meet, which concluded here on Wednesday, decided to start the reconstruction of breached Kosi embankment after the water level goes down in January with an aim to complete the work in March, Nepalese Water Resources Secretary Shanker Prasad Koirala said on Wednesday.

Heading: Rizwanur named uncle, cops guilty in suicide note - Indian Express
Content:
The News Broadcasters Association (NBA) has called for a "public-private-partnership" between the broadcast industry and the Government to ensure the sector is "strengthened" and not "strangulated".

The move comes after the NBA announced the constitution of a nine-member "News Broadcasting Standards (Disputes Redressal) Authority", headed by former Chief Justice J S Varma, to enforce NBA's Code of Ethics and Broadcasting Standards.

NBA president G Krishnan said on Tuesday that the Government cannot and should not be controlling the content through the rationalisation of television rating system, proposed by the TRAI, and should do away with "antiquated regulations".

"In the garb of purportedly rationalising television rating system, it cannot control content and cannot confuse and inter-twine the diverse subjects of 'industry research' and 'content'. TRAI has no role in laying down guidelines for industry research and it should not deviate from worldwide industry practices, which they have relied upon," Krishnan said at the first annual general meeting of the NBA.

Calling for "forward looking guidelines", Krishnan said that the regulatory models should be "incentive based rather than coercive", as this would help promote and encourage flexibility and reach audiences on new platforms.

Krishnan also called for a national digital policy, as suggested by the Indian Entertainment and Media Industry Report 2007 of FICCI Pricewaterhouse Coopers.

The News Broadcasting Standards (Disputes Redressal) Authority members include, under "Eminent Persons" category, historian and author Ramachandra Guha, former president NASSCOM Kiran Karnik, eminent sociologist (JNU) Prof Dipankar Gupta and economist and former under secretary general, United Nations, Nitin Desai. Members under "editors" include India TV's Vinod Kapri, Zee News' B V Rao, Star News' Milind Khandekar and Times Now's Arnab Goswami.

The authority to come into effect from October 2 was formed after months of deliberation by NBA members.

Heading: NHAI panel to probe Lucknow flyover collapse - Indian Express
Content:
Rizwanur Rehman held his uncle and four others "morally responsible" for his death in his "suicide note". On Wednesday, as the CBI placed the note before a court as part of its chargesheet, interim bail was granted to Ajay Kumar, former deputy commissioner of Kolkata police and two other police officers who were the main accused in the case.

In the note, Rizwanur wrote, "The people actually and morally responsible for my death are my uncle Saidur Rehman, uncle-in-law Anil Saraogi, Sukanti Chakraborty, Gyanwant Singh, Ajay Kumar and MLA Javed Khan."

The CBI retrieved the note from Rehman's computer, which was recovered from the home of his maternal aunt after his death on September 21, 2007. The document had been deleted from the computer and the agency retrieved it from its hard drive. The CBI is treating it as a suicide note.

Despite their names in the note, however, former Deputy Commissioner ( Headquarters) Singh, Trinamool MLA Khan and Saidur were not chargesheeted because the CBI could not gather evidence against them. "Only evidence matters in court," said an official of the agency.

According to sources, the persons named had acted with malice and were instrumental in breaking Rehman's marriage with Priyanka Todi.

In the note, Rehman wrote: "...I am leaving this world forever. We live in a so called secular country. But in the last 20 days, I have seen the true face of the administration, which runs on money. There is no law to protect common man. I know I should have contested (my case) in a court of law...but what after that... my in-laws would have made sure that our lives were ruined for ever."

The Sessions Court, meanwhile, granted interim bail to the three policemen on a bail bond of Rs 10,000.

The court also imposed a condition that the officers will not leave the Calcutta Metropolitan area without the permission of the CBI court till October 27. While granting bail, the judge observed that it was not possible for the accused officers to influence the 184 witnesses named in the chargesheet.

The CBI had filed the chargesheet against Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das on September 20 in the CBI court, which had directed them to appear on October 27. The police officers, however, had surrendered on Tuesday. The officers filed a bail petition on Wednesday.

Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti made it clear that the state government had washed its hands of the accused police officers.

Heading: TN couple get ‘alternative Nobel’ for helping landless Dalits - Indian Express
Content:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on Wednesday decided to set up a two-member committee to probe into the shortcoming in the construction of the flyover that collapsed on Tuesday. The committee comprises Professor A K Nagpal, Head of Department of Civil Engineering, IIT-Delhi, and Mahesh Tandon, Managing Director of Tandon Consultant Private Limited, New Delhi.

Officials said the committee will check the design of the flyover for any inadequacy, leading to the accident. Experts will test the quality of the material used in the construction.  

NHAI General Manager R B Sinha has asked the committee to suggest remedial measures and additional safety measures in order to prevent the recurrence of such incidents. The committee has been asked to submit its report within 21 days.

NHAI Project Director M K Jain said the committee will visit Lucknow this week to initiate the inquiry.

About the cause of accident, Jain said: "Prima facie, it appears that the bearings of the girder had slipped, leading to the crash. But the exact cause would be known after the report of the investigation agency."

The flyover was being constructed by the Hindustan Construction Company (HCC). Jain said action may be taken against HCC if any irregularity was reported from their side in the investigation.   

Meanwhile, the HCC has announced compensations for the victims. "We declare a compensation of Rs 1 lakh to the next of the kin of each deceased and Rs 25,000 to each injured person," said U Bhattacharya, project manager of the HCC.

Heading: How can we celebrate Eid? Muslims join Jodhpur mourning - Indian Express
Content:
Perturbed by the massacre of 44 Christian women and children four decades ago, Krishnammal Jagannathan could have taken up arms to fight the dominant landlords.

Instead, she followed the Gandhian way to resolve the issue. Krishnammal supported by her husband Sankaralingam stood up for the weaker sections of the society to realise her vision of social justice and sustainable human development.

In recognition of the couple's efforts to help the landless Dalit Christians to become self sufficient through their organisation Land for The Tillers Freedom (LAFTI), the octogenarian Padma Shree awardees on Wednesday were conferred this year's Right To Livelihood Award, considered as an alternate to the Nobel Peace Prize. The award is expected to be bestowed in December.

As a child Amma, as she is known by one and all, shared stage with Mahatma Gandhi in her childhood and was involved in activism and social work since a very young age. As an active and frontline member of Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan Yatra, she had traveled the lengths and breadths of the country on foot for over 14 years. It was the massacre at Kilvenmani in 1968 that prompted Krishnammal to take up the cause of the Dalit women in a more organised but non-violent way.

However, the problems confronting her were not entirely new — she had seen her mother Nagammal, a Dalit woman from Ayyankottai village, toiling hard to raise the children. In fact, the story goes, that Nagammal was in an advanced stage of pregnancy, but had to trek to the mountains to gather feed for the cattle — the only livelihood for the family — due to extreme poverty. There, she gave birth to a baby and had to labour back carrying the infant in a bundle of grass.

Images of the struggle that women among the 'untouchables' had to face had left an impression on Krishnammal that decided her future, and that of hundreds of others.

To begin with, she faced stiff resistance to secure just one acre land for a Dalit family. "When we first tried to secure land that was in the hands of upper class landlords and temples, to help the poor, we faced severe opposition. Large tracts of lands that were against the ceiling act were benami dealings. As soon as we found such land, the owner would go to the court and use his powers to prevent us from taking it over," she told The Indian Express.

As an innovative way to break the deadlock and secure maximum possible benefits for the poor, LAFTI decided to purchase land, instead of waiting for donations, like the Sarvodaya or usurping like extremist Left outfits. This strategy proved to be a win-win situation as landlords were pleased with the money and the procurers were more responsible to their 'property'. Loans based on the concept of microfinance were also introduced.

Till date, Krishnammal and Sankaralingam have managed to distribute more than 10,000 acres of land to as many families. LAFTI also organises for funds to construct pucca houses as the mud houses "are as dirty as a pigsty".

Heading: Malegaon mulls black on Eid, but on ground, it’s united colour of festivities - Indian Express
Content:
The Muslim community in Jodhpur has collectively decided to hold muted Eid-ul-Fitr celebrations as a show of solidarity with victims of the Chamunda Devi temple stampede.

The community was among the first to organise relief operations at the Meherangadh Fort on Tuesday and has donated Rs 1 lakh to a relief fund as well as begun blood donation drives.

The show of solidarity began on Wednesday afternoon when Muslim youths went around the city putting up posters requesting the community to only offer namaaz on Thursday and not celebrate Eid with the usual pomp. "This stampede is probably the worst such tragedy in Jodhpur ever... How can we celebrate after such a tragedy?" said Ateef Ahmed, Chairman of the Marwar Educational Society and a social activist.

Jamaat-E-Islami Hind's state president Salim Engineer said they have requested Muslims across the state to celebrate a muted Eid as a show of solidarity with the families mourning the loss of their loved ones.

The efforts of the Muslim community have not gone unnoticed. Sunil Rajoria, a resident of the Kallal Colony, which is located just 500 metres from the fort and which lost 10 men to the stampede, said: "We have always lived as one here and Muslims were among the first to rush to hospitals to donate blood and help with the rescue effort. We appreciate this effort by our Muslim brothers in our time of mourning."

He added that this gesture meant far more than the stream of VIPs, who have been coming without a break since Tuesday morning. AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi has dropped in, besides former Rajasthan chief ministers Ashok Ghelot and Bhairon Singh Shekhawat, former foreign minister Jaswant Singh and at least 15 state ministers.

Saying politicians remembered them at the time of elections, Santosh Chauhan too appreciated the gesture by his Muslim neighbours. Muslims and Hindus have always lived as one in the colony, he said.

Both Rajoria and Chauhan hope the move by the Muslims sends a much-needed message to not just Jodhpur but the entire country. "Such a gesture at a time when forces are trying to divide Hindus and Muslims should not go unnoticed," says Rajoria.

Heading: Think before shooting mouth: Badal to his FM - Indian Express
Content:
For a community shaken by repeated attacks and allegations, Eid celebrations at the open grounds of Malegaon tomorrow will be a real test. The message has gone out — the community will wear a black band as a mark of protest.

At the market where 11-year-old Farheen lost her life in Monday's blast, there was a slight buzz today as women came out to buy bangles. In a city, where everything has become symbolic, the sight of Hindu women selling bangles and helping the Muslim women select a good shade did not go unnoticed. It were the police barricades next to the bangle market that reduced the number of casualties that night.

In another corner, it's the Muslims who have come back to work and are busy selling religious items and sacred threads to Hindus on the eve of Navratri. The Attar family is busy selling saffron and turmeric powder to Hindus.

"I have been doing this for generations. The Hindus and Muslims have good terms. It's at the political level that such things take a communal tone. I have been reading and hearing what everyone says about Malegaon after every blast or communal tension. It's just unfortunate," says Allauddin Attar (45).

Today, with reinforced police chowkis forming the backdrop, Muslims were hotly debating whether to wear black bands as a protest or not. "We will get to know the actual participation only tomorrow when people come in the morning for the prayers. We are still debating whether to wear old clothes or new clothes as a mark of protest," said Mukhtar Sheikh, a community representative.

However, the hurt and anxiety over the Government's "attitude" is palpable. "The festivities are marred this year too by investigations, and fingers are still being pointed towards us. They forget that the dead are also Muslims," says one.

Adds Dilshad H, who has been visiting hospitals: "There is poverty and so much apathy here. With every such attack that takes place during important occasions, it is the community's faith that it attacked. It's very unfortunate as the communal divide is becoming more acute."

The divide that Dilshad is referring to is not just between communities. It's also the utter lack of faith in law enforcement, especially the police.

"It's just unfortunate," admits Inspector General S P Gupta. "We will do a review on the entire policing and seek answers on where did we go wrong. For us safety on the occasion of Eid is of extreme importance."

Heading: Starting today, smokers to be challaned like traffic violators - Indian Express
Content:
Making it clear that subsidies are here to stay, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on Wednesday issued a stern reprimand to the state Finance Minister, Manpreet Badal, for a public statement on Tuesday that subsidies should end.

In a strongly worded statement, the Chief Minister said his "Cabinet colleagues should refrain from making irresponsible statements. Every member of the Cabinet and every SAD-BJP legislator should stay committed to the programmes and policies for which the Government received a mandate from the people".

He said all the subsidies, including pensions, free power, atta dal scheme and the shagun scheme for Dalit girls, will continue. "Let me end the confusion once and for all. These policies are here to stay and we have no intention of betraying the trust which people of the state have placed in us," he said.

Stating that people of the state should not be betrayed just to score a "few brownie points", he mentioned that every minister has to "perform creditably within the ideological framework given by the party". "I strongly disapprove of the tendency of saying one thing in the campaign and then doing the opposite on coming to power," he added.

However, this is not for the first time that Manpreet Badal has shown his unhappiness over the subsidies. He has made it well known that he feels subsidies are exacerbating the state's already miserable finances.

Dismissing the idea that these subsidies were populist measures, the CM said, "These are growth oriented policies, based on our deepest sense of commitment to people as well as on sound economics". He attributed the 30 per cent increase in the state's agriculture production this year to free power given to farmers. "We are not the only ones giving subsidies. The Union Government has its own set of subsidies. Even advanced nations like the US resort to heavy subsidisation in their agriculture and welfare sectors. Our government is not for the rich. It is a Government which cares of the farmers, small traders, shopkeepers, employees, poor, Dalits and backward classes. These are the people who form the backbone of our state's economy. They look at this government with hope, expectation and faith. I will not betray them," said the Chief Minister.

Heading: Antony denies rift between Centre and Armed Forces - Indian Express
Content:
With effect from today, people caught smoking in public will be challaned the same way as traffic norms violators are.

The Union Health Ministry has sent challan booklets to all the states and asked the authorities to send notices on the violators' addresses, if they are not able to pay the fine on the spot.

"The fine, which is up to Rs 200, will be charged the on the spot. However, if the violator shows inability to pay the challan money then, then they would be sent a notice at home specifying that they were caught smoking at a public place," said a senior official in the ministry.

"The notified officers will check the I-card of the person to make sure that the notice is delivered at the correct address," added the official.

Meanwhile, the Health Ministry has directed the states to open accounts where the money gathered from fine collection will be credited. However, it is left on the states how to make use of that money.

According to ministry officials, the states can create a separate account, as has been done by the Gujarat Government under the Department of Health, where the fine collected by various agencies/officers would be deposited. "This will enable the Department of Health to use the fund for tobacco-control activities," added the official.

The other suggestion given to the states is that the fines collected by various agencies may be deposited in a miscellaneous account of the Department of Health. In case the states have a separate account for National Tobacco Control Programme in the Health Society, the money may be deposited in that account too.

The implementing Government agencies/ department may also deposit the fine in a miscellaneous account or any other account where the fines collected by other departments like the railways are deposited.

In case the implementing agency in a non governmental/ private body, then the amount collected has to be deposited in the account identified by the State Government.

If the owner, proprietor, manager or supervisor, or in-charge of affairs of the public place fails to act on the report of such violations, he shall be fined the same amount as the number of individual offences. "State health secretaries, district collectors, education secretaries have been sent the final reminder," the health official noted.

FIGURE IT OUT

• There are more than 1 billion smokers across the world. In India, 57 per cent of males and 11 per cent of females use tobacco in some form.

• Second-hand smoking causes lung disease, cancer, heart disease, low birth weight and increased infant death.

• More than 5 million people die due to tobacco consumption each year — more than AIDS, Tuberculosis and malaria combined. In India, 8 to 9 lakh Indians die due to tobacco-related diseases.

• More than 2,200 Indians die everyday due to tobacco use.

• Smoking amounts for 10 per cent of the 10 million deaths per year from all causes. 70 per cent of smoking deaths are in middle age (30-69 years). In India, 36.9 per cent children start smoking before the age of 10.

• Cigarette smoking among youth is high in central, southern and northeastern regions.

• Second-hand smoke in public places is as high as 40.3 per cent.

Heading: Terror war-room in PMO; consensus: no new law just yet - Indian Express
Content:
After talking tough with the Service chiefs, Defence Minister A K Antony on Wednesday sought to downplay the rift as he said there were no differences between the Government and the Armed Forces over the Sixth Central Pay Commission (CPC) report.

His statement comes in the wake of the Defence forces' signal to its 1.5 million personnel on the "anomalies" in the CPC, asking them to "be patient in the larger interest of the Services," which was seen as an act of defiance of the Cabinet decision to implement revised pay scales from September 1.

"There is no difference between the government and the Services, because they are also part of the government. Don't read too much (into the forces' signal)," Antony told reporters after the Defence Accounts Day function here.

Pointing out that the Government had taken a decision in the Cabinet to implement the Pay Commission report after amendments, Antony said the additional burden on the exchequer due to the changes in the approved CPC is Rs 6,000 crore.

"After the decision of the Cabinet, Services' chiefs noted some of the problems and anomalies, specifically regarding the Defence forces, which is but natural. The government is examining it at the appropriate level. Meanwhile, you are reading too much. It is not correct," he said.

Stating that the Armed Forces had already submitted the details for the revised pay scales, the Defence Minister said the Government had issued a notification for paying adhoc arrears to the personnel, due to the delay in calculating their revised pay for October.

"Also, the Prime Minister has appointed a committee headed by my senior colleague Pranab Mukherjee. So there is no problem. As far as we are concerned, there is no difference," he added.

Heading: Manmohan says insulating India from global meltdown top priority - Indian Express
Content:
Within hours of returning from his trip to the U S and France, National Security Adviser M K Narayanan on Wednesday chaired a high-level meeting at the PMO to discuss the strengthening of India's anti-terror legislation.

Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister T K A Nair, Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta, Law Secretary T K Vishwanathan and Defence Secretary Vijay Singh attended the hour-long meeting.

The consensus, officials said, was that instead of immediately framing an exclusive anti-terror law on the lines of POTA, the Government should further augment existing laws, mainly the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, which was amended through an Ordinance to add a section on terrorism after POTA was repealed in 2004.

The meeting also felt that since police was a state subject, adding provisions to existing legislation would be preferable to immediately creating a separate federal agency, sources said. This could be done along the lines of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS), 1985,which has sections empowering both the central and state governments to designate officials to investigate cases. "Given India's size and the federal nature of our polity, a number of agencies both at the Centre and in the states have been empowered to enforce the provisions of the Act," it says.

Officials who attended the meeting said that they had met principally to analyze the recommendations of the Administrative Reforms Commission on terror legislation, and it was the PMO which would now revert to the Home Ministry and the Law Ministry on giving a final shape to a new, stringent anti-terror law.

The M Veerappa Moily-led panel, which made its recommendations public last month, advocated fresh terror laws, with adequate safeguards, to effectively combat and deal with terrorism in the country. The Moily panel had also suggested having a comprehensive and effective legal framework to deal with terrorism, the setting up of a federal agency to investigate acts of terror, and recommended changes in the National Security Act (NSA).

The panel had stressed that laws like the Maharashtra Control of Organized Crime Act (MCOCA) and POTA were not enough to deal with terrorism, and a comprehensive, holistic law that included enough safeguards to prevent its misuse, could be a good bulwark against terrorism.

It is learnt that the National Security Adviser, who held meetings with top intelligence officers and anti-terrorism experts in the U S, is of the view that the government has to take a strong stand to control terrorism. Despite dissenting voices from regional parties, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh is keen to see some headway on the issue.

The central government is also understood to have come to the conclusion that since terrorism has been defined as the "biggest threat" by the U N, India should enter into a strategic sharing of resources with countries such as the U S to check terrorism.

This, sources said, can be possible, as Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws implementing any treaty, agreement or convention with another country or any decision made at any international conference, association, or other body. These include U N resolutions on terrorism, the financing of terror, and the U N Security Council's convention on terrorism.

Specifically, India is a signatory to the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism, adopted by the U N in 1999. The convention asks each member-country to adopt measures, including legislation, to check the flow of funds to terrorist groups.

Heading: As SC raps, Centre says doctors can’t deny care to HIV+ - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has outlined a four-point priority list he says his government will follow as it enters its last lap: "insulate" India from the global financial meltdown; to "put best foot forward" in dealing with terror and Left-wing extremism; more effective implementation of flagship social programmes like NREGA; monitoring inflation which remained a "major worry." Singh said he had his "fingers crossed" that one of the side-effects of the financial crisis could be a moderation of inflation.

Unwilling to be drawn into any speculation of him being the next PM candidate for Congress — party president Sonia Gandhi has earlier suggested that he remains the party's choice for the job — he said he had not applied his mind to the prospect. "The Congress party has several leaders who are equally, if not, better qualified than I am". Singh said that by running the government for almost its full term, he had proved wrong the notion that Congress could not run a coalition government.

Speaking on his way back to India after a nine-day tour to US and France, the PM said that in the global financial crisis, India was less vulnerable compared to others but it could not possibly be immune to these developments. "If capital inflows decrease, if foreign institutional investors, because they need liquidity, take money out, that would certainly affect our stock markets, that would affect Indian corporates raising resources for investment. And if there is a recession in the developed world, particularly the United States, it could hurt our exports. We have to work out a coherent strategy to protect our interests and we are confident we will be able to do so."

Terrorism and Naxal violence, according to the PM, were "major issues" but, at the same time, he ruled out the removal of Home Minister Shivraj Patil. He said it was "not a question of one individual" and that the problem was largely systemic for which efforts will be made.

With National Security Advisor M K Narayanan sitting by his side, he said: "We need to strengthen our intelligence gathering machinery, to streamline our investigation processes, and also our prosecution processes. Those are important aspects of dealing with the terror problem and we will work hard to improve our performance in these areas."

As for flagship programmes, he said these reflected the second phase of what he called India's "new design of reforms" that follows "no ideological positions", which he launched in 1991 as Finance Minister. On the question of inflation, he said there were still uncertainties in the energy market though there was hope that the current crisis will have some moderating impact. "We have to worry about inflation while maintaining the momentum of growth process."Politically, Singh exuded a reassured calm given that the civilian nuclear initiative with US, for which he risked his government, had delivered its first result in the form of the Indo-French civil nuclear cooperation agreement. Yet, he was cautious not to sound triumphant, saying there was still time before the agreement could be operationalised, and hoped that the Left and BJP would see matters objectively.

"I felt very sad when our Left colleagues parted company. I still have not given up hope and carry the conviction that what we have done through the nuclear deal protects all the essential interests of our country, it protects our strategic programme, it opens up new options for India to manage its energy situation and it is part of our policy which would widen our development options. So I sincerely believe that whether it is the BJP or the Left, if they look objectively, there is nothing in the nuclear deal which will hurt the interests of the country."

Asked if he saw a role for the Left if the Congress was once again in a position to form the government after the next polls, he said: "I am not an astrologer. But I would like all friendly like-minded segments of the population to work together to resolve all major problems. India is on a verge of great opportunities and the challenge to India is not so much from external environment as how we manage our domestic politics. I would like all political parties to pool their wisdom, knowledge and experience to deal collectively with all national problems- that applies to the Left, that applies to the BJP, that applies to everyone."

For someone, who is still considered an outsider in politics, Singh was taken aback when asked whether he had transformed into a politician from his days as Finance Minister to now when he is the PM. "As Finance Minister, I was only a member of the team but now I am the captain of the team. It is a coalition government and therefore there are compulsions of managing a coalition which often puts a constraint. The charge against the Congress is that it is not good at managing coalitions. I wanted to prove that statement wrong and I think we have nearly succeeded."

Heading: Khanduri declares sops for statehood ‘martyrs’ - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors who refuse to treat HIV/ AIDS patients will be sternly dealt with, the Centre told the Supreme Court on Wednesday. However, during the hearing on a PIL related to the matter, the court observed that the Government is not doing enough to improve the public healthcare system.

During the hearing of a PIL highlighting apathetic treatment and lack of facilities for HIV/ AIDS patients across the country, the three-member Bench, headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, on Wednesday remarked, "In rural India, there are hardly any doctors. Even in a 50-bed hospital not a single doctor is available. It's only on paper."

As Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium informed the court that the Government has recently asked all the state governments to improve healthcare facilities, and that primary health centres were working satisfactorily in rural areas of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, the court shot back, "Go and check in any government hospital in Delhi, Bihar and UP."

Trying to convince the Bench about the 'remedial' measures taken at the highest level to deal with instances of refusal to persons living with HIV/ AIDS (PLHA) or non-availability of basic medicines or treatment for them, the Government counsel said all the states have been asked to implement the office memorandum sent to them recently. According to the office memorandum, "All doctors, nurses and hospital staff, whether in the public or private sector shall treat PLHAs in a professional and humane manner, treating them always with dignity and care. No doctor or nurse shall refuse to treat a PLHA on account of his/her positive status. In treating a PLHA there shall be no discrimination or stigma whatsoever." It also suggested taking stringent steps against any doctor who refuses to treat any HIV/ AIDS patient.

"The cases of denial of services to positive patients should be viewed seriously and action initiated in all such cases," stated the memorandum, placed before the court. The Centre said private doctors have been directed to make themselves acquainted with National AIDS Control Organisation's (NACO) protocols and policies with regard to the care and treatment, which are available on NACO's website.

The Bench, also comprising Justices Ashok Bhan and P Sathasivam, directed all states to furnish their response to the office memorandum within four weeks.

Heading: Cabinet panel extends NHAI CVO’s term, Ministry miffed - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of the anniversary of the pivotal Rampur Tiraha incident of 1994, Uttarakhand Chief Minister B C Khanduri has announced sops for the activists of the Uttarakhand agitation. Talking to media persons on Wednesday, which also happened to be his birthday, Khanduri said, "We have decided to give recognition to the people who have made sacrifices for the creation of the state. Various roads, schools and other government institutions will be named after them."

Khanduri will also visit to Rampur Tiraha on Thursday to pay homage to the activists who were killed in police firing on the night of October 1 in 1994. The incident is viewed as a turning point in the Uttarakhand agitation.

Khanduri announced that special identity cards will be issued to the activists and due respect accorded to them at all the events organised by the state Government. He said that the state Government has decided to create a Rs 2 crore corpus for helping the activists in need of money and extended horizontal reservation for them by another two years.

Heading: Now Centre tells HC gay sex against  nature’s order - Indian Express
Content:
While things may have been in favour of the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways (MORTH) when it managed to get NHAI chairman N Gokulram replaced last month, the situation is different today as the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has recommended a two-year term extension for NHAI CVO R Mukundan, against MORTH's wishes.

While Mukundan's term ended on June 15, the ministry's efforts to oust him started even before that. However, the ACC has now held that the CVO should continue in the position till the committee arrives at a final decision on the issue. The ACC is learnt to have gone with the NHAI and the Chief Vigilance Commission's (CVC) views and recommended a two-year extension for Mukundan some days back.

Not pleased, Minister of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways T R Baalu is said to have shot off a letter to the DoPT, mentioning that his ministry's views were not taken into account when the ACC took the decision. The ministry has argued that the CVO had applied for positions in other PSUs and was himself not keen on staying on at NHAI, besides not being senior enough for the post. The DoPT, in turn, has now politely conveyed that the decision was taken as per rules and it is its final view on the matter.

The Indian Express had earlier reported how the ministry had written to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), asking for the removal of NHAI's Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) R Mukundan, overruling the CVC's recommendation for his tenure extension. Mukundan was, incidentally, in the line of fire for a decision that is said to have earned him a pat on the back from the CVC. The ACC decision was taken last month and conveyed to the ministry which obviously hasn't taken very kindly to it.

At the heart of the issue that has the NHAI and the ministry in opposite camps is a national highway in Karnataka — a Rs 440-crore project under NHDP III — to four-lane the NH 48 section between Hassan and Devanhalli (near the new airport) on Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis.

There were two bids and while the ministry wanted the second bid opened, the NHAI felt that both should be opened and the one more beneficial to the authority should be accepted — a view the CVO endorsed and the ministry did not. The CVC and even the NHAI were incidentally in favour of extending Mukundan's term. In fact, Mukundan, who completed his three-year term as NHAI CVO on June 15 this year, had got a recommendation from the NHAI requesting the CVC to grant him an extension of term and the CVC had agreed.
