Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: Vijender Singh inaugurates Summit sports competition - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Poona Social beat City Club - Indian Express
Content:
Vijender Singh, bronze medallist in boxing at the Beijing Olympics, on Thursday, inaugurated the Summit sports competition organised by MAEERS MIT held at the MIT football ground. The competition will conclude on October 5.

Vishwas Deval, president of Maharashtra Rowing Federation, Mangesh Karad, executive director-MIT, Padmakar Phad, Chhatrapati awardee for boxing, S N Rane, head of department, human resource management-MIT, former boxer Manoj Pingale, and Vijender's Singh's coach Gurbax Singh were also present at the function.

Vishwanath Karad, founder director, MIT, spoke about the various sporting competitions to be played and gave a brief account on the colleges taking part in the event. Chief guest Vijender Singh was then felicitated and congratulated for his achievement in Beijing. He also kicked off the inaugural football match between MIT COE and PVG College of engineering.

The Summit sports competition consists of 12 disciplines: football, basketball, volleyball, cricket, baseball, badminton, table tennis, chess, carrom, Squash, Water Polo and Swimming. There will be up to 2,000 athletes participating at these games. Cups, Medals and prize money worth Rs five lakh will be given away to the winners. More than 40 engineering colleges from Mumbai, Nashik, Kolhapur, Ahmednagar, Aurangabad, Ratnagiri and Nagpur will take part. The venue for football, volleyball, baseball, table tennis, chess and carrom will be MIT. The basketball competition will be held at Fergusson College, cricket at NCL, Law College and BMCC while water polo and swimming will be held at Tilak Tank.

Heading: Bendre wins  weightlifting competition - Indian Express
Content:
Poona Social defeated City Club 1-0 in a major upset in the club-level Gurta Gaddi football tournament conducted by the Strikers football club held at the CAFVD ground, Khadki, on Thursday.

City Club, runners up in last year's super league, suffered a shock exit at the hands of Poona Social. The only goal of the match was scored by Candidus Davidus in the 20th minute after receving a good pass from Moses Anthony. The winners managed to keep a clean sheet thanks to their strong defence and have now entered the semifinal. In another match, Extreme Warriors beat Ashoka FC 1-0 with Mangesh Vermani scoring a goal in the seventh minute.

Phoenix FC edged past Sangam FC in the tiebreaker after both teams were deadlocked 1-1 at the end of regulation time. Raju Nikam helped Sangam take the lead in the 39th minute and Pushkar Waichal equalized for his team in the 55th minute. In the penalty shootout, Siddharth Dhage, Saket Kulkarni and Rahul Ravendikar scored for the winners and Raju Nikam and Vicky Kadam scored for the losing team. Phoenix won the shootout 3-2.

Heading: ‘Remove sugar from MCX’ - Indian Express
Content:
Prashant Bendre of Tata Motors team won the best weightlifter award at the Industrial Weightlifting Competition organised by the Industrial Sports Association held at the Amenity Hall, Tata Motors Hostel, recently.

Bendre won the 69 kg event securing 80 points in the snatch lift and 105 points in the jerk lift.

Vijay Pawar won the event in the 51 kg category with 50 points in the snatch lift and 65 points in the jerk lift. Atul Chavan from the 512 Army team won the 56 kg category securing 132.5 points in both the lifts.

Ravindra Kakade from the Endurance team won the 62 kg category bagging a total of 155 points in both the lifts.

In the 77 kg category, Hemant Kakade from CAFVD stood first with 170 points. Hemant Jadhav from JCB won the 85 kg category getting 155 points. Hindurao Patil of KSB won the 94 kg event with a total of 157.5 points. MC Balmiki of KSB again won the 105 kg category, gaining 135 points.

Heading: Institute of Engineers celebrate Golden Jubilee function - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the future's trading market in sugar 'nothing less than gambling,' Kaniayah lala Gidwani, All India Congress Committee member has called for the removal of sugar from the Multi-commodity Exchange (MCX) or the National Commodities or the derivatives exchange (NCDEX). Gidwani has written to the Forward Market Commission of the Government of India, asking for the same.

"Since inclusion of sugar in the futures market, one has not witnessed any gains to the sugarcane farmer and year after year, there has only been manipulation of the futures market by some traders who have fluctuated sugar for personal gains. In the past 10-15 days, these very persons have benefited in the futures market by a ten-times gain, an amount which the sugarcane farmer cannot even dream of. The farmer even after toiling for two years on sugarcane has not made this kind of profit," Gidwani said in a press release.

Comparing the prices of the futures market and the spot market, Gidwani said the price difference is as much as Rs 400 per quintal.

"The current ex-factory price is prevailing at Rs 1,550 per quintal for sugar without duty (duty being Rs 100 per quintal). The forward trading rate is hovering at a rate as high as Rs 2,100 per quintal and above. This is only due to some traders deliberately fluctuating the market for their own gains. The repercussion of this sets a wrong indication on the price for spot delivery, which is not good, as rates then on sentimental grounds tend to increase," he said.

Heading: The good earth - Indian Express
Content:
The Institute of Engineers (India), Pune Local Centre, celebrated their Golden Jubilee year on September 30, with Air Marshal S.S.Ramdas inaugurating the function. Jyotsna Despande, Chairman of the Pune Centre speaking on the occassion, said, "The Centre was founded in November 1958 and ever since then it has been awarded the "Best Centre in India" five times."

A special series of lectures was organised for the occasion, which included a series of presentations about the Koyna Dam, seminar on Micro Irrigation, Earthquake Disaster Management and energy saving tips for Households.

D S Gandhe, ex-chairman, elaborating about the programmes said, "The Centre arranges over 150 programmes in a year. Consisting of National Conventions, Seminars, Workshops, Lectures, Exhibitions, Visits, and Competitions. It also arranges guidance classes of AMIE, GATE, BEE, UPSC and MPSC examinations every year."

Air Marshal Ramdas spoke about the history of aviation and the current global scenario. He also said that it was very important to establish new hubs for the betterment of the nation. He also said that the proposed new airport at Rajgurunagar would be ideal for local development.

Heading: Foot prints - Indian Express
Content:
Aiming at neo-conventional construction practices, this foundation releases Earthbags, a guide that offers techniques to responsible construction

It is a saucer shaped structure, where children can get imaginative with papers and blissfully filthy with the clay. This dome shaped learning space that cultivates the creativity of the children of Aman Setu, the pre-primary and primary school, is named Kaleidoscope and has been made using earth bag and bamboo structure. Designed by architects and former students of Aman Setu, the learning space now has a sequel. The Madhavi Kapur Foundation has published its first booklet, Earthbags that is a follow up to the construction of the Kaleidoscope.

Says Kapur, founder of Aman Setu, "The booklet is an effort to offer an alternative to neo-conventional construction practices and provide sustainable techniques, which could be accessible to all. Kaliedoscope stands as a demonstration of the design executed by my students. The intention of sharing this idea with anyone who wants to create something on similar lines led to the book Earthbags. By creating a learning space like Kaleidoscope it lives the message that schools should remain places to inculcate strong values and awareness in students."

Earthbags depicts a technique where prolypropylene bags are filled with earth mix, sealed and stacked in running bond with a barbed wire acting as a velcro mortar between courses and consolidated by tamping. Soarabh Phadke, the author, has been one of the key participants in the building of Kaleidoscope. "Earthbags along with its Marathi counterpart named Maati-Poti pertains to several issues like resource consumption and appropriate construction technologies. The booklet is an on-field guide for builders and for all those interested in responsible construction even in remote areas," he adds.

The book was released at the Manney's Bookstore in Camp by activist Sujit Patwardhan and architect Rahul Rawat on the occasion of the bookstore's 60th birthday. Keeping in mind the preventable use of paper the publication has allowed free download of the booklet through our website www.mkf.in. "We wish to spread the concept and have thus made the copy accessible and free of cost. We would request people to resort to printing only if they are likely to apply the techniques practically. We plan to create a chain of knowledge transfer," adds Phadke. Here's to an initiative that's certainly been thought thorugh well.

Heading: Voice beyond boundaries - Indian Express
Content:
After having inspired three generations with his out-of- the-box socio-political plays, simple yet apt language and uncomplicated but to-the-point presentations, actor, director, playwright Satish Alekar will now inspire generations to come too. And the credit of documenting his theatrical life goes to filmmaker Atul Pethe.

Natakkar Satish Alekar (Playwright Satish Alekar), a film by Pethe unveils the theatrical journey of Alekar and the effect of surroundings, social and political changes on the playwright. The first screening of the film took place at Sudarshan Rangmanch on Thursday. Throwing light on the process of film making Alekar says, "I must say I am overwhelmed. When Atul asked me about this project, it took me a while before saying yes. But even if the first nod was a reluctant one, the filmmaking process of one-and-a-half year was exhilarating. I am happy that through camera as a medium, the socio-political changes in the society and surroundings as seen by me are now recorded."

Atul Pethe adds explaining his viewpoint, "Alekar is a local writer. There is no such concept as a global writer. The greatest writers in the world have always portrayed what happened in and around them. It was the approach that was important. And Alekar has this approach. His place in the Marathi theatre industry is irreplaceable. I have grown up witnessing Alekar's plays. In fact I have acted in his plays- Atireki and Pralay. I personally feel that Alekar took Marathi theatre one-step ahead of Tendulkar's. It was after watching Mahanirvan that I was shattered. This play by Alekar changed my perspective towards theatre."

The result of this shattering experience that took place when Pethe was 13, is the film that in 90 minutes takes the audiences on a journey featuring countless facets of Alekar, the playwright. The film includes doyens from the Marathi rangabhoomi like Mohan Agashe, Samar Nakhate, Ramesh Medhekar, Chandrakant Kale and so on giving their viewpoints on Alekar as a playwright and the complex yet realistic process of portraying Alekar's thoughts on the stage as actors or colleagues. The film unfolds Alekar's journey as a playwright against a changing backdrop of the post independence India, Pune and the Marathi theatre.

"And this is important. We, Indians are a theatre loving community but unfortunately, documentation has never been a priority in our theatre. This film is shot with a motive to create documentation and to archive the thought process of an effective theatre personality. Drama is a live medium and it dies after the play is over. But with camera in front, we can preserve the themes, the acting skills, the culture and the traditions of the glorious moments of the theatre industry so that it inspires generations to come and also tells them what their ancestors were," adds Pethe.

Heading: Down to earth - Indian Express
Content:
Entry to Housefed flats was not a pleasant affair till sometime ago. an army of cattle would roam freely as the slum-dwellers and the residents blatantly threw garbage outside the flats.

The scene was pretty much the same until mid-July when 30 children of Housefed took up the cudgel and decided to give a new look to the high income group flats.

Yashika Puri, a Class IX student of KVM says: "We started door-to-door collection and managed to collect Rs 11,000, including area councillor Tanvir Singh Dhaliwal's contribution of 25 per cent. We also sought help from former district forest officer RR Kakkar."

Palak Dutta, another resident says: "Our parents encouraged us to take up the task and the filth was ultimately removed with this money. The work on the area has been initiated. About 15 days ago, we also planted saplings at the entrance of the building."

Poles and fences were erected to stop the stray animals from entering the building, which also created some welcome parking space.

Kanishak Goyal and Mankaran, part of the group, said: "We picked the wastes ourselves from outside the flats to start the drive." Chavi Shamyok, another resident, says: "We water the saplings every day so that they grow fast. Visitors have appreciated our endeavour."

Heading: Star and style - Indian Express
Content:
Abhishek Bachchan loves to watch superheroes fly. The actor tells us what's special about Drona, his non-flying warrior

With Drona now released, what's your state of mind
I'm excited. I have seen the film and liked it but now, it is for the audiences to decide Drona's fate. Since I was emotionally attached to it, my judgment would be biased. But when people who were not attached to the the making of the film watch it they will judge it on the basis of how they liked it.

Who is your favourite superhero in films and comic books?
Supremo — that was a character in a comic based on my dad. It used to come in the early 80s. I like Superman in films. He was my favourite superhero in childhood. I like superhero films. It is exciting to imagine that you can fly.

Which of these superheroes provided inspiration to you while playing Drona?
It was a beautiful character written by Goldie Behl. There was no inspiration as such because Drona is not a superhero. He can't fly. He is a normal human being.

Did the comparisons with Krrish bother you?
Not at all. Krrish was a superhero. He had special powers. Drona doesn't have such superhuman powers. Also, Hrithik Roshan is a very good friend. The three of us (Goldie, Hrithik and I) have been best friends since childhood.

What's that special factor in Drona that will help you win over the audience?
The USP is that Drona is not a superhero. When you watch the film and come out of the theatre, you will have a feeling that even you can be like Drona. You will not be in awe of the character, the way you generally are while watching a Superman or a Spider-man film.

Will Drona help in continuing with the good run that started with Guru and was taken forward by Sarkar Raj?
I hope it does. We have made the film with a lot of effort. This is a very ambitious project for Goldie and me.

Your first film with Behl didn't do well. What made you work with him?
He is a childhood friend. When he discussed this character with me, I really liked it.

Were you worried over Drona's fate following MNS outrage?
Let bygones be bygones. We should look ahead and start with a fresh perspective.

What are your expectations from Dostana and Dilli 6?
Dostana is a comedy. Comedies are doing well. Dilli 6 is a fantastic film. I have wanted to work with Rakeysh Mehra for a long time. I was supposed to do my debut film with him but that didn't work out. It's nice to work with him finally.

When would we next see you and Aishwarya Rai on the big screen?
In Mani Ratnam's film which is going on the floors soon.

Heading: Face to face with Arjan Bajwa - Indian Express
Content:
Minissha Lamba on her toned new look and her enduring search for versatile roles

From a coy Kashmiri girl in Yahaan to a lovestruck teenager in Bachna Ae Haseeno, Minissha Lamba can best be termed experimental, especially when it comes to the roles she has played. Unassuming and ethereal, she is now upbeat about her next release Kidnap.

"With each film I sign, I look to do roles that are versatile and have a hint of newness in them. I have managed to find that novelty so far. With Kidnap I have pushed the limit. I have actually seen how far I can go," says the pretty actress about the roles she has executed till date.

In the movie, she plays the role of a young girl for whom life is a party till she gets kidnapped. But for Lamba, shooting for this movie was nothing less than a party. "I had a fabulous time working with Imran Khan. He is an extremely warm person and was a big support during the making of the movie. I simply adored the way he would be around all the time." Although she plays Sanjay Dutt's daughter in the movie she did not have too many moments with him. "But whatever scenes I did with him, they were a learning experience. He is a complete actor," she beams.

And with this role, she has taken versatility to another level by undergoing an image makeover. Lamba will be wearing a bikini for a key sequence in Kidnap and she has toned her body to carry it off sexily. "When the director Sanjay Gadhvi came to me with the film, he was clear about one thing — he wanted to completely change my look and make me go through a transition. He asked me whether I was game for it but honestly, I didn't have any reason not to be a part of it. I immediately started working out and went on a strict diet."

Didn't she require any convincing whatsoever? "None at all," replies the actor promptly, "We all know what he has done to his ladies in Dhoom and Dhoom 2. All his actresses have looked fabulous on screen."

Lamba, the current It-girl of the industry, has had the good fortune of being cast opposite Bollywood heartthrob Ranbir Kapoor in Bachna Ae Haseeno and now another popular face, Imran Khan. This has made her an object of envy amongst the female fans. "Soon after the release of Bachna I attended this party where girls kept hurling abuses at me because I got to kiss Ranbir in the movie. I had to leave the place in a short while," she smiles. While she fears that more such instances can occur after Kidnap, she terms it her best role till date. "Besides, the role in Yahaan and Shaurya were special too."

Lamba says she hasn't signed any movies besides Kidnap. "For now, it is just the moment I want to enjoy."

Heading: Very filmi - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
A lot of rock music by Bon Jovi and Def Leppard, the song Ahista Ahista from Bachna Ae Haseeno and Umbrella by Rihanna.

What's your DVD pick?
The Godfather Trilogy, because it's more or less a Bible for all actors, for every aspect of filmmaking.

Your favourite romantic scene in a movie?
The romantic scenes from Forrest Gump, because they're so full of innocence and have been beautifully shot and very well-performed.

Which actress you would love to go on a date with and why?
Charlize Theron because she's incredibly beautiful. Also, because I guess I have a weakness for tall women.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
The dialogue from The Godfather, where Michael Corleone is talking to his brother, "Fredo, you're my older brother, and I love you. But don't ever take sides with anyone against the family again. Ever."

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Nobody inspired me to become an actor. The desire to be one was inborn, I guess. But my father has been a wonderful support system.

The worst film you ever watched?
That list is endless. I won't take any names, because I don't want to offend anybody.

Which film you wish you could be a part of?
I wish I'd been a part of Rang De Basanti, because I loved the movie. It was so in-your-face. Another movie I wish I'd been a part of is Sholay.

What makes you an actor?
I don't think it is easy to define what makes an actor. But the ability to hold your own in front of so many people; that's very important. Then it doesn't matter whether you're a good actor or a bad one.

Quiz: From which film is this line: Dur dur tak kisi gaon mein jab koi baccha rota hai, to uski maa bolti hai, "so ja, nahi to Crime Master Gogo aa jayega."
Andaz Apna Apna (correct).

Heading: Four political bigwigs share dais, enter sparring match - Indian Express
Content:
Sallu's musical inspiration
Music inspires people to do many things, so it's not surprising that the Brawn of Bollywood, Salman Khan, listens to music as he paints. According to Sajid, of Sajid-Wajid music duo, these days Sallu is obsessively listening to the track Manaata from the movie Heroes. "He listens to it at least 25 times while he paints and he loves to sing along with this track ," says Sajid, "We had a ball recording this track and we believe that it will grow on listeners in the coming days."

Heavy duty
SOPHIE Chaudhary is one strong chick. Not many people know that for her item song with Sanjay Dutt in Sanjay Gadhvi's Kidnap, the lady had to wear two heavy costumes—one with mirrors that weighed five kg and one with crystals that weighed over 10 kg. But that didn't dampen Sophie's enthusiasm. "We were amazed at her," says her costume designer Shilpa Bhatia, "she was dancing like breeze." Bhatia adds, "The funniest part was when Sophie would change into her usual get up and tell everybody around that she felt so much lighter and would talk about weight-loss. It was just that removing the heavy costumes made her feel lighter."

No deal
RUMOURS have been spreading about Kareena Kapoor launching a production house. According to recent reports, Bebo's first film as a producer would have her friend Lovely Singh as director and herself and Saif Ali Khan in the lead roles. But the actress is quick to rubbish these reports and says, "I have no intention to turn producer. The rumours are baseless. There is no truth to it." A source close to the actress points out, "Kareena hails from the RK family and with the prestigious RK banner with her, why would she launch an independent production house?" Point taken.

Boys' toys
IT is true that inside every man, there's a little boy obsessed with toys. Why else would producer Sanjay Gupta hire innumerable choppers, eight massive trucks, snazziest sports cars, nothing less than Lamborghinis and Ferraris, super bikes like Hayabusas and Harley Davidsons, SUVs, yachts and speedboats for his new movie Acid Factory? The filmmaker even got a special stunt team to choreograph a never-before-seen action sequence involving four-wheel motorcycles. The team was hired from South Africa and another team was especially flown down from Hong Kong. Even the pilots and drivers have been sourced from South Africa and Hong Kong. Now that is called dedication regardless of costs.

Heading: Woman throws little daughters from sixth floor, jumps to death - Indian Express
Content:
Sharad Pawar, Gopinath Munde, Narayan Rane, Dilip Walse-Patil take potshots at one another

It was a rare meeting of four political heavyweights on one dais.

For those who were waiting for the fireworks, it did not quite pan out. But it was not without its share of political byplay either.

Bharatiya Janata Party National General Secretary Gopinath Munde took a dig at the dismal power scenario in the state, Pune in particular, by thanking state Electricity and Education Minister Dilip Walse-Patil for no power cuts during Thursday's function.

Munde did not spare Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh either, terming him a man of many words and little action.

State Revenue Minister Narayan Rane had a go at Munde and his party asking what the BJP-Shiv Sena combine did when it was in power.

However, Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar, refused to join sides and tried to calm things down by referring to the friendship Munde and Rane had nurtured all these years .

"I am happy that Rane mentioned his friendship with Munde. I feel Munde was a loyal friend as he guided Rane. But Rane has not remained loyal. It was he who left his party. My fatherly advise to Rane is don't leave your friend behind."

However, he could not resist to give a piece of 'advice' to Munde when he asked him to remain patient. "Munde's party has patience. They keep on waiting with optimism as they did in the last Assembly elections," said Pawar.

Pawar, Munde, Rane and Walse-Patil were sharing the dais at the convention of Maharashtra Union of Working Journalists (MUWJ).

Munde started his speech saying, "I am thankful to Walse-Patil that electricity was available throughout the programme." He then referred to various demands of journalists and said, "At present, I can only raise your demands with the state government. But after five to six months there is every possibility that I could actually fulfill your demand."

While making this comment, Munde did not spare the chief minister and said, "If he (Vilasrao Deshmukh) would have been at the function he would have promised you about fulfilling your demands. The chief minister doesn't lag behind in making promises."

Rane hit back at Munde in his speech. "You had an opportunity (when you were in power) to solve these issues. But you didn't do anything. I don't think you will get another opportunity," he said.

Rane, however, tried to pull his punch, calling Munde his 'good friend'. "Munde is my good friend wherever he may be. He even guided me when I left (Shiv Sena)," he said.

Walse- Patil did not get a chance to respond to Munde as he had spoken before Munde's speech.

The main theme of his speech was a staunch defence of his leader. "Even as the food production in the country touched a new high of 227 million tonne this year, the media is holding the Union Agriculture Minister responsible for the suicides in Vidarbha," he said. He also 'advised' the media to be responsible before making any comment on big leaders.

Heading: 200 buses on CYG opening, closing days - Indian Express
Content:
Children, mother die on spot; suicide note cites husband's extramarital affair as reason

In a heart-wrenching incident, a 30-year-old woman threw her two daughters Harshada (5) and Sakshi (4), from the sixth floor of a building in Pudamjee Paradise complex in Bhavani Peth around 10 am on Thursday.

After that, the woman, Sunita Arvind Khandagale, jumped down. All the three died on the spot.

In a suicide note, Sunita said she was taking the extreme step as her husband was having an extramarital affair. The deceased were staying in flat number A/3 on the first floor of Pudamjee Paradise.

"Sunita said in a suicide note that her husband was having an affair with a woman named Sheetal who used to send SMSes and call him frequently on his mobile phone due to which she was committing suicide. She also said her body should be handed over to her brother Kaluram Rokade," said Assistant Commissioner of Police Suresh Pote.

"We suspect that she killed her children thinking that nobody would take care of them after her death. An offence would be registered against her husband Arvind under section 306 (abetting suicide) of the Indian Penal Code," said Pote.

Police said that the victims were from a middle class family. Arvind was an employee of a private firm in Mukund Nagar. He was staying in a two-room apartment in Pudamjee Paradise with his wife, daughters, parents and brother.

Harshada was a student of class II and Sakshi was in kindergarten at a school run by Camp Education Society. On Thursday morning, Arvind left home for his office, after which Sunita took her daughters to the terrace of the building.

She first dropped Sakshi, then Harshada and then jumped down herself. Some residents saw them lying in a pool of blood and informed the police and family members. A few policemen, who were deployed on duty a few metres from Pudamjee Paradise for Ramzan, rushed to the spot.

"The victims died on the spot. Their bodies were sent for postmortem," a policeman said.

"A resident named Faheem Shaikh was standing in the gallery of his flat when the incident took place. Faheem was speaking on his cellphone when he saw the children and their mother falling down one after the other," said another policeman. Shaikh was too shocked to comment.

Soon, a police team comprising senior officers from Khadak police station reached the spot to investigate. Police said Sunita was a native of Mumbai.

Sunita, who married Arvind about eight years back, used to work as a cook for a woman in the neighbourhood. Sunita had told the woman about her problem.

During investigations, the woman told the police that Sunita had talked about jumping from the terrace a few days back.

Sunita's brother and other relatives who rushed from Mumbai, had a quarrel with Arvind's relatives at Sassoon hospital premises and the police had to intervene, saying an offence would be registered against Arvind.

Neighbours in festive mood shocked

People of Pudamjee Paradise and the neighbouring area, who were in a festive mood for Navratra and Ramzan, are shocked. The area where the two children were thrown down from a building by their mother, who also committed suicide by jumping down comprises people from both Hindu and Muslim communities.

Sunita had done the traditional "ghatsthapan" at her home. On Thursday, she cleaned her home and also prepared tiffin for her husband. After her husband left for his office, she went out with her daughters. The family members thought she was going to the market for purchasing vegetables.

But Sunita went to the terrace and committed suicide.

A neighbour said Sunita was a kind woman and was deeply involved in bringing up her daughters properly. The girls were good in their studies and extra-curricular activities. —ENS

Heading: Crop outsourcing: Firms look abroad for a richer harvest - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) has set aside 200 buses to ferry around 10,000 people to the Balewadi Stadium on October 12 and October 18, for the opening and the closing days of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). This will include the 110 buses earmarked for routes leading to Balewadi during the CYG week.

The downside of this is that there will be 200 buses less to ply on the regular routes on these two days. There are around 1,100 buses plying in the city on a given day.

"The stadium can accommodate around 18,000 people. We expect 10,000 people to use public buses, as only around 8,000 will be able to arrive in their own vehicles," said PMPML chairman and managing director S B Patil, during a press conference on Wednesday night to announce the bus utility's plans for the CYG week.

PMPML runs buses in over 220 routes. "Each route will have to give up a bus or two to accommodate the schedules for the CYG," said an officer from the transport department.

Ten zones in the city have been earmarked as parking slots for private vehicles. They are Golibar Maidan in Pune Cantonment Board, Government Engineering College at Shivajinagar, ILS Law College grounds, B J Medical Grounds, Khadki Post Office, Agriculture College, Wadia College, Madanlal Dingra College, Hindustan Antibiotics, Annasaheb Magar Stadium. "We expect people to park their vehicles at these slots and take the bus to Balewadi and back," said Patil.

Buses for Balewadi will run on 19 routes from Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad during the CYG week. On October 2, PMPML started 15 buses on five routes, from Hadapsar, Chandannagar, Kothrud, Katraj and Nigdi. All these buses will pass through the corporation bus stop. The buses on these routes will be available on 30-minute frequencies.

From October 5, around 5,000 accredited volunteers will be able to take an early morning bus to Balewadi from Hadapsar (5.05 am), Kothrud (5.15 am), Swargate (5.15 am), Shivajinagar (5.20 am), Nigdi (5.15 am) and Deccan (5.30 am). This service will be available till October 15.

From October 10, there and additional 10 routes leading to Balewadi from Swargate, Shanipar, Khadkibazaar, Deccan, Katraj, Khadakvasla, Pune station, Vadgaonmaval and Bhosari.

Meanwhile, commuters can avail of concessions during the CYG week as the daily pass rate has been slashed to Rs 30 (from Rs 50) and the weekly pass to Rs 150 (from Rs 225) for the CYG week — October 12 to October 18. All the major CYG bus stops will have senior PMPML personnel on deputation and customers can call on 32601644, 9881495574, and 9881235505.

Heading: Smoking ban up in smoke on day 1 - Indian Express
Content:
Land to be acquired in Paraguay, Uruguay by a group of 16 companies

In a novel move that could yield rich dividends, a group of Indian companies is all set to purchase land abroad for cultivation of crops needed back home. Sixteen companies mainly dealing in oilseeds are taking part in the initiative.

For starters, the experiment will be conducted on 10,000 acre of agricultural land in Uruguay and Paraguay at an investment of Rs 200 crore. The land will be used for soyabean and sunflower crop.

For surveying the land, Pune-based Pranav Agro Industries had led a consortium to Latin America. The government-run State Trading Corporation (STC) has also joined the consortium.

"Last year, about 14 of us in the oilseeds business went to Latin America to see what makes countries like Uruguay, Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina produce more oilseeds than we do. We meet 50 per cent of our oilseed requirement though import and anything from 10 to 40 per cent comes from Latin America, depending on the prices," said chairman and managing director of Pranav Agro Industries, Pravin Lunkad, who is also the convener of the consortium

During the feasibility study, the group found several motivating factors. As compared to India, land productivity was very high but land prices were half in those countries. The farmers there rotated three to four crops a year and irrigation is not a necessity because of good rainfall.

"In addition, it's possible to buy large tracts of land where hundred per cent mechanised farming can be carried out," added Lunkad. All this propelled the consortium to invest in land in Uruguay and Paraguay where labour land and other logistics come cheaper as compared to Brazil and Argentina.

The group, supported by the Solvent Extractors' Association, has now turned to the Exim Bank for financial support.

They also approached the STC which joined hands with them. The STC will get the right of first refusal on the crops, said Lunkad. The surplus, he added, would be available to them for sale in the open market, be it domestic or international.

"The whole idea is to get food security for the country. Given our numbers, India and China need this most in the world," he added.

The Indian government appears to be keen on the initiative and the necessary permissions and guidelines were being worked out. Uruguay and Paraguay have a fairly open investment pattern due to which there would be no regulatory hurdles from their side, said Lunkad.

Some other companies involved in the project are Indore's Ruchi Soya, Morena's KS Oil and Ahemdabad's Ambujas. According to Lunkad, land acquisition should take place by the end of the year. India produces about 7.5 million tonne edible oil, against consumption of around 12.5 million tonne. The consortium plans to sow crops according to demand. Beginning with soyabean, sunflower and then maize, it may proceed with wheat and pulses later.

Heading: Disaster management team set for CYG - Indian Express
Content:
On the first day of the ban on smoking in public places, people were seen defying it. No implementation of the ban by the authorities was in sight and no one was penalised. Smokers are up in arms against the ban.

A call centre executive smoking in Camp area called the ban "ridiculous". Another smoker, Archis Tankhiwale, working with a private firm, felt implementing the ban would be an uphill task. Shailesh Pawar, an IT professional said, "People like us need to give vent to stress owing to work pressure. Now we cannot smoke even outside our work premises. How are we to cope with our work pressure?"

At Pune railway station, smokers were spotted enjoying their daily puff without hesitation or fear. But Pune Station Manager J M Laturkar insisted they hadn't found anyone smoking in the station. "The official directive is to impose a fine on anyone found smoking on the platform or anywhere inside the railway station," he added. The scene at the bus stand was no different with people smoking as usual. Kashinath Telange, Controller at the Pune Municipal Corporation said, "Smoking inside a bus is already banned. With the new law in place, we will ask the commuter (smoking inside the bus) to get down if the person refuses to stop smoking."

Asked about the implementation of the fines he said, "We have no orders as yet, but we will be receiving orders regarding the fines soon. As of now, we have been asked to politely tell the commuter to get down." It seems private firms are adhering to the ban. Shweta Singh, HR head, Wipro said the smoking zone at the fourth floor of their office that used to have a small gathering of smokers after lunch did not see a single person turning up at the place on Thursday. Abhay Khare, GM, finance, Quadrant Communications, said corridors where smokers usually take their puff, especially in the evenings, were deserted. He added that there was an uproar in the office with people voicing their opposition to the notification on the ban.

Heading: Road accidents claim three in city - Indian Express
Content:
A disaster management system is being put in place for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) that will kick off on October 12. With district collector Chandrakant Dalvi heading it, 30 key departments will be part of the core team. Over 100 volunteers will help the officers manage the disaster management plan effectively.

The team is gearing up to tackle possible risks outside the stadium like stampedes, bomb blasts, rain, floods and riots. Airport security is also included in the plan. For the last three weeks, the team has been discussing how the situation can be tackled in case of any eventuality.

According to a senior member of the team, two officials each from the 30 departments have been identified to react quickly to any crisis that may arise. "Police, health, army, irrigation, transport, industrial health and safety, communication, information, civil defence are some of the departments in the core team," said the officer.

The team will call itself the Incident Command System and act as the coordinating agency or resource system for these games, said the officer. "Training of people selected from these departments has been on for the last one month," he added.

A helpline number, 1077, has been activated for the games and mock drills are being conducted by various departments. Hundred National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers, in coordination with the University of Pune, will assist the core team. All public places will be kept on high alert in coordination with the police department, he added.

Translators will be provided for those visiting the city and the India Disaster Resource Network is providing online resources for those coming into the city. One has to just log on to www.idrn.gov.in and put the user name Pune and password 123 for information about the city.

Heading: Outdoor competitions: Vivek Shivale wins 3,000 metre event - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons lost their lives in three road accidents that happened in various parts of the city. Sixteen-year-old Surabhi Mehta was travelling pillion with Aaditya Kavadiya along the Pune-Mumbai highway when a truck hit the scooty from behind near Khadki.

Aaditya was injured severely while Surabhi received injuries on her head. She died while she was being taken to the hospital. A case of rash driving and death due to negligence has been filed against the driver, who fled the scene immediately after the accident. He has been booked under sections 304 (A), 279, 184 Motor vehicle act, and 119/177,132 (1) (A) of the IPC. Sub-Inspector V T Polkar, of the Khadki police station is investigating the case.

In another incident, Digambar Laxman Tompe and his brother Dayanand Kamble were working at the construction site of Bhatia and Raje constructions in Chinchwad, when the crane operator Uttam Hatkar the crane swerved hitting Dayanand and killing him on the spot. The crane operator has been booked under sections 304 (A), 279, and 119/177 of the Motor vehicle act, of the IPC. The case has been registered at the Chinchwad police station and sub-inspector Babar is investigating the case.

In the third incident, NandKumar Vargane, aged 37, was run over by two vehicles. The incident occurred around 12.30 am on Thursday on Pune-Alandi road, near the police quarters in Vishrantwadi. According to the brother of the deceased, Rahul Vargane, his brother, NandKumar was walking alone by the side of the road when a vehicle, which came speeding from behind, rammed into him and sped away. Another vehicle, which came from behind also ran over him. A case has been registered at the Vishrantwadi police station.

Heading: BJP blames UPA for discord between UT Administrator and Finance minister - Indian Express
Content:
Number of land registration deeds at all-time high in July

The real estate market is once again booming in the Chandigarh periphery, if the official figures of land registration deeds are any indication.

The number of land registration deeds touched an all-time high in two years at 446 in July 2008, followed by 393 in August 2008, after plunging to as low as 163 in September 2007.

The state government earned Rs 88.38 crore as stamp duty and registration fee from the 8,324 land deeds between April 2006 and August 2008, in the Chandigarh periphery, falling under the jurisdiction of Majri sub-tehsil. At least 69 defaulters detected between August 2006 and March 2008, evaded Rs 62.62 lakh on account of stamp duty and registration fee.

Official records with Newsline reveal that a record revenue of Rs 7.51 crore was earned in July 2008, on account of Rs 7.32 crore stamp duty and Rs 18.45 lakh from registration fee. The second highest revenue of Rs 6.64 crore was earned in June 2008 from registration of 366 land deeds on account of Rs 6.5 crore stamp duty and Rs 14.25 lakh as registration fee.

The recession in the real estate market last year, was evident from the lowest revenue of Rs 63.27 lakh recorded in October 2007 when 218 land deeds were registered.

The bigwigs, including top politicians and bureaucrats, misused their influence to cause a heavy loss to the state exchequer as they were able to get their land deeds registered without paying any money or paying

less stamp duty and registration fee.

Though the land deeds could not be registered below the minimum rates of registration of land fixed by the Collector, who is also the Deputy Commissioner, but the high and mighty connive with the concerned tehsildars to get their land deeds registered as per their whims and fancies.

In view of the prime location of the areas falling under Majri sub-tehsil, a large number of influential persons own major chunks of land in the Chandigarh periphery.

Audits conducted during the 20-month scrutiny period, pinpointed evasion and shortfall of Rs 60.8 lakh stamp duty and Rs 1.82 lakh registration fee in 69 cases of default.

The cases of evasion and shortfall of revenue in the registration of land are impounded under Section 47-A of the Indian Stamp Act, and sent by the tehsildar to the Additional Deputy Commissioner for adjudication, which also budges under the pressure of bigwig defaulters to meet the dead end.

The prevailing land registration rates require 8 per cent stamp duty and 1 per cent registration fee on the total amount of land deal, which could not be registered below the minimum rates of land registration fixed by the Collector-cum-Deputy Commissioner.

Heading: Quit smoking by ‘mind reprogramming’ - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national general secretary Kiran Ghai blamed the Congress-led UPA government today for the "lack of coordination" between UT Administrator Gen S F Rogrigues (retd) and Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal.

Ghai, who is on a visit to the city, said: "When the UPA government is not in a position to manage the functioning of even a small city like Chandigarh, how can they govern the country?"

She alleged that the UPA government has failed on all fronts, including internal security. "There have been too many instances of bomb blasts in the recent past. We need to improve our security arrangements. It is strange that while the UT Administration moved a proposal for the sanction of extra posts in the Police department, the Finance department rejected it. It shows that security of the residents is not a priority with the government," said Ghai.

L K Advani, BJP's prime ministerial candidate for the 2009 Lok Sabha polls, will visit the city on November 16 to take part in the Vijay Sankalp Sammelan. "A rally will be taken out in the city. Other events including Nav Matdata Abhinandan Sammelan will also be held to encourage first-time voters in the coming days," she added.

Asked about the BJP candidate from Chandigarh in the general elections, Ghai said an announcement in this connection will be made by the party leadership.

"Efforts are also on at different levels to produce suitable women candidates," she added.

Heading: Conviction for rape negligible, none in 2008 - Indian Express
Content:
Popular memory trainer Biswaroop Roy Chowdhury claims to have invented a unique device, the 'Cigavaccine'. In a statement issued today, he claimed that a smoker would turn into a non-smoker once he uses this device. His invention is called 'Cigavaccine' because it works like a vaccine against smoking. It will be launched by November 15, he said.

Hailing the Centre's decision, Biswaroop said, "I am happy that the government has announced a ban on smoking in public places from October 2. Smokers will now have a lesser opportunity to smoke and will have to find an appropriate place to light up. As a result, we can be assured that cigarette intake will be reduced."

According to him, Cigavaccine is a cigarette look-alike mobile chamber. "Inside the chamber, the smoker will have to go through 15 minutes of mind reprogramming, which will help him dissassociate with the past memories of smoking. The taste, smell and even the sight of a cigarette will be associated with extreme mental pain. So the very thought, smell and sight of a cigarette will trigger the planted memory and the smoker will avoid smoking," he explained.

Heading: ‘After special treatment, life is now back to normal’ - Indian Express
Content:
The incident where a German national was allegedly abducted and molested by five youths last Sunday has sent shock waves across the region. While the incident has shattered the city's image as a tourist destination, a review of past cases of crime against women show the police have largely failed to ensure that the accused serve long-term sentences.

According to records of the UT Police, though cases of rape and molestations are rising every year, the figure of those convicted has hit an all-time low.

The number of molestation cases registered in 2006 was 20. Out of them, only one accused has been convicted so far and seven have been acquitted. In 2007, 32 cases were registered under Section 354 (outraging modesty) of the IPC.

So far, 16 such cases of molestation have been registered this year. Among them, while one was convicted, three were acquitted.

The conviction rate in rape cases under Section 376 of the IPC is no different. In 2005, 33 cases of rape were registered.

While 12 were acquitted, 11 of the accused were convicted. The remaining cases are still pending. In 2006, 19 rape cases were registered. While four of the accused were convicted, six were acquitted. Last year, out of the 22 cases of rape registered with the police, only two accused were convicted.

Considering that a very small percentage of women actually come to the police to lodge a complaint of rape, the conviction rate comes as a big discouragement to women seeking justice.

According to police officers, victims turning hostile, long-pending trials and warring parties coming to a compromise decision are a few reasons behind the low conviction rate. In 1994, all the accused in the rape of a French tourist in the city managed to escape punishment, as no one came forward to testify against them. According to legal experts, the conviction rate drops further if it is proved that the victim was either suffering from depression or in an inebriated condition.

Cross-examination is another problem, say lawyers. "In a gangrape case, lawyers for all the accused will cross-examine the victim. Often, the prospect of reliving such trauma over and over again is too much to bear. Many a times, the victim will simply withdraw the case," said N K Nanda, president of the District Bar Association.

Lax attitude of the police who often succumb to pressures of "big shots" is another major hurdle -- the police took a very long time to record the statement of the victim in the infamous Barnala rape case. The case is still pending.

Heading: PU Senate polls: Candidates being finalised for nominated category - Indian Express
Content:
She fondly remembers the night of January 24, when she had an unexpected visitor, in the garb of a policeman, who had been despatched to tell her about her nomination for receiving the state award on January 26 this year. "I was on cloud nine after having received the news," she shares excitedly.

A non-medical student of Class XII at the Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 16, Tanya was also a nominee for the National Child Award in 2007.

Apart from being a talented student, she is a national-level basketball player and has received several prizes in drawing and painting competitions.

Surprisingly, she had not applied for the award for this year. "I had submitted my nomination for the State Award for 2007, but did not receive the same."

"We received separate invitations for everything," she says. Her parents too, have fond memories of the day, when they were made to feel special, and felt proud of their daughter. "Even our car was parked by the attendant, the moment we reached the Governor's house and we were escorted by officials," says Deepak Shreedhar, Tanya's father.

The media too, made her feel special. They thronged her residence to cover her profile with two other schoolchildren, who received the same award.

Having experienced all the limelight, she is now focused on concentrating on her Class XII Board and engineering entrance exams.

"The magnitude of our happiness increased each time someone congratulated us on our daughter's achievement," says her mother.

Their life now, is, back to normal with Tanya putting in hard work to build a bright future for herself. And with sucess in this exam, many awards can follow!

Heading: PU: Rajiv Gandhi Chair vacant since 2005 - Indian Express
Content:
The Panjab University (PU) Senate elections has entered its final stage with the names of candidates being decided for the nominated category presently.

In the 85-member Senate body, 39 members are nominated, while the rest are elected. The results of the elected category were recently declared.

Though the nominations are sent by the Vice-Chancellor, the final decision lays in the hands of Vice-President of India and Chancellor of the university Hamid Ansari.

This year, both students and non-teaching members have demanded representation in the nominated members' category, to which the Senate has decided to have the president of the non-teaching members in the nominated category.

Meanwhile, the decision is yet to be implemented.

Talking to Newsline, a senior senator said: "The Senate has agreed to the demand of the non-teaching fraternity. Though they wanted three members in the nominated category, the Senate has decided to have their president in the Senate. The decision, however, awaits implementation."

He also added that the elected student council will be made a party in the committees formed to look into various matters.

Meanwhile, Ishan Tayal, Departmental Representative of the department of Honours in Education, Panjab University, through a representation, has appealed to PU Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti to ensure student representation through the nominated category.

Heading: ‘Only way to counter terror is the Gandhian way’ - Indian Express
Content:
The condition of research work at the Panjab University seems to be going down the drain, as the university has failed to fill up chairs, instituted in various departments. While a few of the chairs are lying vacant for over five years in some departments, a few like the Rajiv Gandhi Chair were never filled up, ever since its advertisement in October 2005.

The Chair was granted to the university by the Ministry of Human Resources and Development, along with nine other universities across the country. It was decided that an annual grant of Rs 20 lakh would be given for a period of five years for research work.

The university had decided the theme of research as 'Impact of Technology on Society'. Three years later, however, the chair lies vacant still.

Though the name of Dr Mohsin U Khan, was earlier recommended by the PU, his name was cancelled after a writ petition was filed in the High Court.

A majority of the chairs are in the Faculty of Languages, which includes the Sheikh Baba Farid Chair, Guru Ravi Das Chair of Sant Sahitya Studies, Guru Nanak Sikh Studies Chair and Bhai Veer Singh Chair.

While the Sheikh Baba Farid Chair is vacant since 2003, Bhai Veer Singh Chair has seen no takers since 2004 and the Guru Nanak Sikh Studies Chair has been vacant for almost a decade now. Talking to Newsline, an official of the Panjab University said: "The delay in filling the chairs is caused due to the lobbying going around. There are many undeserving people, who want to claim a chair and this is causing the delay."

Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti said the search for suitable candidates is on.

He said: "The chairs shall be filled up as we are working on the same. The delay is because it takes time to recruit deserving people."

Heading: Truck crushes car on highway, 2 dead - Indian Express
Content:
To mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the department of Gandhian Studies, Panjab University organised a lecture on The Key to Mahatma Gandhi's Influence by renowned historian Professor Devender Swarup at Gandhi Bhawan, Panjab University campus on Thursday.

"There was something special about Mahatma Gandhi that eminent persons of different ideologies including Jawahar Lal Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhash Chander Bose and Maulana Azad became his followers," said Prof Swarup.

Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti stressed on the need to reach out to the underprivileged and backward sections of society by following Mahatma Gandhi's footsteps.

A patriotic song, poem and fancy dress competition based on the freedom struggle were held for tiny-tots in the morning session.

Organising secretary of these competitions, Dr Ashu Pasricha said that such competitions enrich the younger generation and help them understand the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi in the true sense.

Professor J N Sharma, chairman of the department of Gandhian Studies, emphasised principles of Mahatma Gandhi as the need of the hour.

"The only way to counter terrorism is by the Gandhian or the non-violent way," said Prof Sharma. "From this year onwards, the United Nations has decided to celebrate the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi as the International Day of Non-Violence," he said.

Meanwhile, the NSS unit of MCM DAV College celebrated Gandhi Jayanti by flagging-off a rally against the stigma of leprosy. Dr Manjeet Singh Bains, Director Health Services, UT Administration was also present on the occasion.

To commemorate the day, a talk was delivered by Lt Col (Dr) Uma Vasudev. Various competitions were held for students.

The volunteers of the college also went to Badheri village to impart knowledge on Gandhi.

College principal Dr Puneet Bedi expressed concern on the issue and urged students to contribute to the cause.

The NSS Unit of Guru Gobind Singh College for Women, Sector 26, also celebrated Gandhi Jayanti on the concluding day of their ten-day NSS camp. 

K K Monga, president of the Lions Club, Manimajra, was the chief guest on the occasion. The function started with a prayer and was followed by a cultural program. The students were educated about the teachings of the Father of the Nation and the importance of non-violence in the present day scenario.

The ten-day camp was attended by over 100 volunteers and many activities were undertaken in the adopted village of Raipur Kalan. A dental camp, breast cancer awareness programme, workshop on HIV/AIDS, drug de-addiction workshop, a tie-and-dye workshop and a literacy campaign were organised in the village during the camp.

The NSS unit of the Government College, Sector 11, hosted a series of activities to mark Gandhi Jayanti and observe International Non-violence Day. A large number of faculty members along with volunteers undertook a cleanliness drive in the college campus.

Lage Raho Munnabhai was screened for the volunteers to make them aware about the depiction of Gandhiji in mass media, such as cinema.

The movie was also followed by a discussion. The volunteers presented a street play Swarnim Bharat to highlight the gap between Gandhi's 'dream India' and present day India. A declamation and patriotic song competition was also held during the event. Principal Dr A L Gauba administered the pledge of non-violence to the volunteers.

The NSS Unit of GGDSD College also celebrated Gandhi Jayanti with the inmates of Chandi Kusht Ashram in Sector 47. The volunteers distributed fruits and sweets to the residents of the ashram. Later during the day, a presentation on female foeticide was given by Aradhna Soni, a student of BSc II year, Biotech Hons.

The Chandigarh Sahitya Akademi organised a seminar at the State Library in Sector 34 on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. Eminent academicians from Panjab University and Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, expressed their views on the occasion.

Talking about Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule, a book written by Mahatma Gandhi, Professor Rashmi Sudhapuri said that the book teaches the gospel of peace and love for humanity very effectively. "Keeping in mind the present troubled times, the significance of this book is greatly increased. Gandhi very rightly defines the true meaning of Swaraj," she said.

Dr Amit Sharma from JNU said that the book contains the quintessence of Gandhi's thinking. "Gandhi looked at the root-meaning of the word which means rule upon oneself. Gandhi believed in taking control of one's desires and freeing oneself from all ego hassles," he said.

Heading: Four accused undergo medical tests, hunt for Sompal continues - Indian Express
Content:
Driver lost control after brakes failed, deceased were on way to temple

Two pedestrians died and a 12-year-old girl sustained serious injuries in a road accident on National Highway 22 at Kalka near Parwanoo on Thursday.

Rekha, a resident of Valmiki Colony, was rushed to GMCH-32 in Chandigarh, where her condition is stated to be critical.

The accident took place around 6 pm when the truck, loaded with apples, turned turtle crushing a Tata Sumo and killing the two pedestrians on the spot.

Traffic was disrupted for several hours near a Kali temple on the highway, where the accident took place. Traffic started to move freely only after 10 pm.

The accident took place after the brakes of the truck (HR-38-D-6705), heading for Delhi, failed. The driver lost control and rammed the vehicle to a side of the highway. The truck overturned and fell on the Tata Sumo coming from the opposite direction.

The deceased have been identified as Himanshu (45) and Brijesh Rai (40), both residents of Kalka. They were on their way to the Kali temple when the accident took place.

Heading: Residents turn a deaf ear to ban on polythene bags, smoking at public places - Indian Express
Content:
Medical tests were conducted on the four people arrested for Sunday's alleged abduction and molestation of a German national.

Pankaj Punia, Harpreet Singh alias Dalli, Sukhwinder Singh alias Sukhi and Maninder Singh Jolly were brought to Sector 16's Government Multi Specialty Hospital on Thursday for the examinations, which also included the DNA test. Though reports are still awaited, police sources claimed the accused have bruises all over their bodies.

Jolly along with Sukhi (23) had surrendered in the district courts on Wednesday. Of the five accused in the case, 20-year-old Punia, was arrested on Monday while Harpreet was held on Tuesday.

Sompal, another accused, is still absconding.

According to the police, Jolly, a drug addict, has a deep cut on his chest and another below his neck.

Sukhi's bruises also point to the possibility that the victim might have inflicted the injuries while trying to save herself, said an officer.

The four were brought to the hospital in a mini bus. Earlier, rumours were doing rounds that the victim had come to identify the accused at the hospital. It was later revealed that Ina, the victim's friend, had visited the hospital.

Heading: Route diversion leaves passengers harassed - Indian Express
Content:
The first day of the ban on polythene carry bags did not see much compliance among the shopowners of the city. In most markets, polythene bags were freely available.

The ban on smoking in public places also seemed ineffective.

Many were found smoking at the bus stand and railway station. Inquiry about the ban generated either a shrug of the shoulders or lack of awareness. "I do not know that I cannot smoke even in an open area. The Administration should try to inform the citizens about the decisions it takes," said Ram Kumar, an autorickshaw driver.

Regarding the ban on polythene bags, while traders rued that there was no alternative to polythene bags, the residents did not seem aware of the ban at all.

During the day, teams from the UT Administration visited several markets to create awareness about the directive. Shopowners who were found defying the ban were issued warnings. No fines were, however, imposed or challans issued on the first day.

A visit to the Grain Market was testimony enough that the ban was not enforced properly.

Both the shopkeepers and their customers were found using such bags. "I was not aware that the use of plastic bags has been restricted. Since I do not find time to read newspapers, I do not know anything about this," said Kiran Pruthi, carrying a polythene full of grocery.
