Manoj, a fruit-seller at Sector 26, claimed he too was unaware of the ban.

"Had I known, I would have never sold the items in plastic. Nobody from the Administration came to inform us," he said.

"Even if I am using cloth bags to sell my merchandise, people are demanding plastic carry bags. It is a costly proposition. The government should also think about products like milk which are sold in plastic bags," said Sanjeev Bansal, a shopkeeper in Sector 17.

A shopowner in Sector 19 said that there are no alternatives to polythene bags. "We do not have units which make paper bags. Importing these from other states will prove expensive. Then the customers will have to bear the additional cost," he added.

Chandan Garg, the manager at Reliance, said though they have introduced cloth bags, from now on, customers will have to pay Rs 4 per bag. "We are offering incentives to those who get their own bags," he added.

While many big brands have switched over to paper or jute bags with ease, small traders claim it is not an economically viable option. Charanjeev Singh, chairman of the Chandigarh Beopar Mandal said they will meet Administration officials on Saturday in this regard. "We have requested the Administration to extend the date of the ban during the festive season," he added.

Naresh Mittal, chairman of Chandigarh Plastic Manufacturers and Traders Association claimed the units manufacturing polythene bags will comply with the orders of the Administration.

Heading: Villagers protest against govt for ‘discrimination’ in plot allotments - Indian Express
Content:
Passengers travelling by Roadways buses faced harassment due to diversion of traffic for the Chandigarh-Delhi route from Karnal via Shamli and Meerut in Uttar Pradesh, bypassing the Panipat National Highway.

Keeping in view security concerns during UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi's rally in Panipat on Thursday, the GT Road between Karnal and Sonepat was closed for nearly seven hours from around 10 am to 5 pm. The buses going towards Delhi from Chadigarh had to take the Karnal-Shamli-Meerut route while those on their way back had to take the Delhi-Bahalgarh-Bagpat-Shamli-Karnal-Chandigarh route.

Around 200 buses on this route not only took excess time to reach their destination, but the diversion reportedly also cost each bus around Rs 300 extra.

According to the commuters, they had not received any prior information about the new route. The buses ran three to four hours behind their scheduled reporting time. Till reports last came in, one way traffic was resulting in congestion.

The commuters were the worst hit.

Many, who wanted to go to Panipat, had to either postpone their trip or look for other options to reach their destination. "I had to go to Panipat. Due to this diversion, I had to postpone my visit till tomorrow," said a passenger of ISBT-17.

Similar views were shared by passengers coming from Delhi. "The bus which was scheduled to reach Chandigarh at 1 pm is now reaching at 4.30 pm. Bad traffic management added to the chaos," said a passenger.

A Haryana Roadways attendant at the Delhi counter, ISBT Sector 17, said: "We were not officially informed about the change in route and got to know through our fellow Roadways staff returning from Delhi. Most of the drivers new on this route are not even aware about the roads."

According to the Haryana Roadways staff, passengers were informed about the diversion before they boarded the buses.

"We are making it a point to inform the passengers that the buses will bypass Panipat and also the extra hours the journey will take," said Dharambir Kumar, a conductor.

Heading: Panel slams consumer forum, sets aside order on HUDA officials - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of the Kalpi village in Ambala district staged a dharna against the state government alleging discriminating in allotting plots, on Thursday. The protesters said the plots were given to "undeserving" people than the needy.

On the occasion of Samajik Kranti Samaroh, possession letters for residential plots (100 sq yards) were given to the scheduled castes, backward classes and weaker section.

Ambala Division Commissioner Mohinder Kumar said the Haryana government was committed to settle people from the three categories and had introduced the new scheme — Samajik Kranti (social renaissance) to bring change in the life of the unprivileged.

As soon as the commissioner left the venue, the villagers stood up and started raising slogans against the government. The protesters gheraoed the vehicle of Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Renu Phulia and shouted slogans against the state government.

Even those who got the possession letters insisted that the government should construct structures on the plots. The situation was brought under control after Phulia assured them of placing their demand before the government.

Heading: Committee to meet today to take final decision - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission today set aside an order of the UT Consumer Forum whereby the latter had awarded two-year imprisonment and a penalty of Rs 10,000 each against three Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) officials.

The commission held that there was no ground to believe that there had been any 'intentional disobedience' on the part of HUDA officials.

The UT Consumer Forum, in its order dated May 2, had sentenced the financial commissioner and principal secretary of the Haryana government, Town and Country Planning department, Chief Administrator of HUDA and the estate officer of HUDA to two-years imprisonment and penalty of Rs 10,000 and an imprisonment of three months of officials in case of default of payment of fine.

The directions were passed against the HUDA officials for not complying with a previous order dated July 31, 2007, for offering an alternative plot in preferential plot in Sector 23, Gurgaon.

Following the orders, the HUDA had filed an appeal under Section 27-A of the Consumer Protection

Act, 1986, against the orders of the forum. It was contended in the appeal that criminal action cannot be taken against the officials by designation as criminal liability is always of the individuals and not an office.

It was contended that the Union Territory State Consumer Forum, Chandigarh, had even passed the orders, while the HUDA officials had nothing to do with the day-to-day affairs and the Chief Administrator of HUDA had already ordered to implement the orders of the Forum.

Therefore, if the Estate Officer had not implemented the orders, no criminal liability could be attached to the office of Chief Administrator who has already taken a decision to implement the order and had also conveyed the same to the Estate officer.

The State Commission slammed the consumer forum and observed that the legal formalities have not been complied with before passing the order, rather it has been passed in a haste.

The commission further observed that there was intentional disobedience of the order dated July 31, 2007 by HUDA since the process had been started and an alternative plot had been allotted.

"The order has been fully complied with. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, the appeal is accepted and the impugned order, being illegal, is set aside," the Commission held.

Heading: 6,000 seats vacant in PTU colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Kidney to ADC: SSPs, civil surgeons, Mohali docs to attend meet

The high-level meeting to be headed by Amritsar Deputy Commissioner will tomorrow take the final decision on donation of kidney to ailing PCS officer and Tarn Taran Additional Deputy Commissioner Kirpal Singh.

The SSPs, civil surgeons from both districts and doctors from Mohali-based Silver Oaks Hospital have been summoned for the meeting.

The fate of Kirpal Singh is hanging in the balance as the authorisation committee, which had cleared the case of kidney transplantation for him, took a u-turn last week after 23-year-old donor Sunny went missing and his parents levelled serious allegations against the PCS officer.

The family of Kirpal Singh, however, said Sunny and his parents had agreed to donate kidney on sympathetic ground. The parents of the youth had approached the local court, saying that the life of their son was under threat and they had never consented to donate his kidney.

The city had hit the headlines a few years ago too due to the kidney scandal, and this case has once again brought back the bitter old memories.

Amritsar DC K S Pannu would be back today from his foreign tour and chair the meeting, said Civil Surgeon Lehmber Singh.

He said the meeting would look into every aspect and doctors and parents of the donors would put forward their statements.

Chief transplantation surgeon of Silver Oaks Hospital AS Bains and his medical superintendent too would attend the meeting, which will also discuss various legal aspects of the Human Organs Transplantation Act.

Meanwhile, Kirpal's health is deteriorating as both of his kidneys have been damaged.

"The authorisation committee had cleared the donation, but then some problems erupted," said one of the family members, adding that they were surprised why the donor and his families have changed their stance.

It was in the absence of Pannu that the authorisation committee, headed by Tarn Taran DC Khushi Ram, who holds the additional charge of Amritsar, had given a green signal to the kidney donation despite the fact that Sunny, who works at dhaba in Chheherta, was not related to him.

His parents have now alleged that their boy was "lured to donate" kidney and have asked the police to trace him and prevent him from going for the operation.

Following submission of a written complaint to the police, Charan Das and Suman, parents of Sunny, later approached the local court and even urged the Punjab Human Rights Commission to help them trace their son. Their advocate, Vishal Gogna, said as Sunny was neither related to Kirpal nor had he consented to donate the kidney, the transplantation would be illegal.

Heading: Renovation of Jallianwala Bagh lane draws flak - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Technical University (PTU) has failed to fill nearly 6,000 seats of engineering courses. Sources said PTU would face a loss of over Rs 150 crore due to these vacancies. It had conducted counselling for Punjab CET-2008 exam for 18,000 seats. The main reason for the seats remaining vacant is prolonged counselling, poor infrastructure in various colleges and under-qualified staff.

There are about 30 colleges under PTU and over 100 seats in each are vacant. Owners of various institutes said PTU should conduct online counselling from next year, as prolonged sessions force the students to join colleges in other states. They said they would meet PTU authorities soon to assess the losses. PTU Dean (Academics) Dr V K Arora said now the vacant seats would be filled by the colleges on their own, on merit.

Heading: Punjab comes to rescue of millers blacklisted by CBI - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the renovation of historical lanes of Jallianwala Bagh as defacement and destruction of the historical monument, president of Desh Bhagat Yadgar Hall Committee (DBYHC) 101-year-old Ghadri Baba Bhagat Singh Bilga today not only announced to hold a massive protest dharna at the site on October 6, but also sought the intervention of Prime Minister in the case.

He also demanded restoration of the two already-demolished historical lanes of Jallianwala Bagh and warned that the third one should not be razed in the name of widening the entry point for VVIPs' vehicles.

Baba Bilga and General Secretary DBYHC Naunihal Singh, while talking to mediapersons here today, said on one hand the government was destroying the historical monuments, and on the other it was celebrating birth centenary of Shaheed Bhagat Singh with much fanfare.

He said these lanes were integral part of the bagh and depicted the massacre of innocent people by General O' Dyre, who had entered the bagh through one of these narrow lanes. They said the government should not convert the historical monuments into a tourist places. They will also submit the demand letter to the government, Jallianwala Bagh Trust and the administration.

Heading: Kotkapura DSP who accused senior of corruption transferred - Indian Express
Content:
Other defaulters asked to pay penalty by November first week

Even as successive state governments have failed to rein in Punjab's defaulters, about 232 millers blacklisted by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for delivering rice beyond rejection limit to the Food Corporation of India (FCI) in the previous years have been allowed custom milling of paddy (for

central pool) in the current procurement season.

On ground that cases against the blacklisted millers are still pending in the courts and debarring them would adversely affect the storage and milling of paddy, the FCI headquarters in New Delhi have conceded to the Punjab government's request for reconsidering its decision on debarring these mills from taking part in the custom milling.

The Punjab Food and Supply Department says the FCI was told to reconsider the decision as the total number of defaulters, including those blacklisted by the CBI, totals up to 700, and putting such a large number of mills out of action when they are expecting a bumper paddy harvest would adversely impact timely milling and storage for the central pool.

However, the effort of the department to rein in the millers who defaulted in timely delivery of levy rice has not gone in vain. In what is perhaps a first in the paddy milling history of Punjab, the department has succeeded in laying down the condition that custom milling will be allowed subject to payment of penalty by the defaulters till first week of November.

In addition to a penalty of Rs 350 per quintal for delay, defaulters have also to make good the gap of levy rice. And millers are not taking any chances. "Against the total penalty of Rs 8 crore, we have already received more than 50 per cent (Rs 5 crore) from the defaulters. Though done for the first time, our conditions have worked well. This will go a long way and we expect not a single rice mill to default next year," said Director, Punjab Food and Supply Department, SP Singh.

Notably, there are about 3,000 rice mills in Punjab, out of which 232 were blacklisted by the CBI after the quality of rice delivered by them in 2004-05 was found to be sub-standard, resulting in filing of criminal cases and chargesheets against millers and FCI officials in the subsequent years.

While chargesheets have been filed against some of those found guilty of supplying rice beyond rejection limit (BRL) to FCI, the CBI had recommended that no business dealing should be carried on with all these mills till the investigation is completed.

As for the financial implication of defaults, nearly 3,00,000 tonnes of levy and custom rice fails to make it to the central pool from the state every year, resulting in wastage of government money used in procurement.

Heading: On wedding day, girl sends back addict groom - Indian Express
Content:
Kotkapura DSP Raj Kumar Jalotra, who had reportedly locked up his office and proceeded on an extended leave out of fear after reporting to higher authorities that a senior police officer had misappropriated funds and pocketed Rs 2 lakh of the recovered loot money, has been transferred to 4 Commando Battalion, Mohali.

Even as Faridkot Range DIG Dr Jatinder Jain, Faridkot SSP Paramraj Umranangal and DSP Jalotra himself did not confirm the transfer, well-placed sources told The Indian Express that the Punjab DGP had faxed the transfer orders to the Faridkot police on Wednesday.

"Today is a holiday. No staff is present in the office. So, I cannot confirm whether transfer orders have been received or not," said Jain.

Jalotra said he was not aware of the transfer orders. "I don't know whether I have been transferred," he said, adding that he had "requested" for a transfer. When asked about the preferences, he said, "Around Chandigarh as my kids study there."

He refused to comment when asked if his transfer had anything to do with his complaint against the senior cop.

Umranangal also claimed that he was unaware of the transfer. "It is the DSP who can tell about it," he said. Asked about the reported allegations of DSP against a senior official, Umranangal said the matter has been brought to the notice of the top brass of the Punjab Police.

As reported in a section of media, the police had arrested a person with loot money amounting to Rs 2.5 lakh in May this year. During documentation earlier last month, the investigating officer showed only Rs 50,000 in recovery. DSP Jalotra, after an inquiry, "discovered" that Rs 2 lakh had been pocketed by the senior cop, following which he reported the matter to the higher authorities. Jagdish Lal, the investigating officer in the case, told The Indian Express, "I can reveal the details of the case to my senior officers only, if they ask." He added, "The tussle between the two officers has brought a bad name to the entire police force, as the issue was trivial. Everything is on records, as had been in the past 35 years of my service."

Heading: GNDU’s research  panel to meet on October 2 - Indian Express
Content:
A 23-year-old Tarn Taran girl today refused to marry a drug addict.

After Rajbir Kaur took the bold step, bridegroom's relatives returned home, only to be followed by a procession led by the father of the girl to bring back the shagun items.

Sources said that they had been engaged for the past over seven months, and Rajbir came to know of Amandeep Singh's addictions last night when he was hospitalised on account of his ill health.

They said Amandeep, who works as a conductor of a mini-bus, had been addicted to opiates for quite some time and had to be often hospitalised.

"I would rather stay unmarried than marry such a man," said Rajbir, a matriculate, adding that every girl had the right to choose her destiny. "Girls often end up marrying addicts under family pressure and lead unhappy lives thereafter," she said. She said she had even advised her four younger sisters to be courageous and vocal in defending their interests.

Sukhdev Singh, father of Rajbir, said, "It is her life and she has the right to chart her own course to happiness. My daughter had sent across a message that will go a long way in empowering girls to take decisions about their marriage and ridding the society of addiction."

He charged the bridegroom's family with keeping him and his daughter in the dark.

"My message to the public is that daughters are precious and should never be given away in marriage to addicts," he said.

Heading: Time to buy - Indian Express
Content:
The Research Degree Committee (RDC) of Guru Nanak Dev University has decided to meet on October 6 to discuss the fate of over 100 PhD researchers pursuing doctorate in education. Their topics were earlier rejected on the ground of being inept after two years of students' hard work.

Shaken by the functioning of the RDC, the researchers are fearful about the outcome of the meeting.

They also said that they had not yet been able to get registered even after two years, though this is usually done within six months of enrollment.

They said many of them might be asked to start their PhD from scratch. "I fail to understand how the RDC functions. First, it asked us to go ahead with our topics with some modifications, then our topics were rejected. And now they decide to meet again," said a researcher, who has received a letter to appear for the meeting.

Dr Jasdeep Kaur, a PhD guide, said, "We are praying that the decision benefits the students."

Dean, Academic Affairs, GNDU Raghbir Singh said the decision would be taken keeping in mind the interests of the researchers and the standards of the university.

Heading: A different beat - Indian Express
Content:
Trendy & affordable watches have changed the concept of one-watch-for-a-lifetime

If only the number of watches one owned had some bearing on the punctuality factor, we could have well changed the dubious reputation enjoyed by Indian Standard Time. While we may not be a good nation of time-keepers, we certainly have become great keepers of time-telling devices. And all thanks to a market that is flooded with classy, stylish, yet affordable time pieces.

Nowadays even a casual movie-going experience can double up as a watch-buying spree, given the costs involved. Indeed, there may be times when the movie ticket may cost more than the watch available at the multiplex! But then who's complaining?

Vishal Pandit, an engineering student, is passionate about trendy, fashion accessories, "I have a collection of over 12 watches. Buying an expensive watch is not possible for me but I get almost all, in fact better designs at much cheaper rates at roadside shops. And to tell you the truth, since the last one year I don't remember a month when I have not bought a watch.''

Muzaffer Shaikh, a salesperson at one of the shops agrees with the trend. "The market's full of smart and affordable watches and a watch is not a luxury item any more. We have people from all sections of society coming and buying watches from us. These watches give the same look as the expensive ones, and are still available in the range of Rs 100 to 200 and can be used without any problems for a least one year.''

The insides of these watches are fabricated and come with fully charged batteries that last for anywhere between six months and one year. "These do not come with a warranty, but the batteries can be replaced,'' adds Shaikh.

While big, colourful dials with metallic and leather belts along with additional features like stopwatch, tachometer are the characteristics of watches for men, the ones for women display fresh and vibrant colours on delicate designs. "I like trekking and part of my trekking gear is a sports watch that I brought from roadside shop. I am a rough user and I prefer losing this watch rather than an expensive one,'' smiles Debika Rakshe another student.

It is the same trend that has compelled even giants in the field of watches to introduce affordable trendy watches in the market. Nods Shabbir Ghadyali, who own a watch shop, "brands such as Timex and Fast Track offer sporty watches at competitive prices. The added advantage is the warranty that comes with the brand. What's more important is looking good and people are getting to look good at cheaper prices.'' Times indeed have changed.

Heading: High Court reprimands govt for doing away with fishing tenders - Indian Express
Content:
Blazing a trail has become a norm with these youngsters. First, it was the first-ever national level debate competition in Chandigarh, now Wordz, the debating society brings to students the WORDZ Model United Nations Conference 2008. "It took us a year to prepare for the event since we began toying with the idea. In India such activities are restricted to metros, but elsewhere students are active in discussing, formulating and sharing opinions on such platforms," Anit Batra, Secretary General tells us. While the first phase of the event was a training session with participation of students and teachers from the tricity in August, the event culminates with a conference from October 6 to October 8 at CII Convention Centre, Sector 31, Chandigarh. "We are expecting 150 students from across the country and many students have approached us requesting individual participation and we are only too happy to have them particiapte," smiles Ashmita Gupta, Vice-President.

The conference is recognised by the United Nations Information Centre, New Delhi, while Alchemist and UT Administration are supporting the event. At the conference students will discuss Prevention of an Outer Space Arms Space and Nuclear Waste Disposal. The Economic and Social Council will bring Coordination of Humanitarian Assistance and Strengthening Children's and Women's Right on the platform, while for the Security Council the agendas will be Myanmar - A Country in Paradox and Unrest In Dafur. "We want to talk about things that matter, and how we as youngsters, can make a difference," Batra hopes to make such events frequent. Here's to new heights!

Heading: Wife files complaint against man for forcing her to indulge in unnatural sex acts - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in July, the govt did away with its policy on tenders and awarded fishing contracts for 54 reservoirs

The Gujarat High Court has reprimanded state Fisheries Minister Purshottam Solanki's practice of doing away with floating tenders for fishing rights contracts in the state reservoirs. The High Court said the move was illegal and was being done on extraneous ground.

Fishing contracts for 54 reservoirs were allotted to different individuals and groups in July, for the first time, doing away with the government Leasing Policy for Reservoirs of Inland Fisheries — 2004, which insists on tenders. The contracts were instead fixed on the basis of upset prices.

A division bench headed by judges R Doshit and S Dave ordered a cancellation of contracts for the Fofal, Bhadar, Aji-III and Macchu-I dams. All the four dams are located in Rajkot district. The High Court also rejected the claim that the tender process had been scrapped to avoid hurting the religious feelings of people.

"In its order, the court said: it is being done by the fisheries minister who has no power to do so under the policy. It has been done on extraneous grounds," said Mukul Sinha, the petitioner's lawyer. The government's tender policy states that tenders are a must while awarding fishing rights in non-tribal areas. Out of the total 54 reservoirs, 48 fall in the non-tribal areas and only three are in tribal domain.

The High Court has now ordered the state government to float tenders and re-allot contracts by October 15. The court gave its judgment in connection with the writ petition filed by a Palanpur resident, Issac Mohammad, against silently awarding the contracts, due to which the state government incurred losses to the tune of several crores. Four other similar cases involving other reservoirs and a PIL have also been filed in this regard.

Solanki, however, told Newsline: "We have not received the copy of the court order yet."

The government's counter affidavit in the case cited nine reasons for not following the tender system, and the chief one was that sentiments of people associated with religious groups are hurt when the tender process is followed. "Taking into consideration the religious sentiments of groups like the Jains, the state government had decided to carry out awarding fishing contracts silently rather than through public tenders," said Solanki.

The government's affidavit also claimed that the tender process had been done away with to support the state's policy of ensuring priority treatment for Padhar, Adivasi and backward community groups.

But there are also allegations that the tender process favours the financially strong groups; the poor are not able to compete in the tenders due to the high bids, besides the huge loss.

Usually, the bids for five-year fishing rights have crossed Rs 10 lakh for the bigger reservoirs extending over 200 hectares. But now, most of these reservoirs have been palmed off this year for pittances without calling any tenders, as was in the case of the Bhadar Dam. The fishing right for Bhadar was tendered for Rs 11 lakh last term, but was given away without a tender for Rs 3 lakh this time. The contracted sums for the rest of the 53 dams have also been drastically slashed the same way.

Heading: GUVNL announces one-day compulsory holiday for industries - Indian Express
Content:
While the Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss is making all efforts to do away with Section 377 of the IPC in order to decriminalise 'unnatural' sex in India, there is a newly married woman in Rajkot, who has used the provisions of the same law to take up her cause before a local court in Ahmedabad.

The 24-year-old woman has accused her husband of depriving her of congenial rights and forcing her to indulge in unnatural sex since marriage. The victim, Shanu Dholakia, who stays with her parents near Lad Society in Vastrapur in Ahmedabad now, has been married to one Mitul Dholakia (29), the son of a prominent Rajkot-based educationist, since January 2007. The Dholakias run a chain of elite schools in Rajkot, police officers investigating the case said.

Incidentally, Shanu was allegedly tortured by her in-laws for not being able to conceive a child for more than a year since marriage.

She filed a complaint before Metropolitan Magistrate J K Pandya of Metropolitan Court no. 5 on September 25 this year, following which the court asked the Karanj police to investigate the matter.

"In her complaint, Shanu has said she has not been able to conceive because her marriage to Mitul has not been consummated. She has also accused Mitul of forcing her to indulge in unnatural sex. We have registered an offence under Section 377 of IPC and are investigating the case," said Investigating Officer, Karanj Inspector, V D Gohil.

Though Shanu has also accused eight of her other in-laws, including Mitul's parents of allegedly subjecting her to cruelty for not being able to conceive a child, the court has only asked the Karanj police to investigate the allegations of unnatural acts of sex.

"We will record the couple's statements and get some medical checks done to ascertain the allegations," Gohil added.

Mitul is also accused of taking Shanu to a sex club in Thailand during their honeymoon and forcing her to watch sex shows, which were not to her liking.

"She has also alleged that Mitul used to force her to watch movies on unnatural sex," Gohil said.

The police said that four days before Shanu filed her complaint in the court, Mitul met Shanu near Bhadra temple in Karanj and tried to persuade her to return.

When contacted for comments, a family member of the Dholakias, said, "Mitul is out of town and does not have a mobile phone."

Heading: Vadodara cops make 23 cough up Rs 200 each for smoking in public - Indian Express
Content:
The looming power crisis in the state, which is an offshoot of the inadequate rains, has made the Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL) announce a compulsory one-day holiday for all noncontinuous heavy and light industries across the state from October 6.

According to a GUVNL press release, the ban will be strictly implemented across the state from next Monday.

Last month, when the electricity demand had gone up in the farm sector, GUVNL had imposed a two-day ban on industries across the state. The ban was, however, lifted within 15 days, when it rained in the third week of September.

The release said the poor and delayed rainfall has increased the demand for electricity in the farm sector. In order to even out the power demand, all heavy and light industries will now have to observe a compulsory one-day holiday.

According to GUVNL, the ban will be effective from next Monday beginning with Rajkot district. This will be followed by Mehsana, Banaskantha, Amreli and Surendranagar on Tuesday, Kheda, Bharuch, Narmada, Porbandar, Bhavnagar, Jamnagar and Junagadh on Wednesday, Patan, Vadodara, Anand, Tapi and Surat on Friday, Gandhinagar, Valsad, Navsari on Saturday and Ahmedabad, Sabarkantha, Panchmahal, Dahod on Sunday.

Heading: False alarm was raised to gather a mob near the train: Nanavati report - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara police were prompt enough to let the citizens know that the ban on smoking in public places has arrived and is here to stay. The police cracked the whip on the first day of the ban and fined as many as 23 people found smoking in public.

The police, along with the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) officials, collected Rs 200 from each of the offenders. Senior officials said the law is going to be implemented with full vigour, but it is the duty of the public to join hands with the police and keep the city smoke free.

Interestingly, despite wide publicity through the media, many of those who were fined were unaware about the new rule.

"There were posters and advertisements in the newspapers, TV channels and other media, requesting people not to smoke in public places from October 2," said Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Gagandeep Gambhir, who along with her colleague, DCP B V Shrimali, is the member of a committee looking after the implementation of the ban.

Gambhir added that on the first day of the ban, officials had decided to go easy for the first couple of hours. "But from Friday, it will be strict," she said.

The police said a sum of Rs 4,600 has been collected from the 23 offenders. The sum collected from the penalties would go to the traffic development corpus in the city.

Heading: Dalits face social, economic boycott in rural Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The Nanavati Commission's conspiracy theory has its basis in the alleged abduction of one Sophia from Godhra railway station and the alleged rumours spread by Salim Panwala about a Muslim girl's abduction.

According to statements given by Sophia — who was 17 at the time of the incident — to both police and the Commission, there was a scuffle between some Muslim vendors and karsevaks at the railway station, as one of the karsevaks tried to forcibly take her towards the Sabarmati Express. She was released after her mother raised an alarm.

Sophia had said this in her first statement to the police on March 28, 2002. In police chargesheets, she was cited as a witness. She was called by the Commission to give evidence on January 13, 2003. The crux of Sophia's statement -- both to the police and the Commission — has remained unchallenged by all parties present.

However, not only does the Nanavati Commission reject her statements, it also draws new inferences from it. "The Commission is inclined to take the view that such an incident had, in fact, not happened and probably what Sophiabanu has stated was at the insistence of Salim Panwala who had spread a false rumour. It appears to be an attempt to pass off the false rumour as true," the Commission says. This conclusion is important in the context of the conspiracy theory, as it suggests that there was a plan to set the train on fire and a rumour regarding the abduction of a Muslim girl was spread to mobilise a mob near the train.

The conspiracy theory would have suffered if the mob had spontaneously reacted to an attempt to abduct a Muslim girl — a version that had found official endorsement in police reports.

While the first chargesheet of the case does not mention Panwala and Sophia, they figure in all the 16 supplementary chargesheets filed later. All the supplementary chargesheets mention the incident involving Sophia and say that Panwala had raised an alarm about the abduction of a Muslim girl. These two incidents are, however, mentioned independent of each other.

In the first part of its report, the Commission has said that Panwala was at a distance from the place where Sophia's attempted abduction took place and had raised a false alarm to gather a mob around the train.

The Commission has mentioned the delay on the part of Sophia to tell others about the incident and the fact that she and her mother had not boarded the train to Vadodara on February 27 after the incident. The report says, "If they had really gone to the station for going to Vadodara, they would have boarded the Sabarmati Express as it would have taken them to Vadodara, but they did not do so."

The report concludes that "if what Salim Panwala had said was true, then an attempt would have been made to look for her while the train was standing on the station for eight to 10 minutes thereafter. But no body did that."

Incidentally, there is no material on record to suggest whether somebody had actually gone looking for Sophia or not, or whether any witnesses had been asked this specific question. Neither was Sophia's version ever disputed. Besides, the state government also never took the stand that the versions of Sophia and Panwala were connected.

Heading: Pak arrests 29 fishermen, seizes 5 boats - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat is busy projecting its progressive and vibrant image across the globe and inviting investors from all over. But century-old caste conflicts continue to assume starker facades in the underbelly of vibrant Gujarat. If not outright violence, rural Gujarat has found a far more effective measure to keep Dalits under check: social and economic boycott.

At least in six villages across the state, Dalits are now facing such boycotts for one reason or the other. The pattern, however, remains the same. No entry for the Dalits in the village grocer's shop, no employment for them in village farms, denial of boarding on commercial vehicles owned by the upper castes, denial of grinding wheat in the village flour mill and so on. While denial of employment strikes a lethal blow on their livelihoods, the rest of the measures ensure that living conditions go for a complete toss.

After forcing their entry into the village temple through police intervention on Sunday, Dalits of Targara village of Botad block in Bhavnagar have now been slapped with a socio-economic ban. "They had a public meeting on Tuesday evening and decided to boycott us socially," said Harji Bala from Targara.

Babu Koli, the sarpanch of the village too did not have any qualms about admitting the boycott. "After all that the Dalits had done, we held a public meeting in the village and decided not to have any dealings with them anymore," he said.

On Sunday, the Dalits of the village demanded that the protective thread, which is taken out of from the temple of Shikotar mata, the village deity, around the village every alternate year, should also include the Dalit ghetto, which has been traditionally excluded from the "Suraksha Kavach." The Dalits also entered the temple, a right hitherto denied to them, in the presence of the police. Later the villagers postponed the protective thread ritual, which was a clear deviation from tradition.

Tension has been brewing in Nesda village of Tankara block in Rajkot district as well. The Dalits in Nesda are being boycotted by the dominant communities since August. The reason is more mundane.

First the Dalits started raising questions on the development funds received by the village panchayat. Dissatisfied with the apathy of the panchayat, they finally refused to carry out their age old customary duty of manually dragging the dead animals and disposing them. Irked with the audacity, the village community held a public meeting and called for a total boycott of the community.

After consistent struggle of two months, the Dalits finally managed to lodge an FIR on Monday evening. Ramesh Bhadja, the sarpanch of the village, however, refuted the charge and said that the accusations are baseless.

"There is nothing in the complaint that merits an FIR. We had to register it because they insisted on it," said Rajkot Rural Police Superintendent ND Solanki. What is interesting is that the Rajkot District Collector admitted that the people from upper castes were refusing to employ the Dalits following some trouble between the communities, and this was an observation made before the FIR was filed.

In some more villages, such boycotts are on for years. In Kotdi village of Sabarkundla block in Amreli district, the Dalits have been excommunicated for the last four years. Their fault was that they refused the villagers to make a road through the two acre land given to them by the state government in 1999. The village has about a 10,000 strong population mostly of Darbars and Ahirs and houses 50 Dalit families.

Ramesh Painter, a Dalit from Kotadi said: "No one in the village hires us in their field, or lets us buy grocery from the village shop. We need to go to Rajula for everything. But even there, we cannot use any of the commercial vehicles owned by the upper castes of the village," he said.

Sarpanch Gobar Patel has a different take on the matter. "There is nothing of this nature in our village. Of course, there are some tussle relating to some land issue between the Dalits and the farmers, but we have asked them to come for a compromise," he said.

The same story is being repeated in Shetriyana village of Chuda block of Surendranagar district. The Dalits have been excommunicated for very same reason here as well.

"They wanted to construct a road through a piece of land, which was given to us by the government. Once we refused, they excommunicated us," said Hemu Parmar, a Dalit villager. He added: "Since June 2007, we are bearing the brunt of this. The biggest problem we are facing is that now we cannot draw water from the bore-wells owned by the Patels in the village. They don't even let us sit in any public vehicle owned by them."

Gujarat Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Fakir Vaghela said: "We view such matters with grave seriousness. Whenever such developments are brought to our notice, the government swings into action fast and ensures redressal."

He said that in cases where the Dalits have migrated due to harassment and atrocities, the state government has taken prompt action to either stop such migration or rehabilitate them. "We are also in the process of strictly enforcing laws pertaining to the prevention of atrocities against the scheduled castes and tribes and will look into these reports seriously," he added.

Heading: Drama unfolds in court over application filed by advocate Munshi - Indian Express
Content:
The Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA) arrested 29 Indian fishermen and seized five boats near Kori creek in Jakhau waters in the Arabian Sea bordering Pakistan on Wednesday. "All these fishermen are lodged in a Karachi jail," said National Fishermen Forum Secretary (Gujarat) Manish Lodhari, who was informed about the same by his Karachi counterpart. This has taken the total number of Indian fishermen arrested by Pakistan to 434 and the number of boats seized to 379.

According to Lodhari, all the arrested fishermen come from the coastal belt of Diu, Wanakbara and Mangrol and three of the five boats have been identified as Upkaar from Porbandar, Bhavnath from Porbandar and Ratnakar from Mangrol. "The arrests happened on Wednesday, which were confirmed by our Karachi counterpart on Thursday," said Lodhari

According to sources in the state Fisheries Department, the Indian Coast Guard authorities have requested them to ensure that the fishermen carry the proper documents while venturing into the sea. "Fishermen would be sent back home if lapses are found during the on-board checking of Indian trawlers on the high seas," they said.

Sources also said that even though the coastal authorities have written to the Fisheries Department warning of strict action in case of lapses, the latter has not taken action in this regard.

President of Indian Fishermen Association, Veljibhai Masani, alleged that PSMA personnel illegally ventured into Indian waters to arrest the fishermen. "Fish-rich Jakhau is a major activity zone in the Arabian Sea and so is the adjoining area in Pakistani waters. But our fishermen took all the necessary precautions of not straying into Pakistani territory while venturing into Jakhau waters," said Masani.

Heading: ‘Slum’ dunk: No toilets, no water, it is pandemonium in city slums - Indian Express
Content:
The sombre confines of court number 11—where the designated Metropolitan Court has been hearing the Ahmedabad serial blasts case—on Wednesday turned dramatic over an application moved by advocate I M Munshi representing some of the accused.

The application stated that the accused were illegally detained by the police for about two months before being shown as formally arrested and were being mentally and physically tortured in police custody. The situation turned volatile during the hearing of the remand application of ten blast-accused including Mufti Abdul Bashar and Sajid Mansuri. At the start of the proceedings, Munshi sent an application to be signed by all the accused. After three accused including Mansuri had signed it, a police officer near the dock saw that the accused were signing two applications instead of the usual vakalatnama. He stopped the rest from signing it.

The application was then presented to Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel who called all the ten accused forward and read the application aloud. Munshi meanwhile kept protesting and said that the application should not be read aloud in presence of the police. He said that either the contents of the application should be read out aloud in chamber or should be given to the accused and left to their decision. After the application was read out, Patel asked the accused to sign it if they so desired. The accused, in the presence of police officers, refused to sign the application and denied that they had been ill-treated by the police.

The three accused including Sajid Mansuri, who had signed the application, rescinded it and wrote that they had signed it without knowing the contents. Mansuri's wife had earlier filed an affidavit stating that he was being physically and mentally tortured by the Ahmedabad Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) and that his leg was fractured and needed medical attention. Mansuri was made to walk before the court and he showed no apparent signs of a fracture. At this point, Munshi remarked angrily to the accused, "sign karo nahin to faansi thai jashe" (sign it or you will be hanged). This elicited a sharp reaction from the prosecution who insisted that Munshi's remark be taken on record.

Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel accepted the prosecution's request and reprimanded Munshi for presenting applications that are premeditated, unnecessary and aimed to demoralise the police. A DCB official angrily remarked: "This is just to prevent us from doing investigation. We follow all the guidelines. The accused are medically checked after every 48 hours. If Mansuri had a fractured leg, could he have walked six floors to the courtroom?"

Heading: GPS transponders to assist fishermen in distress at sea - Indian Express
Content:
"We walk down 4 km to Guptanagar and Vishala and pay Rs. 2 to use the public toilets there," says Natwar Kambhaji, a labourer of Shri Om Nagar, a chawl in Pravinnagar.

Slum dwellers in Ahmedabad are deprived of the basic necessities like drinking water and sanitation. Under the Slum Networking Programme (SNP), the slum-dwellers are entitled to drinking water and toilets in their homes. The SNP has been effective in 45 slums in the city. The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) is now working on four slums namely Chamundanagar, Abuji Kuwa na Chapra, Punjabi Talawala ni chali and Pravinnagar- 2.

According to the AMC, many facilities have been provided to the slums in Pravinnagar and only road development is pending. The various pockets falling in the Pravinnagar slums are equipped with electric metres, water connections and individual toilets.

After a survey conducted by Newsline, however, the various pockets in Pravinnagar like Vanjara Vas, Tulsibhagat ni chali, Lasanwadi ni chali etc were found to be lacking proper water supply and sanitation facilities under the programme.

With the joint efforts of Saath (an NGO) and the AMC, the slum-dwellers have received water connections near their homes. The water is supplied once a day for an hour, but the quality is reportedly bad.

"Although we get water everyday, the water pressure is very low. The pipes were laid low due to which we do not get enough water. Moreover, the water is yellowish and sometimes sticky, with a stench," says Ramesh Vaghela, a resident of Pravinnagar slum.

The slums under the programme are also entitled to individual toilets in their shanties. But their condition is reported to be quite dismal, with rusting doors and leaking roofs. Some toilets are also clogged due to poor drainage.

"We have been given toilets but they are in a miserable condition. Due to lesser water supply, we cannot even use them regularly. We have to bathe in the open since the toilets are small. It is very difficult for the women to manage in this condition," says Bina Solanki.

Anand Patel, Additional City Engineer of West Zone Housing, SNP, claims: "The AMC has passed a resolution that if a house is less than 40 sq m then they get individual no-objection certificates, where water and sanitation facility is entitled to them from the Zonal Office. And most of the slum-dwellers are opting out of this, which has also reduced the pace of SNP."

The slums that do not fall under the purview of SNP are supposed to receive water and sanitation facilities from the AMC. But the slum pockets like Tulsibhagat ni chali have been deprived of water and sanitation. Therefore, the residents have constructed their own bathing areas, but still have to walk a long distance to answer nature's call.

"We have paid about Rs 1,800 for the connection. We even got an NOC for our chawl but the AMC has not taken any initiative yet. We even approached an NGO working in a nearby chawl but they refused to help us, saying that it doesn't fall in their area limits," says Sayra Khatik, a visibly upset slum-dweller.

Natwar Kumbhaji of Shri Om Nagar chawl adds that they have managed to get an NOC from the government but are still facing problems of water and sanitation. "As we do not have toilets, the children are made to defecate in boxes and then dispose them off. Many residents are facing health hazards like malaria and jaundice with to all the filth around.

Heading: CM, Guv outline Gandhian ideals as solution to all global issues - Indian Express
Content:
To assist the fishermen in distress when at sea, the Indian Coast Guard along with the Space Application Centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Ahmedabad and VXL Technologies Ltd, Faridabad, have jointly developed a low-cost GPS (Global Positioning System)-based alert system.

The ISRO-developed transmitter has a battery life of 24-48 hours after activation. It transmits the boat's co-ordinates to the Coast Guard Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre (MRCC) in Mumbai.

The distress alerts sent out by the boats will be picked up by the INSAT 3A satellite which will relay the same to the reception centre at the MRCC. Medical emergencies, fire, capsize or capture of the boats can be reported to authorities on the shore for immediate action.

The transmitter operates through a DRT transponder and can send out continuous alerts for 24 hours once every 5 minutes on an average while staff at the rescue centres track the boat as it appears on a GIS map on their computer screens. Each transmitter costs less than Rs 10,000 with an omni-directional antenna and runs on a lithium battery. It will give its identification number and GPS position of the boat to the Coast Guard. "While the other, similar systems are very expensive, the cost reduction has been done by using our own INSAT 3A," said Wing Commander Satish Menon, Defence Spokesperson in Ahmedabad.

A formal handover function was held by the Indian Coast Guard at Porbandar on Friday for handing over 20 such instruments to various fishing associations along the Gujarat coast for fitment on boats. "Many such distributions will soon follow since we are facing a high demand for the system," Menon added.

Heading: Wild, wild Rajkot to hold Wildlife Education Fair on Oct 4 and 5 - Indian Express
Content:
On the occasion of the 140th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, Chief Minister Narendra Modi attended a prayer meeting at Kirtimandir in Porbandar on Thursday. In the meeting, he clearly mentioned that Gandhian methods can effectively deal with terrorism and global warming.

He further said that in order to fulfil Gandhi's dream of emancipation of villages and to develop them, one needs to follow his steps. The chief minister told the crowd that Gandhi was a global leader and that he strongly believes that following the ideals of Bapu can solve each and every difficulty in this world.

Modi also laid the foundation of the District Service Centre at Porbandar. It is estimated that around Rs 6 crore will be spent on the establishment of this centre. Modi also said that the centre would be for the citizens, especially those who are not economically sound.

Another prayer meeting was organised at the Sabarmati Gandhi Ashram and Governor Naval Kishore Sharma graced the occasion.

In his speech at the venue, Sharma told the crowd that in Ahmedabad and other cities, there are a lot of people who are mentally ill and suffering from several diseases. And there are many who are helping them. Nevertheless, there is a need to establish a proper channel between them so that people who are suffering can get maximum benefits.

Heading: This Navratri, garba artists will feel at home - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the state, the Forest Department and the NGOs are planning to organise a Wildlife Education Fair on October 4 and 5 as part of the Wildlife Week Celebrations. The Rajkot based NGO — Wildlife Conservation Trust, the state Forest Department, the municipal corporation-run Rajkot Zoo and the Rajkot Bal Bhavan are jointly celebrating the Wildlife Week from October 2 to 8 in the city.

During the weeklong celebration, various educational activities like essay writing competition, elocution and painting, besides a quiz contest will be organised for the students. A wildlife education fair, which is being organised for the first time in the state, will be held at the Shyamaprasad Art Gallery in Racecourse ground on October 4 and 5. WCT president Kishore Kotecha said more than seven stalls will be set-up in the ground outside the Shyamaprasad art gallery during the two-day long fair. "This is first time we are organising such an event. There will be less number of stalls but we are hoping that people of Rajkot will enjoy the novel concept for the fair."

He said the WCT stall will educate people about our ongoing campaign of covering open wells in the vicinity of the Gir Sanctuary. "There will be a stall of the Forest Department in which they will display various posters about educating people about wildlife and another stall, which will provide details of medicinal and herbal plants, complete with posters and live specimens. The Forest Department has also decided to distribute free of cost, saplings of some herbal and medicinal plants during the fair," he said.

He added: "The most attractive stall in the fair will be of the wildlife photography exhibition by famous wildlife photographer Bhushan Pandya. Rare picture of Asiatic lions and other indigenous species will be displayed during the exhibition. The Gujarat Ecological Education and Research (GEER) Foundation will also display books and other materials regarding wildlife education at their stall here."

Rajkot District Forest Officer G V Vadi said they have received more than 2,400 entries from the different schools of the district, for all the competitions in the different categories.

"This is the first time that such an event is being organised in any city. Our main target is to educate the children and for that we have organised various contests with a single theme of 'Wildlife in our backyard.' This concept will create awareness in society about the conservation of wildlife. We will present prizes, certificates and trophies to the winners to appreciate enthusiastic winners of these contests," he said.

Students will have to appear at the essay and the painting competition at their respective schools, while the elocution competition will be held at the Rajkot Zoo on October 8.

Heading: Broad-gauge track inaugurated between Dabhoi-Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
With the state government and the corporate sector promoting the Navratri festival as nine nights of revelry to attract tourists from across the globe, many of the reputed garba artists, who earlier chose to visit overseas during Navratri, have enough motivation to stay back home now. The reason: their remuneration for performing at home now matches their income abroad.

"Normally, the non-resident Gujarati community invites artists to perform garba during Navratri," said Digant Sompura, a noted garba artist who is just back from a UN Cultural Exchange Programme in the US. He said with visa procedures getting strict in the US, most garba organisers are now sticking to inviting only the reputed groups. The performers do not want to go, as they have lucrative options back home. "Most of the reputed groups have stayed back in the country this year," he added.

In the US, Garba is organised over the weekends and is spread over a month. "The long stay abroad is another reason why some are unwilling to go," he further said.

Parul Patel, a renowned Baroda-based Garba artist, who has been visiting the US during Navratri for the last 10 years, said: "There are two types of artists who visit overseas during Navratri. While some go through the non-resident Gujarati agents settled there and perform under contracts, others like me go individually and perform traditional garba during Navratri."

She said: "For me it all started many years ago, when I visited the US and saw people dancing to the tune of Hindi Film songs during Garva, adding that that experience propelled her to start performing traditional sheri garba for the Gujarati Diaspora in the US. "People liked it as they had a feeling of strengthening their bond with their roots. I have been performing Garba in various parts of the US for the last 10 years, but this time around I have decided not to go," she added.

Parul said that security is an issue and many are denied visa nowadays. On an average, an artist makes about 3,000 to 3,500 dollars per night of performance. But people now prefer to go there after Navratri and stay till Diwali, she said.

The promoters too now prefer to invite two groups simultaneously and exchange them within cities. "There are many promoters like Varshaben in Florida, Naty Thakkar in New Jersey and Bhavna Modi in Chicago, who are involved in organising these programmes," Parul added.

Heading: Nine die as truck rams into jeep - Indian Express
Content:
Now, commuters from Dabhoi can reach Vadodara in a short time by paying only Rs 5. Minister of State for Railways Naran J Rathwa has dedicated the newly converted broad-gauge line between Dabhoi and Pratapgunj in Vadodara to the public.

"Earlier, the fare was Rs 3, but it would take hours to reach Dabhoi on the narrow gauge tracks. Now, just by paying Rs 5, the commuter can go to Vadodara, instead of paying the bus fare Rs 22 for the same," said Rathwa on Thursday.

Meanwhile, the track between Dabhoi to Chhotaudepur will take another year for completion. "We are planning to connect the new tracks to the Central Railways network through Chhotaudepur and Dhar in Madhya Pradesh, further connecting Jhabua and Indore," said Rathwa.

He said Prime Minister Manmohan Singh will inaugurate the foundation stone of the Chhotaudepur-Dhar railway route in February 2009.

"With the inauguration of the new broad gauge track, the tribal belt in Gujarat and parts of it in Madhya Pradesh will be connected to arterial tracks running between Mumbai and Delhi, which is essential for the economic development of Gujarat and the tribal population in the five districts of the state," said Rathwa.

Incidentally, the 30-kilometre stretch between Dabhoi and Pratapgunj in Vadodara took two and a half years and Rs 80 crore for completion.

Rathwa said: "It was a daunting task and many said it will take five to six years for completion. But, with the help of the railway officials, latest technology and cooperation of the farmers, everything was under control."

Mobile electric flash-butt welding, a relatively new form of technology, was used to join second hand railway track bars to make a long railway track bar, while the existing railway bridges were repaired in what the Western Railway officials described as a record time of one and half years from the day construction work started.

On this occasion, Rathwa also announced a bonus of Rs 3 lakh for the employees of the Western Division for the completion of the railway line ahead of schedule.

Heading: Congress blames BJP for failing to pass GUJCOC Bill - Indian Express
Content:
Nine people were killed after a speeding truck rammed into their jeep near Madhwas village, about 10 kilometres from Pavagadh around 3 am on Thursday. Six passengers died on the spot and two more were declared dead at the Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital.

One of the deceased has not been identified.

Officers at the Kalol police station said the deceased belonged to Bajidora village in Banswada district of Rajasthan.

"There were more than 20 passengers from one particular area who were going to Pavagadh to offer prayers during Navratri. Just near Madhwas, a truck moving at a high speed, rammed into the jeep. The injured were first rushed to the Halol Referral Hospital and then shifted to SSG Hospital. Two more people died during treatment," said an officer at the Kalol police station

He said after the accident, the truck driver escaped from the spot.

The deceased have been identified as Valu Amarji Rawat (27), Ashok Goswami (25), the driver and owner of the jeep, Dinesh Rawat (26), Jamnaben Makanbhai (50), Santoshben Katara (28), Vitthal Pargi (40), Sangeeta Dindor (28), Kailash Damor (12) and an unidentified man.

Heading: Lack of enforcers makes smoking-ban ineffective - Indian Express
Content:
While the BJP is leaving no stone unturned to secure a favourable nod from the Centre for the contentious GUJCOC Bill, the Gujarat Congress Chief Spokesperson, Shaktisinh Gohil, has blamed the BJP for not being able to pass the Bill.

Speaking at a seminar organised by the Progressive Foundation of Human Rights, Gandhinagar, Gohil said that while the Bill was passed by the state government during the NDA regime, even the BJP-led NDA could not pass the Act because of its contentious provisions. "They are now politicising the issue when even their own government could not pass the Bill," Gohil said.

He observed that the Bill in its present form is incapable of dealing with the threat of terror, as words like 'terror' or 'terrorism' are mentioned nowhere in the draft. Further, he said that while Afzal Guru, who has been sentenced to death by the Supreme Court should be hanged, his hanging will follow the legal procedures.

Maha Gujarat Janata Party president Gordhan Zadaphia insisted for a federal law for dealing with the terror threat. "Terrorism is no more an isolated phenomenon, but has assumed a global face," Zadaphia said, adding that while this calls for enhanced awareness from the citizens, there needs to be a stringent federal law to deal with the menace.

Heading: Court puts peddler behind bars for 13 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
The staff and students of Green Land Senior Secondary Public School celebrated the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri. Floral tributes were paid to the two leaders on the occasion.

Addressing the students, Rajesh Rudhra, the chairman-cum-director of the school, exhorted the students to dedicate themselves to the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri. Shabad Rudhra, the school president, said that we must inculcate self-discipline which, he said, will help us eradicate the menace of violence in the society.

While Baldeep Pandher, the deputy director of the school, told the students to imbibe the simplicity of Mahatma Gandhi. T. Chopra, the school principal, also addressed the students and highlighted the importance of practicing non-violence.

A function was also held at Green Land Convent School, Dugri. On this occasion, the school adopted four students for their schooling. Rajesh Rudhra said, "An amount of Rs 4 lakh will be spent on their studies till 12th class. These students will study at Green Land Convent School, Dugri."

To mark this occasion, Guru Gobind Singh Public School, Daad, Pakhowal Road, organised a collage-making competition. The subject was 'Patriots and present leaders'. Students participated with enthusiasm in the competition. The collage arranged by Manpreet Singh of IXth class was declared best in the competition whereas Jashanpreet Singh of class X and Shivam Vasudeva of class X were declared second and third, respectively. A special prize for Kirandeep Kaur was also announced by principal Manjit Kaur.

Earlier in the morning, in the assembly dedicated to the Father of Nation Mahatma Gandhi, the teachers told the students about the ideals Mahatma Gandhi stood for and which were still relevant today. The principal of the school, Manjit Kaur, in a speech depicted the evils at the time of Gandhi ji's stay at South Africa. He opposed the establishment for their stance on colour discrimination.

Birthday celebrations were also held at Shaheed-e-Azam Sukhdev Thapar Government Girls Senior Secondary School, Bharat Nagar. The function was presided over by Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda.

With the efforts of Rotary Club, Ludhiana Central and Parents-teachers Association, seven sewing machines, 28 fans, a generator of 32 kw, two beds for Red Cross room, mattresses, blankets, table chairs, eight almirahs, equipment for science laboratory worth Rs 57,000 was given to the school. Shri Durga Mata Mandir, Jagraon Bridge, has already donated a sum of Rs 1.50 lakh to the school.

On this occasion, students presented a cultural programme. Dhanda asked the students to follow the path shown by these leaders. He assured monetary help for the school in future.

Heading: For senior citizens, it was a day out amid pictures - Indian Express
Content:
Special Judge-cum-Additional Session Judge (ASJ) Ashok Kumar has sentenced Mohammad Bhoora, a resident of Tajpur Road here, to 13 years of imprisonment for possessing poppy husk. The judge also ordered him to pay Rs 2 lakh as fine.

Delivering the verdict, ASJ Ashok Kumar held that prosecution had successfully proved that poppy husk had been recovered from the accused. The judge turned down the plea of leniency raised by the accused.

A case under Section 15 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act was registered against the accused persons at the Dehlon police station on April 2, 2004. The prosecution had claimed that 1.25 tonnes of poppy husk had been recovered from the accused.

A police team headed by Sawinder Singh, Inspector, had barricaded the road leading from Sheelon Kalan village to Doburji village for checking the vehicles. A truck bearing Uttar Pradesh registration number was stopped, and the the accused were found sitting in it. On being searched, the accused were found in possession of 25 gunny bags containing poppy husk. In defence, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication but failed to prove it.

Heading: Insurance company told to cough up claim amount - Indian Express
Content:
For the residents of Senior Citizens Home, Sarabha Nagar, it was a day out amid pictures and photographs. To mark the Gandhi Jayanti and the day for the elderly, the art gallery, Artmosphere, had invited the resident of this old age home for a cup of tea and also for spending some time at the gallery. At present, this gallery has on display a photography exhibition by Jaswant Zafar.

Sixty two-year old Surjeet Singh, while commenting on the pictures, said, "They are so beautiful. They remind me of my younger days when we would visit old places and parks." To this, 82-year old Omkar Nath added, "Such outings for us and that on special invitation are always a pleasure. We never knew that Ludhiana has an art gallery. It is nice to see that this town which is only about money money and more money has a space where someone can display his finer feeling and people like us can come and enjoy such moments."

For 83-year-old Bal Kishan Gupta, "The idea of art gallery is really great. I belong to Amritsar and we have art galleries there. It is nice to see that Ludhiana too has one such art space. It is a great feeling to sit here among so many beautiful pictures."

As the others enjoyed the beauty of the pictures, Kewal Krishan, another resident of this home, remarked, "These pictures have brought back old memories. These pictures have been taken in places like Mumbai, Hyderabad, Mahableshwar and other such places. I have visited all these place and even the spots where these pictures have been taken." Krishan added, "A walk through the exhibition has brought back all those old memories once again."

And do they miss home?

" Not at all," says Omkar Nath, 'For at our old age home, we are very well looked after and above all enjoy a lot of freedom."

Nath explains, "At the end of the day, it all about one's own freedom and space. Children want their space and we oldies want ours. And we all should learn to do that. We have enjoyed our lives and now it is the turn of children to do the same. Why should we become obstacles for them. At the same time, I want my freedom."

"Which daughter-in-law will serve me bed tea at five in the morning be it be summer or winter?," he asks and then adds: "I get it here and I enjoy every moment I spend. My only advise to the youngsters is make some good saving which you can spend later in life."

Heading: To keep fit, Ludhiana police turn to yoga - Indian Express
Content:
The permanent Lok Adalat, while accepting a petition filed by one Shingara Singh of Hargobind Nagar, Giaspura here, has directed the ICICI Lombard General Insurance to pay the claim of Rs 1.75 lakh made by the consumer for accidental damage caused to his vehicle.

The chairman of the Lok Adalat, C.D. Gupta, and members R.S. Khokhar and Nand Lal have directed the company to make the payment within 45 days. In case of failure, the consumer would be entitled for an interest at the rate of 9 pc from the day of the filing of the case.

Shingara Singh of Hargobind Nagar, Giaspura, had filed a case before the adalat and had submitted that he had purchased an Indica car and the vehicle was insured with the company.

The car had met with an accident in which it was totally damaged and matter was duly reported to the police as well as insurance company. The company deputed a surveyor, who assessed the loss. But the accident claim was not paid to the applicant.

The Lok Adalat observed that the company had denied the claim on the plea that the vehicle was being used for commercial purpose even though it was not insured as one. But the court held that the company had failed to prove that at the time of the accident.

Heading: City’s debut Digambar Jain temple opens - Indian Express
Content:
To keep fit, the Ludhiana police have now turned to yoga.

At the Police Lines today, a yoga camp was organised for the Ludhiana police personnel of all ranks. But senior police officers were conspicuous by their absence from the camp. In today's camp, over 150 police personnel of different ranks participated.

"We have planned this programme for all our employees. This programme will continue for one month and during this time, we will call all the police personnel turn-by-turn," said SP (Headquarters) Harish Kumar.

But today the senior police officers were conspicuous by their absence as the places which had been kept reserved for them were left vacant. When questioned about this, SSP R.K. Jaiswal said, "We were busy in conducting security checks in the city in view of the Id festival today and we did not want to take any chance. As for yoga is concerned, this programme will be on for one month and we can participate in it, anytime."

SSP Jaiswal further said that the motive of this programme was to inculcate a habit of yoga among the police personnel so that they keep themselves in fine fettle. "Once they get used to practicing yoga, they can practice it at their homes," the SSP added.

Jaiswal said that from time to time, such programmes were planned for the police personnel. It may be mentioned here that in the annual medical check up camp held in April this year, a number of police personnel were found suffering from various ailments.

Heading: Kamal, Bhavika claim U-14 titles - Indian Express
Content:
The United Nations has declared October 2 as the International Day of Non-violence in the honour of Mahatma Gandhi. Following it, Shri Digambar Jain Mandir, conveying the message of non-violence and vegetarianism, has been inaugurated today. First of its kind in the city, Digambar Jain temple has come up at Dugri, Dhandra Road, in an area of 1,000 square yards.

Amresh Jain, president of the temple, said, "We have installed five-feet tall white marble statue of Lord Mahavira here. The "Pran-Pratishthha" ceremony will be performed from November 28 to December 4 by Digambar Jain saint, who will visit Punjab for the first time." he said.

"Maanav stambh" will be installed outside the temple, on the top of which there will be statue depicting Lord Indera and Lord Mahavira.

Manjul Jain, a cashier at the temple, said, "Various activities will be undertaken in order to inculcate values and sensitize the humankind towards the salient message of Lord Mahavira. His message includes non-violence, non-materialism and respect for different points of view and benefits of adopting vegetarianism."

Jain said that in future, some more projects in the service of general public — like a veterinary hospital or a charitable hospital — would also be started in the same premises. There are about 7,000 people belonging to Digambar sect of Jainism in the city.

Heading: Man held for killing father - Indian Express
Content:
In a one-sided encounter, Madhya Pradesh drubbed Maharashtra by 23-15 points in the women section during the ongoing 20th senior national circle kabaddi championship being held in Chandigarh on Thursday. In men's section, Jharkhand routed out Madhya Pradesh by 27-22 points in an exciting match. From the winning team Jatinder and Ramji scored 7 and 5 points respectively.

Displaying great team work, Rajasthan snuffed out the challenge of Vidarba in a closely fought game at 24-20. Uttar Pradesh also won their match against Maharastra at 33-27. Delhi also came good against Himachal Pradesh registering win at 32-22 to surge ahead.

Heading: Probe delay deepens differences - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-four hours after the security guard of the cremation ground of Lalton village was found dead, the police claimed to have solved the murder with the arrest of his son.

Gurdeep Singh, 30, was arrested from the Daad village bus stand late on Wednesday evening.

Gurdeep told the police that Atma Singh, 60, wanted to establish illicit relations with his wife. Irked, he decided to kill his father.

Atma Singh was murdered on the intervening night of September 29 and 30.

Gurmeet Singh Randhawa, Superintendent of Police (SP), City II, said the police had established Gurdeep's involvement in the murder during preliminary investigations, following which he was arrested. He added that on September 29, Atma Singh tried to molest his daughter-in-law, an incident which Gurdeep witnessed. He decided to kill his father thereafter, the SP said.

Gurdeep told the police that Atma Singh had the similar intentions for his other son's wife, after which the latter had shifted to Ludhiana. On the intervening night of September 29 and 30, when Atma Singh was alone in the village cremation ground, Gurdeep first beat him up and then stabbed him with a sword. The police are yet to recover the murder weapon, the SP said.

Heading: 22-year-old arrested for making hoax calls - Indian Express
Content:
With the delay in inquiry into the sexual harassment case at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), fault lines have clearly emerged on the campus.

Those advising the current regime are the former officials of the university who believe that the delay in settling such issues not only hampers investigations, but also mars the reputation of the institution.

Dr K S Aulakh, former Vice-Chancellor who settled one such case in 2001 said, "Such a complaint is highly condemnable. And I cannot buy the statement that a girl or a woman would make a blatantly false complaint on such an issue. Rather a girl coming out in the open on the issue is a very brave step."

He added, "Delaying inquiry into such a matter is torturous for the complainant and hence should be settled at the earliest. On my part, I would call for an exemplary punishment for the perpetrator."

The issue pertains to a woman employee accusing Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, Director, Students' Welfare, of sexual harassment. Vice-Chancellor Dr M S Kang had asked Dr Neelam Grewal, Dean, College of Home Science, to look into the matter.

It has been over a fortnight, however, since the complaint was lodged and the committee is yet to call in any of the parties to record their statements.

This delay has inadvertently led to fault lines emerging on the campus. Sources said a delegation of wardens met the Dr Kang on Wednesday evening and submitted a letter in support of the DSW.

While Dr Kang is out of country, a senior warden on condition of anonymity said: "We are not saying anything against the complainant. We have only told the V-C that we have all worked under the DSW and never faced any such problem."

Amandeep Kaur, a diploma student of the

College of Home Science, said: "The basic idea is that an inquiry into this matter should be conducted as soon as possible. This issue is not about just one girl but about all the women students on the campus. If this matter is handled well, more and more girls will be motivated to voice their problems."

Dr S S Johl, former Vice-Chancellor and director research, Punjab Agricultural University, said: "The girl has even submitted evidence in this case, although it was never needed in the first place. The university authorities should take action as quickly as possible as even the name of the institute is at stake."

Heading: Children take up the cudgel for greener living - Indian Express
Content:
A 22-year-old youth has been arrested for making hoax calls about possible bomb explosions in the city. The police said the youth had tried to create panic by making nearly six hoax calls in the last one week.

Pardeep Kumar alias Rahul alias Karamjit is a resident of Kirpal Nagar and runs a rehri to earn his livelihood.

Gurmeet Singh Randhawa, Superintendent of Police (SP), City II, said Pardeep was arrested on Wednesday by the Basti Jodhewal police. Last week, Pardeep had made calls on the mobile phone of Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) R K Jaiswal and on the landline number of the police control room. After thorough searches, all these calls were found to be a hoax.

"His motive was to create panic, keeping in mind the recent serial bomb blasts at different places in the country," the SP said. Further investigations are on in the case, he added.

Heading: Game is Booked - Indian Express
Content:
A group of youngsters on Friday indulged in violence at an auditorium in the city, where an audition for a reality show was on, prompting police to use force to disperse them.

A number of people, who had gathered for the audition of MTV's 'Roadies' programme at an auditorium in south Delhi's Hauz Khaz, were injured in the police action, a senior police official said.
