The incident took place at about 1 pm when a group of youth entered the auditorium and started smashing the window panes as the group discussion was progressing, the official said, adding the attackers also burnt some posters and tried to damage a motorcycle.

Police was informed immediately as about 100 private security personnel deployed at the auditorium failed to contain violence.

Police resorted to canecharging in which a number of youths are injured. However, officials refused to provide the exact number of those injured in the incident.

The injured were rushed to AIIMS hospital where some were provided primary treatment as their wounds were not of serious nature.

The violence during the programme prompted the organisers to cancel the audition. The new date for the audition will be announced later, organisers said.

Around 5,000 youngsters had assembled at the auditorium for the audition.

The audition in the capital was the fifth of a total of six such exercise to select participants for the programme.

Auditions have earlier been done in Kolkata, Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Chandigarh.

Heading: Passion Plate - Indian Express
Content:
His life resembles the reels of Chak De! India, but former India hockey coach Mir Ranjan Negi now reveals it all in a book

When Kabir Khan's motley team of girls won the imaginary World Championships in Chak De! India, there was a collective sigh of relief in the cinemas. But for one viewer, Mir Ranjan Negi, it was as though a moment of his life was blown up on the screen. Negi did not share Kabir Khan's sexy bearded looks, but somewhere the pain matched. "Shah Rukh Khan acted exceptionally well, but I had actually lived out those sentiments," says Negi.

There have been endless discussions on whether or not Negi's life inspired the blockbuster, but this time he has decided to do the talking. The 50-year-old former goalkeeper and coach is ready with his autobiography, From Gloom to Glory (Popular Prakshan). The origin of gloom is in the 1982 Asian Games. Negi was the goalkeeper of the Indian hockey team which was badgered 1-7 by Pakistan. The country wept — and then fumed against Negi for conceding the goals. Almost ostracised, Negi slunk away — but not quite. He redeemed his destiny 16 years later — when the men's hockey team he coached won the gold in the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games. Four years later, the women's team trained by him won the gold at the Commonwealth Games.

"I have no complaints about hockey. It gave me the worst days of my life but it also made me redeem my fate," says Negi, going on to reminisce the two moments of agony and ecstasy. "I feel I could have done things differently. For instance, while stepping on the field for the match against Pakistan in 1982, froth was spilling from my mouth. I shouldn't have played that day. Also, I had chances of slyly injuring the main Pakistani player, but hesitated. This might have cost us the game. I did not speak much after our loss against Pakistan since I was stopped by the hockey federation," says Negi, "I felt vindicated only when the men's hockey team won the gold at Bangkok."

From Gloom to Glory comprises a series of anecdotes and Negi's diary entries after the 1982 games, but the book doesn't begin there. It starts with a personal loss — the death of his eldest son Abhi in a motorcycle accident three years ago. And then he goes on to his brief Bollywood days when he became associated with the making of Chak De! India. "I was offered the project of Chak De! days after my son's demise. I was in a dilemma whether to accept the offer or not. But after a little convincing I accepted it," says Negi, who had finished the book well before Chak De! India happened. The draft was later tweaked to include the experience of working on the film. He writes: "Chak De! turned my life on its head. From relative anonymity I came under the arc lights."

Negi has hung up the boots though he put on the dancing shoes for a while for a season of Jhalak Dikhla Ja. The distress has returned, though, after watching the Olympics where India did not even qualify. "I wish glamour would come back to hockey, something like Twenty20."

Heading: Push the Tempo - Indian Express
Content:
Amigo at Greater Kailash goes beyond Tex-Mex and explores the cuisine of Aztecs and Mayans

The latest restaurant in the buzzing culinary scene of Greater Kailash II is Amigo, a Mexican specialty diner. The menu valiantly attempts to trace the culinary tradition of the Mayans, the pre-Hispanic inhabitants of Mexico. So, popular stews and grills from Mexico's coastal belt along with recipes influenced by Latin America find their way into this trendy diner.

Shrivats Singhania, who makes his debut in the food world with Amigo, also works in his family business in JK industries. "I thought of starting a restaurant in Delhi while studying in the US. There's very little Mexican food on offer here," says Singhania, 25.

The kitchen is supervised by sous chef Sanjay Singh Yadav, who joins after a seven-year stint at Delhi's Mexican restaurant chain Rodeo and has increased his repertoire of recipes substantially with a particular section devoted to south Mexico. There is butterfly quail, a Guerrero specialty; seared duck with pecan prune, a popular recipe of the Incas, and pan-fried red snapper, a classic dish from Acapulco.

The interiors are minimal, even the sombrero, the predictable Mexican accessory, isn't on display. Amigo is spread over two levels, with a formal dining area on the ground floor, and a lounge atmosphere with test-tube chandeliers upstairs.

Must-try

Each order is artistically crafted, keeping in mind the Mexicans' passion for colour. We begin with a balmy broth of Green Pozole (Rs 275), described as an 18th century creation from Guerrero. The soup, cooked with green tomatillos and serano chilli, is laden with bits of corn, kidney beans and chicken. If you're craving for Mexican salad, go for Molcajete (Rs 275). A trolley stacked with avocado fruits and a variety of condiments is rolled in. Pick your fruit and it is ceremoniously scooped and mixed with onions, chillies and jalapenos. The dip is a good accompaniment for the rest of your meal and accompanies tortilla rings for a crunchy munch.

The kitchen also offers the traditional tamale. We tried Chicken in Mole Sauce (Rs 275) that fetched us two packs of minced chicken dusted with masa flour and steamed in a corn-leaf wrap. Open the pouch and a delicious steaming concoction greets every mouthful.

Among quesadillas, Mexico's quintessential street food, we sampled spinach and goat cheese (Rs 250) that served us four triangles of grilled tortillas stuffed with a delicious filling. Stuffed Chillies in Walnut Sauce and Pomegranates (Rs 450) brings a colourful platter of different peppers stuffed with spinach, pine nuts and raisins. The dish is bathed in walnut and pomegranate sauce.

Seafood lovers are in for a special treat. Coco con Mariscos (Rs 650) a seafood stew from the Gulf Coast, takes the lead with its beautiful presentation and an equally delightful flavour. Bits of crab meat, shrimps and fillets are cooked in a cream sauce and stuffed in coconut shells.

Give a miss

The Salmon Maya (Rs 850) is tad overpriced considering it is just a fillet of fish stacked on a plate of potato crispies and kidney-bean paste. The dish did not impart any memorable flavours.

But if you forget Salmon Maya and are ready for a buffet of ethnic Mexican flavours, you can take off your sombrero right here.

Meal for two: Rs 1,800
Location: Local Shopping Centre, Masjid Moth, Greater Kailash II
Contact: 29216220

Heading: It’s all smoke, no fire on Day One - Indian Express
Content:
Parched throats will sip on sake and shochu and nibble on salmon teriyaki as Ai, the Japanese restaurant at The Metropolitan Mall, opens its bar today. Called The Love Hotel, Ai's bar is set to soak in the Japanese aura further as DJ Super Cozi weaves a nuanced, electronic beat into some fast, thumping trance music. "It's my first time in India and I'm really looking forward to my performance," says Cozi who has already performed in Mumbai and Bangalore with some success. Today, Cozi will belt out her mix of acid jazz and break beats at The Love Hotel.

A mother of two, the 42-year-old DJ is also a composer, producer and owner of the three-year-old record label called Hypo=Espresso Records that promotes independent artists and producers.

"As an artist I have seen the bad side of being with a major label. The constant fights affect one's creativity," says Bali-based Cozi, who started at a young age with a punk band in Tokyo in the late 1980s and has been experimenting with strong techno sounds and a psychedelic twist to her songs ever since.

As she prepares to release her fifth solo album Babylondon in the coming months, her trip to India, she says, is also about promoting her band, Zen Lemonade. "Babylondon is a dance compilation and I will be playing some of the songs from it," she says. Cozi is known to throw in a dash of retro flavour into her performances, right from Led Zeppelin to Herbie Hancock. "Retro pushes up the tempo in a bar. It's going to be fun," says Cozi. Get ready to rock, Japanese style.

Heading: For smooth sailing, turn left - Indian Express
Content:
The Day One of the Union health ministry's ban on smoking in public places turned out to be an anti-climax. Though Delhiites scrambled to roads and balconies to sneak in a drag, the anti-smoking squads were nowhere to be seen — Thursday being a national holiday.

Dr R P Vashisht, head of the State Tobacco Control Cell, said: "Most public spaces were shut, so we didn't challan anyone. But people will have to be careful from tomorrow."

As per the ban, smoking has been prohibited in all places to which the public have access — auditoriums, health institutions, government buildings, restaurants, courts, public transport, stadiums, railway stations, bus stops, workplaces, shopping malls, refreshment rooms, discotheques, pubs and airport lounges.

The ban will not cover open spaces but will be applicable at bus stops and shelters.

While the health department has about eight squads to implement the ban — imposed in the Capital since 1997 — the figure may be doubled.

"Given the huge task at hand, we are planning to constitute eight more squads. These will be visiting all places and people will be challaned if found flouting norms," Vashisht added.

As per the National Tobacco Control Act, anybody found smoking will be fined Rs 200.

As per the figures provided by the health department, since 1997, the squads have managed to challan 88,456 people and have raided 91,066 public spaces.

While no one was fined in 1997 despite 545 raids, the squads fined about 1,131 defaulters in 2008 after raiding 1,319 places.

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences, meanwhile, had taken the lead by declaring the entire campus a smoke-free zone a day before the ministry deadline.

The guards at the campus have reportedly been given the additional responsibility of ensuring the ban.

The president of DUSU, Nupur Sharma, too welcomed the ministry's move. "Last year, we put a ban on smoking. So the fresh ban will not make much of a difference. But now, anyone can be fined for smoking in a public place. This will make the ban more effective," she said.

Manoj Pant, the Campus Development Committee chairman in Jawaharlal Nehru University, said the university has banned smoking in the academic complex, classrooms and libraries. The committee will now put up circulars banning smoking in common rooms and games rooms.

Restaurants yet to feel the heat
While the city was divided over the blanket ban, most pubs and restaurants have switched to the no-smoking mode. "We used to have a smoking section at our cafe earlier. But from today, we have made the entire place a no-smoking zone. Smokers are however allowed to go to the terrace," said a spokesperson at Market Cafe in Khan Market.
Thursday being a dry day, most restaurants are yet to feel the pinch. "We have made the area a no-smoking zone, but there have been less people walking in. So we haven't received any complaint or felt a dip in the business yet," said a spokesperson at QBA in Connaught Place.

Heading: Road rage in Dwarka: Armyman shot at by youths - Indian Express
Content:
Cops suggest 45 intersections for slip roads, PWD to build 25

Be ready for easy traffic on the left at all major traffic intersections. The Traffic Police have suggested to the Public Works Department to construct slip roads — or side lanes at intersections — to facilitate left turns.

And for the purpose, the department had shortlisted 45 intersections across the Capital.

"Wherever there is no slip road, the left-turning traffic accumulates at the junction, unnecessarily increasing the vehicular load. As a result, the traffic is delayed," said the Joint Commissioner, Traffic, S N Shrivastava.

There are locations which have slip roads, but they are badly constructed. "A majority of slip roads do not serve any practical purpose, as they are made too close to the traffic intersection," Shrivastava said.

The Traffic Police had made a detailed presentation to the PWD to convince them of the utility of properly constructed slip roads.

The presentation included the example of the Africa Avenue Road, which has four intersections, but no slip roads. The worst-affected point on it is the intersection leading to the Outer Ring Road.

Other examples quoted by the Traffic Police include August Kranti Marg with the Outer Ring Road. There, the slip road is right on the intersection.

Of the 45 intersections, the PWD has agreed to construct slip roads on 25 which come under its jurisdiction. "We will be approaching other civic agencies for the rest," Shrivastava said.

At the turn from Aurobindo Marg to PTS Malviya Nagar, the Delhi Police have donated their own land to make space for the slip road.

"According to the suggestion of Commissioner of Police Y S Dadwal, the boundary wall of the Police Training School at Malviya Nagar will be shifted a little backwards to give space for the slip road," Shrivastava said.

The Traffic Police will be conducting a further study of other intersections for the purpose.

Heading: Once extinct in city, Kala Titar finds a home in Aravalli Park - Indian Express
Content:
An Army man was shot at by local youths in Dwarka on Wednesday night.

SP Sharma (22), posted in 13 Base Repair Depot of the Army, received a bullet in his leg and has been admitted in Army Base hospital. He is in a stable condition.

The shooting followed a heated argument with some youths, whose car had hit Sharma's bike. The incident took place around 8.30 pm when Sharma was drinking a glass of juice at a shop near the railway crossing in Dwarka, close to the Cantonment area.

According to a police officer, when Sharma asked the driver to be careful, four youths emerged from the car and began beating up the two. "They called for help but the youths called in more friends. Then one of them pulled out a countrymade pistol and fired at Sharma," the officer said.

A case under Section 307 (attempt to murder) has been registered at Dwarka. The culprits are absconding, but the police hope to catch them soon as they are all locals.

Heading: Arushi murder case: Accused Rajkumar, Krishna in Nepal - Indian Express
Content:
It took just a clutch of specially-planted grass and some habitat protection to enable a locally extinct bird, the striking Kala Titar, to make a comeback to the Capital.

With red, black and yellow markings and a distinctive "klik cheek-cheek-cheerakik" call, the Kala Titar, also called the Black Francolin, had become extinct in Delhi following habitat loss.

But in a mark of how even small changes can bring back fauna, scientists at Vasant Kunj's Aravalli Biodiversity Park, who recreated the bird's habitat, sighted it two months ago.

"The Kala Titar was once commonly found in Delhi but it was hunted out and it faced wide habitat loss. At best it may be found only in very peripheral areas of the NCR. This is also the state bird of Haryana, and Delhi falls in its natural habitat. It is a very shy bird and its presence indicates that the ecosystem is in good health," says Dr M Shah Hussain, scientist in- charge, Aravalli Biodiversity Park, which aims to rebuild the habitat of the Aravalli mountain range and Ridge.

Ironically, the Black Francolin is also facing the problem that has driven the common sparrow out of the city: lack of habitat and overuse of pesticide, which decimates insects, their staple food base.

While in both species, the adult birds eat most things — grains, berries, shoots and tubers — the soft-billed chicks have to be fed insects.

The Kala Titar is typically found near fields. It nests in bushes or bamboo thickets. "We planted special grass and created a range. We were hoping that the bird would return and it did. We expect the bird to breed here," he added. The scientists had to remove the Vilayati Kikar tree (Prosopis Juliflora) — which is a weed and not part of the native habitat.

Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit has taken up the cause of the sparrow, asking biologists to create a nature trail at her home, part of which is especially for sparrows.

Other rare birds which once frequented Delhi, are meanwhile, visiting the 692-acre Aravalli Park. The Migratory Flycatchers were last winter's guests.

Heading: Police question Soumya’s family, friends for clues; call it a ‘blind case’ - Indian Express
Content:
Rajkumar and Krishna, the two accused in the Arushi-Hemraj murder case, are in Nepal since last week.

After the CBI failed to file chargesheet in the case, they were granted bail by the Ghaziabad court on September 12.

"They have gone to meet their parents, the court had not barred them from going anywhere," said Naresh Yadav, Rajkumar's lawyer. "They are in touch with me and in keeping with the court's order, they will come if the CBI needs to question them," he said.

Both have left their addresses and phone numbers with the CBI. "The agency, if it wants, can call them or contact them through us. They are not on the run," added Yadav.

On September 9, the CBI had announced that they will not be able to file a chargesheet against the accused within 90 days. They also admitted that no material evidence against them had been recovered.

For now, the agency is pinning its hopes on conducting investigations in Nepal. A few days after Rajkumar and Krishna got bail, CBI Director Ashwani Kumar had told Newsline that a team was to be sent there. To that end, the officials said they will send a Letter Rogatory — a formal request for judicial assistance — to Nepal authorities.

Despite no evidence against Vijay Mandal, Rajkumar and Krishna, the agency has maintained that they are still the main suspects.

Heading: Court raps cops for falsely implicating detainees in chain snatching cases - Indian Express
Content:
Going through the call details of Soumya Vishwanathan, the TV journalist who was found murdered in the early hours of Tuesday, police has found that after she made a call to her father at 3.15 am, there was no call on her number —outgoing or incoming.

Top police sources said that chances were remote of somebody known being behind the killing. From the circumstances it does not seem that somebody was accompanying her in the car. Police officers say they are also probing the angle of local criminals or drunk youths shooting her from outside. At present, however, there is no headway and police officers are calling it a 'blind case'.

Police are also questioning Soumya's friends to know more about the incident and also trying to find out from family members if she had personal enemities.

"We are working on various angles, including personal enmity and road rage, but nothing concrete has come out yet," said HGS Dhaliwal, DCP, South district.

Police have also tried to recreate the incident by driving on Nelson Mandela Marg. The forensic reports are yet to arrive. The DCP also confirmed today that only one bullet was fired at Soumya on Tuesday. The tyre reportedly got punctured when the car collided with the central verge of the road. They have also questioned some local criminals in this regard but they have not been able to find out anything yet.

Soumya (25), a producer with Headlines Today news channel, was found dead with a bullet in her skull on

Tuesday. She was reportedly shot when she was headed for her C-9 Vasant Kunj home after finishing work. According to the police, there is no eyewitness to the incident. The cyclist who reportedly made a call to the police has also not been able to provide any more information about the incident.

Heading: Court hearing on land compensation rates delayed as govt fails to move protesters - Indian Express
Content:
Hunting in pairs, creeping up from behind on bikes and fleeing with jewellery and bags before one could even blink his eyes — that's the modus operandi of the Capital's army of snatchers.

Unable to rein in the menace, the Delhi Police seem to be developing their own way of keeping criticism at bay, while simultaneously improving their records by claiming to have cracked the cases.

How? Detain a few persons who are already in custody in connection with other cases, and extract confessional statements regarding their involvement in the chain snatching incidents.

For obvious reasons, the accused would refuse their Test Identification Parade (TIP), which could very well be made the ground for filing a chargesheet, amounting to prima facie evidence to make them stand trial.

Result — a pat on the back for nabbing the "snatchers" and perking up police records as far as solving the cases in the jurisdiction is concerned.

The "modus operandi" of the investigating officers of a police station, however, shocked a city court, for it meant putting innocent persons behind bars for no fault.

While the cops' act amounted to "malpractice", it also meant the wastage of precious judicial time as the case would, in all probability, end in acquittals of the falsely accused, observed Metropolitan Magistrate Sandeep Yadav.

The revelation came during a recent hearing before the magistrate when an investigating officer of DBG Road police station produced before it two accused, Monu and Suraj, in connection with a chain-snatching incident that had occurred on June 10.

According to the police, the motorcycle-borne duo snatched a gold chain from the complainant Anju, who was on foot with her husband and daughter.

The police claimed that Monu had disclosed his participation in the crime while in custody for an Arms Act case registered with a different police station, and also told the investigators that Suraj was the pillion rider. The cops added that their complicity was also indicated by their refusal to join the identification parade.

As the investigating officer placed the chargesheet in the court, M M Yadav was quick to note that in all four cases of chain snatching listed on that day, the accused persons were the same. While the chains had not been recovered in any of them, the officers pressed charges only on the basis of their refusal to participate in TIP.

"The facts of this case and the other three cases disclose the "modus operandi" employed by the police to claim that the case has been solved."

"When the investigating agency fails to arrest the real culprits and to recover the stolen items, the investigating officer extracts confessional statements from detainees accused in other cases. The accused is then produced before the court for the purpose of TIP," noted the court.

Denial of the accused to participate in TIP is made the basis for continuing detention and chargesheeting the accused for the offence. This is the "malpractice adopted by the police to solve the case which otherwise would not have been solved," it added. Noting that the "malpractice" needed to be curbed, M M Yadav then directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Delhi Police Commissioner for looking into the matter and taking necessary remedial steps.

Heading: HUDA invites applications from private companies for stalled metro project - Indian Express
Content:
While the farmers of six villages in Northwest Delhi, including Kanjhawala, have kept up their agitation demanding a further hike in the compensation rates for farmland acquired by the NCT Government for infrastructure projects, judicial work on the same continue to suffer owing to the "non-serious" response of the administration.

A large number of files required by the courts to proceed with the civil disputes still are lying at the office of the Deputy Commissioner at Kanjhawala, as scores of farmers continue to stage a sit-in protest outside the building. Officials have been unable to move the files as the protesters turn violent whenever they try entering the building, according to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of Sarswati Vihar, Ranjit Singh.

The turn of events had prompted a city court to intervene as the same had been coming in way of justice administration.

Terming the agitation as a matter of "serious concern," Additional District Judge (ADJ) Kamini Lau had urged the government over a week ago to take necessary steps to remove the protesters.

However, the hold-up has continued.

During a hearing on Friday, the SDM cut a sorry figure when asked to produce the required file, citing "the lack of assistance from senior officers of the administration and police" to bring the documents out of the DC office.

Irate, ADJ Lau noted that the government did not seem to be taking the court's directions in this regard seriously, leading to delay in the case.

"The work of this court and judicial time cannot be allowed to suffer merely because the administration finds itself incapable of handling and sorting out its affairs," said the court.

ADJ Lau then imposed a penalty of Rs 10,000 on the NCT Government for its failure to comply with the court's direction and said the money should be deposited with the Advocates Welfare Fund of the Delhi Bar Council.

A large group of protesters have been staging a protest outside the DC's office since September 11, forcing the official to carry out his work from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer at Kashmere Gate, while others are performing their duties through makeshift arrangements.

The Delhi government had acquired 1,450 acres of agricultural land on August 25, 2005 through a notification. The government revised the compensation rate from Rs 15.7 lakh to Rs 17.5 lakh per acre within four days of the notification. In a meeting last week, the rates were again revised to Rs 75 lakh per acre but the farmers continued to protest as they claim that market price of the land is now nearly Rs 3 crore per acre.

Heading: On Eid, encounter hangover looms large over Jamia Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
The multi-crore DLF metro project that has been hanging fire for over six months now might be revived with the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) inviting Expression of Interest (EOI) from private companies under an open bidding system.

HUDA has asked interested companies to apply by December 10 for the purpose and has also raised a demand of Rs 200 crore as "connectivity charges" from the company that would get the contract.

The proposed line would be an extension from the Sikanderpur Metro station till NH-8 through DLF City II, III and DLF Cybercity.

Last year, real estate major DLF had announced its plan to begin its own Metro rail as a feeder service to the Delhi-Gurgaon Metro line being constructed by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation for providing better connectivity, after the DMRC opened doors for private developers opting for Metro connectivity. Work was to begin early this year, with designs and plans for the 3.5-km long Metro stretch project ready on time. The project has, however, been grounded for months now as DLF authorities are still awaiting approval from the HUDA over line alignment.

Sources said the state government wants to impose certain conditions on the builders before work begins. Newsline had reported in March this year that the state government had been delaying the project as it wanted to claim a share in the revenue collected, citing that the enterprise would drastically raise property prices of surrounding areas, most of which is owned by DLF.

DLF had applied for the sanctions in November 2007, with a tentative plan of beginning construction by February-end or early March. The Centre had then approved the project this January and passed it on to the Haryana government. A clearance from the state government is still awaited.

"There was no profit motive behind our proposal, we just wanted to provide connectivity to all those who stay in DLF societies. The government however, seems keen on stalling the project for some reason," said C B K Rao, Adviser, DLF, and former Director (Project & Planning), DMRC. "But considering the high connectivity cost we do not think any private party would be ready to take up the project," he added.

The administration, though, is more optimistic. "We have invited EOI and are hoping that many private companies will be interested in taking forward the Light Rail Transit System metro line,"a HUDA official said. "If DLF is still interested, they would have to apply under the open bidding system now," he added.

Heading: Jamia forms legal aid committee to provide aid to arrested students - Indian Express
Content:
With children attired in their festive finery running around amid a sea of white-capped men emerging from the morning namaz, the mood in Jamia Nagar was cheerful and relaxed.

This spirit was, however, missing in the lane on which L 18, Batla House stands, which still looked like a fortress, with policemen guarding the house.

"Obviously, the mood for celebrations gets disrupted when something unpleasant occurs. But things are crawling back as we try to attain some kind of normalcy. We are going to each other's houses and celebrating Eid," said Reshma, on her way to visit her sister in the Batla House area.

The people living in the lane treated the policemen guarding L-18 to sharbat and sewai, and included them in the traditional three-hug greeting after the prayers. "It is Eid today and though the celebrations this year are subdued, we will still welcome everyone into our home on this day. God does not distinguish between anyone," said Badar Taslim, resident of L 17.

At the morning namaz at the Jamia Masjid and the Khalilullah Masjid, a number of people wore black bands on their arms as a mark of sorrow for the blasts in Delhi and the "harassment of ordinary Muslims" in the aftermath of the blasts.

Collection boxes for the Legal Aid Fund for the arrested Jamia students were also visible near the mosque gates. Mufti Ahmad Nadir Al-Quasimi of the Fecqa Academy, Zakir Nagar told Newsline that Muslims in the area felt harassed and hurt over the allegations that the area was providing shelter to terrorists.

The flavour of the day, however, was of hope and aspirations. The Dua (prayer) at the end of the namaz asked for the Almighty's blessings on the people trapped in the Bihar deluge, and concluded with a prayer for peace.

"The Muslim youth are the backbone of this country and will act as the masterminds of the technological growth, and not for spreading terror in the country," said Al-Quasimi.

"The blasts and the killings are just an attempt to break the thousand-year-old communal camaraderie between the Hindus and Muslims who have lived together for centuries and as Indians, we have the same cultural roots," said Pyare Main Azizi Abul Ilahi, of the Sufi Khanquah in Jogabai Extension at Jamia Nagar.

The man playing to the tune of "hum pyar karne wale hain koi gair nahi" on an ektara in the lane will only agree with this sentiment.

Heading: Protesting Christians hold peace march, demand CBI inquiry - Indian Express
Content:
Jamia Millia Islamia has formed a Legal Aid Committee to provide legal assistance to Zia-ur Rahman and Mohammed Shakeel, the two students of Jamia who were arrested on September 21 for their alleged involvement in the Delhi serial blasts of September 13. Heading the committee is Professor Radha Kumar, who is also Director of the Mandela Centre for Peace and Conflict Resolution, Jamia Millia Islamia. The committee has been asked to investigate the incident and submit a report to the university Vice-Chancellor.

While Prof Radha Kumar is the Convener, Prof Azra Razzack and Prof Biswajit Das have been appointed as members of the committee as per the decision taken by the Academic Council of Jamia to unequivocally condemn terrorism and communal violence.

"We will defend our constitutional, legal and moral rights while preserving the varsity's liberal secular character. It is outrageous to castigate an 80-year old university on the basis of unproved charges against a couple of students," said Prof Kumar.

Prof Kumar said her team would first find out facts. "There may be truth in the allegations made by the police, but we cannot sit on judgment on anyone. Our first step is to find out the facts, which we are working on, and it will take some time," Prof Kumar said, also terming the 'media trial' that has been taking place right from the beginning an irresponsible act.

Zia-ur-Rahman was a student of the BA Programme and Shakeel was a final year student of MA (Economics) in the university.

The Legal Aid Committee is likely to come out with its first assessment report by the end of next week.

"We cannot give a hasty turn to our investigations, like the police or media has done. While we met police officers on Wednesday, we are yet to meet the two accused students, their families and the lawyers," said Prof Kumar.

Irrespective of the truth regarding the two alleged terrorists who were arrested from Batla House in Jamia Nagar, Prof Kumar said there is a separate issue of the encounter which they need to delve into.

"We also need to know whether it was a real encounter or a random shootout. Other students of Jamia are now being questioned, which is giving a heightened communal colour to one of the three largest universities' in Delhi. Not only that, Jamia Millia Islamia is being ostracised, nobody wants to come here now," said an irate Prof Kumar.

"At a time like this, it is important that we do not help the seeds of communalism and fundamentalism proliferate by sitting on judgment on a selected few, without even questioning anybody's credentials," Prof Kumar said.

Heading: Traffic diverted from Gurgaon toll road on Eid - Indian Express
Content:
With communal violence on the rise in various parts of the country, the Christian community in Delhi held a peace march on Thursday and demanded a CBI inquiry into the incidents of violence. They also stressed on "the need for a judicial inquiry by a Supreme Court judge".

A week since they began the protest at Jantar Mantar, members of the All India Christians Council marched to Rajghat.

John Dayal, General Secretary of the All India Christians Council, said: "Thousands of people have been rendered homeless and driven away from their villages. We want the central government to interfere."

"People have lost faith in the state government," he added.

The council has demanded that Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) be banned by the government.

After the murder of VHP leader Lakshmanananda Saraswati on August 23 — for which the Maoists claimed responsibility — Sangh Parivar mobs have unleashed terror on the Christian population, driving them into forests, relief camps, or out of the district.

According to Dayal, at least 69 children have died and many women have been gangraped in the district. Close to 4,300 houses have been destroyed and about 50,000 people rendered homeless.

As per the account of the activists, the VHP cadres were not allowing the villagers from the community to return to their homes. Thousands of people were still living in the refugee camps set up by the government and other organisations.

"The VHP men have put a precondition that everyone returning to the village will have to reconvert to Hinduism," said Dayal.

The protesters stressed on the need for rehabilitating the homeless villagers.

John Das, a protester, said: "We want the people to be sent to their villages. They need to be given compensation in order to rebuild their houses."

The VHP cadres have allegedly burnt down hundreds of houses of the tribals who have converted to Christianity. "People (from VHP) have been searching for the Christians so that they can attack them," a protester said.

Heading: Kumartuli foresees a grim future - Indian Express
Content:
A minor traffic diversion was reported on the Gurgoan Expressway on Thursday morning due to a huge gathering of people near Rajiv Chowk, who had come to offer their prayers on Eid, said the Gurgaon police.

The diversion was reported between 8 am and 10.30 am when thousands of people gathered near a masjid at Rajiv Chowk. The traffic on the toll road was diverted between Subhash Chowk and Hero Honda Chowk on both sides of the toll road. A senior officer of the Gurgaon traffic police said since the influx of vehicles was comparatively lower due to it being a national holiday, there was no major inconvenience caused. However, neither the police nor the highway authorities issued any advisory in advance to inform people.

Heading: In this Dum Dum pandal, folklores have come to life - Indian Express
Content:
As the festive season catches up and the city lights up for one more Durga Puja, there are some pandals, which have decided to seize the day to spread a word of wisdom.

Celebrating their 77th year, Kumartuli Sarbojanin Durgotsav Committee has decided to give a different look to their pandal.

The pandal, which usually sees a footfall of 4-5 lakh people per day, will be stressing on the importance of saving the environment.

"During the Pujas, huge crowds assemble together, so it is the best time to spread awareness. While our pandal will have models of human skeletons inside, the idols will have a completely different look," said Debashish Bhattacharya, convenor of the committee.

The committee has drawn inspiration from a church in Portugal, which showcases human skeletons to reflect what the future of mankind might be unless environmental destruction is checked.

Last year, the committee had Hirok Rajar Desh's Jantar Mantar concept as their theme through which they tried to educate people about class disparity.

"We have done research only after which we decided to do a replica of a church in Portugal, which has skeletons spelling doomsday. We will tell visitors about how water should not be wasted, trees should not be felled and pollution should be curbed. If these precautions are not taken, we will show what might happen to humans in the long run," said secretary Bacchu Bhattacharya.

The pandal that once had Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose as the president of their committee, will have models of lanterns, poles, chandelliers made up of 3,500 skulls and bones created out of thermocol and fibreglass.

Taking a different line from the conventional concept of Durga, the committee has decided not to include mythological enemy, Ashur.

So instead of Durga defeating Ashur, she will be seen with folded hands. Instead of 10 hands each holding a weapon, all her hands will carry flowers while one will hold onto little Ganesha.

Kartik will hold onto his mother's sari.

"With the recent blasts all over the country, we decided it was high time that people realised that there is no point in indulging in violence. That is why Durga will not be fighting Asur but pleading to mankind to promote peace," said Debashish Bhattacharya. Durga's children will be seen as much smaller than the usual age, reflecting innocence.

Heading: Women snatchers send alarm bells ringing before Puja - Indian Express
Content:
It doesn't take a poet's imagination to picture the completed Dum Dum Park Tarun Sangha pandal. Thousands of diyas floating on a water body, a makeshift ghat and quaint little huts along the way — the organisers of this north Kolkata pandal sure do know how to make use of the ample space at their disposal.

"The pond adds to the beauty of the pandal and it will be foolish not to make use of it," said Rabin Ganguly of the Dum Dum Park Tarun Sangha organising committee.

But this year, the committee members are depending on something more than the area's natural advantages to lure the crowds.

Colourful Midnapore diwali dolls are the focus of this year's pujo. "This used to be one of the most popular traditional art forms of the state. But today it has taken a back seat due to modernisation," said artist Prasanta Pal, who conceptualised this year's pujo theme for the pandal.

A group of 40 artisans from the east Midnapore district of Norghat have stationed themselves at the pandal to realise Pal's vision.

"The idea is to project this art form in the best possible manner. These dolls depict mythological figures in a unique way, which will capture the imagination of many visitors," added Pal.

A typical Midnapore diwali doll is a clay figure depicting pantheons in their quintessential poses — Maa Ganga perched on a crocodile, Maa Manasa astride a hooded cobra. "These figures represent deities of the villages. There are folklores attached to them," said Pal.

Artisan Bhim Chandra Bera of Norghat, whose

family has been associated with the art for generations, said: "Snakes are a menace in our village. This is why Maa Manasa is our local deity. We worship her so that she protects us from snakebites," he said before slapping a coat of paint on a clay model.

Each of these models, around a feet and a half tall, take about half a day to make. "We first make a model out of straw, then coat it with clay. Then it is dried and painted after which it is lacquered," says Bera.

These dolls, which are popularly used as diyas during diwali, will also light up the pandal. "A hundred of these diyas will be lit during the pujas," he said.

The idol of Durga, which is in traditional ekchala format, will have a distinctly rustic look.

Heading: Unable to find way, CPM considers abolition of NCTE - Indian Express
Content:
The recent arrest of two women snatchers in Dakshineshwar has sent alarm bells ringing before the Durga Puja. According to police sources, a majority of the women snatchers who operate in and around the city during Pujas are from South Indian states. 

"Nearly 99.9 per cent women snatchers are from states like Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. In fact, their network operates from Bandel. The women usually wear expensive saris and gold jewellery and mingle with the devotees," a police officer told The Indian Express.

Most of them operate on Mahalaya and Astami at places like Kalighat, Dakhsineshwar. Working in three or four-member groups, they pass along stolen goods to their accomplices. Even if they are nabbed, the stolen articles are seldom found on them.

In contrast to to nearly 30 cases of snatching reported before Pujas last year, there were only three cases during the Pujas.

"These women usually target shoppers. Apart from wallets and gold jewellery, they also steal clothes. Women are far more attentive if they stand next to men, but in a women's queue they feel comfortable, which makes them easy targets," said the source.

Deputy Commissioner (Detective Department) Javed Shamim confirmed that there were a lot of women gangs who come from other cities. "The police are becoming increasingly vigilant about these gangs. This year, due to the bomb scare, the police are being extra vigilant," Shamim said.

Samir Gupta, Officer In-charge of the New Market police station, confirmed that this year no cases of snatching were reported in his area so far.  "But the police are extra cautious, and there are a lot more policemen on the road to ensure safety," he said.

Heading: KMC ignores mapping of areas prone to diseases - Indian Express
Content:
Undecided on the issue of Primary Teacher Training Institutes (PTTIs) in the state, senior leaders of the CPM are now considering the abolition of the Central regulatory body — National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE).

On October 1, the Calcutta High Court had derecognised 122 PTTIs in the state and held that the NCTE recognition was necessary

for them. The court also directed that the fees of the students who could not take the examination would have to be returned.

"I cannot say what step the government should take on this issue, but there seems no other way but to abolish the NCTE," said Kanti Biswas, former school education minister and member of the CPM committee on education.

"In August 2007, I met Minister for Human Resource and Development Arjun Singh and discussed about the abolition of the NCTE. The decision awaits the final nod of the Cabinet," Biswas said.

"The government amended the West Bengal Board of Primary Education Act which was ratified by the Centre and the PTTIs not recognised by the NCTE were thus allowed to run," said the former minister, hinting that the state government has not done anything wrong by allowing the PTTIs to run.

School Education Minister Partha De said the government would take a final decision once the School Education Department received a copy of the judgment.

"We demand the government should think about an out-of-court settlement on the issue," said Ashok Rudra, leader of the West Bengal Primary Teachers' Training Institute's Students Union. The union is going to organise a protest rally on October 3 on the issue. The students will also rope in the support of political parties like the Trinamool Congress.

A number of teachers' organisations have also voiced their support for the PTTIs. "The people who committed the mistake by permitting the PTTIs to run without the NCTE approval were not punished and the students will have to pay the price," said Bhimsen Biswal, secretary of West Bengal Primary Teachers' Association.

Heading: For 21 months, primary teachers’ provident funds stay locked - Indian Express
Content:
Despite being advised to carry out entomological mapping of areas vulnerable to vector-borne diseases by the state health department and the School of Tropical Medicine (STM), the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has done very little in this regard.

According to a senior health official, the state health department and STM have asked the civic body since 2005 to prepare a map identifying the areas prone to vector-borne diseases in the city but to no avail.

"This (the mapping) will neither incur a huge cost nor involve a large manpower. It can be easily done as most of the field workers are quite familiar with the breeding zones and vector-prone areas. The mapping would have ensured proper surveillance of the city," said the official.

According to the records of KMC health officials, some boroughs, including borough II, IV, V, VI, VIII, IX and X, are vector-prone zones.

"The KMC should identify the vulnerable wards so that it can carry out an active surveillance before the breeding season begins. Once there is an outbreak it cannot be controlled," said Dr Amiya Hati, former director, STM.

"There are many universities — Jadavpur, Calcutta and Vidyasagar — which carry out geographical and entomological mapping free of cost. Several proposals have been sent to the civic body but they have not been considered by it," Dr Hati said.

The KMC health officials blame the delay in carrying out the surveillance work on the lackadaisical attitude of the senior health officials.

Heading: Leather complex turns threat to environment - Indian Express
Content:
About 500 retired teachers of the primary schools in Kolkata are waiting for their provident fund for the last 21 months. Another 6,000 teachers working in about 1,200 primary schools in the city have not been able to draw a single penny from their provident funds during the same period. The primary school teachers, whose salary is around Rs 5,000 per month, cannot access their own provident fund because of the procedural delays caused by the Kolkata district primary education council.

Chittatosh Ghosh, a 54-year-old primary teacher of Deshbandhu High School, applied for a loan of Rs 1 lakh for a bypass surgery from his provident fund, but his request was turned down. "I had to borrow money from other sources," said Ghosh.

Before March 2000, the deduction of the provident fund from the salary of the primary teachers was deposited in the account of the District Inspector (DI) of schools. After this, a rule was made that the money was to be deposited in the account of the Kolkata primary education council. Thousands of teachers in the state did not receive their PF because of the procedural delay in the transfer of funds from the DI's account to that of the district primary education council.

To further complicate matters, the pay & accounts office of the government made an objection to the existence of different heads for the deposition of the provident fund and subsequently the payment to the teachers was stopped since January 2007.

Chairman of the Kolkata district primary education council, Kartik Chandra Manna, admitted there has been a problem and some teachers could not get a loan from their PF or the entire amount. "The council will start distributing the funds from November this year. In the presence of various teachers' organisations the DI has handed its share but the verification is yet to be done," he said.

Heading: Buddha ready for a last try - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta Leather Complex at Bantala in east Kolkata is in a mess as the common effluent treatment plant (CETP) at the complex is not functioning properly and the toxic waste is overflowing into adjoining areas, creating environmental hazards.

A portion of the 1,100-acre complex was earmarked as a special economic zone (SEZ) for information technology (IT) companies. But the pollution caused by the chemical effluent is affecting the construction activities taken up by many of these companies.

"The condition in the complex is so precarious that IT companies have started complaining against the tannery units. We have recently received a complaint from Cognizant Technology Solutions," said Jagmohan Dalmiya, chairman of ML Dalmiya & Co Ltd, who was given the project under the Built-Operate-Transfer model.

The state IT Department has also started feeling the heat. "Several units have complained about the pollution. We have forwarded the matter to the Commerce and Industries Department," IT Minister Debesh Das said.

According to the treatment plant officials, delay in constructing the CETP, which is an essential part of the complex, is behind the problem.

"The network of the pipelines connecting all tanneries to the treatment plant is faulty. At various places the pipelines are choked. We have asked the government to work on the system and to construct two more modules, but nothing has been done so far," said Arnab Jha, member of the CLC Tannery Association, which maintains the CETP.

Three years have passed since the Bantala complex was inaugurated. But the state has completed only four modules of the CETP, although the design of the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation had recommended that at least six modules are required for the effluent plant to treat the chemical waste.

Since the existing four modules do no function properly, the pollution caused by the untreated waste affects the complex and its environment.

However, the Commerce and Industries Department denies that the government is responsible for the construction of the remaining two modules. "According to the deal between the government and the developer, the latter was assigned to construct it," said Mousumi Guha Roy, special officer of the department. Dalmiya, however, said setting up of the CETP was never his responsibility. 

Meanwhile, M L Meena, principal secretary of the Environment Department, said: "We are not concerned about the IT complex as it was set up without the environmental clearance."

Heading: On Eid, city comes together against terrorism - Indian Express
Content:
In a make or break situation, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee is all set to request the chairman of Tata Motors — perhaps for the last time — to resume work at the Nano plant in Singur. Bhattacharjee is scheduled to meet Ratan Tata on Friday in Kolkata.

Work had been suspended at the factory August 29 onwards after a dharna was staged outside the plant by the Opposition.

The meeting between the two is likely to be held at the Writers' Buildings and the stakes involved for both are high, said senior government officials. The fate of the plant is to be decided in this crucial meet, which will also be attended by Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen, and other senior government officials.

Though the state government has assured the Tatas that it will provide all administrative help to them to ensure protection, the latter has made it clear that they will not run the factory under police protection.

While former captain of the Indian cricket team Sourav Ganguly has also written to Ratan Tata requesting him to resume work at the plant, Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi said he still had hopes for a way out. "Like the Prime Minister I am also hopeful of a solution for Singur. People of West Bengal desire and deserve a solution," the Governor said at Gandhighat at Barrackpore on Thursday, where he went to offer homage to Mahatma Gandhi.

Last week, the state Cabinet issued a statement requesting the Tatas not to shift their plant. It also requested the Opposition to accept the compensation package announced by the government.

A section of the CPM leadership is also peeved at Tata's threat. CPM parliamentarian Hannan Mollah said: "How can they leave after going so far? It will be an injustice

to us."

According to the package, the government is willing to arrange for 70 acres of land from within the project area and an additional 50 per cent of the award money has been offered to all the dispossessed farmers. In addition, the government will arrange for rehabilitation of these farmers.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, however, continues to stick to her demand of returning 300 acres of land from within the project area and 100 acres from outside the project.

State government officials indicated that with all options exhausted, the chief minister will be taking a tough stand should there be any more disruptions to functioning of the plant. Due to violent protests by Trinamool-led Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee and the dharna work at the site had to be suspended.

"The government so far had adopted a soft approach while dealing with the protestors. The Durgapur Expressway was blocked for 20 days, employees working at the plant had been beaten up. The administration has shown slackness. Now the government will act tough. And that is what the chief minister is going to tell the Tatas," a senior minister told The Indian Express.

CII chief mentor Tarun Das on the singur imbroglio:
"The situation in Singur is unfortunate and the solution to the present stand-off lies with Ms Mamata Banerjee... The Nano is a unique project and the Tatas have to be credited with its right to design its plant. Any forced change to its plan of implementation will delay the launch of the Nano and also impact the cost, which will disappoint thousands of people across the country aspiring to own a safe four wheel personal transportation. Presently, the ideas for the implementation of the project is being offered by individuals who have no experience in developing an automobile manufacturing plant and definitely no perspective on a unique product like the Nano... The future of the state lies in developing a strong manufacturing sector creating several jobs for the people of the state."
— ENS

Heading: Rizwanur case: Uncle ready to accept verdict if found guilty - Indian Express
Content:
Eid-ul-fitr was celebrated throughout the state with much pomp and vigour on Thursday.

Marking the end of the holy month of Ramzan, Eid-ul-Fitr saw a huge congregation thronging the city from various parts of the state. The main congregation was, however, held at Red Road, where people offered namaz. Prayers were also offered at the Nakhoda Masjid, Park Circus and Garden Reach areas of the city.

People were seen exchanging sweets and greetings with undaunted enthusiasm. "This year, our message to the people was curbing terrorism. We asked our Muslim and Hindu brothers to come together and fight the dreaded menace that has spread across the country. Apart from terrorism, we also asked the people to fight against injustice," said Maulana Fazlur Rahman of Imam Idain.

Tight security arrangements were made throughout the city today. According to the police, security was beefed up at mosques and other vulnerable areas of the city to avoid any untoward incident.

Heading: Midnapore violence: Three policemen injured by hawkers - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the CBI appended a "suicide note" by Rizwanur Rehman to the chargesheets against the seven accused naming, among others, his uncle Saidur Rehman as being responsible for his death, Saidur said on Thursday that he would accept the verdict of the court if it found him guilty.

"There have been allegations against me in the past that I accepted a sum of Rs 21,000 from Ashok Todi for passing on information about Rizwanur and Priyanka Todi. I have been questioned by the CBI, and if they did not chargesheet me I suppose it was because they could not find any wrongdoing on my part. I am a Trinamool worker and I run an NGO," Saidur said.

The suicide note names Saidur and TMC MLA Javed Ahmed Khan as being "morally responsible" for his death, among others.

Khan, however, said the inclusion of his name in the suicide note was an "afterthought" by the government, which he claimed is bent on protecting the police officers and the Todi family. "Why was the note not included in the initial report submitted to the Calcutta High Court by the CBI? I met Rizwanur's family before his death. Till date they have not accused me of any wrongdoing."

Khan, who participated in a rally taken out by Mamata Banerjee on Thursday in Rizwanur's area on the occasion of Eid, said: "I will not comment on whether the suicide note is true or fabricated, but there seems to be a political conspiracy behind the inclusion of my name."

"Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and his party have not come forward to help Rizwanur's family. Since the beginning it is the TMC that has been fighting for justice on their behalf. And lastly, there is no question of a suicide note as we believe it to be a cold-blooded murder," Khan added.

Rizwanur's brother Rukbanur defended Khan, saying the MLA had visited to inquire after them when news of his brother's inter-community marriage with Priyanka was making waves in their locality. "What I find astonishing is that Rizwanur named our uncle and Khan as being responsible for his death, while forgiving the Todis. Of course, we still hold that it was no suicide but a pre-planned murder."

Heading: Barriers crumble as city comes together to celebrate Eid - Indian Express
Content:
Three policemen were injured and two police vans were set on fire by hawkers protesting against their eviction in Midnapore town on Thursday.

West Midnapore SP Rajesh Singh said the hawkers were given prior notice to clear the pavements before Durga Puja.

"The district administration and the civic body had already intimated the hawkers about the eviction, but they refused to abide by the notice. The police had to carry out a drive to evict them. The hawkers clashed with the police and resorted to stone pelting. They set two of our vehicles on fire. Twelve hawkers have been arrested in this connection," Singh said.

Sources said the mood in Midnapore town was still tense and Rapid Action Force was deployed to prevent attacks by the hawkers. According to police, the protesters attacked the outer walls of the district magistrate and SP's bungalows, besides torching 12 shops in the vicinity on Thursday.

Heading: Thief arrested within 12 hours of looting shop - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of the widespread violence that marked the past month, the city ushered in another Eid, with enough optimism to fight away any dampened spirits that may still have been lurking.

"This is a special day for us. The month that comes before is supposed to be an auspicious and happy one, but it has not been so. But Eid is still a day to be happy," says Abdul Qadri, a shopkeeper at Mohammed Ali Road.

While the community has had their share of troubles with the recent blasts and their aftermath, the mood still remains upbeat as many believe that the festival is a time to celebrate, not mull over the past. "I don't think this Eid will be any different because of the incidents of the past few months. I have friends here who will still celebrate the way they used to," says a Hindu taxi driver who drives a taxi owned by a Muslim. "This is a time to be happy. It's not that we don't remember what has happened in the past month, it's just that we must focus on the good," says another shopkeeper, requesting anonymity. "Whoever has done these things is wrong. This is all because of politics and one party trying to outdo the other," he adds. "Of course we are saddened by whatever has happened in the past few weeks. It should never have taken place. We have no idea what will happen at any time, but Eid is not the time to worry, but to celebrate," says another shopkeeper, Ali Jalan. "This is a day to make amends, and to correct past mistakes, and we will celebrate Eid in that spirit", says Qadri.

Heading: Thane riot victim spends Eid alone in burnt home - Indian Express
Content:
The leaders of Europe's four biggest economies - Britain, France, Germany and Italy - will meet Saturday, Paris announced, amid sharp divisions over how to respond to the global financial crisis.

President Nicolas Sarkozy's office said the summit would help European members of the Group of Seven developed nations

coordinate positions before next week's meeting of their finance ministers in Washington, US.

But the build-up to the Paris talks has already revealed a split between European powers on how to protect the banking sector, with Germany dismissing calls for a joint European fund to bail out failing banks.

Sarkozy told reporters that France had not suggested creating such a 300-billion-euro fund and the finance ministry insisted publicly that neither the figure nor the idea had come from them.

Nevertheless, a European official in Paris confirmed that France had not ruled out a large-scale bail-out, despite opposition from Britain and Germany. "London and Berlin are oposed to a Paulson-type plan and prefer a case-by-case approach," he said. "France thinks you should not exclude the idea, which could be useful," he added.

Dutch Prime Minister Jan Peter Balkenende also denied reports that his government was proposing a single Europe-wide bailout fund. Many media commentators have blamed France for the confusion, suggesting Sarkozy was so keen to take credit for leading Europe's response to the crisis that he forged ahead with the summit plans without consulting his partners first. Sarkozy has invited Brown, Germany's Chancellor Angela Merkel and Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to Paris.

European Commission president Jose Manuel Barroso, European Central Bank chief Jean-Claude Trichet and the head of the eurogroup finance ministers' committee, Jean-Claude Juncker, will also attend. Paris has been keen to develop a European response to the crisis, which began when US banks found themselves dangerously exposed to bad debt and then spread round the world as credit markets choked up.

Heading: Riding on new schemes, BEST hopes to cut losses - Indian Express
Content:
Maqdoom Ali Bangi (47) had made purchases in advance for Eid, and the family of nine was looking forward to wearing the new clothes. However, today he spent the day sifting through what remains of his charred home at Rabodi in Thane after the riots on Monday evening. Tension over a Navratri pandal had led to the violence.

Bangi has been living in Bangi Chawl, adjacent to the Rabodi police station, for the last 36 years and this is the first time he says his family isn't together, at home, for Eid. The women have been shifted to an uncle's house while the children are putting up at Bangi's sister's place.

All his belongings were lost in the fire set by rioteers and when one of the cooking gas cylinders burst, the roof was ripped open. The clothes that Bangi, a tailor by profession, is wearing were donated by local corporator Najib Mulla. "Only my mother's railway pension card, that too partially burnt, was all I could get from house," says Bangi.

Also gone are proofs of identity and other documentation, at a time when these things have acquired a life of their own. However, Bangi says he isn't worried about the papers as these can be reproduced. What he laments more is that even the books and school certificates of his daughter Nidha, a Class XII student, were burnt. "She was inconsolable," says Bangi.

As soon as it is possible, he plans to return and start rebuilding his house. "Though it will take a long time to get the house back to the state in which we had abandoned it, at least we can start living on our own with some repairs," he says.

Bangi admits they will feel unsafe, but adds he has few options. "Where would I go?" he says, eyes welling up. "This is the place I was born in. This is where I will die."

Heading: Documentary on math genius Ramanujan to hit screen - Indian Express
Content:
Gone are the days when the Brihanmumbai Electric and Supply Transport (BEST), the city's transport arm, was a loss-making venture. The BEST this year is expecting to cut down its losses. According to BEST chairman Uttam Khobragade, while it incurred a loss of Rs 371.81 crore in 2007-08, BEST is hoping to restrict its losses to Rs 121 crore for the financial year 2008-2009.

BEST's yearly earning during 2007-2008 was Rs 854.89 crore which is expected to cross Rs 1023.07 crore in 2008-2009. But the expenditure for the year 2008-2009 has seen an increase. The BEST spent Rs 1226.70 crore in 2007-2008, in contrast to 2008-2009 in which it has spent Rs 1273.66 crore. However Khobragade justified the increase in expenditure claiming that over 80 crore has been spent on the gratuity and Voluntary Retirement Service scheme which could not be included in the earlier budget.

As per the budget submitted by the Khobaragde, BEST is likely to earn revenue of Rs 1085.03 crore in the year 2009-2010. More avenues for revenue earning are being explored. "Since the last decade, the number of BEST buses has remained constant at 3400. But by March 2009, we plan to take the figure to 4000 buses", said Khobaragde. He added that various schemes have been introduced to attract more passengers such as the reduction of the rates in spite of the fuel price hike, which have worked well.

Last year BEST also introduced new Air-conditioned (AC) buses on the Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) routes which over a period of time got a good response from the people. The BEST earned Rs 64.33 crore in 2007-2008, but the revenue through other incomes like advertisements rose up to Rs 112.12 crore. It also started providing its buses to schools and corporate companies- currently 41 schools and 12 corporate companies ply BEST buses.

Heading: Man killed, wife & son injured in mishap - Indian Express
Content:
How's it that a boy from a lower-middle class family in a small town in Tamil Nadu, with no formal training in Mathematics went on to become one of the world's most brilliant mathematicians? An upcoming documentary on the life of Srinivasa Ramanujan, one of India's most revered mathematicians, can give answer to this question. Titled 'God, Zero and Infinity' and filmed at Kumbakonam, Ramanujan's hometown in Tamil Nadu, among other places, the documentary will give an insight into his life. Born in 1887, Ramanujan went on to compile new formulae and identities that made the rest of the world to sit up and take notice. Though he met an untimely end in 1920, he had managed to make a significant, if not a vast contribution to the field of Mathematics, making a mark in India, and at Trinity College, Cambridge, England, where he worked with mathematician G H Hardy.

With Tom Alter as the narrator, the documentary also includes interviews of Ramanujan's adopted son, and other famous mathematicians, including President of the American Mathematics Society George Andrews. Beginning with his birth at his home on Sarangapani Street, Kumbakonam, the documentary revolves around Ramanujan's stint at Trinity College. Parts of the documentary have also been shot at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in the city.

"Every mathematician we have met was thrilled to know that we were making a film on Ramanujan. When we started, it was a small project, but after we completed the project, it was beyond our expectations," says Santosh Dhavala, director of the movie. The documentary also includes interview with A P J Abdul Kalam, who was reportedly delighted on hearing that there would be a film on Ramanujan's life.

Among Ramanujan's contributions to Mathematics, the documentary focuses on composite functions, Rodger-Ramanujan identities and the Ramanujan theta function. The documentary will be available on DVDs and CDs and screend at educational institutions. "Since Ramanujan had died in 1920, we had to make to do with just four photographs of him and this was the most difficult situatuion while we were making the film," says Dhavala.

Ramanujan's life, however, has been the topic of a few other endeavours in the past. In 2006, British actor turned director Stephen Fry and Indian Director Dev Benegal had announced the making of a film on Ramanujan's complex relationship with Hardy and in 1991, a book by Robert Kanigel called 'The Man Who Knew Infinity: A Life of the Genius Ramanujan' was published.

Heading: Smoking ban: Day One of mixed emotions and missing enforcers - Indian Express
Content:
A fifty-year-old man was killed and his wife and son were seriously injured at Vikhroli (East) on Thursday morning after a dumper rammed a Buddha Vihar where the family was sitting. The police arrested the driver of the vehicle.

The accident took place at 9.30 in the morning, barely a few minutes after the namaz at Tagorenagar's Babasaheb Ambedkar slum in Vikhroli.

The victim, Mahadeo Wakude, his wife Lilabai and their 21-year-old son Manohar were engrossed in a chat at the entrance of the Malgandh Buddha Vihar when a yellow dumper which was parked a few metres away came speeding and collided into an autorickshaw before hitting the structure. While Wakude came underneath the vehicle and succumbed to his chest injury at the spot, Manohar's foot was crushed and Lilabai suffered injuries on her hip and back.

"I came out to fill water when I saw the dumper moving towards the houses. But the driver lost control and instead of maneuvering the vehicle towards the road, he accelerated and came straight towards the Vihar. In a split of second, I heard a roar of a wall collapse followed by screams," recalled 20-year-old Nagina Rambhau Sonwane, whose house is located next to the Vihar.

The police, who were on duty to keep a watch on Eid celebrations in the area, rushed to spot along with residents and arrested the driver.

"After the namaz, driver Jitlal Shobharam was trying to start the vehicle when he lost control and pressed the accelerator," said Senior Police Inspector H R A Ansari from Ghatkopar police station.

Heading: After Middle Vaitarna, city to tap into Pinjal project - Indian Express
Content:
Hotels, restaurants put up 'no smoking' signs; cops clueless on their role, BMC says will implement today

As the clock inched towards midnight on Wednesday night, the manager at one of the city's most famous pubs in Bandra, Toto's Garage, began requesting patrons to stub their cigarettes — the law banning smoking would come into effect at midnight. For smokers and non-smokers, it was akin to witnessing history as the crowd then proceeded to cheer loudly and shout: "Ten, nine..." As the countdown continued, cigarettes were puffed at furiously, before a collective stubbing out amid cheers, as well as boos, at the stroke of midnight.

Business could be affected, the management said, since patrons usually enjoy a smoke with their drink.

The mood on Day One of the smoking ban at the country's public places and workplaces was somewhat the same, some welcoming a forced chance to kick the butt, others grumbling at the extra effort that now goes into planning a cigarette break.

While most hotels and restaurants sported signboards, smokers puffed on the streets outside. The law enforcers took it lightly on the first day, with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation staffers mostly unavailable and the police busy with bandobast duty, but big joints and hotels took it upon themselves to impose the ban. The fact that the Thursday was also a dry day probably helped.

South Mumbai's Café Mondegar and Leopold's Café where glimpses of Mumbai's bohemian are to be seen also obliged to the latest order. Mondegar was closed on account of Gandhi Jayanti being a dry day, while the air at Leopold's Café was free of all traces of smoke. Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss's order — enlarged and laminated — was stuck on the entrance wall. "Till now nobody has lit a cigarette," said Eric Anthony, the manager. "We'll implement the ban across the restaurant."

The ban would not have any effect on overall business, he added. "Everything is the same and I don't see any fall in business," he said.

At big hotels too, it was the same story. The lobby at the Trident Hotel was minus all its ashtrays, all replaced by 'no smoking' signs.

However, the ban enforcers were less proactive. Executive Health Officer of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said: "Thursday being a public holiday, all sanitary officers are off duty. We will start implementing the ban on Friday in hotels and restaurants."

Police officials were mostly clueless about their role too. Senior Police Inspector Surendra Jaiswal from the Kandivali police station said: "My office has not received any kind of circular about the ban on smoking in public." ACP Dilip Suryavanshi from the DN Nagar division said his office had not received any communication about enforcing the ban either.

The paan shop owner outside Toto's perhaps summed it succinctly: "Whoever has to smoke will come outside and smoke. How much can you stop somebody if he really wants to?"

Meanwhile, Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss stated his next big wish: To see a ban on all tobacco products.

Heading: New system to track air traffic, predict landing delays - Indian Express
Content:
Water supply:Yield reports in, project has a better potential, so Gargai may be taken up later

After experiencing a delay of more than a decade in implementing the Middle Vaitarna water project, which would provide 455 million litres a day (mld) of additional water to Mumbaiites, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is now putting the Gargai and Pinjal water supply projects on the fast-track. Having received the "yield reports" for both projects, the civic administration is now planning to go ahead with the Pinjal dam project first and complete it before the scheduled deadline.

Contrary to the earlier estimation by the Chitale Committee in the late 1980s, the yield study report submitted by consultant Mott McDonald to the BMC this week has identified that Gargai project would yield 227 mld and Pinjal 1475 mld.

The original plan had been to complete the Middle Vaitarna project, and then Gargai by 2020 and Pinjal later by 2025. However, after getting a different picture on the source augmentation, the civic administration is planning to start work on the Pinjal project first. Civic officials pointed out that Pinjal will be able to provide more water than Gargai project. "Though the combined water supply to Mumbai will be the same, we may have to go for Pinjal project first. We may also consider going for both Gargai and Pinjal projects simultaneously," said a senior civic official.

While the civic administration had earlier estimated that Gargai would yield 455 mld and Pinjal 1210 mld, it is also having second thoughts about constructing the Gargai dam. "The water yield is very low and it will be too costly to build a dam for Gargai. We would have to go for a weir and divert some water from Pinjal into it," the official added.

The yield report is the first step which would give an idea of how much water to expect from the dam projects. A feasibility report (expected by December) and later a Detailed Project Report will follow. Environmental clearances and funding will be the next stages.

The dam across Gargai — a tributary of Pinjal river in the Thane region — is proposed to come at Ogade, about 120 km from Mumbai, while the Pinjal dam was proposed near Andheri, about 130 km from the city. Of the 1475 mld water from Pinjal, the BMC will be entitled to a share of 868 mld of water while the remaining will be used by the state government for irrigation purpose and for suburban areas of Thane district (Virar-Vasai region).

After getting the yield study report, the civic administration is now looking for funding. Although the Japan Bank for International Co-operation was approached last year, no reply has been received yet. "It is too early to say about the funding pattern, but since Central funding through JNNURM will not be available till these projects are undertaken, we may have to look for outside funds or the World Bank," an official said.

Taking into account the increasing demand for supply of water in the city — the current shortage amounts to 1,000 mld —- civic officials said there is a need to undertake either of the two projects immediately after the completion of Middle Vaitarna project in 2011.

Heading: Event manager stabbed to death - Indian Express
Content:
Deadline December 2010; talks on with US aviation agency

Although air traffic at India's busiest airports — Mumbai and Delhi — has come down considerably because of the current slump in the aviation industry, aircraft still have to wait for their turn to land, forcing them to circle the airport. But soon this wait could be avoided if the national air traffic flow management system (ATFM) — a system that would be capable of tracking traffic at airports across the country and analyse expected delays for aircraft landing — is implemented, for which the target date has been set for December, 2010.

"At present talks between AAI and the United States' Federal Aviation Authority (FAA), with which the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MCA) is in a collaboration, to implement the system are in a nascent stage," a Mumbai airport official, on condition of anonymity, told Newsline. According to officials at Mumbai airport, which currently handles about 650 flight movements a day, such a system would be able to gauge the exact delay that an aircraft taking off from another airport will face when it lands at the destination airport.
