Heading: Biden benefited from Senatorial perks - Indian Express
Content:
Democrat Barack Obama and Republican John McCain stayed on the high road on Wednesday, eschewing direct attacks on each other and talking up the financial rescue legislation before returning to Washington to cast their votes for the Senate version of the bill.

With several new polls showing Obama building a lead over McCain, the Illinois senator rallied an estimated 15,000 supporters who filled the streets of this town on the Mississippi River.

Obama assured them he was doing whatever he could to help pass the $700-billion bailout "to safeguard the American economy".

The Senate endorsed the $700 billion economic bailout plan on Wednesday, leaving backers optimistic that the easy approval would lead to House acceptance by Friday and end the legislative uncertainty that has rocked the markets.

"Even with all these taxpayer protections, this plan is not perfect. Democrats and Republicans in Congress have legitimate concerns about it; I know many Americans share those concerns," Obama said. "But it is clear that this is what we must do right now to prevent a crisis from turning into a catastrophe."

Campaigning in Independence, Missouri, McCain hailed Democrats and Republicans working together to craft a federal assistance package, and said such bipartisanship should occur more frequently.

"Crises often have a way of revealing our better selves, of showing what we're made of and how much we can achieve when we're put to the test," the Arizona senator said, speaking to about 100 supporters at the Harry S Truman Presidential Library and Museum. "It should not require extreme emergencies, when the future of our entire economy is on the line, to bring out the best of us... We are supposed to do that even in the calmest of times."

Several new polls showed that Obama had raised his standing after Friday's presidential debate.

According to a poll conducted by Quinnipiac University, Obama leads McCain in three key states: Ohio, Florida and Pennsylvania.

Combined, those states are worth 68 of the 270 electoral votes needed for victory on November 4, 32 days from now.

Obama's growing popularity was also cited by the Pew Research Center for the People & the Press.

Its poll showed that Obama moved to a 49 per cent to 42 per cent advantage among registered voters after the debate.

The race was virtually even in early August and mid-September.

Now: Obama UP

The latest Gallup Poll Daily tracking update of registered voters finds Barack Obama at 48%, and John McCain at 44%

Jab they Met

John McCain and Barack Obama meet on Tuesday for the second of their three debates. Their last four meetings, over the past three weeks, have produced cold vibes, sparks and some comradeship. Here's what happened

September 11, New York SHARED EMOTIONS

They met at ground zero in an air freed from politics and infused with memory, to honour the dead of America's blackest day. They shook hands, patted each other on the back, and walked down a long ramp chatting. After laying flowers at the memorial standing side by side, they shook hands again, half-hugged and patted each other on the back.

September 25, Washington STRONG, SILENT

They met at the invitation of President George W Bush, in an unprecedented emergency meeting on the economy with the top political leadership. Obama sought clarifications on Bush's planned intervention; McCain, despite his well-publicized concern over the crisis, was, by all accounts, largely silent. There were no reports of any one-on-ones.

September 26, Mississippi GLOVES OFF

During the first presidential debate, they differed on ways to tackle the financial crisis, and clashed fiercely on Iran and Afghanistan. Obama was calmer, more accommodative: looking McCain in the eye, calling him 'John' and conceding where McCain had a point. McCain did none of these, was irritable, and appeared to talk down to Obama.

October 1, Washington FROSTY BITES

They were at the Capitol for the Senate vote on the bailout bill, and Obama made the move to walk across to the Republican side to shake McCain's hand. The response was chilly: McCain barely pivoted his body as he took Obama's hand. The handshake lasted just a moment; eye contact was just as brief.

Heading: Some major issues gone unaddressed - Indian Express
Content:
For the millions of voters getting to know him, Senator Joseph R Biden Jr, the Democratic vice-presidential candidate, portrays himself at times as an average guy who takes the train to work, frets about money and basically has led a middle-class life.

"Ladies and gentlemen, your kitchen table is like mine," Biden said when Barack Obama introduced him as his running mate. "You sit there at night after you put the kids to bed and you talk... You talk about how much you are worried about being able to pay the bills."

Biden certainly can trace his roots to the working class neighborhoods of Scranton, Pennsylvania, and Claymont, Delaware, where he was raised. But these days, his kitchen table can be found in a 6,800-square-foot custom-built colonial-style house on four lakefront acres, a property worth close to $3 million.

Although he is among the least wealthy members of the millionaires club that is the US Senate — he and his wife, Jill, a college professor, earn about $250,000 a year — Biden maintains a lifestyle that is more comfortable than the impression he may have given. A review of his finances found that when it comes to some of his largest expenses, he has benefited from resources not available to average Americans.

Biden has been able to dip into his campaign treasury to spend thousands on landscaping for his home and some of his Amtrak travel between Delaware and Washington. And the acquisition of his waterfront property a decade ago involved wealthy businessmen and campaign supporters, who bought his old house for top dollar, sold him four acres and lent him $500,000 to build his new home.

There is nothing to suggest Biden bent any rules. "He was a VIP, so he was treated accordingly by the bank," said Ronald Tennant, a former loan officer who handled the mortgages. The senator, said David Wade, his spokesman, "has never forgotten where he came from, or how he grew up, and those middle class values motivate his work for the middle class.

Heading: How to make your PC green - Indian Express
Content:
In her 22 months in office, Palin has not addressed many of the matters - education, healthcare, trade, budget - in a significant way, pursuing a narrower agenda rooted in Alaska's resource-based economy.

Palin has approved increased spending for education and the elderly, sued the federal government for listing the polar bear as a threatened species, and pushed for a bill that would have reduced state regulation of new medical facilities. But by and large, oil and gas issues have dominated her tenure.

"You can't think of another area where there's been another drive or initiative coming out of the administration with the same level of intensity," said Scott Goldsmith, a professor of economics at the Institute of Social and Economic Research at the University of Alaska Anchorage.

Well before she became the Republican vice-presidential nominee, Palin was positioning herself nationally on resource development and energy issues. She is the chairwoman of the natural resources committee of the National Governors Association. The committee has not yet taken action under Palin, but a spokeswoman for the association said committees usually did not take up business until later in the fall. Palin's work on oil and gas issues was part of a wider effort at overturning the work of her predecessor, Governor Frank H Murkowski, also a Republican.

Palin does not appear to have made any trade missions since taking office, and former state officials said the state's trade staff had been reduced under her watch. Palin has shown support for developing Alaska's natural resources. Her views are largely in line with those of voters in her state, but not with environmentalists.

Even with the state enjoying a multibillion-dollar surplus because of high oil prices, Palin has vetoed about $500 million in capital spending projects requested by state lawmakers in two consecutive budgets.

Heading: Bombs kill 19 near Shi’ite mosques on Eid - Indian Express
Content:
Reusable tote bag? Check. Prius? Check. Rooftop solar panels? Check.

In a bid to secure your green bragging rights, you have the usual suspects covered, but what about your PC?

A standard-issue PC and monitor left on all the time consumes,109 kilowatt-hours a year, according to estimates from the Environmental Protection Agency. A user can do something to reduce the carbon footprint. Read on to learn ways to run your PC more efficiently, make ecologically intelligent purchasing decisions and dispose of an old computer properly.

Don't leave your computer on all the time. Shutting it down after an 8-hour workday provides 16 hours of savings each day. Your computer should be set to go to sleep after periods of inactivity. Different parts of your system can be set to sleep at different times.

Ditch your screensaver. Screensavers can use your hard drive to power up, and photo screensavers may require the extra use of a graphics card.

There's also the issue of "phantom" or "vampire" power. Many pieces of electronics use power even when they are turned off. To combat the vampires, take your computer and peripherals and plug them into a device like the Smart Strip power strip.

Finally, download a free power-management tool. These applications show how much energy can be saved by adjusting settings and will make those adjustments for you in a few clicks. http://desktop9.google9.com9/plugins9/i/energysaver9.html_Google's Energy Saver(http://desktop.google.com/plugins/i/energysaver.html) will show you the collective energy savings of everyone using the product; it also integrates into Google's own Desktop application. When it comes to recycling your computer, picking the right recycling company is critical. If done right, recyclers should reuse the parts they can and manage waste responsibly.

Heading: UN to pull out staff’s children from Pak - Indian Express
Content:
Suicide bombers struck Shi'ite worshippers as they gathered for prayers at two mosques in Baghdad to celebrate the Muslim Eid al-Fitr feast on Thursday, killing 19 people and wounded nearly 60, officials said.

For most of Iraq's Shi'ites Thursday is the main day of Eid, marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan. It is one of the Muslim calendar's most festive days when families exchange gifts and dress in their finest to attend prayers and feasts.

A leg and other body parts could be seen more than 100 metres from where a bomber detonated a taxi after ramming it into a police vehicle guarding a Shi'ite prayer hall in the Zafaraniya district, said a Reuters TV cameraman at the scene. Blood poured from a vegetable truck used to carry away the bodies and glass was shattered in surrounding buildings.

A witness to the Zafaraniyah attack said he saw a white car speed toward the mosque and then heard a huge explosion that sparked a fire and heavy smoke. Ammar Hashim, 25, who runs a car parts shop nearby, rushed to the site and saw "a damaged and burned Humvee with dead and burned bodies and many injured people crying out in pain".

"Pools of blood and the smell of burned flesh was everywhere and I saw a man of about 70 bleeding and lying on the ground from injuries," said Hashim, whose brother was also injured by broken glass in his shop.

Baghdad security spokesman Major-General Qassim Moussawi said the Zafaraniya attack killed 10 people and wounded 31.

In the other strike, in the New Baghdad district, the bomber was a teenage boy, who was accosted by a member of the security forces before blowing himself up 80 metres from a mosque, killing six people and wounding 26, Moussawi said. Both districts are Shi'ite areas in the east of the capital. The death tolls could rise, police said.

Suicide bombs — increasingly borne by women or teens — are the signature tactic of al-Qaeda and like-minded Sunni Arab militants who frequently target Shi'ite civilians during religious festivals.

Government officials had warned that militants might strike during the Eid holiday, which Sunni Muslims began observing earlier in the week.

Outside the capital, gunmen opened fire on a minibus carrying a family to an Eid celebration in volatile Diyala province. They killed six people, including women and children.

Thursday's strikes were the second major spate of attacks in recent days linked to Eid. On Sunday evening four bombs killed at least 32 people in Baghdad, many of them out buying Eid gifts in the busy Karrada shopping district.

The Government has declared a six-day public holiday to cover sects who observe Eid on different days.

Violence overall in Iraq is at four-year lows and al-Qaeda militants no longer control large numbers of villages and city districts as they did until 2007. But militant cells are still active and able to carry out bomb attacks.

Heading: ‘Pak has right to seek n-deal’ - Indian Express
Content:
The United Nations on Thursday increased the security level in its offices in Pakistan and framed plans for withdrawing children of its international staff from the country in the wake of the deadly suicide attack on the luxury Marriott Hotel here last month.

"The UN Secretary General has approved the increase of security level from Phase II to Phase III and the move will apply to offices in the cities of Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Quetta and nine districts of Balochistan," UN spokesperson Ishrat Rizvi said.

The children of international staff will be sent out of Pakistan though spouses will be eligible to remain in the country, Rizvi said.

The measures will be applicable for an interim period and the UN will conduct a review as soon as the security situation in Pakistan improves, she said. Rizvi said all programmes, projects and operations of the UN in Pakistan will not be affected by the measures.

"The projects and programmes will continue as usual. There are more than 20 UN entities in Pakistan and we stand committed to humanitarian development and support for the Government of Pakistan," she said.

The UN's move came a day after Britain said it would pull out the children of all its diplomats in Islamabad in the wake of the September 20 suicide bombing of the five-star Marriott hotel that killed nearly 60 people, including the Czech Ambassador, two US Marines and a Danish intelligence official.

The al-Qaeda is believed to have been behind the attack on the Marriott and the group's deputy leader Ayman al-Zawahiri has described the UN as an "enemy of Islam and Muslims".

The Pakistan Government tightened security across the country after the Marriott blast. Special security measures have been put in place in the "red zone" in the heart of Islamabad, which houses key Government buildings and the diplomatic enclave. However, many western diplomats believe the measures are not enough. Senior officials of western missions have had a series of meetings over the past few days to review the security situation.

Heading: ‘Pakistan made a scapegoat in war against terror’ - Indian Express
Content: With the US Congress giving its nod to the civil nuclear deal with India, Pakistan Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani on Thursday indicated that the country may seek a similar arrangement with its close ally China. "Pakistan will now make efforts for a civil nuclear deal and they (the world community) will have to accommodate us," Gilani said.  Stressing that there was "no need to worry", Gilani said, "....Pakistan will have the right to ask for a similar deal because we do not want there to be any discrimination."

Heading: Indian curry, naan tickle Japanese taste buds - Indian Express
Content:
Terming terrorism as the "single biggest challenge" faced by it, Pakistan has said it is being made a "scapegoat" for the "failures" of the US-led coalition forces in Afghanistan and sought help to sustain democracy as a panacea to combat all the ills facing the nation.

"The struggle against terrorism is the defining struggle of our times," Pakistan Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi said in an address at the prestigious Princeton University in New Jersey on Wednesday.

Describing terrorism that has devastated Pakistan as the "single biggest challenge we face as a nation", he said that when terrorists hit the twin towers in New York in 2001 it was not an attack on the US alone.

"It was an attack against all civilised societies. Terrorism poses a threat to all of us. It demands a response from all of us," he said.

Interestingly, there was not a single reference to the Indo-Pak relations or the vexed Kashmir issue in his lengthy speech.

He said it would be helpful if one could understand the genesis of the genie Pakistan was grappling with. "We inherited the terrorism issue in the wake of the war against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan," he said.

"Unfortunately while we won the war, we lost the peace. The spectacle of the Berlin Wall being breached and Soviet satellites gaining freedom in Europe claimed US attention and just when Afghanistan and Pakistan needed US and international support the most, it found itself abandoned," he said.

The rise of the Taliban was a natural corollary to developments in Afghanistan following the Soviet withdrawal and the US turning away, Qureshi said, adding that the Taliban regime, which seized Kabul, offered a haven for terrorists, including Osama bin Laden.

He asserted that Pakistan was combating al-Qaeda and Taliban militants actively in its restive tribal areas bordering Afghanistan which the US-led West has said that was being used as 'safe havens' for terror attacks against coalition forces in Afghanistan.

Heading: Pushy mums produce confident daughters: study - Indian Express
Content:
In Japan, Indians are virtually synonymous with 'curry'. Indian food has now got the Japanese hooked and is gradually replacing Chinese and Thai, their other favourites, with hundreds of restaurants mushrooming across its islands and an unprecedented rise in food imports from the country.

In fact, the Japanese are so fascinated with the 'Indian' food that even restaurants owned by Pakistanis, Bangladeshis and Sri Lankans display the Indian tricolour and add the prefix 'Indian' to the names of the eateries. So you have restaurant chains like the Siddique's 'Indian Pakistani', which has over 20 outlets and Indian Sri Lankan. "The Japanese identify 'Indian' with good and delicious food. If a restaurant serving any South Asian fare does not have the Indian tag, the Japanese will not go to it," says Mohammad Sageer, a chef working for Potahar who came from Islamabad eight years ago. There are others like the Maharaja, Khana, Sapla, Great India, Bombay, Ali Baba, Jantar Mantar and Agra. There is also a restaurant named 'Gandhi' in Washington Hotel in Shinzuku that was set up 25 years ago by a Japanese.

Potahar, in Shinzuku, Tokyo, is owned by a Pakistani, but the Indian flag hangs outside. A small eatery with hardly a sitting place for a dozen people, it caters to over 100 people, mostly Japanese, who queue up for "curry and naan" in just two hours during lunch time.

The Indian restaurants are thriving on Japanese clients as only a minuscule 30,000 Indians stay in the country. "The Japanese love food and are ready to try new things.

They particularly like the Indian curries because of the many spices. Among children, naan is the favourite," says Bella Chandrani, owner of Spice Magic Calcutta, who has been in country for 38 years.

Also, the Japanese are waking up to the fact that Indian food is healthy in many ways, she says, adding that a liberal visa regime for chefs and rules that easily let you set up restaurants have provided a fillip to the South Asian food industry in Japan. "Earlier Chinese food was very popular, but recent concerns about its safety has also made Indian food more popular," says Rajesh Soumaya of Indogen foods that is importing about 150 food products from India. There are many Japanese families who have turned completely vegetarian and import their food from India, he says. There has been a major spurt in consumption is the last five years. Indian food is now almost figuring regularly at parties and "we even served at the US embassy here," he adds.

Heading: Four hugs a day secret to a happy marriage - Indian Express
Content:
Like mother, like daughter. Pushy mums produce confident daughters, for a new study has revealed that women's success in life depends on how high their mothers expectations are.

A team at London University team has carried out the study and found that a women's sense of self-worth is actually rooted in the expectations their mothers had for them — the mother's confidence and ambition is likely to rub off on her female offspring.

Researchers, led by Dr Erini Flouri, have based their findings on an analysis of data on more than 300 men and women who were born in the year 1970, leading British newspaper the Daily Mail reported.

At the age of ten, their mothers were asked at what age they believed the child would leave school. The question was chosen to illustrate the mother's belief in her child's capabilities.

Twenty years later, the children answered questions designed to measure their self confidence. The answers showed the women's — but not the men's — self-esteem was linked to their mother's belief in them as they were growing up.

The link held even when other factors such as class and education were taken into consideration. And, it's thought that women are more likely to push their daughters rather than their sons to achieve.

The study has been published in the Journal of Educational Psychology.

Heading: On target - Indian Express
Content:
Move over, expensive gifts. The secret to a happy marriage is priceless - just four hugs a day, says a new study.

According to the study, spending at least 22 periods of "quality time" with your spouse every month, such as going for a short stroll or sharing a romantic dinner, are also key to maintaining a healthy relationship.

Researchers have based their findings on a poll of 4,000 couples who were asked to describe themselves as "happy" or "very happy" to estimate how much time they spend together in an effort to work out the secret of their success. Analysis of their responses revealed that the couples looking for happiness should spend at least seven evenings together every month with two dinner dates, The Daily Telegraph reported.

Other important elements included two romantic walks a month and at least one visit to a pub or theatre without the children or other friends, the study found. The couples also recommended that husbands should give their wife flowers or another gift at least once a month.

Heading: The sweet life - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Now we know who can enforce ban on smoking - Indian Express
Content:
Preeti Shenoy, in her first book, talks of the varied lessons that everyday's trivial incidents teach us

How many times has your philosophical mind wandered while you enjoy the sweetness of a candy and made you compare that little thing with people in your life? Well, the probability is negligible. We can compare people with Gods, demons or for that matter, superheroes, but candy is too trivial a thing to be considered.

In her book 34 bubblegums and candies, Preeti Shenoy gives more reasons for us to consider little goodies in life a bit more worthy. A known blogger, Shenoy, brings in loads of humour that promises some light reading and a lot of relating to the content.

"My book comprises all that we face in everyday life, it could be an ugly situation or a rib-tickling scenario. I think life gives you enough matter to enjoy, to learn from and sometimes to cry over," opines the Pune-based author who also writes a much-read blog called justamotheroftwo.blogspot.com.

Well this mother of two has shared some of humourous blunders that have accidentally taken place with her in the blog. And each has evoked good response. "Given this response for humour I decided to make my first book a humourous one. However the book is complete with flavours of other emotions as well," she adds.

Talking about the content of the book, Shenoy says that some chapters are deeply moving while others might leave you in fits of laughter. However, the beauty of the book lies in it being a commonplace, that is, people can relate to it instantly.

Humour, according to Shenoy, is the lifeblood and our body needs regular doses to keep going. "No matter how grave the problem is, humour finds a way everywhere. It's so important to live each day fully and this is demonstrated through various incidents from daily life through out the book," she says.

Narrating the story behind an unusual but catchy title, Shenoy says, "I find people like bubblegums and candies. Some come into your life, give their sweetness and fade away like candies. And some, meeting whom has been such a pleasure that you feel like meeting them time and again, are like bubblegums — you relish them even after the initial flavour is gone.

"No matter how small the reference might be or how inconsequential the issue, it gives a hidden message. And that is exactly what I have tried to highlight in my book, which also deals with young AIDS patients, who yearn for love," she adds.

After posting the preface of the book on her blog, she has received encouraging remarks. So those who are looking forward to grab a copy, the book that will be released on Saturday at Crossword will available in all leading bookstores.

Heading: Is astrology a science? Test over, now the result - Indian Express
Content:
List includes school and college heads, gazetted officers, HR heads at private firms

It's not just cops and FDA officials who will monitor and implement the ban on smoking. Food and Drug Administration officials in Pune received a notification on Friday that empowers excise inspectors, gazetted officers of state and central governments, heads of schools and colleges, bank officers and others to prevent smoking in their respective areas.

These officials can impose the penalty on people who violate the rules, says Sharad Kulkarni, Assistant Commissioner (Food). The FDA office in Pune has received a directive from Mumbai with a list of 10 more departments that would be authorised to prevent smoking. These include central excise, income tax, customs, sales tax and health, whose inspectors have been directed to monitor the ban at public places.

Railway stationmasters, postal officers, medical superintendents at private and public hospitals, heads of institutions, HR managers of private firms, college and school principals, airport managers, directors of public health and library officials are also authorised to crack down on smokers, Kulkarni said.

The ban applies to all public places, including restaurants, bars, offices, airports and even bus stops, though there will be exceptions made for larger establishments that set up separate smoking rooms. The ban has been introduced under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution), Act, 2003.

Kulkarni said FDA inspectors had collected Rs 23,000 as fines in August from people in Pune division, which includes Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Solapur, and Rs 26,420 in September this year for violation of the Cigarette and Tobacco Products Act.

Laws already exist to prevent smoking in public places. But the government has struggled to enforce them and fines for offenders are small. "If people know they can complain and can object (to smoking)... they can challenge it," said Dr Sundeep Salvi, Director of Chest Research Foundation.

Threat to kids
If one needed any prompting to help enforce the ban, one need look no farther than a pilot study of 1,000 students in four schools in Pune by School of Health Science, University of Pune and Chest Research Foundation. It found that children of 730 parents who smoked at home had a threefold risk of developing asthma than those whose parents didn't. Maria Cheraghi, PhD student, was guided by CRF director Dr Sundeep Salvi in the study.

Heading: Too late to build arsenal, cops settle for extra forces for CYG - Indian Express
Content:
Three days from now, scientists and rationalists will make public the result of what was possibly the first-ever attempt in the country to challenge and systematically test the claim that astrology is a science. Predictably, it should ruffle feathers.

In May, the Andhashradha Nirmulan Society (ANS), backed by astrophysicist Jayant Narlikar and the Inter University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA), threw an open challenge to astrologers, inviting them to join a test that could settle the age-old debate.

The methodology involved the collection of about 100 horoscopes each of mentally challenged and normal children and handing over about 40 of these at random to the participating astrologers. Based on the data in the horoscopes, the astrologers would be asked to predict which horoscope belonged to a normal child and which to a mentally challenged one.

The logic was the belief that intelligence and mental retardation are the two distinct and prominent characteristics that determine the future of any individual, said Narendra Dabholkar, president of ANS.

Initially many astrologers accepted the challenge but within a few days most withdrew. However, over the past two months, ANS and IUCAA got 50 astrologers to participate and sent them the 40 horoscopes of some brilliant and some mentally challenged children.

Prof Sudhakar Kunte of the Statistics department of University of Pune was given the responsibility of studying and compiling the responses. "I am functioning merely as a neutral observer between the challengers and the participants," said Kunte who met Dhabolkar and Narlikar at IUCAA on Friday morning to discuss the findings.

"To my knowledge this is the first such scientific test to be conducted in India," said Dhabolkar.

According to Narlikar, the predictions need to be at least 90 per cent accurate for them to take astrology seriously. "If the predictions are less than 70 per cent correct, then the hypothesis that astrology is a science will be rejected. If the success rate is between 70 and 90 per cent then further testing will be called for," Narlikar had said while the test was on.

"From my studies of the subject and based on the tests made on it abroad, I do not regard it (astrology) as having a scientific base. However I am keeping an open mind so far as the present test is concerned," he had said then.

The organisers of the test are tight-lipped about the results, which they will announce on Tuesday at a press conference.

Self-defence
The Jyotish Vidya Prasarak Mandal, which participated in the test, claimed to have shown 51 per cent accuracy. to Siddheshwar Marajkar, one of the five trustees of the mandal, said they were given 200 horoscopes and showed the results to the ANS and Kunte about a fortnight ago, after which they were informed about their performance. Asked whether this puts a cloud over their craft as the accuracy standard was set at 70 per cent, Marajkar said they are satisfied with the results as it is above 50 per cent.

Heading: Day after woman killed kids & self, husband, lover held - Indian Express
Content:
The police have run out of time to buy sophisticated equipment for security at the Commonwealth Youth Games. Instead, they have now reinforced the bomb detection and disposal squad.

The government had sanctioned Rs 17 crore for purchase of vehicles, bomb masks, scanners, cameras and other equipment for security, particularly for bomb detection and disposal. The police have so far bought cars, jeeps, police buses, motorcycles, doorframe metal detectors, hand metal detectors and various types of barricades, but could not manage X-ray scanners and modified bomb trucks on time.

The vehicles used by the city squad are outdated. It needs not only a modified truck but also bulletproof jackets.

"We have not yet bought the modified bomb truck. It is not possible to buy all the required equipment before the Games start," Additional Commissioner of Police Rajender Singh said.

Sources said the country has very few suppliers of security equipment, leaving the Pune police with little time to contact them and check the quality of their products. There were also "technical problems": for instance, the amounts sanctioned for certain products were less than the actual market cost, the sources said.

As a backup, 50 trained personnel on Friday reinforced the police's bomb disposal squad, with whom they will remain till the Games end on October 18. The additional personnel will carry out extensive searches in and around the Games venue in Balewadi.

"We will take help from the army and bomb squads from other parts of the state. There are five bomb disposal teams in Pune and we have already called five teams from other police divisions," Singh said.

The Pune police had recently formed 10 assault teams and a commando squad for patrolling in sensitive areas. A special team of commandos had been called from Delhi. A full-fledged control room has been set up for disaster management during the Games.

The police have banned cellphones in the Balewadi sports complex during the Games. Also banned are cameras, water bottles, carry-bags and inflammable material.

Heading: IIT Masters degrees beckon Bharat Forge employees - Indian Express
Content:
The Khadak police on Friday arrested the husband of the woman who had killed her two daughters and herself, leaving a suicide note that cited the husband's infidelity. The police also arrested her husband's lover and his brother.

Sunita Khandagale had flung her daughters Harshada (5) and Sakshi (4) from the sixth floor of her home in Bhavani Peth and then jumped herself. In her suicide note she not only mentioned the extramarital affair but also alleged harassment by her in-laws.

The police picked up her husband Arvind (32) and brother-in-law Anil (45) from their home and Arvind's lover Sheetal Kshrisagar (32) from Yerwada.

The police also booked Sunita's father-in-law, mother-in-law and two sisters-in-law. The arrested were produced at Shivajinagar court on Friday and remanded to police custody till October 6.

Additional public prosecutor Sharayu Lingayat said that the remaining accused should also be arrested as the entire family had abetted Sunita's suicide. He demanded that mobile phone conversations between Arvind and Sheetal be intercepted.

Police said that Sunita's in-laws had asked her to get Rs 1.5 lakh from her parents so that they could buy a new house. She failed and they had been harassing her, the police said.

Sub-inspector N B Gawade is conducting the investigation.

Heading: Public-private partnership essential for development, says Deshmukh - Indian Express
Content:
Corporate India continues to forge ties with centres of educational excellence in the country. City-based Bharat Forge Ltd (BFL), the flagship of the $ 2.4 billion Kalyani Group and a supplier to the automotive and capital goods industry, signed a letter of intent on Wednesday with Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay (IITB) for the creation of an M Tech Programme for its employees.

The two-year, full-time M Tech (materials, manufacturing and modelling) programme will be specially designed to suit BFL's requirements, with a view to boosting the research and development capabilities of its available human resources, the company said in a release. The proposed course is trans-disciplinary in nature and will be the first of its kind in the institute. During the first year, BFL employees will be deputed to IITB for full-time classroom training ; in the second year, the employees would do their respective projects jointly at BFL and IITB. The first batch will start in July 2009.

The letter of intent was signed by IIT director Prof Ashok Misra and BFL's chairman and managing director B N Kalyani.

Kalyani said, "I am pleased to announce the beginning of this partnership with IIT Bombay and am sure that such technology-oriented partnerships will be mutually fulfilling, enhance the much-needed interaction between the industry and educational institutions and benefit the nation."

Pointing out that BFL was a "technology-driven manufacturing company", Kalyani said it was working towards creating a "global talent pool". As part of this initiative, BFL has tied up with the Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS), Pilani, for BS (manufacturing engineering) and Warwick University for MSc in engineering business management. "With the IITB letter of intent now in place, we will be in a position to provide learning opportunities to our employees at all levels," he said.

Prof Ashok Misra said, "The tie-up will expose BFL employees to upcoming technological areas. The course will enable them to emerge as multi-skilled individuals, prepared to face global challenges. From IITB's perspective, the collaboration with BFL will promote active research, synergise and mutually benefit academia and the growing Indian industry."

Heading: Sixth Asian Film Fest from Oct 16 - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the land acquisition process is posing a major hurdle for development projects in the state, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh lauded the Amanora Park town, under the state's special township policy for its unique "public-private" partnership.

With farmers playing as crucial a role as the developers in the development of a city, this could set an example in the state, he said. "This is a model project which can serve as a model for other townships,"' Deshmukh said after inaugurating the Pawar Public School-Amanora School I in the township on Friday.

The township has followed a proper rehabilitation policy — employment and training for the affected.

Deputy CM R R Patil urged the townships to look at low-cost housing under this policy. Earlier, Rajya Sabha MP Supriya Sule said that the Pawar Public School under the Pawar Public Charitable trust will look at inclusive education and will stress on first-come first-serve basis and not on marks. "It will look at identifying the talent among children rather than just admit children with good marks," she said. With 360 students till the sixth grade, Sule said that this is the third school to be set up under the trust, the earlier ones being at Bhandup and at Talas. Classes commence in June. Managing Director City Corporation Ltd, Aniruddha Deshpande speaking earlier, said that the entire township is spread over 400 acres and will be a self containing property with schools, college, hospital, restaurants and sports complex within the township.

NCP chief Sharad Pawar, mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale and Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar were also present.

Patil defends police force
Defending the police force today, Home Minister R R Patil said that they were well-equipped and are ready to take on the terrorists. "Our police are on their toes to face any danger," he said. Reacting to a skit put up by Bharat Dabholkar, Patil said that the new lot of police force has educated policemen contrary to the belief that policemen are not well-educated

Heading: No new sugar mills, master plan required: Report - Indian Express
Content:
The sixth Asian Film Festival will be held in Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad from October 16.

Over 70 films from 15 countries — including Japan, China, Israel and Taiwan — will be screened in the eight-day festival which will be held in three venues — City Pride in Kothrud, National Film Archive Of India and Dhruva Auditorium at the Indira University Campus in Wakad.

Festival director Virendra Chitrav said, "Film festivals have always received overwhelming response from Puneites. This time, to cover a larger audience, we have decided to conduct part of it in Pimpri Chinchwad for the first time. A lot of students in Wakad, and adjoining areas as well as IT professionals will be able to be a part of the festival."

Two Marathi films will be premiered along with last year's seven best films.

Convener of the festival Dr Mohan Agashe said, "Asia is, at present, the focus of the social and political change and the shift is also reflected in cinema. The festival will bring the best of the Asian countries to our audience."

"Interactions with directors and artists will also be organised in 'Open Forum.' We have also organised a special section devoted to films from the SAARC countries along with special screenings of Israeli director Dan Wolman and Korean Director Kim-Ki-Duk's films in the Retrospective section," said Satish Jakatdar, festival director.

Registration for the festival will be open from October 4.

Heading: ME in printing tech for the first time in India - Indian Express
Content:
No new sugar mills should be allowed in the state, even if the sugar commissioner has granted certificates, said Shivaji Deshmukh, director general of Vasantdada Sugar Institute (VSI) in a report that was submitted to the Bombay High Court in late July. The report calls for a master plan to be prepared for the sugar industry in Maharashtra. The report was made public last week by the petitioner Ashok Kulkarni, who filed a case four years ago demanding that irregularities in the industry be examined.

"No permission for new sugar mills should be given by the government until the government prepares a master plan with the sole objective of development of the sugar industry with due consideration to area development, availability of irrigation potential duly assessed by an expert committee and not relying on the certificates issued by the commissioner of sugar," Deshmukh said in his report.

Earlier, the High Court had asked an expert (Deshmukh) to report on whether the capacity of the existing mills need to be enhanced so that no sugar goes waste, whether to have redistribution of sugar between the efficient sugar mills and whether new sugar mills need to be established.

In his report, Deshmukh expressed concern over the number of sick sugar mills in the state in the last few years. "In spite of the number of recommendations of various committees on sickness and support of number of packages by the state and central governments, the number of sick units are increasing," he has written, while calling for the liquidation of sick units. In some cases, they can be amalgamated with efficient ones. The present practice of giving lease on short-term basis should be discontinued, as it would result in lengthening the sick period with no consequential benefits, he said.

Heading: After road work, over 6,000 BSNL lines go dead in Khadki - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in India Pune Vidyarthi Griha's College of Engineering and Technology (PVGCOET) will be starting a Masters of Engineering (ME) course in Printing Technology for the year 2009-2010. Annouincing this Dr R P Joshi, director of the College said on Friday, "We recently received the approval from the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) for the course.. He added that the course would have 18 seats and would begin by 2009-10, when the state government passes a resolution on the same.

Joshi was speaking during the inaugural function of PVGCOET's new building.He said that the number of seats for MCA is also likely to be increased. The college is also set to open a hostel for 100 students in Sadashiv Peth with subsidised rates for lodging and boarding.

Speaking about the college's plan outside Pune, Joshi said, "We have sent a proposal to the state government to start an engineering college in Nasik and are positive about the government's response."

Dr Pramod Chaudhari, chairman and managing director of Praj Industries who was the chief guest for the function said that students who opt for core engineering branches like mechanics, chemical, electrical should stick to those branches while taking up a job, rather than falling for job offers from the IT sector. "The manufacturing industry, which offers equally lucrative salary packages and foreign trips, is falling short of skilled manpower. It is the manufacturing industry that creates wealth for the nation and not IT, " he said.

Heading: Elements of desire - Indian Express
Content:
After frequent electricity problems, the ongoing road development work are giving a tough time to the residents of Khadki as nearly 6,000 Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) telephone lines have gone dead. The list of harrowed customers include many defence establishments and emergency services like Khadki Military Hospital and Khadki police station.

BSNL officials C V L Nagleela, general manager (West and Chinchwad), Hemant Borale, deputy general manager (West and LD), briefed reporters about this constant menace posed by the civic body. BSNL officials have alleged that the lackadaisical attitude of the PMC and its contractors was making it count losses and also tarnishing its image in the public eye.

Nagleela said, "The latest incident happened in Khadki, where PMC's JCB machine scooped out telephone 10 different cables, which turned approximately 6,000 phones non-functional. The areas hit include Khadki, Dapodi, Aundh Road, Bopodi, Range Hills, etc. This has been happening time and again. Before initiating a road-digging work, the PMC is bound to inform us, which it conveniently skips. It is only after we start receiving complaint calls, we get to know about the problem and start our repair work."

"Due to these constant service breakdowns, about 20,000 customers have surrendered their connections and shifted to other service providers. Now, since the problem is on a rise, we fear that that more and more customers from Khadki and Baner areas will choose to disconnect our service," Nagleela said.

Borale said, "We have issued a demand note of Rs 28 lakh for the losses incurred and planning to initiate a legal action against the civic body."

In July, the BSNL had even lodged a complaint against PMC with the Chatuhshrungi police for digging the university road before President Pratibha Patil's visit.

Heading: LAST BITE  with Dia Mirza - Indian Express
Content:
Nestling amidst natural elements and serving up the contemporary delicacies of Europe, Stone Water Grill is an experience in sheer fine dining

For all those meticulous food lovers, who swear by the authenticity and flavors of exotic cuisines, there cannot be a better place to splurge than this one. Bringing in contemporary European cuisines the Stone Water Grill has ushered in experimental dining in a classy ambience.

It is a restaurant that boasts a unique setting, amidst a water pool, tall palm trees and a beautiful landscape. The place is further segregated into four areas — a lounge, a dining area, a private dining and banquet spot. "The idea behind this place is to bring in a new dimension to dining with innovative setting and authentic cuisine. The contemporary European food we offer is emphasised by a wood-fired oven and a charcoal grill to give the food a smoky earthy flavour, which is an original element of cooking. We also have an array of Japanese and Mexican food. It's going to be a space where people can step in for dinner, host a private party or simply interact over cocktails," says Riyaaz Amlani, CEO, Impresario Entertainment and Hospitality.

One can dine immersed in a pool at the private dining tables or chill by the fifty-foot bar and even host a party by the river. With an endless list of delectable dishes including vegetarian enticements such as charcoal grilled vegetables and Ratatoulille pilaf, Stone Water Grill has a long wine list with eighty plus wines as well as mocktails.

"We have juxtaposed ingredients and there are flavours like vanilla penacotta and peppercorn, liver plate and apple marmalade and so on. Some of the out of the ordinary dishes are Jerked Norwegian Salmon Grilled lobster and Beetroot Risotto, Fillet Mignon with Wasabi Wash and much more. The restaurant is by the river and water surrounds most of the dining area. To further heighten the natural feel, there are pebbles and stones around with a big Nepali green stone, unique because of its turquoise color. It is a restaurant in a landscape rather than the other way round. We intend to have all food lovers, especially those who are well travelled, over here," adds Amlani. Stone Water Grill opens today in Koregaon Park, near Club Polaris.

Heading: Meal Ticket - Indian Express
Content: What makes a meal memorable for me is the company and not what I eat. Last week I caught up with a cousin after a decade-long gap. I had a really good time with her and kids besides my aunts at their place in Mumbai. I was treated to delicious mutton kababs (Muththi) with rice and daal, pickle and potato curry. Although the menu was simple, it was divine to eat homemade food. As I am on a strict diet, I didn't have any sweets. But the day was filled with fun and cheer and lots of family bonding.

Heading: Released! - Indian Express
Content:
Foodies' day out
In the festive season, treat your taste buds and savour some of the most delicious snacks and meals like cutlets, dhoklas, Rajasthani gatta, paneer butter masala, aloo sambhariya, jodhpuri kadhi, methi paratha, surti gujarati dal, dahiwadas, Chinese fried rice, manchurian gravy, sitafal rabdi and dudhi halwa. Sanskruti brings you all this and more fun amid the mesmerising tunes and captivating beats of dandiya and garba at just Rs 300 for adults and Rs 200 for children.

Italian Weekend
To experience a delicious Italian weekend, head to CCasanova Carlsberg Weekend Brunch at Kalyani Nagar. The sumptuous meal is spread over five courses. The brunch begins with fresh salads, to be followed by mouth-watering starters. The main course comprises of a variety of delicious pizzas and pastas followed by a choice of desserts, both in veg and non-veg, culminating with a sweet ending. All of this accompanied by unlimited Carlsberg beer! The brunch is for Rs 400 per head, inclusive of taxes. The timings are from 12 noon to 3:30pm. This offer is not valid on the ala-carte menu.

Thali time
On October 9, Chokhi Dhani will celebrate Vijayadashmi by dishing out elaborate Rajasthani cuisine served at Sangri, the village-dining hall. The event will take place at the ethnic Rajasthani cultural village at Wagholi, Pune. Mouth-watering, authentic vegetarian food will be served on a leaf platter, in the tradition of Manuhar with a variety of 22 items in each thali. There will be a welcome drink counter, which will serve chhaas or jaljeera. Unlimited entertainment and unlimited food will all be available at affordable rates. As an added attraction, traditional entertainment will come in the form of kacchi ghodi, ghumar, kalbelia, bhopa bhopi, nat (acrobatics). The highlight of the evening would be the effigy of Ravana, stuffed with firecrackers, being set ablaze.

Heading: Municipal Commissioner seeks clarification on care-taker policy - Indian Express
Content:
In the city to promote their film, Kidnap, Imran Khan and Minissha Lamba, shared their captivating experiences

He won the audiences' hearts with his boyish charm in his debut film. She has been a personification of the sweet girl next door on screen. Both have now come together — Imran Khan and Minissha Lamba — to capture the audience in their latest release — Kidnap where both have walked out of their stereotype image. The stars were in Pune on Friday evening at Inox multiplex to promote the film.

Having raised expectations with his debut film — Jaane tu.., Imran appeared as casual as he is on screen. "I am aware that after my first film, expectations are high. But then personally speaking, I do not expect anything from my films. Filmmaking is a risky business as a lot of it depends upon the masses. I am confident though that Kidnap would do good as well," said the unassuming actor.

Imran who in his previous film was projected as a college going lover-boy, has broken this image with Kidnap. "My role in this film is an angry and wild character. I don't think that I naturally have those dangerous looks. But director Sanjay Gadhvi sure managed to get that image out of me," adds Khan.

Imran Khan has also been a filmmaking student and differentiating between acting and technicalities of filmmaking, he explains, "As a filmmaking student, I understand the technical aspects of films. It's like knowing why the camera is there. But acting is totally different. My job as an actor is to keep doing different roles."

And he surely is trying his hand in a variety of roles. With a eclectic mix of films in his pocket like Luck, Delhi Belly and so on, the young actor dreams of eventually becoming a director. "I don't know when and how but yes, I finally want to become a director. But before that I am enjoying my acting stint."

This is also the first film in which Minissha Lamba claims to have broken her girl next-door look. "I myself was surprised when the director asked me about this role because this is not what I have been doing. This role is completely glamorous and that is what got me interested in the role. I play a 17-year-old called Sonia who is kidnapped by Kabir, played by Imran."

However, Kidnap has generated mixed reactions from the audiences and according to Lamba, "Filmmaking is a creative process. There is no set formula for success. Everyone has his or her own approache towards films. I am happy that the positive reactions are more than the negative."

We don't know about her films but Lamba seems to know the secret of generating a fan following. Because she constantly kept waving at the audience saying, "I love Pune. The city is a vibrant, young and energetic place to be." Well, she sure seems to have got that right.

Heading: 2 testify in Ramabai firing case - Indian Express
Content:
Eleven months after the state government issued a stay on the controversial 'care-taker policy' on open spaces, Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak has now sought clarification regarding the stay. He has appealed to the authorities to lift the stay on adoption of plots demarcated as recreation grounds/ playgrounds.

Civic officials said that there is a complete stay on the adoption of RG/PG and a number of applications from NGOs and other organisations to adopt the plots for maintenance and beautification are now pending.

"We have sought clarification for the stay on the adoption of smaller plots and are asking the state government to lift the ban," Phatak said. Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev said that there is currently a stay on all adoptions of open spaces by private parties. "The state government fears that the plots on adoption can be converted under the care-taker policy and facilities like club and gyms can be constructed on it," he said. Organisations adopting the plots under adoption policy—reserved for five year—can later apply for caretaker policy where the plot will be given for 33 years and 33 per cent of land will be available for construction.

In November 2007, following protests by citizens and political parties, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh had stayed the civic body's 'care-taker policy' under which plots given to private institutions can be used to construct clubs, gymkhanas, restaurants and bars. There are a total of 884 plots of open spaces with the BMC. Out of these, 287 have been given on an adoption basis and 10 on a caretaker basis.

Heading: Five arrested for robbery in Big Bazaar godown - Indian Express
Content:
Two prime witnesses in the Ramabai Nagar firing case testified on Friday, contradicting the prosecution's version of the incident.

In his testimony, Constable Sanjay Nikam, who was part of the seven-member platoon that had fired 10 rounds on a furious mob, told the court that the police resorted to firing only for half an hour after the mob went out of control. Stating that the police had fired on the orders given by Manohar Kadam—an officer attached to the state reserve police— Nikam told the court that all bullets were targeted only below the waist of the people who were part of the mob.

According to the prosecution, the police were firing indiscriminately at the mob. "We never expected Nikam to support our case. He was part of the police platoon. He is bound to shield his senior," said Special Public Prosecutor Vijay Pradhan.

Another witness Namdeo Shinde, a driver of the BEST bus who had parked his vehicle near the Ramabai chawl, said in his testimony that a mob of as many as 50 people had tried to set his bus on fire. But the police doused off the fire. He also claimed that it was the police's timely intervention that saved the bus.

Shinde also said that he had asked the passengers and the conductor to get out of the vehicle before the angry mob tried to set the bus on fire.

On July 11, 1997, Manohar Kadam, a state reserve police officer, had ordered his platoon to open fire on a mob of Dalits for rioting at Mata Ramabai Ambedkar Nagar following desecration of Dr B R Ambedkar's statue. As many as 10 persons were killed and 26 sustained injuries in the incident.

Following this, a commission was appointed under Justice S D Gundewar in November 1997. The commission that completed its inquiry in August 2008 indicted Kadam for firing indiscriminately on the mob.

Heading: On Day 2 of smoking ban, enforcement begins - Indian Express
Content:
The Sewree police have arrested five people for their involvement in the robbery that took place in the go down of Big Bazaar shopping mall situated at Dharamshi Manohar compound on August 20.

The accused— identified as Manoj Gupta (22), Vishwanath Gupta (19), Mohammad Shafi (38), Mohammad Naushad (24) and Chandrakant Singhe (42)— were arrested on October 1.

Goods comprising watches, i-pods and mobile phones worth Rs 10 lakh were stolen from an electronics goods unit in the godown premises. According to DCP (Port Zone) Madhukar Kohe, Big Bazaar's godown at Sewree has seven units. Each unit houses different electrical appliances. On August 20, the warehouse manager of the place, Sandeep Agarwal, was told by one of his staff members about a break-in at the unit containing electronic goods. A police complaint was then filed.

According to Kohe, during the course of their enquiries, the police received a tip-off about a man staying in the Pardhiwala slums seen with an expensive mobile phone in the locality.

"Based on the information, we picked up this man, later identified as Gupta, on September 28. After interrogating him, he confessed to having committed the theft along with four others. We then picked up the other accused from various parts of the city," said Kohe.

He added, "Gupta had worked in one other unit of the godown a year ago and knew about the value of goods stored inside. This probably gave him the idea of the theft and he roped in his friends for committing the crime. The accused have been remanded to police custody till October 7."

Heading: On terror trail, city cops say close to major breakthrough - Indian Express
Content:
Woman caught smoking in office building fined, so were three airport workers

A day after the ban on smoking in public places came into force across the country, authorities finally displayed some clarity on how implementation would proceed.

When an executive from a media house was taken to the Azad Maidan police station after being caught smoking on the stairway of her office building, she was fined Rs 200. An official from the Azad Maidan police station said: "We also issued a receipt for the fine. These receipts are the ones we have been using for offences like sale of tobacco products to people below 18 and other violations related to tobacco products."

On Thursday, three airport workers were also fined Rs 200 each at the local police station for smoking in the airport premises.  

Alongside that optimistic note on implementation, the BMC also charted out its plans. Besides civic officials and school teachers, the Clean Up marshals — private agencies responsible for implementing the cleanliness and sanitation bylaws — will also be entrusted the job of penalising people found smoking in public places.

Executive health officer of BMC Dr Jairaj Thanekar said challan books will be printed soon. "These will be distributed to all ward offices. Additionally, a special booklet explaining the various rules with regards to the ban will also be distributed to the civic officials," Thanekar said.

While there are only 100 sanitary inspectors across the 24 wards for monitoring and inspecting small restaurants and eateries, they would also simultaneously implement the ban during the day time. "The police department is in charge of the implementation of the ban, so there should be no issues over monitoring in the evening time," said Additional Municipal Commissioner Kishor Gajbhiye.

Meanwhile, non-governmental organisations and groups of non-smokers are also trying to support the ban. "A 15- yea-old was seen smoking just outside his college. In spite of requesting the police officials, they did not fine him and instead confiscated his college identity card," said Vincent Nazareth of Crusade Against Tobacco, a voluntary organization.

And, there are still many restaurant owners who are unaware of the ban. "Fourteen restaurant owners in Vile Parle did not know about the ban, also police officials refuse to fine people as they themselves are unaware of the law. Union Health Minister had issued notification in the month of May but it was not circulated to the first-line enforcers. Unlike other cities, Mumbai is lagging behind in terms of awareness," said Nazareth.

Heading: Kasliwal wants to come back to city, moves HC - Indian Express
Content:
7 teams sent across country; raids conducted in Pune, Mangalore

The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Friday revealed that it was on the verge of a major breakthrough in connection with the recent terror strikes in different parts of the country and the terror-emails sent by the Indian Mujahideen. Seven teams from the Crime Branch have been sent to different locations within and outside the state.

"We are on the verge of a major breakthrough, but cannot disclose any details at this stage as it will jeopardise our operations. We are very, very close and are confident of getting at our targets," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

"Based on the information obtained through the interrogations of the five Indian Mujahideen members already arrested, seven teams have been sent to locations in and outside the state," Maria added.

Additional Commissioner of Police Deven Bharti was camping in Mangalore on Friday, and was in constant touch with Maria to co-ordinate the raids with police teams in other states.

"Pune and Mangalore are two of these locations. Raids have been conducted at these places on the basis of certain leads on specific suspects, and our teams have moved on after getting information from these locations. However, no arrests have been made by us so far," said Maria, adding, "I implore the media not to speculate on arrests, suspects and locations as they have an adverse effect on our operations. None of the names of suspects being thrown around is true."

According to sources, one of the suspects the police are looking for is an Azamgarh native identified as Abu Rashid. All five alleged Indian Mujahideen members arrested by the Crime Branch also hail from Azamgarh. Sources also said that a major announcement regarding the Crime Branch's ongoing operation is on the cards in a couple of days.

Heading: Former cop booked for using ‘police’ sign in car seeks anticipatory bail - Indian Express
Content:
Abhishek Kasliwal, accused in the alleged rape of a 52-year-old woman, has moved a fresh application before the Bombay High Court seeking relaxation of restrictions imposed on him so that he can come back to Mumbai. Kasliwal, who is in Delhi as per court directions, has sought to return to Mumbai stating that his business is getting affected while the trial is still pending.

Kasliwal, son of industrialist Ambhuj Kasliwal who owns Shree Ram Mill and the S Kumar's brand, was earlier granted permission to go to China, Hong Kong, Thailand and Dubai for official purpose. He was also granted permission to travel anywhere in the country except Mumbai. The court had refused him permission to come to Mumbai after the prosecution expressed apprehension regarding tampering of evidence.

The court had directed Kasliwal to approach the police station concerned and deposit Rs 50,000 whenever he wants to go abroad and the money would be given back once his passport is deposited after the trip.

In the current petition, Kasliwal contends that there has been no progress in the trial even after the elapse of one year. According to his advocate Shamsher Garud, summonses have been issued to the witnesses and the trial is expected to resume in November.

Kasliwal contends that he has been away from his family and his business is getting affected as he has not been able to assist his father in the same.

Kasliwal was arrested on March 12, 2006 in connection with the alleged rape. He got bail in April and was directed to stay in New Delhi and his entry into Mumbai was restricted to avoid any manipulation of evidence. At the time of granting bail, on a bond of Rs 50,000, the court had orally observed that in such cases sex with consent was a possibility.

In March 2008, the police was reprimanded by the City Civil and Sessions Court after the court was informed that 52-year-old victim has gone missing and could not be served the summons to be produced before the court to record her evidence. This happened in spite of a High Court direction in April 2006 asking the police to provide protection to the victim until the trial is over.

The trial court had last month issued notice to the Commissioner of Police seeking a reply regarding the status of the missing victim.

According to the prosecution, on March 11, 2006, Kasliwal had offered the victim a lift in his car from Colaba area in the wee hours and then allegedly raped her. The victim had lodged a complaint with the police and Kasliwal was arrested and after spending over a month in prison, he was granted bail by the HC on April 18, 2006 on the condition that he would not enter city limits until the trial is over.

Heading: Modasa: Police draw a blank at ground zero - Indian Express
Content:
A Former Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySp), Jehangir Zaveri (69), has moved the Sewri session's court seeking anticipatory bail in a case of impersonation registered against him at the Byculla police station. Zaveri, who retired from the police force in 1997, was booked for travelling in a car carrying the 'police' sign even after his retirement.

According to his application to the court, Zaveri retired with an unblemished service record from the Mumbai Police force and is a permanent citizen of the city with no criminal antecedents. Thus the police registering a case against him was incorrect. He was booked under Section 171 of the Indian Penal Code (wearing grab or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent), which attracts a maximum punishment of three months or a fine of Rs 200.

His application further stated that he joined the police in 1964 as a sub inspector. On February 28, when he had parked his Fiat car (MZV-1399) outside Jijamata Udyan, a traffic police constable came and towed it to the Byculla traffic police station on the ground that his car was obstructing traffic. Initially, he was charged under Section 15 (1) and Section 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act. However, later the police, after consulting Deputy Commissioner of Police Harish Baijal, registered a case of impersonation against Zaveri, the application said.

Defence lawyer Vidhya Kasale said, "The ground on which he has been charged is irrelevant. The 'police' sign on the car was not there with an intention to mislead anyone. It has been there since many years and it's not even prominent. Neither does Zaveri had any wrong intentions. Thus the case is totally uncalled for," she said.

The application will come up for hearing next week.

Heading: CBI files corruption charges against four senior officials of Kandla Port Trust - Indian Express
Content:
Senior police officers investigating the September 29 blast in Modasa are calling the investigation 'very much open' in the absence of any crucial leads in the case. One person was killed and 10 others were injured in the explosion that occurred outside a mosque in Suka Bazaar area of the town last Monday night.

But even four days after the blast in the small town of Sabarkantha district, senior police officers say they do not have any clues to pursue the case.

Sabarkantha Superintendent of Police R B Brahmbhatt told Newsline: "We do not have any concrete clues in the case. We are looking for some eyewitnesses who could have seen the person(s) who might have parked the bike at the blast site. But so far, no one has come forward. Apart from that, we are yet to establish the identity of the bike, which was used in the blast. It has been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory in Gandhinagar for the same," he said.

A senior police officer said some of the locals suspected to have been involved in the case are being interrogated, but so far, nothing has emerged.

The police are also scanning through thousands of mobile phone records, which were active in the town during the last one week starting September 29.

Heading: SSNNL employees get notice for renting out their govt quarters - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a case of corruption against four senior officials of the Kandla Port Trust (KPT) and the owner of a Jamnagar-based private company.

Former KPT chairman A Janardan Rao and the respective heads of Finance, Traffic and Mechanical departments at KPT, A Krishnan, R Revenkar and A Gadhkari, have been accused of allegedly misusing their official position to facilitate the setting up of a CFC at the port in 2005 by the Jamnagar-based Seabird Marine Service Ltd. According to the CBI, this eventually led to the government of India and the Central Warehouse Corporation (CWC) at Kandla to incur losses to the tune of crores of rupees.

The CWC had established a CFC at Kandla in 2002. An agreement was signed between the CWC and the KPT then, restricting the port to allow any competitor to have a CFC at Kandla.

But three years later, when Seabird approached the Union Ministry of Commerce for permission to have a CFC at Kandla, the accused KPT officers gave it a green signal. The CBI said this was in violation to the agreement that the KPT had with CWC since 2002. Interestingly, just a year prior to this, when the Container Corporation of India (CCI) had approached the KPT in 2004 for establishing a CFC at Kandla, the former was denied permission on the grounds that KPT had an agreement with CWC.

A CBI officer said: "The accused officers had misused their position and facilitated the private company to have its CFC at Kandla. The four, along with the owner of the private company, are accused of corruption and cheating."

Till reports last came in on Friday, the CBI was conducting searches on 10 premises owned by the accused.

Heading: Banned this Navratri: Backless cholis, low-waist ghaghras in Rajkot - Indian Express
Content:
The Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) on Friday served notices to around 290 employees at Kevadia Colony in Narmada district for renting out government quarters to the locals.

Nigam authorities, however, refused to provide further information, saying that they were reviewing the situation and that action will be taken according to the government norms and regulations .

SSNNL Chief Engineer K J Trivedi said: "Many of those who have been served the notice are Class IV and III employees. We are yet to make any further progress on this issue."

He added that most of the quarters were rented to the shopkeepers and businessmen and it was after a month long survey that the SSNNL decided to take this step.

Heading: It’s a daily struggle for HIV-positive fisherman released from Pak jail - Indian Express
Content:
Sonu Mehta (20), a third year B.Com student from Kundaliya College, spent over Rs 1,000 to get a perfect backless choli and a ghaghra to go with the festive trend. But she has kept the ensemble in a corner of her closet, as she does not want to take a risk of being 'thrown away' from the garba venue.

In Rajkot, it is the police and the commercial organisers who decide on the dress code for the garba revellers. Backless cholis and low waist ghaghras may be the traditional ensemble of Gujarat, but young girls are being discouraged from donning it as it is considered 'obscene and provocative' by the organisers and the police.

"We have been clearly told by a couple of organisers to come only in 'decent' clothes. Women in rural Gujarat wear backless cholis. It's a traditional dress of communities like the Rabari and the Bharwads, and there is nothing obscene about it," said Sonu.

Rajkot Commissioner of Police Sudhir Sinha has issued an order to all the commercial organisers to ban the entry of participants in 'obscene and provocative attire.' Incidentally, Rajkot is the only city in Gujarat where the Commissioner's office has issued such an order to the garba organisers.

For the strict implementation of the order, organisers have also been asked by the Commissioner's office to depute a special security officer to keep an eye on the dress of each and every participant entering the garba venue.

Organisers are more than happy to follow the order, as they believe it helps in maintaining the sacred and spiritual atmosphere associated with the worship of the Goddess during the nine nights of Navratri.

"Dandiya-Garbas are a form of worship. No one should be allowed to wear anything that can spoil the sanctity attached to the festival," said Nitin Bhardwaj, the organiser of Race Course Club, one of the biggest organisers of commercial garba in Saurashtra. The other big player, Pioneer too is following suit.

Bhardwaj, who is also the Rajkot city BJP president, added: "We ask participants not to come in backless or low waist dresses. Though we agree that it is an individual choice, but we aim to maintain a decorum. It is an arvachin (traditional) event and not a fashion parade."

Sinha said that the order has been issued on the basis of the existing law of obscene conduct. He added: "Only transparent clothes have been banned in the order."

Heading: Govt sits tight over retired cop’s service-extension request - Indian Express
Content:
Rebuffed by his family and the government, the past six months have been a struggle for acceptance and survival for 18-year-old Narendra Dhobi, a fisherman from Omar Gaun in Valsad district. Life turned for the worse since Dhobi was detected HIV positive in a Pakistani jail in Karachi. When sent back, his family showed him the door and the state government turned down all his pleas for seeking rehabilitation and medication.
