Dhobi was arrested by the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA) along with other fishermen in January 2008. A health check up by the Karachi Jail authorities, which confirmed his HIV positive status, was only the beginning of a tough time ahead for him.

In April 2008, after the HIV test, the Pakistani authorities sent him back on humanitarian grounds.

But as Dhobi said, home coming has been sadder. "My family did not accept me and the government refused to provide any help," he said.

He moved from pillar to post, from the AIDS control agencies to the Health Department officials and even Minister Jay Narayan Vyas for support, but in vain.

Let alone medical support, Dhobi is still awaiting the compensation he is entitled to from the state government, which is given to every fishermen lodged in a Pakistani jail.

"The Fisheries Department pays Rs 50 per day compensation to fishermen lodged in Pakistani jails. Even after six months, I am awaiting the amount due to me," he said.

He added: "I have been supported by the NGO 'People Living with HIV positive' in Surat. They have sponsored my treatment at Reliance Hospital in Surat. I want to go home and I want the government to support me to start a new life. I have no job and money to get the medication."

H Dave, Deputy Commissioner, state Fisheries Department said the compensation release in the case of Dhobi has got delayed due to technical reasons. "He declared Maharashtra as his native place in the registration form submitted to the Fisheries Department, but he belongs to Valsad in south Gujarat."

The official added that formalities have been completed and Dhobi will soon receive an amount of over Rs 6,000 from the Fisheries Department.

Meanwhile, Vyas told Newsline that he will look into the matter. "We will get the case details. The state government is willing to extend all possible help to anyone in distress," he said.

Heading: State SMEs look to traditional ways of business: study - Indian Express
Content:
The Modi government, voluntarily gave four consecutive extensions to Noel Parmar, the investigating officer in the Godhra carnage case. But it is yet to respond to a service extension application filed by V L Solanki, the retired CID officer who blew the lid off the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case of November 26, 2005.

The 59-year-old policeman retired as an Inspector from the CID Ahmedabad zone office on August 31, 2008, after a year-long service extension. Nearly a month before his retirement, Solanki had sent an application to his seniors seeking another extension on grounds that he was closely associated with the inquiry and the investigations into the Sohrabuddin case, which is now being heard by the Supreme Court. The government, however, is yet to respond to this application.

If sources in the Police Bhavan in Gandhinagar are to be believed, then Solanki might have to face disappointment this time. "His application seeking one year extension is lying in the DGP's office for nearly two months and I don't think it is even being considered now," said a senior IPS officer on condition of anonymity.

Interestingly, even Gopal Subramaniam, the Additional Solicitor General (ASG) and amicus curiae in the Sohrabuddin fake encounter case, had acknowledged the detailed probe that Solanki had conducted in the case.

The ASG had criticised the Gujarat government for alleged attempts to scuttle the investigations and protect the accused policemen. He had also submitted before a bench comprising Justice Tarun Chatterjee and Justice Aftab Alam, earlier this week, that "Solanki's report was neither taken into consideration while filing the charge sheet nor was it brought to the notice of the apex court by Inspector General of Police Geetha Johri."

Acting on a writ petition filed by Rubabuddin, brother of Sohrabuddin, and his mother, Jaibunisa in January 2006, two months after the fake encounter, the Supreme Court had asked the Gujarat DGP for further inquiry into the case. Subsequent to this, the CID (crime) was asked to inquire into the matter.

Solanki was a key member in this team headed by Geetha Johri.

It was also Solanki, who had found that Sohrabuddin and Kausarbi were picked up by a team of Gujarat ATS, when they were travelling from Hyderabad, and then shot in a fake encounter by the Gujarat and Rajasthan Police. Solanki had also established that Sohrabuddin and Kausarbi were kept in confinement at Disha farm in Jamiatpura near Gandhinagar.

In his detailed report, Solanki had mentioned the names of the accused police officers and their role in the murder.

Interestingly, while Solanki, who stared his career as a Sub-Inspector in 1974, was promoted only once in his entire service life, Noel Parmar, who rose to the rank of Deputy Superintendent along with his four extensions .

Court grants interim bail to Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case accused

Express News Service

Ahmedabad, October 3

The Ahmedabad City District and Sessions Court, on Friday, granted interim bail to police officer Balkrishna Chaube, who had been arrested in connection with the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case.

Additional Sessions Judge P B Desai granted bail to Chaube from October 13 to 27 on the ground that he has to see his ailing mother, who is suffering from a lung disease and is supposed to undergo a major surgery on October 18.

CID (Crime), the investigating agency in the case, had arrested Chaube in June 2007 for his alleged involvement in the case. He was working as an Inspector in the Gujarat Police Anti Terror Squad (ATS) in November 2005, when Sohrabuddin was gunned down in a joint

operation by the ATS and a Special Task Force (STF) of the Rajasthan Police.

Chaube was posted at the Ahram Bungalows in the outskirts of Gandhinagar where the police had allegedly confined Sohrabudin's wife, Kauserbi. He is expected to be one of the important witnesses in the disappearance of Kauserbi.

Out of the 13 policemen arrested in the case so far, only Deputy Superintendent of Police Narendra Amin and Rajasthan IPS officer Dinesh M N were granted bail by the Sessions Court, which the Gujarat High Court cancelled later.

Earlier, IPS officer D G Vanzara, the key accused in the case, was granted three days interim bail in February 2007.

Heading: Strike against ban on groundnut oil keeps markets closed for third day - Indian Express
Content:
A CII-Deloitte study titled 'fast growing enterprises of Gujarat: scaling new heights' has found that the Small and Medium enterprises (SME) in the state are inward looking and look to traditional models of growth. The study has found that the SMEs in the state will be in danger if they do not change their mindset and look towards unconventional, inorganic and aggressive growth models.

The study concluded after examining the responses of 55 fast growing industries that most of the SMEs consider revenue growth as the most important strategic focus for growing fast and big. Most of the industries believe that accelerated growth can be achieved through cost efficiency and product differentiation coupled with revenue growth.

The study shows that SMEs still believe in the organic model of growth rather than inorganic, which is considered as the faster model of growth globally. A large number of state SMEs identified traditional models like quality improvement, enhancement of productivity and brand building as crucial elements for increasing revenue.

Most of the SMEs in Gujarat are unwilling to raise funds through non-conventional methods of private equity, mergers and acquisitions. This is because Gujarati entrepreneurs do not want to lose ownership.

"In order to grow big, enterprises need to break down the conventional wisdom of growth and need to explore opportunities of multi-fold growth in revenues through mergers and acquisitions and joint ventures," the study says.

The pan-Gujarat study covered a cross section of industries and based it on three major aspects—growth strategies, strategic decisions and important growth challenges faced by the SMEs. The 84-page study report will be released at a function on October 7.

Heading: City students deliver ‘peace’ punch to Rain God’s watery plans - Indian Express
Content:
The ban on export of edible oils kept the market yards in Saurasthra and Kutch closed for the third day on Friday. Farmers and other people associated with subsidiary industries of groundnut oil gave a firm signal to continue with the strike indefinitely till their demands were met.

The trouble in the edible oil industry, and more specifically the groundnut oil industry in the state was scripted on March 18 this year. A circular issued by the Director General of Foreign Trade banned the export of all edible oils from the country for one year, to tide over the rising inflation and soaring oilseed prices.

While Friday saw no trading in groundnut oil, business went as usual for cottonseed oil and palm oil, both of which saw slight decrease in prices due to a slump in the Malaysian market. The Malaysian markets influence both cottonseed and palm oil; Malaysia being the major exporter of edible oils to India.

For the farmers in Saurasthra, which is the predominant groundnut growing area in the state and produced a bumper crop of 21 lakh metric tonnes this year, a ban on exports means settling for a lesser amount as the prices in the domestic market are not that high.

The quantity of groundnut oil exported every year from the state is in the region of 20,000 metric tonnes.

Praful Senjalia, president of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh (BKS) who is supporting the strike in all the 24 market yards of Saurashtra said: "We will continue with the closure of market yards till our demands are met. The ban on export will result in losses for all. This year, the prices have come down to Rs 400-450 (per 20 kg) from the Rs 550-600 last year."

The BKS has now submitted a charter of demands, which includes increasing the minimum support price for groundnut and removing the embargo on exports.

Senjalia said: "At the prevailing price, the farmers will not be able to even recover the costs."

The Saurashtra Oil Millers Association (SOMA), a powerful lobby, has also thrown its weight behind the strike. SOMA president Uka Patel said: "The support price for groundnut should be increased to Rs 700-800. Unless it happens it will not be feasible for the farmers. There should also be no ban on exports. It is a premium product and hardly forms seven percent of the edible oil production in the country. It has no connection with the price rise."

Another factor that has pushed the price of groundnut seed lower this year is the cheap availability of substitutes like Palm oil. Due to the reduction of import duties, palm oil is now available for Rs 350-400 per 20 kg, according to industry sources.

The impact of the closure of market yards, however, is not significant in the short term. A market insider said: "In the short term, it will just affect the physical availability of groundnut. It will not affect the commodity exchanges. It is just an attempt to increase the prices of the fresh batch that will land in the markets."

Heading: ACB arrests three on corruption charges in separate operations - Indian Express
Content:
Students from 18 schools in the city brave heavy showers to stage a brilliant display of art installations

Picture this: a thousand origami exhibits drenched in the rain. A few posters with ink blots as reminders that once they carried significant messages. A bunch of students mouthing motivational songs of peace under a tree with the erstwhile royalty as their audience. It all sounds a bit too cinematic to happen in reality. Yet all of this happened in the city on Thursday.

Students from 18 schools in the city braved a heavy downpour to stage a brilliant display of art installations under a tree in the vicinity of Maharaja Fatehsinh Museum. They were part of a Peace Awareness Initiative Display conducted by a new city learning centre, Aura. The theme was 'One For Peace on Gandhi Jayanti'. There was no contest or audience. Yet, indomitable spirit and courage reigned supreme, as the children stayed put, undeterred by the rain.

Aneri Patel (11) from New Era School said: "My classmates and I had come across a story, in a workshop conducted by Aura few months ago, on a certain Sadako Sasaki, who died of leukaemia due to radiation from Hiroshima bombing. She had absolute faith in the origami concept, which states that a sick person can recover completely by making a thousand paper cranes. Sadako made 644 cranes, but died before she could reach thousand. Touched by her faith, a group completed the number and carried out a fund raising campaign in Japan to erect a Children Peace Monument."

Jagruti Gala, the founder of Aura, said, "It was after we received positive feedback from the students during an origami workshop that we decided to conduct this daylong event."

The verve of the students was infectious after the workshop. They came up with some interesting lines such as 'Shape of peace is a straight line' and 'Peace is when our intelligence is not measured by exams', said Jignasha Pandya, another member of Aura.

The display had posters with inspirational messages like 'In the world full of peace, every one will live with ease' on them. Students sang songs like Yaad Taari Nahi Re Bhulay and Amare Rehu Gandhi Bapu from a small podium. The display was watched by the members of the erstwhile royal family of Baroda.

Heading: CCTV in women’s loo: GU panel hears complaints against V-C - Indian Express
Content:
In three separate operations, the Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB), Gujarat, on Thursday arrested three persons, including a police officer, on charges of corruption in Rajkot.

The accused have been identified as Siddique Sathar, an Assistant Sub Inspector with Rajkot police, Rasikbhai Kanjibhaim, Circle Officer of Mamludar office in Surendranagar and Ajit Rathod, Talati of village Ranpur in rural Ahmedabad.

They were arrested in three different operations laid by the ACB on Thursday.

Sathar was arrested while accepting a bribe of Rs 7,500 from one Jeevabhai Godhania.

Rashikbhai and Rathod were nabbed while they were accepting Rs 1,000 and Rs 1,100 respectively from one Raghubha Parmar and Babu Okhadia, the ACB said.

The arrests were made following complaints filed against the three accused.

Police traps were laid using the complainants in the three respective cases, Godhania, Parmar and Okhadia as decoys.

"The trio has been booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA) and the investigations are on," an ACB officer said.

Heading: Man poisons wife and daughters to death, hangs himself - Indian Express
Content:
Non-teaching staff had approached Women Development Cell over the issue on September 25

The special committee formed on September 28 to look into the complaints by the women non-teaching staff of Gujarat University against Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Parimal Trivedi, over the installation of CCTV cameras in the women's toilets, met all the complainants on Friday.

The three-member special committee of Sudhir Nanavati, Rajshree Bhatt and Mukul Shah listened to all the complaints for more than three hours in the evening and decided to meet again on Sunday afternoon.

According to sources, discussions on other matters like promotion of the senior staff members, revocation of two suspension orders to two non-teaching staff members and transfer of 10 other non-teaching staff members also took place.

The special committee, however, refused to give details of the talk between them and the complainants.

On September 25, the women non-teaching staff had given a written complaint to the Women Development Cell (WDC) of the GU over the CCTV issue. The special committee was formed on September 28 at the previous Executive Council (EC) meeting.

Meanwhile, the members of the Gujarat State Youth Congress and the National Students Union of India (Gujarat state) walked into the office of the V-C and gheraoed him. They also asked for the resignation of the V-C.

Mihir Shah, president, Gujarat State Youth Congress and Indervijaysinh Gohil, president, National Students Union of India (Gujarat) called for a stop on discussing GUJCOC. They also asked Trivedi why GUJCOC was discussed at the last EC meeting on September 28, as it was not on the agenda list.

They said the V-C wanted to earn the favour of the ruling BJP for securing a second term at the office. They called for withdrawing GUJCOC from the agenda within 72 hours, pending which they will start a demonstration.

Heading: Two gruesome murders in tribal Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
In a shocking incident, a 35-year-old man allegedly committed suicide after killing his wife and two daughters at his residence in Shiv Shakti Society in Radhanpur area of Patan district on Friday morning.

Ashok Thakkar, who worked as a small time vendor, allegedly gave poison to his wife Sonal (28) and daughters, Foram (2) and one-month-old Dhruvi, before hanging himself from a ceiling fan at his residence.

According to the police, Thakkar may have taken the drastic step because of the severe financial crisis he was going through.

Thakkar's brother, Kamlesh, said that the former had taken a house loan about six months ago and was facing difficulties in paying back the installments.

"This seems to be the reason that provoked Thakkar to take the extreme step," Radhanpur police sub inspector, R L Nimana said.

The dead bodies have been sent for post-mortem. The police are waiting for the reports to ascertain the time and cause of the deaths. Meanwhile a case of accidental deaths has been registered and the police have also filed a case against Thakkar on charges of three murders.

Heading: MSU social work students out to help dyslexic slum children - Indian Express
Content:
Two gruesome murders were reported at Naswadi and Rangpur talukas in the tribal belt of Vadodara. In the first case, a man allegedly killed his brother-in-law at Naswadi, while at Rangpur a wife killed her husband after the latter physically assaulted her.

According to the police, one Ghunghrabhai Tapariya (35) attacked his brother-in-law, Naskar Ramji (37) when the latter was on his way to a garba function alone on Wednesday in Dhansimha village. Ramji was beaten to death on the spot. The murder weapon was a wooden log, which the assailant had used to deliver deadly blows on the deceased's head and chest. Tapariya's sister Pinta (23) had eloped with Ramji six months ago as per the Bhil custom. But Tapariya was against this marriage, as he had filed a complaint against Ramji in the Adivasi gram panchayat for cattle theft. He had, therefore, applied to the panchayat alleging that Ramji was morally corrupt and had abducted his sister. However, the panchayat had cleared him after the couple returned from Talav, a neighbouring adivasi tribal village.

In the other incident, Kasturi Nayak (41) of Badaliya village under Rangpur police station attacked her husband, Kalsinh Nayak, with a sharp object after being a victim of domestic violence. Sub-Inspector V L Patel said that Kalsinh would come back home drunk and beat Kasturi up. On Thursday, a scuffle ensued between the two and Kasturi killed her husband.

Heading: Civic ‘slum’ber: Sewerage a major problem with improper maintenance by municipality - Indian Express
Content:
To initiate a survey on children who have behavioural, emotional, scholastic and learning disabilities in two slum areas of the city

When the film Taare Zameen Par hit the theatres a year ago, city-based NGOs and various other institutions across Gujarat were quick to begin intervention programmes to help families and teachers of children who were mentally challenged and had learning disabilities.

But seemingly, this sensitisation drive just lasted for a

few months. It is now that

M S University (MSU) Faculty

of Social Work (FSW) Child Guidance Clinic, in association with city-based NGO United Way of Baroda (UWB), is working towards community-based intervention in two slum areas of the city.

"Child Guidance Clinic has been providing in-house counseling to slum children for the last 32 years. However, there is a lack of awareness about such services being offered in these areas. Generally, parents visit us in the clinic only when their children, who have disabilities, are in a bad shape," said Dhramishtha Nanavati, counselor at the Child Guidance Clinic.

She added: "Thus, FSW students are in the process of initiating a survey on children who have behavioural, emotional, scholastic and learning disabilities in the slum areas of Kalyan Nagar and

Pensionpura."

The UWB has sanctioned

Rs 70,000 to the clinic for one year to carry out a survey in the slum areas.

The FSW students, as a part of their assignments, will interact with anganwadi workers, public as well as private schools and other institutions and individuals who are in direct touch with the slum children, said Nanavati.

"Our idea is to continue the community intervention programme for five years as the counseling of the child and his/her family is a long drawn process," she said.

Prof Arun Khasgiwala, FSW dean, said: "Such an activity needs to be carried out in the slum areas in order to make the slum population aware about the services provided by FSW."

The checklist for the survey has already been prepared and the students have started contacting anganwadi workers, said Nanavati.

Heading: Oriental Insurance ordered to pay Rs 18,000 to customer - Indian Express
Content:
Slums are often found in the abandoned sections of the cities. Sewerage and garbage disposal are the absolute necessities in these areas and the absence of these can pose a serious health hazards. The Slum Networking Programme (SNP), however, guarantees sewerage and solid waste management in the slums under its purview.

The SNP is active in 45 slums where sewerage facility has been provided. Every household has an individual drainage pipe connected to the main sewer in the neighbourhood. But the success of the SNP project at Sanjaynagar does not hold true for the rest of the slums that have been given the guaranteed facilities. Slums like Sinheshwariagar, one of the most discussed successful projects of SNP still has problems with sewerage.

Sarita Kanaji of Sinheshwari Nagar says: "We have got sewerage lines, but every second week, they get blocked. We have to send an application to the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) at least thrice before they send someone to clear it. We also have to pay Rs 5-10 to the man who cleans it. But most of the time, we have to clean it ourselves."

The slums of Hanuman Nagar and Narsinhji na Chapra at Gomtipur also face similar problems. .

According to Somaji Thanaji, of Narsinhji na Chapra, narrow sewerage lines have been laid by the AMC. Even after days of opposition, the government did not lay new drainage lines but merged the old drainage lines with the newly-constructed main cesspool provided under the programme.

Somaji further adds that the individual connections of the drains are connected to the main pipeline, which is seldom cleaned. The blockage of the main sewer leads to overflowing of individual sewers and even clogging in the toilets .

Slum pockets like Shri Om Nagar of Vanjara Vas have made pits in front of their homes to collect the wastewater. When it reaches the brim, they dispose it in front of their shanties. The wastewater collected thus leads to stench and filth outside the homes. Residents of Tulsibhagat ni chali at Pravinnagar had appealed to the AMC for drainage pipelines, but it has been over a year and there is still no help in sight.

"We paid to get a no-objection certificate (NOC). We even paid for the drainage connection, but nothing has materialised in the last one year. Every month, we go to the Usmanpura office to request the officials to lay the pipelines, but all that they tell us is that the pipeline is coming up in a week," says Sayra Khatik of Tulsibhagat in chali in Vanjara Vas of Pravinnagar.

The slum-dwellers are also entitled to benefits of solid waste management. The city generates more than 1400 tonnes of garbage everyday. The city is divided into five zones and 11 distribution centres to manage solid waste. There are about 9,000 sweepers in these five zones. The waste is collected and disposed of in the southwest fringe of Ahmedabad.

The Hanuman Nagar slum has been found to have poor waste management. This slum pocket consisting of 294 hutments has a sizeable population. Although waste collection is supposed to be done everyday, the visit of garbage collectors are few and far inbetween. The slums of Narsinhji na Chapra in Gomtipur also face the same predicament.

"The garbage collector doesn't come everyday and argues with us if we ask him to come regularly. Many times, we have collected the waste ourselves and have walked far to dispose it. The government had also assured us of dustbins, but it has been a yearlong wait already," says Savita Thanaji, a resident of Narsinhji na Chapra.

Even when the slum residents have expressed their willingness to pay for services, the speed of work has been reportedly slow. The substandard infrastructure of the slums falls apart during monsoons causing inconvenience to the residents.

The storm water drainage project has also not been satisfactory with the slums under SNP. There are about 42 discharge points out of which only 27 are functional. A considerable percentage of slums reportedly face severe problems during monsoon.

Heading: Buddhadeb’s Nano new Bengal dream is over - Indian Express
Content:
The Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Oriental Insurance to pay Gautam Shah, one of its customers, a sum of Rs 18,000 with nine per cent compound interest from the date of filing of complaint till realisation, and Rs 5,000 as cost.

The order was issued on a complaint filed by Consumer Education and Research Society on behalf of Gautam.

According to the complaint, Gautam had taken a personal accident policy from the insurance company with a risk cover of Rs 65,000 for himself and Rs 30,000 for his wife.

Gautam met with an accident while the policy was still in force. He was admitted to the hospital with serious injury on two toes of his right foot. He was discharged after the surgery, but experienced severe pain on his right leg. A consultation with another surgeon on the advice of the doctor, who had earlier treated him, revealed that gangrene had set in. Gautam was advised to go in for another surgery and get the second toe of his right foot amputated.

Gautam submitted his claim papers along with the treatment certificate from the surgeons, but Oriental Insurance, repudiated the claim on the grounds that the gangrene had set in due to diabetes, which Gautam had for the last 18 years, prior to taking the policy.

Gautam, who had been holding the policy for the last 18 years and renewing it every year, then complained to the Forum.

The insurers contended before the Forum that Gautam had neither intimated them of the accident nor sent the documents with the claim papers. They further said that the insured did not fall within the definition of 'consumer' under the Consumer Protection Act and that the operation done by the surgeons for gangrene suggestively indicated diabetes and not road accident.

The Forum, however, passed a verdict in favour of Gautam. It held that the insurers failed to prove with evidence that the operation on Gautam's foot was due to diabetes and not due to a road accident. It further said that the insurers had relied on the report of their panel doctor, who had neither treated Gautam nor had checked his injured leg.

Heading: SINGUR: BLAME GAME BEGINS IN LAST ACT - Indian Express
Content:
TATAS PULL OUT OF SINGUR: After meeting CM, Ratan Tata says we're shifting because of Mamata Banerjee, late-night protests break out in Singur

I think two years ago, I once mentioned that if somebody puts a gun to my head, you pull the trigger or you take the gun away because I have not moved my head. I think Ms (Mamata) Banerjee has pulled the trigger." With these words, chairman of Tata Motors Ratan Tata made announced what many had come to expect: he was pulling out of Singur — the world's cheapest car will not be manufactured in West Bengal.

Aware that Durga Puja — the state's most-awaited festival — is two days, Tata said: "Perhaps, it was not the best day to announce such a decision — on the eve of the Pujas. But we do not see any change in the horizon."

This announcement came after a meeting with Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen.

Looking visibly upset, Tata said: "The decision to move out the Nano plant was taken with great pain. It shatters many dreams we had. But at the end it's a great feeling, too. Great, because we feel we are doing the right thing."

Sources said that although Bhattacharjee and Sen were aware they were fighting a losing battle — with Mamata not yielding an inch — the finality of today's announcement came as a severe setback. Especially when the Chief Minister had made the Nano project the prime showpiece of his attempts to put what he boldly called the "wasted years of the state" behind.

Blaming Mamata's"destructive agitation," Sen said: "It is the saddest moment for the state on the eve of festivity." Late at night, a group of villagers in Singur set up a road block on the Durgapur Expressway protesting against Tatas' decision and threatened an indefinite blockade condemning Mamata Banerjee.

Asked where he planned to shift the Nano plant, Tata said that the company had offers from several states. "We have just taken this decision to shift today. We have not decided on where to shift. But, hopefully, there are locations with congenial environment. We do not have this kind of agitation either in Pantnagar or elsewhere," he said.

"We have to shift because of Mamata Banerjee, not because of any other reason created by the government," he said. "Banerjee publicly said that people of West Bengal decided that you should not be here."

Asked what transpired at the hour-long meeting today he had with state Chief Minister, Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, Tata said: "He was distressed. He was very persuasive that we do not move out of Singur. But I had to explain that we cannot run a plant when boundary walls are broken, we cannot run a plant with intimidation, we cannot run a plant with employees being assaulted, we cannot run a plant with police protection. At the end, whatever the loss or cost, we have to move out."

"He (Bhattacharjee) finally conceded," Tata said. "The decision to move out was ours. We parted as friends. We will continue to look at West Bengal in our future investment plans even if Nano moves out of Bengal...We believe and respect the trust, faith and confidence in Bhattacharjee's leadership. It has not diminished. I have assured the CM about future investments in Bengal. We continue to be bullish about what can happen in Bengal," Tata said.

He added that there was a need to understand why Tata Motors came to the state. "The Nano project was to be a showcase plant which would have enhanced the visibility of the state, created jobs for younger citizens and through the company's community programme would have enhanced the quality of life of the urban and rural population."

He said that those Singur residents who are being trained would become part of the Tata Motors family. "They will be deployed in other Tata facilities. They obviously can not remain in Singur," he said.

"Like our Prime Minister, I was hopeful for satisfactory solution until the last moment. I feel very sad," said West Bengal Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi, who had tried to broker a peace that never took shape.

Reacting to the decision, Mamata said it was a conspiracy by the West Bengal government and the Tatas to push her into a corner.

Trinamool Congress supporters in Singur are to hold a victory rally tomorrow. Banerjee also renewed her demand for return of land to the farmers.

Why this is a serious blow to Buddhadeb
* Mamata may be villain of the piece but fact is after the Nandigram bungle, the party and the govt couldn't assert themselves in Singur despite a favourable court order, despite a majority of the farmers on board.
* With 85% of the Nano plant complete, it was the only tangible, visible project. That's gone.
* Buddha's entire emphasis has been on inviting investment, promoting industry. Singur ghost will haunt him at every forum on industry. The fact that Nano was a global, not just an Indian, story has added to the damage.
* First time in over three decades, CPM's political clout rendered ineffective in the state

What next
* Buddha will have to fast forward Jindal Steel Plant, several other integrated steel projects, Bengal aerotropolis project (air port and industrial park), IT and Bio-tech, food processing units.
* Growing dissent in CPM as they see a weakened Chief Minister; Mamata supporters smell blood

Heading: Mamata disrupting state’s growth, says Nirupam - Indian Express
Content:
At Ground Zero, some rejoice other rue

Following the announcement of Tata Motors' small car plant pulling out from the state, public opinion seemed to be divided in Singur.

While those associated with the Save Farmland Committee rejoiced, many who had given up land and were expecting an economic revival in the area, rued the decision.

"This is a victory for our struggle," said Becharam Manna, convener of the Save Farmland Committee. Residents celebrated in Beraberi, Khaserbheri and Gopalnagar villages as the news of the Tata's pulling out reached around 7.30 pm.

Since morning, discussions in these villages centered round the meeting between Tata Motors' Chairman Ratan Tata and Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. Incidentally, the number of unwilling farmers was the highest in these villages. "We plan to take out a victory rally," added Manna.

On the other hand, villagers who had given up their land and were in the hope of getting a job expressed shock at the decision. "People here are very angry. There is dissatisfaction among those who had given up land. Others, too, were hoping for an economic revival in the area. We want the Tatas to stay," said Jiyarul Sheikh, a resident of Joymollah village. He added that some villagers plan to set up a dharna manch at the gates of the Tata Motor's factory to persuade the company not to leave Singur.

Dibakar Das, a local CPM leader, said: "We will go now to the people to make them understand what a huge loss this has been for Singur."

The police, meanwhile, have been asked to be on alert. A source in the district police said there are apprehensions that a law and order situation may arise in the area. The officers, however, refused to comment on the issue.

"We are keeping a close watch on the situation and are awaiting orders from the higher authorities," said Kalyan Bandopadhayay, SDPO, Singur.

Heading: Pullout a conspiracy to malign Oppn: Mamata - Indian Express
Content:
State Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen blamed the "destructive and irresponsible movement" led by the Trinamool Congress for the pullout of the Nano project from Singur.

Addressing the media, Sen said the Tatas did not want to run the plant under police protection.

The chief minister himself had requested Ratan Tata during the meeting not to pull out of Singur. The government did not anticipate this kind of outcome, Sen remarked.

The state government did not support the decision of Ratan Tata. In other states too, people have held protests outside factories but that did not lead to their closure. But he also justified the decision of the Tata Motors. "The company has a commitment to its shareholders and bankers as well as a deadline for the rollout of the car," he said, "so they did not want to continue with the Singur project."

Sen admitted that the decision of the Tata Motors would have a negative impact on the overall image of the state and affect future investment. Now, it was the task of the state to revive its image.

But he assured that the withdrawal of Nano would have not effect on the other projects already in the pipeline. Tata has assured the government about the implementation of its other projects, which are under construction. He also appreciated the role of the state government and its support and cooperation, Sen said.

The Trinamool Congress and Opposition parties took a stand to disrupt the development of the state — be it industry, road projects or anything else, he said.

In reply to a query, he ruled out the possibility of returning the land to the farmers. Some other industry would be set up at Singur as the 997 acres had been acquired for industrial purposes, he indicated.

Industry talk
It is indeed regretful that the Tatas have had to pull out of Singur.

The CII feels that the Tatas have been very patient. The political consensus should have happened and such an iconic project should have come up in the state of West Bengal
Chandrajeet Banerjee
Director General, CII

It is bad news for Bengal. It will discourage investment in the state and to create an atmosphere of investment will take some time
P K Agarwal
President, Bharat Chamber of Commerce

New investors will defer their plans of investing in our state for the time being and this is a bad Puja gift
Sanjay Budhia,
President, Indian Chamber of Commerce

The Tata project could have brought about a major change in the industrial scenario of Bengal
A statement released by FICCI

Heading: Rural Bengal to come alive at Behala pandal - Indian Express
Content:
The first reactions from Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on the Tata Motors' decision to pull out from West Bengal were aimed at both the Left Front government and the car making firm.

She said that the pull out decision is a conspiracy by the Left Front government and the Tatas against the Opposition. "This government doesn't want industrialisation and never has. If they were so pro-industry, they would have agreed to our demands," she said.

Terming the comment made by Tata Motors' chairman Ratan Tata that the Opposition's ongoing protest in Singur had mainly contributed to their decision to shift the Nano small car project out of the state "unfortunate", she said: "I will not respond to Ratan Tata's comment about our protest and demands, as I don't want to get personal."

Banerjee had been demanding return of 400 acres of land — acquired by the government and leased to Tata Motors — to the "unwilling farmers." The Trinamool and other political parties jointly held a dharna outside the car factory site that led to Tata Motors to suspend their work on September 2. At that time, Tata said that his company would not like to work under police protection. "There's no danger in Singur. Our protest was peaceful. We have not hampered work at the Nano plant. If the Tatas had really wanted, they could have carried on with their work. It's clear that the Tatas wanted to move out from the very beginning," Banerjee said.

Adding that the exit of the Tatas will have no bearing on their agitation against land acquisition, Banerjee said the land "has to be returned." On Tuesday, Banerjee had met UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and is said to have asked for Centre's intervention to resolve the Singur issue. During the meeting, she had said she was not "anti-industry".

Heading: Metro Cash and Carry licence runs into rough weather again - Indian Express
Content:
Puja pandals in West Bengal have gone through a string of changes, evolving according to the mood and taste of the generation organising the Puja. From simple, colourful bamboo structures to globalised replicas of Sanchi Stupas and Eiffel Tower, pandals in the state and now socially relevent themes, they have come a full circle.

The theme Pujas, however, which appealed to the people for a number of years, seem to have become lifeless eyesores for the present generation. Hence, to add some zing, the Puja committees are including live performances to attract more people.

Behala Nutan Dal puja committee in Kolkata, too, has joined the bandwagon. In order to make their partially rundown village mansion look lively, the organisers have invited a group of ten artistes — who specialise in singing tarjas — to stay in their pandal all through the five days of Pujas.

"Tarjas used to be integral to most rural Pujas. The tradition, however, has declined rapidly over the last few decades to the point of extinction," said Debobroto Mukherjee, an organiser of the Puja. Thus, to give the artistes their due and also to introduce the present generation to cultural strains that are slowly dying out, the organisers found out the tarja singers from Netra, a small village in 24-Parganas.

"We have specially made an uthon-like structure where the tarja singers will be available in shifts," added Mukherjee. Tarja, depicted memorably in films like Anthony Firingi (1981), is a form of oral poetry where the performers usually debate on various social, political, religious and cultural issues in a musical way.

"One of these singers claims to have a school in the South 24 Parganas," said the organiser. Apart from tarja singers, the pandal will also have ten baul singers who will add a rustic charm to their theme. "The artistes will try to engage the audience by composing various kinds of music," said Mukherjee.

Artiste Rono Banerjee has conceptualised the Rs 14-lakh Puja pandal as a rural mansion, a section of which is in a dilapidated state to show the lack of care.

"I have tried to base this year's Puja theme on the migration of Bengalis to other states, due to which the ancestral homes and the traditions find it difficult to survive," said the artiste.

The pandal, in fact, tells a story about an imaginary village called Jibonpur, which, according to the artiste, reflects the issues of several villages in the state.

"I have created the structure around a story where one of the two brothers is trying to hold on to old traditions while the younger brother has no charm for home," he said.

The structure, created in a space surrounded by closely-built houses, stands out for the use of space.

The biggest challenge for the organisers was to cover up the façade of the surrounding houses to make the village home look authentic.

Work for the pandal started in April which involved the growing of trees on the land so that an authentic look could be given. "The base, including the verandahs, has been made of cement," says Banerjee.

Moss has grown on the walls over the last six months. A space in the structure will also house a chariot. Broken walls on the other side of the structure and pigeons flying all around the house add to the authentic feel.

Heading: New Town to get new, state-of-the-art police station - Indian Express
Content:
Following Tata Motor's pull out from the state, German major Metro Cash & Carry's licence renewal has also run into rough weather.

Although Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee had instructed the Forward Bloc to not impose any conditions on the German major that might force it to pull out, the Bloc has complicated the matter by setting business guidelines for the company.

To settle the licence issue, a meeting was held between the CPM and the Forward Bloc on Friday, following which, Bloc members said the German major would have to comply with a number of guidelines to get the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) licence on October 10.

Bloc leader Naren Chatterjee said that along with the APMC Act 1972 and APMC Rules 1982, the company has to accept the guidelines drafted by the Left Front.

According to the guidelines, the company has to ensure that it will not indulge in any direct and indirect retail business in future. The billing amount for a single item purchase has to be above Rs 5,000 and in case of two items, the amount will be doubled.

Besides these, the retailers, who buy agricultural produce from the German major, must have an APMC licence to sell it. Metro Cash & Carry cannot opt for contract farming. Moreover, the company has to notify the government about minimum quantity of various commodities to be sold.

These guidelines are neither mentioned in the APMC Act 1972 nor in the APMC Rules 1982, but the Bloc members said the company has to sign an MoU that will include all the guidelines before the licence is issued to it.

"There are provisions in the APMC Act that some guidelines can be imposed on retail and wholesale majors. We have to restrict these kinds of businesses in the interest of the poor," Chatterjee said.

The German major has, however, preferred to remain tight-lipped on the issue.

"We cannot comment on the issue until we are officially informed about the meeting as we have not received any official correspondence from the APMC Board yet. But we are not bound to accept any such terms and conditions that are not applicable for other companies doing business in the state. The law must be uniform," a spokesperson of Cash Metro Cash & Carry said.

Heading: See Durga’s 51 avatars under a single roof - Indian Express
Content:
In keeping with the modern look and facilities of New Town, the state government wanted to create a modern police station, equipped with the state-of-the-art technology for the area. As a first step, a new building of New Town police station, which will in future become an outpost, was inaugurated on Friday.

In the near future, one would be able see closed-circuit-cameras on the 10-lane roads of New Town. Seated in their offices, policemen would be able to monitor traffic movements and immediately identify any vehicle that commits a crime or violates traffic rules. This is just one of the many technologies that the state government has in its plan for policing in the New Town area, said Housing Minister Goutam Deb.

"If the police department does not have the money, Housing Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd. (HIDCO) will provide it," claimed Deb, who is also the chairman of HIDCO.

It is predicted that New Town will have a total population of more than 2.5 lakh in the near future.

"Keeping in mind the estimated population, we need more police officers to maintain law and order of this metropolitan city," said Surajit Kar Purokayastha, IG (South Bengal), West Bengal police.

There are also plans for setting up a new commissionerate for New Town, said Deb.

This vision, however, seems unreal if one takes into account the strength of the new police station, the first to be set up in New Town.

The police station has a strength of just 18 police personnel with two sub-inspectors, four assistant sub-inspectors and 12 constables.

According to the national regulations and recommendation of various committees, a population of one lakh people spread over an area of one km should have a police strength of 361 police personnel.

"It is good that a separate police station has been created. But the police personnel would not be sufficient to man the entire area," said Amal Sarkar, a resident of Utsa residential complex, located a stone's throw away from the new police station.

"All the housing complexes have to hire private security men for safety. We do feel unsafe as it really gets deserted after evening," said Maloy Das, another resident.

Glimpse of technology
* CCTVs will be installed on the roads of New Town.
* Policemen will monitor traffic movements and immediately identify any vehicle that commits a crime or violates traffic rules, seated from their office

Heading: Puja organisers queue up for temporary power connections - Indian Express
Content:
Well, how many avatars of Goddess Durga are you aware of? According to mythology, the goddess appears in 108 forms. Of these, devotees will see 51 avatars when they visit the Ranikuthi pandal near GD Birla School.

Moving away from the quintessentially traditional concept, the Netaji Jatiya Sebadal has chosen this unique concept for their pandal.

"We will have 51 images of Durga for the first time in Bengal. Most of us know that there are 108 different avatars of Goddess Durga. But to see them together at a single Puja pandal was never possible before. To make this idea happen we have decided that there will be 51 images of Durga at our Puja ground," said Sayantan Mukherjee, cultural secretary, Netaji Jatiya Sebadal.

The various forms of the goddess will be on display for the devotees that will include Mahishashuramardini, Ugratara, Aparupa, Sarveswari, Kushmanda, Parbati, Chakreswari, Ambika, Chandrabati, Kaktarani, Bikalakshmi, Amrashur, Ugrachanda, Bogola, Kamala, Mahamaya, Narasingha, Mahalakshmi, Padmabati, Baisnavi, Shondamata, Bipadtarini, Kalidurga, Mahakal, Shailoputi, Gouri, Bhabani and Baishnamata.

The 5,000-sq ft pandal will be adorned with wood work and illumination. As one enters the temple-like structure of the main pandal, one can see two big structures of Natmandir displaying eight of Durga's forms while several other smaller Natmandirs will have one idol each of the goddess.

The biggest of the Natmandirs will house the main Durga idol — Mahishashuramardini.

The main idol will be made of clay and earth, including its dress and jewellery unlike the other forms of Durga. "We believe that it is one of the most innovative themes and are hoping it will be acclaimed as one of the best Pujas in the town," said Mukherjee.

Heading: PTTI students protest against HC ruling - Indian Express
Content:
With Durga Puja just a few days away, nearly 3,000 Puja committees have got the approval for temporary power connections from CESC, indicating towards a growing awareness among Puja organisers to abide by the law and not indulge in electricity theft. "CESC has already processed more than 3,000 applications for temporary connections and a few more are under consideration. Last year, 3,040 pandals had applied for connections," executive director of CESC D K Sen said.

Power consumption in pandals is estimated to be 3 million units this year. However, many power-consuming pandals have applied for lesser loads as compared to last year. The Maddox Square Puja committee, which had applied for a load of 340 kw, has reduced it to 316 kw this Puja. Similarly, the Ekdalia Evergreen Puja committee has applied for 160 Kw compared to its last year's demand of 175 kw.

To deal with power disruptions during Pujas, CESC's Loss Control Cell has decided to launch a special drive against pilferages and unauthorised connections. According to CESC officials, the company has formed 40 teams to check 1,500 pandals across the city.

Besides usual power supply provided by the West Bengal State Electricity Development Corporation, CESC has made special arrangements to procure 100 mw from Madhya Pradesh.

Although CESC has already tested the option of 20 kilovolt generators to provide power during service faults in some areas, the power supplying company is planning to standardise the practice.

"In some areas, we used to run temporary generators during service faults, but they were scattered trial runs. Now, we plan to standardise this practice," Sen said.

Heading: Kolkata police, fire department conduct mock drills - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTI) came out on the streets on Friday to protest against the Calcutta High Court ruling derecognising 122 of the 142 PTTIs in the state.

Thousands of students of the institute participated in the rally at Esplanade. Kolkata police arrested 272 students, when they refused to lift the blockade at the crossing and demanded to meet the school education minister.

A scuffle broke out between the students and the police, with the former being forcibly taken to the police headquarters. They were detained till late evening, after which they were released.

The rally, in which nearly 1,500 students participated, began from College Square at 12 noon and reached Esplanade at 2 pm. The students burnt the effigy of the School Education minister, Partha De, at Esplanade and outside Calcutta University.

On October 1, the Calcutta High Court derecognised some of the institutes on the grounds that they were operating without obtaining the permission of the National Council for Teachers Education.

Later in the day, the Chhattra Parishad, the students' wing of Congress, also came out in support of the students of the PTTIs. "We will send a delegation to the Human Resource and Development Minister, Arjun Singh, explaining the situation to him and the fact that the future of thousands of students would be jeopardised due to this decision," said Sourav Chakraborty, state president, Chhattra Parishad.

"We think that the Centre should intervene as the state government is not serious about the issue. We will also participate in the demonstration at Rani Rashmoni Crossing on October 16 along with the PTTI students," he added.

The students owing allegiance to the All India Democratic Students Organisation also participated in the rally.

"We want the state government to find out if an ordinance can be moved and the degrees of the students who have passed out can be recognised. It is a question of the future of thousands of students and if the government does not think seriously about the matter we will have to launch state-wide protests on the issue," said Ashok Rudra, a PTTI students union leader.

Heading: BESU panel to look into appointments, promotions - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata police and the Fire Service Department organised a joint mock bomb scare drill on Friday to check the preparedness of their personnel for any such eventuality during Pujas.

After the drill, senior officers of both the departments expressed satisfaction on the preparations.

Around 7:15 am, the Fire Service Department received a call from the Kolkata police headquarters at Lalbazar about a suspected bomb planted at College Square. Similar calls were made to the bomb disposal squad, the College Street police station and the local security authorities, asking them to immediately rush to the spot.

"Since the police are on a high alert, our officers immediately reached the spot," Deputy Commissioner (Headquarters) Vineet Goyel said.

The entire area was sealed off and the bomb squad launched a search operation in the area. The fire brigade personnel also reached the spot with their firefighting equipment.

"We received a bomb threat call from the police. Our firefighters were ready to face any eventuality and they reached the spot all prepared," Director-General of the Fire Services Department Gopal Bhattacharya said.

Except commanding officers of both the departments, nobody knew anything about the drill. "This was done to ensure that everyone took the matter seriously and their agility could be tested," Bhattacharya said.

Similar mock drills were carried out at two multiplexes of the city and the New Market area.

Heading: Writers’ Workshop completes 50 years of literary glory - Indian Express
Content:
The Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) has appointed a committee to look into appointments and promotions of faculty and other officials of the university since 2000.

The representatives of the Bengal Engineering and Science University Teachers Association (BESUTA) have, however, said the decision was a retaliation by the university authorities as the teachers' association had objected to the appointment of the university registrar earlier.

The committee was set up by the university's Board of Management and is headed by Arun Kiran Chakraborty, an educationist. The committee will submit its report directly to the board of management.

"Had the decision been taken in honest spirit, we would have appreciated it. But it seems a retaliation and we condemn it," secretary of the teachers' association Manas Hira said.

The association said all the appointments and promotions were made by the Board of Management and if any irregularities were found by the panel, the board should be held responsible for it.

Heading: Difference of opinion crops up among HERC members - Indian Express
Content:
Ever since it was founded in 1958, the Writers' Workshop in Kolkata has not only produced nearly 3,800 copies of literary works, but has also given the world of English literature a number of Indian geniuses.

To mark the workshop's 50th anniversary, the first volume of the recreated book and DVD version of The Mahabharata of Vyasa was launched by Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi at a function on Friday evening. The occasion also aimed at honouring Professor P Lal, the founder of the Writers workshop.

Holy Cow, a book of poetry by Surendra Nihal Singh, a former editor of The Indian Express, was also released on the occasion.

The workshop, which has provided a platform to many celebrated literary figures like Vikram Seth, Anita Desai, Nissim Ezekiel and Ruskin Bond, was founded by Lal to make up for the lack of publishers interested in Indian writers writing in English.

Speaking on the occasion, Gandhi said that a few people possess the gift of words and Lal was one of them who utilised it to the fullest. "There is an organic tactility that came out of the Writers Workshop," said Gandhi.

Prof Lal, who has been associated with the St Xavier's College, however, claimed to have been blessed for doing such kind of works.

"There are 6,000 small presses in the city, run in small garages or in the corner of a room. They are run by young Bengalis to inspire people, promote culture and instill literary values. Those volumes are sold at low prices. I am proud to be born in a city that promotes literature," said Lal.

Lal, who is known for his translated version of The Mahabharata, also spoke about the need for the four ideals — artha, dharma, kama and moksha — in literary text for the betterment of life.

He said while most people appreciated his contribution to literature, the real contribution came from the family of binders who had been binding his books for generations.

"I am a translator. In today's fast world people read books but they don't really understand them. It is a translator who has to explore every single word," he said.

Also present on the occasion were luminaries like filmmakers Suresh Kohli and Siddharth Kak, professor of Dhaka University Sayeed Islam and former diplomat Krishnan Srinivasan, most of whose works had been published by Prof Lal's workshop. Kak, whose only book of poetry had been released by the workshop, also read out portions of his poetry.

Heading: State set to get four new flying training centres - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission is reportedly planning to remand back the Annual Revenue Report (ARR) proposal of the UHBVN and DHBVN for the year 2008-09 to the state power utilities. The decision was arrived at by a majority of two members in the three-member commission, including the chairman, while one member had dissented. The two distribution companies had proposed a tariff hike to fill the revenue gap, which seems to be the bone of contention between members.

Tej Singh Tewatia, the HERC member who dissented, said there was no provision in the Regulatory Commission Act for a remand-back of the proposal at this stage. The commission could either accept or reject it, but could not remand it back, he said.

Expressing his difference with the majority, Tewatia said,"I reject the aforesaid majority decision of the commission as illegal and ultra-wires. Seeking more clarification at this stage,when the financial year to which the ARR and tariff proposal relates is almost half over, is also not appropriate."

His basic concern, he said, was not whether the tariff was hiked or not, but he only wanted a timely decision on the matter. "The other member of the commission, T R Dhaka, will retire in December this year and the new member would not be able to sign on the final order, since he would not be a part of the public hearing on the proposals that took place last month. This would further delay any decision on the power rate order," he added.

Tewatia said it was wrong to say that the nigams had suffered due to un-remunerative tariff and hence suffered cash shortage and financial crisis. "More than Rs 3,000 crore had been allowed to the DHBVN and UHBVN as subsidy and other charges from the financial year 1999-2000 and if these are added to the base tariff, the tariff in Haryana would become one of the highest in the country."

Talking to The Indian Express, Bhaskar Chatterjee, chairman of the HERC, said the commission was examining all the issues associated with the tariff proposal and would take a decision soon.

Heading: DHBVN to erect 554 new feeders - Indian Express
Content:
In a move that could pave the way for career opportunities for the youth in the civil aviation sector, the state has mooted a proposal of setting up private civil aviation centres under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode.

By opening up four domestic airstrips, at Pinjore, Karnal, Narnaul and Bhiwani, to the private sector, the state government expects participation from the private parties in providing flying training to the interested candidates. Expressions of Interest (EOI) have already been invited, last date for which is October 20. The interested parties would be given a project briefing on October 6.

Giving the information, M Ramshekhar, adviser, civil aviation, said, "By leasing out the airstrips, we intend to put them to multifarious use, wherein private companies will provide flying training, besides operating and maintaining the airstrips. They will also act as competitors to the existing flying clubs, managed by the Haryana Institute of Civil Aviation (HICA), and provide those interested with more choice."

The department of civil aviation has decided that the parties interested in operating these airstrips as private flying training academies would have to pay Rs 10 lakh as the annual license fee and Rs 8,000 to 10,000 per month per aircraft as operation charge, depending on the aircraft's weight. Charges for built-up hanger or office space would be Rs 500 per square metre annually.

Ramshekhar further said, "The players will have a right to use the airfield but only temporary structures will be allowed to be built on the airfield, that too after they pay the due charges."

Even at the flying clubs at Hisar, Karnal and Pinjore, the Haryana Institute of Civil Aviation is making efforts to spruce up the infrastructure. "Two new Cessna 172 aircrafts have been bought for Hisar and Karnal aviation clubs. The one deployed at Hisar club is an advanced version with glass cockpit and has been given to us by the Aero Club of India. We are also recruiting new instructors for these flying clubs as we are short of pilot instructors," said Ramshekhar.

"On an average about 30-50 candidates undergo flying training at these clubs. The government has also been subsidising the expenditure incurred by HICA by granting about Rs 40-45 lakh per annum, apart from the internal funds," he added.

Heading: Last suspect surrenders: ‘I made a mistake’ - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to improve the quality of power supply, the DHBVN would soon start segregation of domestic and agriculture load on rural electricity feeders in the state. Talking to The Indian Express, Financial Commissioner and Principal Secretary (Power), Ashok Lalvasa, said that segregation was at the top of the priority list of power development works, to give more power supply to domestic consumers in rural area and to make the supply to agriculture sector more reliable.

He said the nigam would erect 554 new 11-KV feeders to segregate rural domestic and agriculture load and the work on erection of lines of about 250 feeders has already been completed. With the creation of this system, there would be three-phase power supply for and there would be no shortage of supply for drinking water purposes and for other activities dependent on three-phase supply.

Lalvasa also announced laying of aerial-bunched cable-based system all the villages and towns. The system of would first be laid in villages having more that 30 per cent aggregate transmission and commercial loss.

Heading: HC raps PU: ‘Why ignore meritorious students?’ - Indian Express
Content:
Was in Haridwar since the incident, says Sompal

Sompal, one of the five accused in the German national molestation case, who was absconding since Sunday, surrendered in court on Friday. He has been remanded to two days in police custody. Sompal admitted that he had committed a mistake and added that he was in Haridwar since the incident.

Sukhwinder Singh alias Sukhi (23) and Maninder Singh Jolly (24) had surrendered in the district courts on Wednesday. Twenty-year-old Pankaj Punia was arrested on Monday while Harpreet Singh alias Dalli was arrested on Tuesday. The four accused have been sent to 14-days' police remand after their two-day remand expired today.

Following an application moved by the police, Harpreet and Pankaj have agreed for the identification parade while Jolly, Sukhi and Sompal refused.

On Thursday, medical examination of four of the accused was conducted at Government Multi Specialty Hospital, Sector 16. Although all had bruises, a police officer said Jolly had suffered the severest injuries, including a deep cut on his chest and another below his neck. According to the police, Jolly is a drug addict and used smack regularly.

Heading: Heart of the matter: Cardiac ailments arrest more youths - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today expressed its surprise and despair over the Panjab University "favouring" certain individuals while ignoring meritorious students at the time of admissions.

"What is wrong with the university? Shall we impose a fine now?" the division bench questioned.

The division bench, headed by Justice Hemant Gupta, made the observations while pronouncing orders on a few petitions filed by students.

The admissions in question were cleared by Dean University Instructions (DUI) S K Kulkarni.

In the first case, the High Court allowed a petition filed by Gursimran Sekhon, a resident of Mohali, against PU and chairman of the Department of BPharmacy.

Sekhon (who placed third in the sports category list) was demanding admission against the two reserved seats for the sports category. The petitioner had sought permission for reconsidering her candidature after one of the seats fell vacant.

The petitioner alleged that someone else was granted admission even though she had higher merit.

In the second case, Hina Gupta, a resident of Sector 7, Panchkula, filed a petition against the chairperson of the joint admission committee, demanding that the admission of Piyush Jand in a BPharma course be quashed.

The petitioner submitted that she placed higher in merit than Piyush, "who was granted admission only on the basis of his Class XII marks".

The High Court allowed the petition and expressed shock over the admissions granted by the university.

Heading: Pink October: Cancer is not the end of life - Indian Express
Content:
20 per cent of all heart attack cases come from the below-30 age bracket, PGI studies have shown

Heart disease is catching up with the youth. And they are falling prey at an alarming rate as well, say PGI doctors. According to repeated PGI surveys, 20 per cent of the total heart attack cases treated each year comprise people below the age of 30.

Heart attacks aren't new to the region, but the rapid advancement in the age group of patients is a cause for concern, say cardiologists.

"In the last few years, cases of heart attacks among people in their late 20s have increased significantly. On an average, we end up seeing one or two such cases every week. Change in lifestyle, increased smoking and stress is to blame for this disturbing trend but the genetic disposition of Indians, who are at risk of suffering premature heart attacks, adds to the problem," said Dr Yash Paul Sharma, Head of the Department of Cardiology, PGI.

"PGI treats between 1,500 and 2,000 cases of heart attack annually," said the HoD, "and half of these require surgery. Repeated data collection at the institute has seen that nearly 250-500 of the patients are in their 20s or early 30s."

Dr J S Thakur of School of Public Health at PGI, said studies have established that Indians, or rather Asians, are prone to heart attacks at least 10 years earlier than Westerners.

Dr Thakur is also associated with the UT Healthy Heart project. "Our studies too have highlighted that instances of cardiovascular diseases in the youth have increased in recent years. Also, earlier the urban population comprised the majority of such cases but the gap between the urban and the rural is fast diminishing," he said.

For the cardiologists, in addition to the sheer numbers, equally crucial is the fact that the prognosis of the heart ailments is more severe and fast progressing in the younger population than in the older population.

"Heart ailments tend to spread much faster, just like malignancy, in the youth. Which is why the severity of heart attacks is higher in the young population," adds Dr Sharma.

In 1990, the PGI had conducted a study to assess the risk profile of people below the age of 40.

This study was repeated in 2001, with people below 35 years of age and found that the number of people in the new age group had increased substantially.

Things to do

* Walk everyday. You should aim to cover five km in 45 minutes

* Your blood pressure should ideally be at 115/75

* Your HDL (good cholesterol) level should be around 50 mg/dL

Causes ...

* Smoking

* Stress

* Family history — hereditary reasons and genetic disposition

* Sedate lifestyle, obesity

* Hypertension

Heading: Trader battered to death, body set on fire - Indian Express
Content:
A student leader wanted in atleast two criminal cases in Chandigarh was arrested in Mohali on Thursday night and arms and ammunition were recovered from his possession.

Nitinpreet Singh Brar, a resident of Jaito in Faridkot district, is a former member of Students' Organisation of India (SOI). He was held with a .32 bore pistol made in England and two live cartridges, of which, he failed to produce a license, the Superintendent of Police (City) Varinder Paul Singh told Newsline.

Initially, Brar said his name was Ramandeep Singh alias Zora but during investigations, his real identity was revealed, following which, his previous track record was verified.

SP (City) also said that the preliminary investigations had revealed that Brar was wanted in a case of attempt to murder registered under Section 307 of the IPC at the Sector 3 police station in Chandigarh on August 3, 2007, and in another case of assault in Manimajra about two-and-a-half-years ago.

The attempt to murder case pertained to the firing in DAV College in Sector 10, Chandigarh, which had left two students injured in the run-up to the student council elections. The then Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) presidential candidate for the DAV College student council had a providential escape when two shots were fired during a group clash. The police investigations, however, has not been able to establish whether the pistol recovered from Brar was the same used in the college shootout.

In the Manimajra case, Brar was accused of physically assaulting a bus conductor. In both the cases, SHO Tarlochan Singh said Brar was evading arrest and the Chandigarh Police had so far failed to apprehend him.

Brar fell in the police net during a routine check at the Ivy Hospital T-point in Sector 71 at 8 pm when a Maruti Alto car with a Chandigarh registration number, was signaled to stop because of tinted windows.

SP (City) divulged that during the search of the car, a bag was recovered in which a pistol and two cartridges were found. With the local court today remanding Brar to judicial custody till October 17, the Chandigarh Police will have to get production warrants to procure Brar's custody.

A case under Sections 25, 54 and 59 of the Arms Act was lodged against Brar in Mohali.

Heading: On Track - Indian Express
Content:
murder most foul : 35-yr-old's partially burnt body, charred bike found along railway line

A businessman from Chandigarh was battered to death before being set on fire near Swara village in Mohali district late on Thursday night.

Thirty-five-year-old Gurcharan Singh's nearly charred body and fully burnt bike was found along Mohali-Kharar railway line. The victim, a resident of Sector 30-B in Chandigarh, was identified with the help of his TVS Sports motorcycle's chasis and engine numbers, Sirhind GRP SHO Sub-Inspector Gian Chand told Newsline.

Gurcharan married one Kamaljeet Kaur in July 2008 and was running an electronics and photography shop on Badala Road in Kharar.

While the motive behind the murder is yet to be ascertained, preliminary investigations revealed that the killers had called Gurcharan on Thursday evening on his cellphone.

The SHO, who is the Investigating Officer in the case, said that Gurcharan received a call, which was not yet traced, around 6.30 pm, following which he left his shop on the motorcycle and told his employee that he was going home.

Around 11.15 pm, the GRP police station in Sirhind (Fatehgarh Sahib) received a call from their Kharar counterparts saying that a body was burning along the railway line.

"We immediately rushed to the spot and found the body simmering," said the SHO, adding that the charred motorcycle was found 400-500 metres away from the body.

A grievous head injury above the right ear, which was believed to be inflicted with some sharp-edged weapon, was visible and circumstantial evidence hinted that after being killed, Gurcharan's body was set on fire.

With no vital clue or apprehension so far, a case under Sections 302, 201 and 34 of the IPC has been lodged against unknown killers at the GRP police station in Sirhind.

The victim's body was handed over to his brother Joga Singh after autopsy examination this afternoon.

Jurisdiction Dispute

The area residents first spotted the burning body around 9 pm and called the local police, which immediately rushed to the spot. Walking ahead in the fields, the policemen and villagers were shocked to find a burning motorcycle. Senior officials of Mohali district police supervised the operation and put sand on the burning body but around 11 pm, they discovered that the spot fell under the jurisdiction of Railway Police, who were later handed over the investigations.

Last call to help

The call details of Gurcharan's cellphone, which is yet to be recovered, were likely to help track the killers. "It is believed that the call, on receiving which Gurcharan left the shop, was by the killers, who had called him at some pre-planned destination to carry out the crime," revealed a senior police officer.

No Robbery

With the family yet to report if any cash or other valuables was missing, preliminary investigations have so far ruled out the possibility of robbery being a motive behind the murder.

Heading: HC raps govt over crunch in human rights panel - Indian Express
Content:
With several independent bands composing for films, Bollywood tunes are set to change

Randolph Correia, of the relatively small electronica duo band Shaai'r n Func, has for the first time composed a full soundtrack, for the movie, Saas Bahu aur Sensex. The movie may have been a dud but Correia feels that it's a headstart for him, since it's his first serious exposure to Bollywood, and towards making mainstream popular music. Though music from the Indian film industry has always been catchy, the predictability of the tracks is about to change, with bands that have focused on creating original sound coming in. "A lot of music from Bollywood sounds exactly the same," says Correia, whose tracks for Saas Bahu.. has a lot of progressive electronic sounds instead of dance and bhangra beats.

Kailasa is another group that has created a separate Bollywood identity for themselves and like to call them the Kailash-Paresh-Naresh trio. Departing from their conventional Sufi sound, the trio is ready to bring in unplugged and acoustic beats with their composition for Sushant Shah's Dus Vidhaniya starring Vinay Pathak and Neha Dhupia.

"The music that we have done for the film is new for us as well," says Paresh Kamath, guitarist of Kailasa, who have recorded their music live. "There's a certain human element that lengthens the songs shelf life when it's live," adds Kamath. The trio has also composed two tracks for the forthcoming Chandni Chowk to China that even includes a quwwali with a twist.

But not all consider Bollywood a progression, though all musicians acknowledge it the fastest way to get noticed and top the charts. "I'm not progressing to Bollywood. In fact it is a step down for me as a musician since it cannot provide any inspiration. But it is a decent money-making proposition," says Correia, who has also produced a track for Drona. Agrees Rahul Ram, bassist, Indian Ocean who says, "Bollywood is not our final bastion. The filmmakers are coming to us for our sound." The band has composed the soundtrack for the recently released Hulla and a film titled Bhoomi is in the pipeline. "The soundtrack for Hulla basically has one main song and three versions of it apart from the background score. But the sound for our films, be it in the past or the future, will continue being the sound that is Indian Ocean," says Ram.

Most of these bands are continuing with their independent work that only benefits from their exposure to Bollywood. "It aligns your creative thought process with what people want to hear which can be a challenge," admits Ram. "Working on a script written by someone else makes us think differently which may not have been possible otherwise," says Kamath.

While Correia is busy with his albums for his groups Shaai'r n Func and Pentagram to take the band to next level, Kailash-Paresh-Naresh turn back to Kailasa to record their third album. And Indian Ocean, which has just released their DVD, Indian Ocean Live in Delhi, is still hoping their fans will go and pick a copy

Heading: Haryana govt to HC: No attempts to tap judges’ phones - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab State Human Rights Commission, which receives around 15,000 complaints on human rights violations every year, and hears around 80 complaints daily, is running with only two members (instead of five), comprising a Chairman (Retd Chief Justice R S Mongia) and a non-judicial Member (K K Bhatnagar).

The Commission decides on matters like custodial deaths, custodial torture, custodial rape and illegal detention, among others in division benches. In case the Commission decides to make any recommendation to the state government on any matter, it has to constitute a larger bench (of at least three members). One post of a member fell vacant in August 2007, and two more posts fell vacant on May 4, 2008, leaving only two members in the panel. Recently from July 31 to August 15, the working in the panel came to a halt as under the rules, a single member cannot take cognisance of new matters. All new cases had to be adjourned.

The petitioner had sought directions to the state government to fill up the vacant posts and the PIL came up for a resumed hearing today. The chief justice repeatedly asked the Additional Advocate General as to what steps had been taken by the Government for filling up the three vacant posts, but the response could not satisfy the Bench.
