The law officer informed the Bench that the Government has initiated a proposal before the Cabinet for reducing the strength of members from existing five to three. At this, the Chief Justice asked the law officer: "Then why the third post has been kept vacant so far?"

The Bench refused to grant one months' time to the government. "You cannot make these panels non-functional by delaying the filling up of posts," the Chief Justice said. Taking umbrage at the non-filing of reply in this case by the government, the court passed a detailed order describing the manner in which the present situation arose, and directed the government to file a detailed affidavit within two weeks explaining the steps it has taken since May 4 to fill up the vacant posts, and further directed: "If the needful is not done by the government, then the State's Home Secretary shall be present in the court on the next date of hearing." The PIL will come up for resumed hearing on October 24.

Heading: Fast Forward - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana government submitted in the Punjab and Haryana High Court today that none of its agency or officer has ever attempted to tap mobile phones of judges.

The government's reply was filed in wake of a suo moto notice taken by the Punjab and Haryana High Court on a news item in an English daily. The reply filed by S K Joshi, IAS, Special Secretary to Government of Haryana, stated: "The state government is fully aware of the constitutional position of the judges of the superior judiciary. It is an article of faith with Haryana government that the dignity of institution be maintained at all costs. The state holds the institution in high esteem and accords it the highest respect."

Similar replies have already been filed by the Punjab government and the UT Administration denying allegations of tapping mobile phones of any of the High Court judges. Taking on record the replies of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh, a division bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Surya Kant disposed of the petition.

The news item had claimed that after the judge-bribery case, a few judges suspected that their mobile phones were being tapped and that someone was eavesdropping on them.

Content:
The change of season has brought with it a host of new shows on television.

We are well past the middle of the year. In fact, we are approaching the fag end but looks like this change of both season and weather has brought with it not one but a host of new shows on television. Perhaps, it's got to do with the festivities in the air that make you want to let go of the old and bring in the new! Taking cue, channels are dishing out new fare with gusto. Here's what you can tune in to:

* Supernatural Weekend : Channel 9X is all set to add even more variety to its weekend primetime band this month. Starting Friday, October 10, 'Sambhav Kya?' will air from 10 pm to 11 pm every Friday and Saturday. Produced by Siddharth and Antara Kak's Cinemavision, 'Sambhav Kya' aims to explore the ambiguity and mysticism of the supernatural to create an engrossing watch based on folklore and legend. The stories will be held together by a powerful narration by the show's host and popular television actor Iqbal Khan. According to veteran television producer and presenter Siddharth Kak who is also the chairman of Cinemavision, what makes 'Sambhav Kya?' a unique and gripping show is the "thriller element in the stories, which are based on real incidents. These will prove the adage truth can be stranger than fiction."

* Mushy Moments : Looks like supernatural is the flavour of the month. 'Kaisi Laagi Lagan', premiering this Monday on October 13 on SaharaOne Television is a supernatural show against the backdrop of a family drama. According to the show's makers, it's a love story which is twisted by destiny and turned by lives' unexpected moves. "It's more like a saga of a cursed marriage and whether it can it be overpowered by the positive energy of love and faith," Nilanjana Purkayastha, Business Head, SaharaOne Television pitches in with the details. Playing the love struck couple - Pratha and Raghav - are debutantes Mahi Vij and Asmit Kaushik. Produced by Cinevistas, 'Kaise Laagi Lagan' will air every Monday to Friday at 11 pm.

* Dance drama : You know a reality show is doing well, when it enters not just another season, but it's fourth! If you loved all the dance and the drama that came with 'Nach Baliye'. Come Friday, October 10 and Star Plus will roll out new jodis set to compete on the dance floor. Produced by Wizcraft, Nach Baliye 4 has Chandigarh's star couple Jaspal and Savita Bhatti in the fray too. Judging the show this year is director-choreographer Farah Khan and actor Arjun Rampal. The dances will roll out every Friday and Saturday.

* Double Act : This one is brand-new, literally. After dishing out TRP grossers like 'The Great Indian Laughter Challenge' and the just wrapped up 'Zara Nachke Dikha', Star One is set to roll out its first of its kind 'original' hunt for India's Best Impersonator in a show called 'Pehchaan Kaun?' At present they are combing the length and breadth of the country and looking for contestants who can copy the style and voice and come closest to mimicking their favourite celebrity - it could be a Bollywood star, politician or even a TV star!

* Laugh It Off : He's television's funniest find so far. Raju Srivastava, the immensely in-demand stand-up comedian who has been off late appearing everywhere, has finally got his own show on NDTV Imagine. Set in the backdrop of a cafe, 'Raju Hazir Ho', produced by Endemol India, will capture a new side to Raju, who plays host to his friends from the entertainment world. The show with Raju's observational humour, mimicry and humorous acts, will revolve around a special theme. Each weekend, the comedian will invite two very special guests to join him on the show. And that's where the fun will begin. "Mere doston ki mandli jab ho mere saath, hassi ki aayegi baraat! I am very excited that the channel has given me the opportunity to host my own comedy show. Ab har hafte, aapko milega paisa vasool entertainment," remarked Srivastav in his imitable style. Catch him doing what he's best at this month.

* Religious Timing: on the tube, the country's shifted gears into festive mode with the onset of the Navratras. Offering a spiritual takes is SaharaOne with its show 'Mata Ki Chowki' which aims to enlighten viewers about the nine avatars of Mata. All through the nine days of Navratra that concludes with Dusshera, the lead character of Mata Ki Chowki, Muskan aka Vaishnavi will narrate the story of each avatar of the Goddess. You can catch the Durga Puja special episodes of 'Mata Ki Chowki' at 10.30 pm.

Heading: CFC T-20 cash prize tournament from Oct 19 - Indian Express
Content:
With scores of 1 and 0, his test debut against Sri Lanka there was nothing much to write about. However, he returned back with a bang and scored an unbeaten 78 runs until he ploughed straight into Mark Waugh and mangled his knee. After the recovery, he smashed two elegant tons at Lord's and Headingley to come back into the reckoning. However, bright things didn't last long and, after two years and 21 tests, he again found himself on the sidelines.

In India, to play in the second edition of Indian Cricket League, Matthew Elliott has a piece of advice for the Indian batsmen. 'Attack the Aussie spinners'. According to Elliot, "Spin is the weakest link in the current Australian squad and since the spinners are on the tour to India for the first time, they would be nervous. India should capitalise on that and dominate them mentally. Playing an aggressive game will certainly provide edge against the Aussies. Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma played splendidly against the Aussies during the first innings for Board President XI. I feel the pacers will bowl more in the series and the Aussies will look upon Bret Lee and Mitchell Johnson to provide the breakthroughs. The Aussie spinners wilhave to watch out because Indians are good players of spin."

He dispels the notion that this is the weakest Australian side to have toured India. "It would be harsh to tout them as weak. History has shown that the hardworking side always wins in India. Australian board has done a good job by selecting some good players," says the southpaw.

So will the Aussies find it hard to fill the void left by McGrath and Gilchrist?

"Definitely, they are legends and it would be hard to replace them. But I am sure Brad Haddin will have a good series.

Any Indian player that he thinks will do well in the series. "Sachin has always done well against the Aussies. He is always a threat for the Australians. So, I guess the Master Blaster will make a difference."

"Having seen the Australian's performance against the President XI, it seems that India will walk into the series as favourites," he adds.

Meanwhile, the world's first-over specialist bowler, Daryll Tuffey who made his test debut against Australia in 1999-2000, also shakes his head in affirmation. "Given the fact that Australians are low on experience and several of their players have left, Indians would start as favourites in the series," says the former New Zealand fast bowler who didn't have much success against the Aussies.

Content:
In view of providing easy access to cricket fans across India, the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) today announced online sale of tickets for the second India-Australia Test match, of the four-match series, to be played at Mohali from October 17 to 21.

Except for the student block (Rs 100) and chair block (Rs 300) tickets of which will be sold at the PCA Stadium, tickets of five other blocks - VIP Block (Rs 1,000), North Pavilion (Rs 2,000), Pavilion Terrace (Rs 5,000), AC Lounge (Rs 10,000) and Corporate Box (Rs 20,000) - would be available online.

According to PCA spokesman, offering tickets online and offline, PCA, in keeping with international standards, has decided to make the process of purchasing tickets to the match easy and convenient for cricket fans.

The tickets booked online would be delivered at the residence or could be picked up at designated spots, he added.

Adding further, for the will-call pickup option, customers can collect tickets at the venue starting October 12 to 15 and at PUDA Bhawan, Near Fortis Hospital, Phase 8, Mohali from October 16 to 21. It is recommended that tickets be picked up before match days to avoid rush and potential delays. Customers will need to bring the credit/debit card used for the purchase, a valid photo ID, a clear copy of the photo ID and the confirmation page. If sending someone else to collect on their behalf, customers are requested to send an authorization letter in addition to all of the above. The person authorised also needs to carry her/his original photo identification along with a photocopy.

PCA president IS Bindra said in a statement, "Our goal is to provide access to all cricket fans in and around Punjab and all across India to some world class cricket between India and Australia."

He said to that end, PCA was facilitating a convenient process for people to purchase tickets and get access to all pertinent information regarding the facilities from the comfort of their home, office or nearby convenient store.

Buyers can log on to www.kyazoonga.com or call the KyaZoonga ticketing call centre at 011-2323-7527 for further assistance.

Box-office locations at the PCA Stadium will be operational from October 14 until the final day of the Match on October 21.

Heading: ‘Wanted’ ex-student leader held with arms, ammunition in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
The UGC Pay Review Committee's recommendation of a salary hike of over 70 per cent was welcomed by the teachers of Panjab University on Friday.

What comes as a major cause of celebration is the recommendation made by the pay panel of enhancing the retirement age to 65 years. The UGC panel also recommends that the teachers may be reappointed on contract basis after superannuation upto the age of 70 years.

Talking to Newsline, MS Johal, a PU professor said, "This was long due for the teaching fraternity and definitely is a reason to cheer about. The enhancement of retirement age would lead to optimum utilisation of professionals in the country." The committee observed that institutions should fill the vacant posts on priority basis and the ban on recruitment should be lifted immediately. About contract teachers, the committee said that teachers should be appointed only when there is a dire necessity and their qualification and procedure of selection should be the same as for a regular teacher.

Ronki Ram, PUTA president said, "The government has finally started thinking in the interest of the teachers and we hope that these recommendations will be implemented too. This would go a long way in developing higher education."

PU professor VK Mahajan added, "The committee has finally given us a reason to smile. Our long pending demand of increasing the retirement age has finally been taken care of which would be beneficial for the country at large."

More sops

The committee has recommended five advanced increments instead of the present four to a PhD degree holder at the time of recruitment as assistant professor. It also suggested that the age of retirement should be 65 years and teachers may be reappointed on contract basis after superannuation upto the age of 70 years.

A grievous head injury above the right ear, which was believed to be inflicted with some sharp-edged weapon, was visible and circumstantial evidence hinted that after being killed, Gurcharan's body was set on fire.

With no vital clue or apprehension so far, a case under Sections 302, 201 and 34 of the IPC has been lodged against unknown killers at the GRP police station in Sirhind.

The victim's body was handed over to his brother Joga Singh after autopsy examination this afternoon.

Jurisdiction Dispute

The area residents first spotted the burning body around 9 pm and called the local police, which immediately rushed to the spot. Walking ahead in the fields, the policemen and villagers were shocked to find a burning motorcycle. Senior officials of Mohali district police supervised the operation and put sand on the burning body but around 11 pm, they discovered that the spot fell under the jurisdiction of Railway Police, who were later handed over the investigations.

Last call to help

The call details of Gurcharan's cellphone, which is yet to be recovered, were likely to help track the killers. "It is believed that the call, on receiving which Gurcharan left the shop, was by the killers, who had called him at some pre-planned destination to carry out the crime," revealed a senior police officer.

No Robbery

With the family yet to report if any cash or other valuables was missing, preliminary investigations have so far ruled out the possibility of robbery being a motive behind the murder.

Heading: Punjabi varsity prof to feature in Marquis Who’s Who - Indian Express
Content:
Neem-based bioinsecticides will soon be commercially produced by the Thapar University's bioprocessing unit. A joint effort by the Punjab State Council for Science and Technology (PSCST), the unit has an installed capacity of 50 kg per hour.

The unit is the first-of-its-kind in the state and will produce 4 tonnes of insecticides in the first year.

A nursery at the university's Science and Technology Entrepreneurs Park (STEP) has also been established for cultivating neem or Azadirachta indica that will be supplied to the unit. This is to ensure the sustained supply of neem fruits for the bioinsecticide production.

Abhijit Mukherjee, director of Thapar University said, "We are confident that herbal bioinsecticides have tremendous market potential and will become a promising small-scale business venture. Bioorganic farming has assumed significance as bioinsecticides and biopesticides are herbal and non-toxic. These environment-friendly products do not cause contamination of soil and the ground water and have wide applications."

Discussing future plans, he said, "We aim to promote production, processing and the use of herbal bioinsecticide for environment-friendly and hazard-free farming in the state."

He revealed that in the first phase from July to August this year, 22 tonnes of neem seeds were procured. "The first batch is ready and the university's faculty has organised several farmer meets and awareness camps in adjoining villages and on the campus to popularise the use of bioinsecticides," he claimed.

The indiscriminate use of chemical insecticides and pesticides has a detrimental effect on the soil, ground water and the final produce. Besides bringing down production costs and eliminating pesticide residues, bio pesticides are also more eco-friendly.

Heading: PU awaits PM’s visit - Indian Express
Content:
Rakesh K Garg, a senior professor in the Department of Forensic science, Punjabi University, has been selected for inclusion in the 2009 edition of Marquis Who's Who in the World.

This new edition will feature the biographies of more than 50,000 accomplished men and women from around the globe and across all fields. "It is his hard work and dedication that have earned him a place in Who's Who," said a university official.

Garg also has the distinction of being the first Indian to get a national scholarship from the government in the subject of Forensic Science (1984). He has also completed his post-doctoral research from the John Jay College of Criminal Justice, USA and has visited a number of forensic science laboratories across the world. Garg also got the Bernard Friedmen Scholarship from the New York Microscopical Society, USA in 1987. He has also guided several PhD students over the years who have completed their research work under his supervision.

Heading: HC dismisses petition over use of Punjabi in MC list - Indian Express
Content:
The Panjab University authorities are still awaiting a confirmation from Prime Minister Manmohan Singh for inaugurating the Diamond jubilee celebrations. Confirming the news, PM's PU DRP Sanjeev Tewari said, "We at the varsity are still awaiting the PM's visit as he is an alumnus of the university. There is a heritage museum made especially to be unveiled by him. Also there is a book on the history of the university, which we want him to release. Many reminders have been sent to the PM office and are expecting a reply soon."

Meanwhile, the Diamond Jubilee year celebrations that was to come to an end on October 1 has now been extended to October 17. The university had come up with several proposals including introducing facilities to make the university more disabled-friendly. It was decided that ramps would be put up in various departments but the same is yet to be implemented. The officials, however, maintain that the matter is being looked into and steps are being taken to provide better facilities and improve the infrastructure.

Heading: Victim’s father waits for promised job - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday dismissed a petition filed by one Om Parkash Gupta and nine other members of the Mandi Gobindgarh Municipal Council, challenging the reservation of the post of president in the various Municipal Councils of the state. They had challenged this on the ground that since the official language of the state is Punjabi, the list of the Municipal Councils should be prepared in Punjabi and not in English. The High Court, on the last date of hearing, had asked the state to file an affidavit, stating whether it had issued any notification, which requires all acts and rules of the state government to be published in Punjabi.

The Law officers, in the meanwhile, said since no notification has been issued by the Punjab government, it is not binding on the state government to frame its acts, rules and orders in Punjabi.

Heading: Groups clash in Dadu Majra, six held - Indian Express
Content:
Every second of the night of Feburary 4 is etched in the memory of 60-year-old Niranjal Lal, who saw his 20-year-old-son, Jamuna, die before his eyes. Jamuna, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, succumbed to his injuries when the lintel of the main entrance gate, being constructed at the Mansa Devi road, collapsed.

A dozen labourers were also injured in the accident.

The work was being carried out by a private company, Shakti constructions, on behalf of the Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board, under the supervision of the Haryana Urban Development Board (HUDA).  

While contractor Vijay Goyal, was arrested on the same day, the District Administration announced a compensation of Rs 1 lakh and a job for Niranjan Lal at the Mansa Devi Shrine Board.

An SDM level inquiry was also instituted, which later gave a clean chit to the contractor, declaring it an accident.

Eight months on, however, Niranjan Lal, is shuttling between departments, for the 'promised' job.

"It has been eight months since I lost my son. With all my other children below the age of 10 years, he was the only earning member of the family. It was only after Newsline reported about the delay in paying the compensation that it was given to us. But as that cannot substitute for a job, I kept shuttling from one department to another, requesting the officials to provide me with the job," says Naranjan Lal, with tears in his eyes.  

He added that he has been trying very hard for a job. "Every day has turned into a struggle. There are days when I get work and at times, we have to manage with whatever little I have earned. I have deposited the compensation money in a bank to provide my children with some financial security," he said.

Talking to Newsline, Rajender Kataria, DC, Panchkula, said: "He had to submit some documents about his educational qualifications, which he said he would do after a visit to his village in UP.

I have asked my men to get him a job at the earliest."

Heading: Checks in city a day after polythene ban - Indian Express
Content:
Tension gripped Dadu Majra Colony late on Thursday night following a clash between two groups. On Friday morning, the residents of the colony blocked traffic to protest against the alleged laxity of the police in arresting the accused.

Following this, police booked six persons, four for setting a motorcycle on fire and two on charges of rioting. They were identified as Monu, Tinda, Kunji, Salman, Sham Kumar and Kuldeep and will be produced before the magistrate on Saturday.

According to police, the six, armed with sharp-edged weapons, chased two members of a rival group — Manish and Goldy — on Thursday night. Manish reportedly lost control of his motorcycle and both managed to flee the spot, leaving behind the motorcycle. Thereafter, the six allegedly set the motorcycle afire.

The supporters of Manish and Goldy protested against the inaction of the police, alleging that the policemen stood like mute spectators while their bike was set on fire.

Ashok Kumar, Manish's father, told the police that he was assaulted by the same group which was forcing Manish to sell drugs.

Heading: Pinjore Heritage fest starts at Yadavindra Gardens - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 480 places were inspected by a team of the UT Administration today. The teams had been constituted to check compliance of the ban on polythene bags by shop keepers across the city. No challans were, however, issued to the defaulters.

The team confiscated a large number of polythene bags from the Kisan Bhawan, where an exhibition was going on and also submitted a report to Deputy Commissioner R K Rao.

Rao said: "The various teams found that there was a 80 per cent compliance with the orders, while in 20 per cent cases, it was being defied. The defaulters will be scrutinised on Monday and challans might be issued against them."

Around 40 teams have been constituted by the Administration to ensure that the ban is adhered by the shop owners across the city.

Members of the Chandigarh Beopar Mandal and Chandigarh Industries Association, meanwhile, have requested the Administration to implement the ban after the end of the festive season. MPS Chawla, President, Chandigarh Industries Association, said they hope the Administration will extend the date of the ban, after which, the traders will voluntarily switch to paper bags.

47 fined at Mansa Devi shrine

Nearly Rs 33,000 was collected by the District Administration on Friday as 47 persons at the Mansa Devi Shrine, Panchkula, were issued challans for use of polythene bags in the shrine premises. The violators were charged fines ranging between Rs 500 and Rs 1000 by the authorities. "We surveyed the area around 9.30 am and issued challans to 47 persons," said Rajender Kataria, DC, Panchkula.

Heading: Movie Reviews - Indian Express
Content:
The three-day Pinjore Heritage Festival was inaugurated by Union Minister of Tourism and Culture Ambika Soni, in the Yadavindra Gardens today.

"The place wore a look of the Mughal Mahal with artifacts and illuminations giving a festive look to the area," said the spokesperson.

He said the guests were escorted to the Street Bazaar, especially crafted like the Anarkali Bazaar of the ancient times where artisans from across the country showcased the handicraft tradition of ancient India.

"Special emphasis was given to the artisans dealing in the specialties of the Mughal times," he added.

While appreciating the efforts of Haryana in promoting tourism, Soni said that the Rs 50 crore earmarked for the state in the 10th Five-Year Plan, had been judiciously spent. She said a circuit of Delhi-Haryana-Punjab-Himachal Pradesh could be developed on the pattern of Delhi-Agra-Jaipur triangle. Those present on the occasion included Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Minister of State for Tourism, Forests, Environment, Sports and Youth Affairs Kiran Chaudhary among others.

Chaudhary said that work on making Pinjore and Bhima Devi an integrated destination would start soon.

Heading: HC seeks reply on illegal admission in dental colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Ramchand Pakistani

CAST: Nandita Das, Rashid Farooqui, Syed Fazal Hussain; DIRECTOR: Mehreen Jabbar

Seven old Ramchand crosses the border, from Pakistan to India, without knowing that his straying steps are taking him to a place from where there is no return. Both the boy and his father who runs after him, are arrested. Ramchand Pakistani,based on a true story, tells it like it is, without embroidery or excess.

And that is debutant director Mehreen Jabbar's film's real strength. The village in which Ramchand (Syed Fazal Hussain) lives with his father Shankar (Rashid Farooqui) and mother Champa (Nandita) is all mud huts and abject poverty. Being Hindu and Dalit is a double burden: they are treated as outcasts in their own country, as well as the one that lies over the border, separated by a small strip of sand.

The lady officer in the Indian camp which houses prisoners like Ramchand epitomises the divide beautifully: she is willing to teach him what she can, but he is not allowed to touch her utensils because he is 'achhoot'. Her change of heart is one of the high points of the film. So is Syed Fazal Hussain's affecting, natural performance as Ramchand: child actors in Hindi cinema can learn a thing or two from their counterparts in Pakistan.

What happens with Ramchand and Shankar is not just the story of that father and son, but of countless ordinary individuals from both countries, who become victims of politics and animosity.

The film was meant to be a simultaneous release in both countries, but it opened in Pakistan a couple of months earlier. It's good timing, regardless: a good Eid present, as well as a pointer on Mahatma Gandhi's birthday towards peace and goodwill between countries which have been struggling for these past decades to reach accommodation.

Well worth your time.

Kidnap

CAST: Imran Khan, Sanjay Dutt, Minissha Lamba, Vidya Malvade; DIRECTOR: Sanjay Gadhvi

Can n-cut Imran Khan, after playing good so well, go bad with equal felicity? Not if his director is Sanjay Gadhvi.

Curvy lass Sonia (Minissha) has an altercation with equally curvy mom (Vidya). Off she goes for a dip in the sea, all the better for us to see some more of her waist-to-hip ratio. Next thing, she wakes up in a strange house, with a strange guy (Imran), with his back to her, making tea on a stove. This is a kidnap, strange guy intones, and keeps stirring the pot. Out pops protective pa (Sanjay) on a rescue mission, which consists of a series of lax wild goose chases all over Mumbai.

Clearly, all ideas of knife-edge suspense and adrenalin rushes were very far from the director's mind when he dreamt up this long-drawn plot which mixes childhood trauma, revenge, and unhappy marriages, with less than average results.

It's a pity because it could have been much more. Sanjay Dutt is a dab hand at revenge sagas, having done so many before. And Imran had shown his ability to do a superb character read in Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na: here he has to act deadly serious and dangerous, but can't muster an iota of menace. Gadhvi, who had created 'dhoom' with both the Dhoom movies, swings unconvincingly between suspense and song, and gets neither right.

The Dhoom overhang is evident in Minissha's bikinis and tankinis (just like Aishwarya and Esha before her). She is also plonked under a waterfall in a transparent white shift, with Imran brooding by the side. The words of the song (oh yes, she sings, in the middle of being kidnapped) go thus: "Mausam ye awesome bada..."

Don't say we didn't warn you.

Drona

CAST: Abhishek Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra,

Kay Kay Menon, Jaya Bachchan;

DIRECTOR: Goldie Behl

Superheroes who save the world are still, despite Hrithik Roshan, a Western conceit. The Roshan lad wore a zig-zag mask, which hid half his face, and a flowing cape: he spoke Hindi and romanced Priyanka, but he looked faintly like Superman.

Abhishek takes on the mantle of the next Bollywood superhero — a totally desi 'mahapurush' avatar — in a white tunic embossed with golden stars. He also speaks Hindi and romances Priyanka, but looks nothing like Superman. He doesn't even, sigh, have a mask.

What he does have is a mean-and-nasty mother-and-son duo making his life miserable.

Every so often a blue rose petal floats in to comfort him. And then one day, he acquires, in rapid succession, a gem-studded bracelet, a gorgeous female bodyguard (Priyanka), the knowledge that his own mother Rani Jayati Devi (Jaya) abandoned him when he was a young child, and that he is not an ordinary mortal, but a Drona, keeper of the faith. Which he has to save from the evil jaadugar Riz Raizada (Kay Kay).

Oh, this could have been such a wonderful fantasy, harking back to ancient Indian tales of intrigue and mystery, full of tilasmi nagris, and jaadui talwaars.

The special effects are absolutely fabulous; the top-notch quality is a first for Indian cinema. But the plot's ludicrous. Goldie Behl filches from here and there (Harry Potter, Lord Of The Rings come instantly to mind), and gives us a slow, slack story.

Fairytales work only when the strange and fantastical are buoyed by credible characters, not by poor misguided actors looking as if they had strolled out in fancy dress.

Abhishek can't lift his turgid Adi aka Drona off the ground; Priyanka's martial arts moves are buried under the billowing red and yellow cleavage-flashing shifts.

Only Kay Kay, the black-hearted magician, carries off a gelled Mohawk and a curved silver hook on his forefinger with élan.

If only his magic had spilled over to the movie.

—SHUBHRA GUPTA

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

Heading: BSNL celebrates eighth anniversary - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has given four weeks' time to the Dental Council of India (DCI) and MD University, Rohtak, to file an affidavit regarding the action taken against dental colleges in Haryana giving back door admissions to students.

The directions were passed in wake of a petition pending in the High Court. The petitioner had made the allegations against certain dental colleges in Haryana after which the High Court had constituted a committee to look into the matter.

The committed, after an inquiry, stated that the DCI be approached to take a strong action against the institute and trust, Sri Guru Govind Singh Tercentenary Dental College and Research Institute, Budhera and Dasmesh Educational Charitable Trust, New Delhi. It further called for de-recognition of the institute. The colleges were directed to deposit Rs 1 lakh per student within 10 days, an order that has not been compiled with till date.

Heading: Kidney donor takes U-turn, says he was lured by ADC - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) celebrated its eighth anniversary on Friday. Pradip Mehra, Advisor to the UT Administrator, was the chief guest on the occasion. He said the world has become a global village by the virtue of telecommunications.

Mehra also gave away the Vishisht Sanchar Seva medals to six employees of BSNL in the Punjab Circle.

Heading: Despite assurance, CCI  fails to pick up cotton - Indian Express
Content:
In a volte-face, 23-year-old Sunny, who was to donate kidney to ailing PCS officer and Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) of Tarn Taran Kirpal Singh, today said he was "lured" by the officer and his family to part away with his vital organ.

He appeared in his advocate Vishal Gogna's chamber today and said that he was "under pressure" and "lured", but now he has decided not donate his kidney.

Notably, Sunny had yesterday said that he was an adult and took a decision to donate the kidney to the officer out of "love and affection" for him. "I was never told that my life would be in danger after donating a kidney," said Sunny, adding that he was tempted with a government job, treatment of his ailing parents and a promise to get him married.

"This all seems a hoax to me now. My parents were right in discouraging me," Sunny said. He, however, could give no satisfactory answer when asked if any exchange of money was involved.

Earlier, a high-level meeting, presided over by Amritsar Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Paramjit Singh, today stayed the transplantation. Neither Sunny nor any member from Kirpal's family or doctors from Mohali-based private hospital were present in the meeting.

Notably, Sunny and his parents had earlier submitted an affidavit before the authorisation committee, which had cleared the kidney transplant case.

SSP Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, Civil Surgeon Lehmber Singh and representatives from the Indian Medical Association (IMA) were present in the meeting that lasted for over two hours.

The panel recorded the statement of Suman, who was happy to see her son after over a week now.

"We had summoned both the parties but only Sunny's mother appeared before us. We were expecting Sunny too, but he did not turn up," said Paramjit Singh, adding that he would have to appear before them to record his statement.

Meanwhile, Sunny said he would appear anywhere to say "no to donation".

Family of Kirpal had said that the proposed transplantation was as per the laid procedures and no pressure or force was being used to lure the youth.

Sunny's advocate Gogna said they would file a fresh appeal before the authorisation committee to review the case, as no one could forcibly take kidney of his client.

Heading: Forest dept says Patiala MC usurped its land - Indian Express
Content:
Despite an assurance from Chief Managing Director of the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) SC Grover, the agency has still not begun to purchase cotton.

As a result, private players picked around 28,000 quintals of cotton today for Rs 2,500 to Rs 2,800 per quintal.

Punjab head of the CCI Ved Parkash Nagpal said, "We had sought permission to purchase cotton directly from the farmers, which has not yet been granted. Our employees are ready, and the moment we get the green signal from the Punjab government, we will enter the market. Some cotton farmers met the CM today during a Sangat Darshan and I think our file will be cleared soon."

Punjab Mandi Board chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal said, "We have cleared their file. Buying directly from the farmer would mean that the CCI will not have to pay 2.5 per cent tax to the arhtiya. For this relaxation, we had asked them to pay 2 per cent extra to the farmer and keep the 0.5 per cent. The file is pending in the CM's office now."

It was learnt that after the Punjab Mandi Board's clearance, a delegation of arhtiyas recently met the CM at Talwandi Sabo and urged him not to clear the file.

Subsequently, the CCI, which is buying cotton from neighbouring states of Haryana and Rajasthan, has not entered Punjab.

Meanwhile, farmers are being forced to take their produce to Haryana or Rajasthan at an additional cost.

Harjinder Singh, a farmer from Bathinda, said, "I had a bumper crop, but there are no buyers. Till last month, the price was about Rs 3,500 per quintal, and now I am getting Rs 2,500."

Heading: ‘Child marriage’: cops unaware of law - Indian Express
Content:
Government officials have reportedly usurped and later tried to auction Forest Department land measuring 52 kanal in Jhill village.

Since 20002, senior officials of the district administration, Patiala Municipal Corporation (MC) and District Revenue Office (DRO) have been under the scanner following inclusion and subsequent attempt to auction reserved forest land worth crores on the Sirhind Road.

The MC got the mutation deed transferred in its name in connivance with officials the District Revenue Office and the DC office. Patiala Forest Division is planning a civil suit against the corporation, as it hid facts from them and didn't inform them about the auction, for which advertisements were also issued.

On September 1, the Forest Department wrote to the MC commissioner, saying that despite informing the Patiala DC repeatedly since 2002, the land was not marked and later usurped. Notably, the state government, in a letter issued in 1976, had made it clear to all corporations to take possession of only "shamlat or land under rehabilitation".

"The provisions in the Forest Conservation Act, 1980, for conservation of forests and the matter contained therein must apply clearly to all forestlands irrespective of ownership or classification of any area rewarded as forest in the secret record," said the letter, quoting a 1996 Supreme Court judgment.

"After we wrote the letter, they cancelled the auction," Divisional Forest Officer K S Jattana told The Indian Express.

The letter also mentions the earlier "unscrupulous acts" of the MC, where it had tried to unsuccessfully grab forestland in Lehal village and Patiala Chetna Kender. "If now any other land is taken over by the MC, action under Section 2 of the FCA Act will be taken against all the officials involved," said the letter.

Patiala Divisional Commissioner SK Ahluwalia, who is also the acting municipal commissioner, said it was the MC land and they had all the documents. "Why didn't the Forest Department take action against some shop owners who have occupied the land? Auction will be soon held," he added.

Heading: Punjab Biotechnology Incubator gets rolling in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
A case of alleged child marriage has come to light here after the step-mother of a boy, Kuldeep Singh, who she claims is still a juvenile, was married to a 23-year-old girl. The boy's family says he is 18, though the step-mother, Jeeto, claims he is 15-year-old.

However, in both cases, the marriage is illegal as per the Child Marriage Prohibition Act, 2006, which stipulates the minimum age for marriage of boys to be 21.

It was learnt that the marriage took place in Jamalpur village in a family of Baazigar community, in which child marriage is a tradition, and the boy belongs to Ucha Pind Sanghowal.

The matter was reported to the police by Jeeto, but they are yet to take any action, saying that the marriage was solemnised before the police reached and the boy's family had given an affidavit, saying that the boy was 18-year-old.

Sadar police station SI Bhupinder Singh, who had visited the spot, said the boy's father, Balbir Singh, gave an affidavit claiming that boy was 18-year-old.

However, girl's family produced a ration card on which her age was mentioned as 23 years. "The panchayat members of Jamalpur gave in writing that it was a custom in their community to get their children married at an early age and the gauna (the girl shifting to the boy's home) takes place later," he said. When told that even if the boy is 18-year-old, the marriage is a punishable offence, he claimed that some relaxation was given to certain tribes, where the consummation of marriage takes place later.

Heading: Kidnappers kill Nurmahal boy in Manila - Indian Express
Content:
With the setting up of the Punjab Biotechnology Incubator (PBTI) in Phase V on Friday, the city got the first part of its "Biotechnology Cluster".

The PBTI will later be shifted to the upcoming Knowledge City, Sector 81, along with the Biotechnology Cluster, which was being set up at an estimated cost of Rs 380 crore.

Punjab Minister for Science, Technology and Environment Bikram Singh Majithia, who inaugurated the PBTI, said, "The Punjab government and the Union Department of Biotechnology (DBT) have jointly sanctioned and approved the setting up of the PBTI in Punjab Biotechnology Park at a total cost of Rs 10.97 crore."

The Incubator facilities were sanctioned to carry out the quality testing and certification, value addition of products and processes of agriculture and related sectors, training and dissemination of information on quality and food safety aspects, added the minister.

PBTI Chief Executive Officer Dr S S Marwaha said that the laboratories were equipped with the latest hi-end equipment for the analysis of pesticide residues, heavy metals, mycotoxins, minerals, vitamins, fatty acid profile and food additives among other things.

Heading: Intruder shot dead in Attari sector - Indian Express
Content:
A 20-year-old local boy was killed by his kidnappers in Manila a couple of days back. Sunil Kumar, alias Sonu, son of Nirmalajit Singh of Kila Mohalla, was living in Manila for the past many years along with his father. Banga Ram, his grandfather, said Sonu was kidnapped a few days back and a ransom of Rs 50 lakh was demanded from his father, a moneylender.

"The father of Sonu talked them into reducing the amount to Rs 12 lakh and also paid the ransom," Banga Ram said. But the kidnappers murdered Sonu and threw his body in flowing water, he added.

Notably, many Punjabi boys, mostly into money-lending business in Manila, have been killed in the past many years. However, neither the Philippines government nor the Indian authorities did anything to stop the killings, besides asking deputy commissioners of Punjab to stop youths from going to Manila.

Heading: Finance, animal husbandry depts lock horns over Rs 4-crore revenue - Indian Express
Content: BSF's 65 battalion on Friday foiled an infiltration attempt by gunning down an unidentified intruder at Rattar Khurd, near Attari sector, while he was trying to cross over under the cover of darkness in the wee hours. Sources said the accused was spotted around 2 am, and when the BSF asked him to stop, he started to run back towards the Pakistani side. On this, BSF jawans fired at him, killing him on the spot. Rs 3,000 Pak currency was recovered from his possession.

Heading: Pay rates for re-employed medical teachers - Indian Express
Content:
Bone of contention: FD says amount should be directly deposited in treasury

The Punjab Finance Department and the Department of Animal Husbandry have locked horns over the issue of Rs 4-crore revenue generated by way of user charges for artificial insemination.

For the past several years, the amount was being directly deposited with the Punjab Livestock Development Board to meet expenses incurred on projects that are under way. Last week, the Finance Department (FD) formally communicated to discontinue the practice. The FD has asserted that the amount should be directly deposited in the state treasury.

The Animal Husbandry Department has said that it would stall the move. It contend that the decision, if implemented, could hamper the pace of development of several of its projects for want of funds. The department has now taken up the issue with the government.

Officials said in the event of the revenue directly reaching the treasury, the cash flow required for various projects, including funds for its bull farms, artificial insemination project to breed exotic varieties and equipment storage, could be adversely affected.

A sum of Rs 20 is collected from users at bull farms for artificial insemination.

With finances in Punjab still in the woods, officials feared that the Finance Department may not accord priority to matters of the Animal Husbandry Department.

A senior official said, "The FD clears funds and bills depending on the priority. The cash crunch has often led to inordinate delays." The performance of the state treasury too has been sluggish. "The treasury payments have invariably been stopped or slow," an official said.

However, officials in the FD said the procedure to deposit the revenue with the treasury was once long ago in practice, but altered several years ago, for which the Punjab Livestock Development Board reportedly had not taken approval from the government.

Sources in the government said during an audit review too, this issue of was pointed out. Now, a formal approval has been sought from the government, and it hit a roadblock following the FD's objection.

Heading: Fresh hope: Sarabjit to meet law minister - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government on Friday notified pay rates for contractual re-employed medical teachers up to the age of 65 years for government medical colleges in Amritsar and Patiala. Re-employed teachers would be allowed private practice as they would not get non-practicing allowance. An official spokesperson said for those who were not getting any pension but employed as professors would get Rs 55,000 per month and an associate professor would get Rs 48,000. In the same category, an assistant professor would get Rs 44,000, lecturer Rs 31,000 and senior resident medical officer Rs 25,000 per month. For those getting pension from the state, Centre or defence forces, the pay rate would be less.

Farmers end stir

Moga: After one hour of dialogue between Deputy Commissioner Satwant Singh Johal and Moga SSP Ashok Baath, agitating farmers on Thursday night lifted the blockade. The rail traffic, which was suspended by the authorities after 4 pm on Thursday, resumed this morning. The traffic on the Moga-Ludhiana section was suspended following blockade by the farmers under the leadership of BKU (Ekta) general secretary Sukhdev Singh. They were protesting against the "inaction" of police against two commission agents of Ajitwal for allegedly snatching of tractor-trolley of farmer Karnail Singh.

Heading: School board to introduce semester system - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani Law Minister Farooq Naek will meet Indian death row prisoner Sarabjit Singh on Monday to review his case following the Indian government's appeal for clemency, official sources said, raising hopes of his release.

Sarabjit, 42, has been on death row since he was convicted for alleged involvement in four bomb attacks that killed 14 people in the Punjab province in 1990. His family insists that he was wrongly convicted.

Naek will meet Sarabjit at Lahore's Kot Lakhpat jail on Monday and conduct a review of his case, official sources were quoted as saying today by Geo News channel.

Naek will also consider the Indian government's clemency appeal for Sarabjit, sources said. Sarabjit was earlier set to be hanged on April 1 and his execution was deferred for 30 days by President Pervez Musharraf.

This was done so that the new Pakistan People's Party-led government could review his case following India's appeal for clemency. Pakistan's Supreme Court had earlier turned down Sarabjit's mercy petition.

After Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani intervened in the matter, Pakistani authorities put off his execution "till further orders".

Gilani announced a proposal to commute the death sentences of thousands of prisoners into life imprisonment on June 21 to mark the birth anniversary of slain PPP chairperson Benazir Bhutto, but it is still not clear if the move would benefit Sarabjit.

In August, the government informed the Supreme Court that it was yet to take a final decision on the proposal to commute death sentences to life imprisonment.

Several political parties and Islamic groups, including the Jamaat-e-Islami, have opposed any move to convert Sarabjit's death sentence into life imprisonment.

Heading: Attari gears up to attract more tourists - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, the Punjab School Education Board, Mohali, has decided to introduce semester system in classes XI and XII from the coming session. And following the Central Board of Secondary Education, the PSEB will also introduce internal assessment in all the subjects. This decision was taken in a recent meeting of the board officials.

Dalbir Singh Dhillon, PSEB chairman, said, "We have discussed the modalities of semester system with various school principals and teachers. The first semester will be from April to September and second from October to March. This will enhance the capability of the students. But before its implementation, the staff will be trained to run it smoothly."

He said the PSEB would be the second board in India to start the system, first being the Haryana School Education Board. The system would be introduced in class X from 2010-2011 session, he added.

Notably, two years ago, the CBSE had introduced internal assessment in social studies and mathematics in class X. Dhillon said, "In each subject, 10 marks will be of internal assessment."

Meanwhile, principals are finding it tough to work on the semester system. Shashi Sharma, principal of Everest Model Senior Secondary School, Moti Nagar, said, "It will increase work load of schools, as the exams will have to be conducted twice a year."

Heading: HSIIDC to have 4 pc equity in Delhi-Mumbai corridor - Indian Express
Content:
Union minister Ambika Soni to open Neem Chameli Project on October 7

After Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Ambika Soni inaugurates Neem Chameli project on October 7, visitors to the Retreat Ceremony can treat themselves to the Punjabi cuisine and hospitality. The event is likely to be attended by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal.

Sources said the international portal, which received thousands of domestic and foreign tourists daily, had been lacking in basic facilities, such as drinking water, refreshments, parking lots and toilets. The multi-crore project, which had invoked the ire of the border farmers, who had accused the government of not giving them right compensation, has been named 'Aman Umeed Complex', in view of the thaw in Indo-Pak relations. Principal Secretary Geetika Kalha said the complex would be a hot favourite with tourists. The complex includes a diner, where at least 100 people would be able to get the taste of the Punjabi cuisine at a time, rooms for overnight stay, fast-food counter, beer bar, cyber café and ATM.

Raj Kumar, a regular visitor to Attari, said earlier, the tourists had no other choice but to buy water from the stalls outside at high prices. DC K S Pannu said, "The tourist inflow to Attari border, which is already overwhelming, is likely to increase manifold with the inauguration of this complex. Ten acres of land had been acquired to provide parking facility to the visitors."

Heading: HC quashes land sale deed - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) would four per cent equity in the prestigious Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) project being undertaken by the Central government with Japanese collaboration.

The decision has been taken in response to the letter sent by the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry wherein Haryana Government was requested to participate in the equity of the newly-formed Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (DMICDC).

The state government has approved the participation of HSIIDC in the equity of the corporation with an investment of Rs 40 lakh. The managing director of HSIIDC has been nominated as special representative of the state government on the board of directors of the DMICDC.

HSIIDC MD Rajeev Arora informed that a MoU would be signed between HSIIDC and DMICDC for the purpose shortly.

A Dedicated Freight Corridor between Delhi and Mumbai, with terminals at Dadri in the National Capital Region of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai, which is to be around 1,500 kilometres in length and would pass through the states of Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra is being developed by the Centre. In order to tap the immense opportunities likely to be thrown open by the corridor, a band of 150 to 200 kilometres around both its sides is being developed as the Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC).

The DMIC project would be developed in phases, with Phase I to be implemented by 2012 and Phase II by 2016. As a strategy towards development of the project, pockets have been identified within the corridor as Investment Regions (IRs), with minimum area of 200 square kilometres and Industrial Area (IAs), with minimum area of 100 square kilometres. These regions would include self-sustained industrial townships with world-class infrastructure.

Heading: UK varsity panel visits RIMT institutes - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has quashed a land sale deed belonging to one Avnash Rani, a resident of Ferozpur, which was fraudulently executed by some local residents. Avnash Rani and her daughter Ritu Bala had moved the Court against Ferozepur Additional Deputy Commissioner; Jalalabad Sub Registrar and one Rakesh Kumar.

Ritu Bala had entered into an agreement with Rakesh for selling land measuring 9 kanals and 10 marlas, which belonged to her mother. The sale deed was executed for an amount of Rs 6,15,000. The petitioners alleged after payment of Rs one lakh the sale deed of the land was fraudulently executed with the help of 'influential' people of the area.

Heading: Literary-cum-cultural festival ‘Koshish’ kicks off at PCTE - Indian Express
Content:
A three-member delegation from Brunell University of United Kingdom visited RIMT Group Institutes here today. The delegation comprised of Prof Keith Dickson, Head of Brunell Business School, Marjorie Baker, acting head of Brunell International Office and Dr Prof Satwinder Singh, liaison officer of the university.

The team is on a three-day visit to study and assess the academics affairs of the RIMT Group Institutes. According a warm welcome to the delegation, the RIMT group chairman, Hukam Chand Bansal said, "Our group always encourages an exchange of views with institutes of international standard."

The delegation also interacted with students and the members of the faculty. Prof Keith Dickson, who has done an extensive research on intellectual property rights in small and medium enterprises in UK. delivered a lecture on the IPRs and shared his experience about the same.

He threw light on the IPRs and their implications in the contemporary business world. He said SMEs in UK were coming up with IPRs but facing uphill task of infringement of these rights. They face extreme difficulty in protecting these rights in the court of law as the legal process was quite costly. Only the big enterprises can afford the IPRs like patents, copy rights and can manage resources to protect them.

Dr Satwinder Singh, in his lecture, discussed the financial crisis gripping the US and its implications in Europe and third world countries. He discussed various possible strategies to counter the crisis.

Baker, who is also a special representative of the Brunell University VC, said their team was quite impressed by the infrastructure and academic standard which the group institutes were maintaining.

Dr B.S. Bhatia, the director general of the institute, said the delegation had explored the possibilities of collaboration in academic affairs in future. He said the RIMT group and the Brunell University might sign MoU in the areas of mutual interest in the coming days.

Heading: CMCH hands over body to relatives - Indian Express
Content:
The three-day long intra-institutional literary-cum-cultural festival, Koshish-2008 kicked off at the Punjab College of Technical Education (PCTE) on Friday.

Twenty one members including faculty and students of IQRA University, Islamabad, in Pakistan are participating in the festival. IQRA University is an academic partner of PCTE.

The function started on Friday morning with Business Quiz, Solo Dance and Clay Modelling competition after Sarojini Sharda Gautam, Registrar, PTU, announced the function open.

In Software Development (senior wing), Kapil and Deepak of BCA final (A section) got first prize, Gaurav and Shilpi of MCA-II got second prize, while Ravi Kumar and Gaganjot of BCA (final) Section C bagged the third prize.

In software development (junior wing), Varun and Rohan of BCA-II C won first prize, Pushpinder and Preetinder of BBA-II C bagged second prize and Parajeet and Inderpreet of BCA-II B secured third prize.

In Business Plan (senior wing), the first prize was bagged by a team of MBA final year section A students, 2nd prize by BBA final year section A students and third prize by a BCA final year section B students. In Case Presentation (Junior Wing), first prize was bagged by BBA 2nd year section C, second prize by BBA 2nd year section B and third prize by BBA 2nd year section C.

Dr K.N.S. Kang, Director, PCTE, congratulated the winners and wished them luck for the next competitions.

Heading: Rakesh Khanna: Man who rung in signature jewellery line - Indian Express
Content:
After four days, Najjar Singh's body was finally released from Christian Medical College and Hospital. Notable here is that Najjar Singh is a resident of Sahnewal had succumbed to injuries that he received during a clash in July this year. After two months of hospitalization, Singh died last Friday.

But then all this not happen without Najjar Singh's family holding a protest dharna at the hospital which ended only after the body was released.

The relatives of the deceased were protesting against the hospital authorities as the hospital authorities had refused to hand over the dead body of the deceased to his relatives as the family owes the hospital a bill of about Rs. 2.18 lakhs.

Dr Kanwal Masih, medical superintendent, said it's true because here in the hospital we start the treatment immediately and other hospital charge in advance. He said that the body had been handed over to the family. Dr Masih said the management decided to hand over the body after the villagers pleaded that family of the deceased was in penury.

Heading: Held for selling liquor on Dry Day - Indian Express
Content:
He says his line's launch in 1984 was flamboyant, neon signatures floating in the pool and champagne popping and same holds true for this jewelry designer whose works and attitude speak just the same.

It is for the first time in his career spanning over two decades that Rakesh Khanna, who owns a signature jewellery line, has displayed his work at Hotel Park along with his son Nipun and daughter Gayatri. While his exquisite pieces of jewellery have the women gushing over the sheer beauty of jewels on display, the man himself, Rakesh Khanna, plays it cool. " I have waited for the this change to come," he smiles.

A fifth generation jeweler and also India's first designer to win the De Beer's-instituted Diamond International Award, known as 'Oscar' of the jewellery world, for excellence and originality in jewellery design, Khanna says, "When I launched my line way back in 1984, people had no clue about signature lines. I think I was ahead of my times but I waited. I was bringing about a change in the way jewellery business is done and also waited for the change in the buyers. My idea is that one need not wear a complete set to adorn self, a single piece — it may just be a bracelet — can look as amazing."

His work has been featured in the Vogue, Madame and Cosmopolitan, and spans over assignments like New York's Cooper Hewitt museum in 1987 where Khanna received accolades for ingeniously blending East and West design ideas and for his use of gold to create textures similar to brocade, paisley and other fabric weaves.

"The basic idea is to blend the modern and tradition. The women today go to the pubs but also attend the pujas and for the women of today we make personalised pieces which can be worn with denims and also with sarees," says Khanna who swears by hand-crafted piece. "For this is my forte and not the dye cast jewellery pieces that are made in hundreds and sold out. While a single piece may take weeks to complete but then this is the way I work."

About Ludhiana, the designer remarked, "This city is like Las Vegas, Texas. I have clients from this city and I am here on personal invitation. I do not exhibit my work and this is first for me."

Heading: Wait gets longer at Land office after staff arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Khanna police arrested a liquor vend employee on the charge of selling liquor on Thursday, a dry day, and recovered 131 boxes of country-made liquor.

The employee, Vipin Kumar was reportedly selling liquor from the adjoining shop of the vend. SHO of city police station, Naveen Kumar said, "The police party led by ASI Davinder Pal Singh raided the liquor vend belonging to Bittu and Co. at Amloh road and arrested the accused, who were selling liquor on the dry day."

A case was registered. The SHO said that Vipin Kumar had been sent to judicial custody for 14 days by the local court.

Heading: HC raps PU: ‘Why is the university ignoring meritorious students?’ - Indian Express
Content:
With the Vigilance Bureau having nabbed the sub-registrar, Land Registries, along with a constable and a cashier for taking bribe on September 19, the work at the office is crippled owing to insufficient staff. Over 200 persons were waiting from 7 a.m at sub-registrar's office to get their registry done on Friday.

One of them, Major S S Aulakh said, "Though the office opens at 9 am but people normally come here early. To our surprise no one came till 11 am today and I was compelled to call the deputy commissioner to explain him about the entire matter."

Registries finally began at 1 pm when Mandeep Dhillon, a tehsildaar from Payal, started attending to customers at 1 pm.

All those who could not be attended to were given token numbers so that they could come on Monday. The residents, meanwhile, have demanded a permanent solution to the problem of long queues which has intensified after the arrest of the sub-registrar.

Heading: Ram Leela: Diverse expressions for same epic - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today expressed its surprise and despair over the Panjab University "favouring" certain individuals while ignoring meritorious students at the time of admissions. "What is wrong with the university? Shall we impose a fine now?" the division bench questioned.

The division bench, headed by Justice Hemant Gupta, made the observations while pronouncing orders on a few petitions filed by students. The admissions in question were cleared by Dean University Instructions (DUI) S K Kulkarni.

In the first case, the High Court allowed a petition filed by Gursimran Sekhon, a resident of Mohali, against PU and chairman of the Department of BPharmacy.

Sekhon (who placed third in the sports category list) was demanding admission against the two reserved seats for the sports category. The petitioner had sought permission for reconsidering her candidature after one of the seats fell vacant.

The petitioner alleged that someone else was granted admission even though she had higher merit.

In the second case, Hina Gupta, a resident of Sector 7, Panchkula, filed a petition against the chairperson of the joint admission committee, demanding that the admission of Piyush Jand in a BPharma course be quashed.

The petitioner submitted that she placed higher in merit than Piyush, "who was granted admission only on the basis of his Class XII marks". The High Court allowed the petition and expressed shock over the admissions granted by the university.

Heading: Complainant: ‘Stop accused from provoking students against me’ - Indian Express
Content:
The epic of Ramayana is being staged in the city by different Ram Leela committees with each staging performances in their own distinct styles.

The Ram Leela Committee, Bhai Randhir Singh Nagar, combines the use of Hindi and Punjabi. While some, totally abosrbed in their roles speak dialogues in Hindi, in between scenes, the narrator pitches in with inputs in Punjabi.

At Agar Nagar, the Ram Leela commitee has a group from Vrindavan performing in the lush green park.

While the touch of Avadh is reflected in their dresses and their usage of Hindi enthralls the audience, a clown is a regular crowd-puller.

At the historical ground of Daresi, the participants are brought in a well decorated "dola"(palki) from Thakur Dwara Nuaria, an old temple in the city.

The performances are staged on the ground itself, following which the performers are again carried back to Thhakur Dwara Nauria in the same way.

Ram Leela is also being staged at Dugri Phase-1 and at Kichlu Nagar.

Heading: Husband, in-laws sentenced to 10 yr RI in dowry death case - Indian Express
Content:
The complainant in the Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) sexual harassment case has again submitted an application to the Vice-Chancellor Manjit Singh Kang and Dean, College of Home Science, Neelam Grewal urging them to stop Dulcha Singh Brar from "provoking students and teachers against her".

On September 14, a woman employee had accused Brar, Director Students' Welfare, of sexual harassment and had submitted a written application to the PAU V-C.

Sources said the complainant had expressed in the application that she feels "uneasy and threatened" on the campus after she lodged the complaint. "The situation is aggravated when she has to go to Brar's office to attend meetings," added the source.

Neelam Grewal, who has been asked to the probe the matter by the V-C, said: "I have not seen the letter yet."

Asked why the complainant is sent for meetings chaired by Brar, Grewal said: "This is a routine affair but we ensure that she is protected. I had sent extra staff along with the complainant and had briefed them to take care of her."

When contacted, the complainant and Brar refused to comment on the issue.

Heading: 5-hr powercuts, 2 weekly offs, industrialists hit hard by PSEB - Indian Express
Content:
A local court, on Friday, sentenced four people to ten years' rigorous imprisonment in a dowry death case involving one Babita who was burnt to death in July 2002.

Those convicted include the deceased's husband Surinder Kumar, her father-in-law Ashok Kumar, mother-in-law Parveen Kumari alias Pinki and brother-in-law Mohinder Kumar alias Vicky of Sheera Colony, Tibba Road, Ludhiana.

Mamta, sister-in-law of the deceased along with her husband Naresh Kumar were, however, acquitted as the prosecution failed to prove its case against them.

On the statement of Babita's father, Jai Kumar, a case under Section 304-B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) was registered on July 9, 2002, with the Basti Jodhewal police station, Ludhiana, against Babita's in-laws.

The prosecution claimed that while sufficient dowry was paid when Babita was married to Surinder Kumar, her in-laws were unhappy and maltreated her.

Immediately after marriage, the accused raised their dowry demands and asked for a scooter and television, the prosecution asserted.

Jai Kumar alleged that on July 6, 2002, Surinder Kumar strangulated Babita while the other accused poured kerosene oil and set her body on fire.

The accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication on the other hand.

Pronouncing the verdict, Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) G S Saran, held that the prosecution had successfully proven the guilt of the accused and thereafter granted them the sentences accordingly.

Heading: Govt to hire PWD engineers on fast track to meet Games project deadlines - Indian Express
Content:
Unscheduled powercuts of upto five hours a day coupled with the two weekly offs imposed on the industrial units by the electricity board, seems to have irked the city industrialists.

Also, the induction furnace unit owners have increased the price of steel from Rs 35,000 to Rs 36,000 per ton, following the announcement of the two weekly offs.

The industrial associations complain that the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) is not making any effort to buy electricity for the industrial sector while they purchased and provided electricity free of cost to the farm sector during the paddy season.

Avtar Singh, general secretary Chamber of Industrial And Commercial Undertakings (CICU) said, "PSEB had been purchasing electricity from other states at the rate of Rs 7 per unit during the paddy season and had been providing it free of cost to the farmers.

On the other hand, the industrialists who pay the maximum are being denied even the minimum requirement of electricity."

Upkar Singh, joint secretary, CICU, further added, "We were waiting for the paddy season to be over so that we can heave a sigh of relief, but the situation has worsened."

While the industrial associations are upset over the sudden decision of furnace owners to increase steel prices, the furnace owners have their own reasons. They claim their production has reduced significantly due to the two weekly offs and hence they have no choice but to increase the prices as their units cannot run on genrators.

The industrialists also added that they are made to face three-hour long powercuts during peak hours, which sometimes extends to 9 hours as well.

Heading: PrÊt Á Pratap - Indian Express
Content:
With exactly two years to go before the Commonwealth Games commences in the national capital, and expenditure on civic infrastructure pegged at Rs 65,000 crore to be put in place by 2010, the Delhi Government has now sent a proposal to the Urban Development Ministry to allow hiring of engineers on a fast track.

The government is looking at creating a separate cadre of engineers as a result of a severe "shortage of engineers" in the PWD. Senior government officials said the separate cadre will be much like the separate health cadre that the Delhi Government created to fill vacancies for doctors in government-run hospitals. "Recruitment will be through the UPSC," said a senior official.

Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta said, "Right now our engineers are those repatriated from CPWD — firstly the numbers are not enough and secondly, the transfers take time. We want a State PWD created to ensure that there are no hitches in carrying out the projects. Right now the shortage, even at a senior level, is such that engineers are reluctant to take on new projects, citing that they are overworked. We want to carry out all recruitments for a state PWD with no repatriation from the Centre."

The Chief Secretary added that the requirement for engineers is dire keeping in mind that infrastructure development will be put into high gear early next year onwards to finish projects in time for the Games. According to senior officials, Delhi presently needs three additional chief engineers, six superintending engineers and approximately 100 junior engineers in the PWD alone to carry out and complete slotted projects for the Commonwealth Games.

Over the next two years, Delhi will be building 26 flyovers, bridges, railway overbridges and underbridges (between the PWD and the MCD), work on only 16 of which has begun. Besides these, flyovers and bridges that will provide connectivity to the Games Village and venues include: ITO Chungi, connecting the Games Village to the IGI Stadium, Velodrome and Chhatrasal Stadium (to be completed by June '09), Airport corridor— Aruna Asaf Ali Marg or Africa Avenue, BJ Marg or RTR Marg and Nelson Mendela or Vivekanand Marg to connect the Games Village to the airport (to be completed by June '09), among others.

Govt plans facelift for areas around Games venues
Gearing up for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, the Delhi government has decided to give a facelift to areas around all games venues in the city by installing touch screens, information kiosks and phone booths. According to officials, the government has decided to install all these within a two kilometre-radius of all games venues for the convenience of tourists attending the event. There are about 12 games venues in all.

"Since lakhs of foreign as well domestic tourists will be coming the city for the events, the area around the venues will be aesthetically developed and beautified for their convenience. Touch screens, information kiosks, food stalls and public conveniences such as phone booths, help desks and benches will come up in the area," an official said.

Rainwater harvesting and planting of trees will also be carried out, officials added. Energy-saving streetlights will also be installed. While agencies such as the MCD, NDMC and DDA will be responsible for developing the roads around the stadia, NDMC has already appointed two consultants and floated a tender for its two venues — Sardar Patel Marg Swimming Complex and Talkatora Stadium.
—ENS

Heading: Blast victim’s family faces stigma - Indian Express
Content:
Rajesh Pratap Singh makes a subtle style statement in Paris

Recession isn't hip, but it is happening. And if there is one thing that is on top of the designers' minds, it is the slide in the US economy. Not just in New York, but in faraway Milan and Paris, designers have focused on the essential rather than the extravagant. While baroque splendour is out, simple yet exciting collections like Raf Simons for Jil Sanders have earned applause for their socially relevant work.

That might be a reason why, when designer Rajesh Pratap Singh took his latest spring-summer 2009 collection to the runway at the Paris Fashion Week on Sunday, the simplicity and the easy charm of it worked on the Parisians. "This was our second show at Paris and we had decided to keep things as minimal as possible. We had concentrated on making the clothes wearable and when the show ended, the reaction was spontaneous," says Sapna Mehra, Pratap's business partner and sister-in-law, who has just got back to India after the show. The designer, who is still in Paris for the sales session, is equally happy with the way things have shaped up. "I have always believed in making clothes which are not loud or in your face. Like always, I concentrated on the structure, but I deliberately kept the clothes simple. I wasn't sure if the audience would get it, but the response has made me happy. Considering that business is slow this year, the orders have been good," he says.

The focus of Singh's collection has been a play on fabrics such as cotton and organza. "The whole onus has been on making a contrast between sheerness and opacity. He has worked with counts of cotton which he used to construct drapes that emphasise the difference," says Mehra. Singh's palette, too, has shown a marked departure from his usual pastels or, more recently, reds. For his Paris showing, Singh has worked with bright corals, deep pinks, fuchsias, graphite greys, even ecrus. One of the highlights of this year's collection is the way Singh has blended in seemingly obsequious tailoring elements like seams into embellishments. He has also done his own range of accessories that include chunky jewellery that highlight the tonal contrasts and shoes in transparent leather and acrylic. "Though we sell the shoes, I wasn't planning on marketing the jewellery. But it seems to have gone down well with the buyers because we have received several queries. I think we might sell it now," says Singh.

Singh's show was attended by his regular international clients like Maria Luisa and his newfound admirers, Armand and Michael Hadida of the Tranoi Fair, where he will be participating next. From India, those present included Aman Nath and Francis Wacziarg of Neemrana and fashion stylist, Sujata Assomull.

Heading: A Musical Spin - Indian Express
Content:
While the family of Santosh, the 13-year-old who died in the Mehrauli blast on September 27, was given the compensation cheque of Rs five lakh, nine other injured victims were also given cheques of Rs 50,000 each on Friday.

Though the Delhi Police has categorically said that they were only conducting a regular enquiry of all victims of the Mehrauli blast on September 27, the family Allaudin Mukti Khan, the 23-year-old victim of the blast with abdominal injuries, alleges the police have subjected them to interrogation in the last few days.

"It is only since Thursday that the police have stopped interrogating our family, but our kids are now having a hard time in school. My brother's seven-year-old son Hamid, who studies in Class I in a private school in Chhattarpur, was told by his teacher that his uncle (Allaudin) is a terrorist," said Sahabuddin, the victim's brother.

"He is an innocent child who doesn't know what all this means, and so he came back and told this to his mother. But there are older children too in the family, who will probably commit suicide if something like this is said to them," Sahabuddin said.

According to the family, the police have rounded up Allaudin as a suspect because he possessed a passport, two licences: one from Delhi and the commercial licence from Nagaland, and a PAN card. "All these documents are with the police, which they haven't returned to us till date," rued Sahabuddin.

Meanwhile, the SDM (South) on Friday distributed compensation cheques to nine victims admitted at the AIIMS Trauma Centre. "We have given compensation cheques to the Mehrauli blast victims today. The family of Santosh was given cheque of Rs five lakh, and nine others injured who are still admitted in the hospital, were given Rs 50,000 each. We will revise the compensation after verifying with his relatives," said Sarvan Bhagria, SDM (south).

Heading: Munnabhai MP? - Indian Express
Content:
Four years after it was first staged in Delhi, the musical Magic of Broadway returns with the story, songs and razzmatazz of the American stage

An artist straight off West End is thrown in with a bunch of talented, eager amateurs — and they come up with a musical along the lines of Broadway — on Broadway. "This is essentially a musical that traces the history of Broadway from 1925 to 1986," says Jyotsna Laroiya, the producer of the musical, fittingly titled The Magic of Broadway.

Laroiya, who had staged the production earlier in 2004 in Delhi, has collaborated with performing artist Fiona Hedger-Gourlay to transform the musical into a Broadway-style performance. "There are lots of movements with flashy costumes, and lighting is very important," says Hedger-Gourlay who has energetically put together her ambitious directorial venture.
