A West End artist, Hedger-Gourlay has acted in productions like The Hot Mikado and My Fair Lady, played the clarinet for a band and acted with two pop groups in the 1980s. Currently, the spirited lady runs an all-woman choir group called Delhi Divas. The 75-minute musical will see some snappy dance sequences with contemporary jazz, rock and roll and the customary, old-school-style dancing seen in West Side Story. "We begin with Yanky Doodle Dandy and a comic bluster act. And we have made sure that every cast member is grooving throughout the musical," says choreographer Angela Samantha. So, picture the chorus girls warbling from Annie Get Your Gun with expressive gestures.

Laroiya says she has always been fascinated by Broadway. "I believe the musical would be quite educational as it exposes the audiences to 60 different shows in a short span of time," she explains. The proceeds from the concert will go to HelpAge India.

The musical, which opens in mid-October with 18 singers and half-dozen dancers, will have the cast singing songs from Broadway hits like Oklahoma, Les Miserables, Sweeney Todd, Les Cage aux Folle, Grease and Phantom of the Opera. "We begin with songs from traditional American shows like Yankee

Doodle Dandy and Crazy Girl," says Hedger-Gourlay.

Squeezing in all these different styles of music and blending them into a 90-minute performance was no easy task. "We chose some of the best shows and we won't be singing entire songs," says Hedger-Gourlay. Most of the cast members manage a day job and rehearsals. "We have a student, a management consultant, a corporate trainer and publisher who are all part of the musical," says Laroiya.

The seven-act show promises syncopated passages with amazing ease under the baton of Hedger-Gourlay. "You have a mix of choruses followed by a solo. The tempo is kept high throughout," says Hedger-Gourlay. Situ Singh Buehler, who heads the Delhi Opera Ensemble, will sing Think of me from the Phantom of the Opera while Hedger-Gourlay will sing the title song Cabaret from the show Cabaret. The finale song is from the delightfully melodic A Chorus Line.

The musical is on October 18, 19 at Kamani auditorium. For tickets, contact jolaroiya@gmail.com

Heading: Militants or martyrs? Funeral prayers offered for duo slain in encounter - Indian Express
Content:
With 20 films under his belt, a new production house and political ambitions, meet the new, improved Sanjay Dutt

A career going great guns and a seemingly happy personal front, life is all roses for Sanjay Dutt. Kidnap, his first big film of 2008, is out, and movies like Blue, EMI and Aladin, will see the light of Friday in the last quarter of the year. Dutt has also turned producer with the launch of his banner, Sanjay Dutt Productions. Its two films — an action adventure directed by Soham Shah and another action film directed by Milan Luthria — are scheduled to hit the floors next year. Talks are also on with five more directors, which make it seven films in all. And Dutt will act in all of these. The actor is also committed to a couple of film assignments for Balaji Films. In all, the actor has almost 20 films in various stages of production.

"I'm very charged up about life and want to do a lot of good work. Thankfully, I'm still getting it," he says with characteristic nonchalance.

There are other things that Dutt is contemplating. Promoting boxing is one, ever since Vijender Singh got home a bronze from Beijing. Trying his hand in politics is also on his wish list, but that will happen, he says, when the work pressure is less.

Kidnap, a high-action drama, has him essaying the role of a multi-millionaire whose daughter is held for ransom. The role is special for Dutt because it is for the first time that he is playing father to a teenage girl, close to his daughter's age, one of the reasons he was considered for the role. "Sanjay Gadhvi saw me with my daughter Trishala on a show and said he could think of no one but me to play the part. There are times in a person's life when all the money in the world can be of no use. Working in this intense drama between a father and a daughter was an emotional experience for me. I also enjoyed working with Imran Khan whom

I found to be a very confident actor," says Dutt.

The actor hotly denies that relations between him and his daughter are strained because of his marriage to Manyata. "Trishala was with us in the Bahamas when I was shooting for Blue, and even otherwise we are on the Net everyday. She is studying forensic sciences and just the other day she called to say that there was a body with a bullet in the head lying in front of her. She was so cool about it, but it really blew my mind," he smiles indulgently.

Heading: not Just a fine, smokers pay for every puff too - Indian Express
Content:
Some 3,000 people today gathered at funeral prayers for Atif and Sajid, exactly two weeks after the alleged masterminds of September 13 serial blasts were killed in an encounter at Batla House, Jamia Nagar.

Wearing white 'Eid' kurtas with black armbands and waving black flags, the residents took out a protest march and gathered at the Batla House graveyard for the 'namaz-e-janaza' (funeral prayers). Jamia Nagar Coordination Committee, an organisation of community workers and local politicians, organised the mass prayer.

"We are expressing solidarity with Atif and Sajid, victims of a fake encounter," Irfanullah Khan, a Samata party member and convener of the committee, said.

S Q R Ilyas, Jamat-e-Islami spokesperson and a committee member, said, "This is a 'ghaibana namaz' — a funeral prayer held in absence of the corpses. There's no time limit for such a prayer. Besides, Atif and Sajid were killed on a Friday; today is also a Friday." Ilyas also blamed the police for burying Atif and Sajid at Nizamuddin graveyard, though "relatives wanted to bury them in Batla House".

As Khan gave a fiery speech alleging loopholes in the encounter and demanding a judicial inquiry, the emotional crowd chanted "Allahu Akbar" as dozens of policemen looked on.

Shazib, 26, who claims to have an MBA degree from the US and is a neighbour of Adnan, the youth detained a day after serial blasts and released later, said: "Adnan told me the cops put him in a cold storage and quizzed him. When he was unable to offer an answer to any question, he was slapped."

But many found "political motivation" behind today's gathering. "These politicians are only cashing in on emotions of the people as elections are round the corner," said Firoz Bakht Ahmed, grandnephew of Maulana Azad and a former madrasa teacher.

On area MLA and AICC secretary Parvez Hashmi meeting Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit to demand a judicial inquiry, he said, "Hashmi, the impostor, arrived with the police on the day of the encounter and warned people to go inside their homes. His about-turn is a farce. He has done nothing for this area for 15 years."

Heading: Teen makes hoax threat call to Vodafone, arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Two Spanish tourists, one from France, a suicidal taxi driver and a Railway employee on a lunch break — these people from diverse backgrounds had one thing in common on Friday— they were all issued challans at the New Delhi Railway Station for smoking on the second day of the blanket ban on smoking in public spaces.

As the government gears up to strictly implement the ban by doubling the number of squads meant to keep an eye on smokers to 16, Newsline followed the Central District Flying Squad keeping a vigil on Connaught Place and the New Delhi Railway Station area during the day and caught them in action at the railway station this morning:

10.30 am: Led by Dr K J S Bansal, Additional Chief District Medical Officer, a team of six officials leave their office in Paharganj to reach the New Delhi Railway station. Drive begins outside the railway station at the Ajmeri gate side at 11 am.

12.30 pm: With merely 10 challans issued in the morning, officials declare the day as 'dull'. "I think most people know about the ban already," says a 'dejected' Rajesh Bhardwaj, after dealing with an agitated smoker.

12.35 pm: Bhardwaj finds Zaeed, a taxi driver lighting a cigarette near the VIP parking stand. Frustrated over not finding a single customer all morning, Zaeed refuses to pay, picks up a brick and threatens to injure himself. His friend, who incidentally had pulled out a cigarette just before the crackdown, offered to pay for Zaeed after a cop intervened.

12.45 pm: With Zaeed still screaming about his right to smoke on a bad day, the squad proceeds to the platform. "These are the problems we have to face while dealing with the public. We need protection as well," remarks Bhardwaj, adding that once they begin a crackdown on restaurants and pubs, they will have to take police constables with them.

12.50 pm: Bansal spots a catch: a man nonchalantly smoking near the left end of Platform 4. The squad rushes to intercept him. Railway employee Deen Mani is given a handbill first. He sheepishly hides his beedi and apologises. Bhardwaj issues a challan and Mani admits that he knew about the ban. "Jaldi aa gaye squad wale," he says as he painfully takes out Rs 200. He is left with only a Rs 50 note for the day.

1.10 pm: The squad finally makes it to the crowded Paharganj end. Dr Bansal finds a crowd near a corner paan shop and says, "This law is primarily to protect the rights of the passive smoker. We cannot stop smokers from smoking at the railway station until we remove these kiosks from the entrance. But then that's not a part of our job."

1.25 pm: 50 year-old Kailash is spotted near a public convenience. As he pockets the handbill laying down the rules, he tells Bhardwaj, "I am from Rajasthan. Never heard about the law in my state."

1. 30 pm: This time the catch is an unsuspecting Jamsher from Gorakhpur, caught near the auto stand. He hands out Rs 200, with much regret.

1.50 pm: Vijay Kumar of Janakpuri sees the squad and throws his lit cigarette. Apologises for breaking the law but is allowed to go only after he pays the challan.

2.15 pm: After warning a foreign traveller just as he started lighting up, the day's catch is a tourist trio brandishing their cigarettes while heading towards the station. French tourist Antonio surprises Bhardwaj and Bansal by asking them for their ids and then going on to lecture on how the space outside the railway station is not a non-smoking area in his country. He agrees to pay the fine.

His friends from Spain too agree to honour the rule of the land. "Smoking in India is very expensive," says Maria.

Heading: HC directs police to let lawyers, relatives visit blast accused - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh police claim to have arrested a Firozabad native for making a bomb hoax call to Aegis, a call centre of Vodafone. The accused allegedly called after he was fed up with the calls he received from the mobile phone service company. Company officials, however, have received two more hoax calls on October 1.

The first bomb hoax call to the call centre located at A-5, Sector 3, was received around 8.30 pm on September 29. "The matter was reported to DIG Vikram Singh and Additional Deputy General of Police (Law and Order), Brij ,Lal along with the local police. The call was traced to Firozabad," said a senior police official.

Noida Police arrested a 16-year-old for making the call. Tinku Yadav, the accused, has an interesting reason for making the hoax call. "The phone service provider kept on disturbing me with unsolicited calls while I was tilling the fields. I was fed up with their regular calls asking to take some scheme or the other introduced by the company," said Yadav defending his act. His bail application is yet to come up in court.

Yadav told the company that he is a commander of Indian Mujahideen, a terror outfit allegedly behind recent spate of attacks across the country, and threatened to blow the building. "I told them that I am commander 'A' of Indian Mujhahideen. I have been hearing about commander 'A' quite frequently," said Yadav. It was when the police arrested him that he realised the enormity of his crime, the official said.

The police said the call centre had received two more bomb hoaxes - one from Hapur, Ghaziabad, and the other from Mawana village of Meerut. "We are not in a position to take such calls lightly," said SP(City) Ashok Tripathi.

Heading: MCD parking plans go awry - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday directed the police to grant access to lawyers representing five suspects arrested in the September 13 serial blasts.

A Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar passed the order while hearing a petition filed by Zia-ur-Rahman, one of the five persons arrested by the Special Cell in connection with the blasts last month, through his counsel Shanti Bhushan and Prashant Bhushan.

Listing the case for hearing on October 15, the court provided "liberty" to any of the persons concerned to approach the High Court any time before the scheduled date of hearing. The court allowed the suspect's sister and two lawyers to meet him for an hour at 7 pm on Friday at the office of Assistant Commissioner of Police Sanjeev Kumar Yadav on Lodhi Road. The court observed that if a "similar request is made on behalf of any other arrested person, the person shall have access to two lawyers as well as one relative on similar lines."

The court has also agreed to allow the same right of access to another of the five accused, Saqib Nissar, who had filed a criminal petition in this regard before the High Court. In his petition, Rahman said lawyers and relatives who approached the police on October 1 and 2 were denied access.

"It is stated that the police on October 1, 2008 asked the sister of Zia (Rahman) to come to the police station on October 2 at noon. However, when she went along with her lawyer, she was denied access," the Bench quoted from the petition.

Defending the police, counsel Mukta Gupta said Rahman was taken for "investigation" at the time of the lawyers' visit on October 1. The counsel submitted that no one had turned up for the meeting on the next day despite the police informing the family.

"Though his (Rahman's) relations were informed that they could visit him at 5 pm on October 2, none visited him on that day," Gupta contended. She submitted on record that the police had no objection about today's meeting. Both accused were arrested on September 21. They have been suspected of providing logistics support for the serial blasts which claimed over 20 lives.

NEW DELHI: Relatives of Zia-ur-Rehman and Saqib, arrested for their alleged involvement in Delhi blasts, had come to meet the duo at the Special Cell office in Lodhi Colony on different occasions, their lawyers said. While Saqib's relatives arrived to meet him at about 6 pm, Zia-ur-Rehman's sister and maternal uncle arrived at 7.05 pm — the time given to them by the court. Both families remained inside the police station for about half-an-hour today.

Zia-ur-Rehman's advocate Prashant Bhushan said, "The family members have met him and he seems to be fine." Asked whether Zia was tortured, he said, "There were no such signs and he looked fine."

Bhushan added that his family members didn't even know that Zia has been kept in the Cell's office and they came to know it through the media. "The relatives didn't know about their rights that they could meet him in custody," he said. "We filed a petition in High Court and got the order to meet him."

Zia's relatives did not want to talk to the media.

Heading: Back in the Picture - Indian Express
Content:
In July 2007, Lieutenant-Governor Tejendra Khanna laid the foundation stone for the proposed multi-level underground parking lot in Kamla Nagar market. More than a year on, the MCD is yet to get clearances from other public agencies to get ahead, let alone begin construction work.

But going by the civic body's record that hardly sticks out like a sore thumb, for the municipality's plans include making 24 such multi-level underground parking lots before the Commonwealth Games in 2010. And none of them are anywhere near the starting block as far as beginning construction goes.

An MCD source said the municipality rushed announcement of the project without doing even basic paperwork. "There is a water and sewer line below the park in Kamla Nagar," the source said. "MCD will have to first take permission from the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) to make the parking lot. Some clearance was also necessary from the DDA.

"But since the project was already running behind schedule, the Corporation first laid the foundation and later went to get necessary clearances."

As per MCD schedule, work for nine parking lots was to take off by this March, and the civic body had announced in June that work for all other lots would take off. On ground, though, it's an entirely different story.

Interestingly, Mayor Arti Mehra had flown off to Germany, Italy and Hong Kong a few months ago to study multi-level parking — the expenses came to lakhs, as reported by Newsline on October 1. She had assured that these parking lots would be ready by 2010. But officials of Suvidha Parklift, MCD's consultants for parking projects, said it is "impossible" to finish these projects before the Games.

MCD Standing Committee chairman Vijendar Gupta, however, said: "The parking project has nothing to do with the Commonwealth Games — this (2010) is just the target we have set for ourselves. We are hoping that we would complete all work before the Games but too many departments are involved, and there is too much paperwork to be done. (So) the project is getting delayed."

Some proposed sites
* Main market, Kamla Nagra
* Shastri Park, Karol Bagh
* Main market, GKII
* Greater Kailash-II market
* Main market, South Extension
* Defence Colony market
* Green Park market
* Rajouri Garden
* Lajpat Nagar
* Rani Bagh
* PVR Complex, Saket
* PVR Complex, Vasant Vihar
* Minto Road
* Kutub Road, Paharganj

Heading: Eight-foot python found in Capital - Indian Express
Content:
They were lying forgotten in crates for over a quarter of a century — the negatives that Kulwant Roy, an Associated Press photographer, had carefully dispatched to Aditya Arya over the years, the last batch reaching Arya just before Roy's death in 1984. Now, they are out of the boxes and on the walls of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts. And they are delightful images from the past — Mahatma Gandhi gesturing to Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who almost looks exasperated; Gandhi collecting money for the Harijan Welfare Fund in Delhi sometime in the early 1940s; Jawaharlal Nehru clutching a cricket bat in one picture and playing Holi at Teen Murti Bhavan in another, and Sardar Patel arriving at the 1945 Simla Conference in a hand-drawn tonga as Nehru and Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan walk beside. The personal delightfully merges with the political in them.

These are just a few of the 100 black-and-white images that Arya, a Delhi-based photographer and a family friend of Roy, has selected and digitised.

"The agenda of the time was to create an iconography of the important people," says Sabeena Gadihoke, who has curated the exhibition "History in the Picture".

Alongside the heroes, there are also pictures of the nameless multitude, like the workers building the Bhakra Nangal Dam, the temple of Nehruvian India.

Arya, 48, says it would take a couple of years to digitise and restore all the pictures. Unfortunately, many are lost for ever. When Roy was travelling across the world in the 1960s, he put his pictures in boxes and mailed them to his Delhi address. None of them reached. Roy searched the post offices and garbage dumps of Delhi, but never found them.

The exhibition "History in the Making" is on at the Indira Gandhi Center for the Arts till October 21

Heading: Roadies turn rowdies - Indian Express
Content:
A house near an old Shiv Mandir in North Delhi's Civil Lines has revealed an unlikely resident straight out of mythology: a 20-kilo, eight-foot long adult python. Residents of Chandrawal area in Civil Lines reported they saw a snake late Wednesday night. It turned out to be a 20-kilo python, found on the roof of a household. An excited crowd had gathered below the house.

"The python was lodged in the thin roof between two houses. It seems to have climbed a tree and reached the roof. It was noticed only at night and the call came at 11.30 pm. A huge crowd had gathered below the house to watch the operation," said Sanjay Acharya of Wildlife SOS, who rescued the snake.

Heading: Toll 2: 6 days after Mehrauli blast, Lucknow man dies at AIIMS - Indian Express
Content:
Things took an ugly turn at the auditions of the MTV's adventure reality show Roadies as thousands of youngsters lined up at the gates of the NCUI Auditorium on Friday morning, when a violent mob vandalised the venue, breaking the glass of the main entrance door, burning pamphlets, breaking chairs and tables and throwing bottles of water all over the place.

"This is the sixth season of the show and it is the first time something like this has happened. We still don't know what exactly triggered it off. Certain rowdy elements took upon themselves to ruin the fun everyone had come for," said Vaibhav Vishal, associate VP for content, MTV.

The auditions were scheduled to begin at 9 am and were delayed by an hour. It was after four group discussions that the crowd turned violent, around 11.30am. "We had conducted about four group discussions, each having 20 people, when suddenly a large group of boys started creating a ruckus and forced the gates open," said Vishal.

The auditions, which were spread over three days from October 3 to 5, were finally cancelled till the management finds itself a new venue and zeroes in on another date schedule — information on which might be found on the MTV website or the channel.

The sixth season of Roadies plans to take 20 contestants to Australia to fight for a prize money of Rs 10 lakh. While a total of 7,000 people had turned up for auditions in Delhi last year, this year the number seemed to have gone up to anywhere between 8000 and 9000.

"The show has a cult following and we are already through with conducting auditions in four cities. Everything has gone smoothly so far. It's unfortunate that something like this would happen in Delhi because it is one of our favourite cities and we get some of the best contestants from this city," added Vishal.

A senior Delhi Police official said the police were not "informed about such a huge turnout".

Heading: Ex-workers ‘threaten’ Graziano officer - Indian Express
Content:
Declared brain dead on Thursday night, Dipu, a victim of the September 27 blast in Mehrauli, became the second fatal victim of the mystery explosion — he died at AIIMS on Friday afternoon. A nine-year-old boy had died in the blast earlier.

Most critical of the injured victims, Dipu, 23, was identified three days after the blast.

Dr M C Mishra, casualty medical officer at AIIMS Trauma Centre, said they could get the Lucknow-based family's permission for organ donation too late in the day to salvage the organs. Doctors met the family this morning, and agreed to donate Dipu's kidneys, lungs and eyes, Dr Mishra said.

"But he was already running a low blood pressure and was kept on life-support system," Dr Mishra said. "Organ removal becomes doubtful in such cases; he died at 2.35 pm, before we could operate on him."

Dipu came here last year and lived in Gadaipur village near Mehrauli; he worked as a security guard in a farmhouse there.

One of his roommates Shravan, 21, said Dipu had gone to the market that afternoon to buy clothes and a small cylinder.

The victim's brother Shamsher said the family had been asking Dipu to return home in Lucknow for quite some time. "He insisted on staying in Delhi, though he had promised to come home on Diwali," Shamsher said. Doctors at AIIMS said Dipu received serious head injuries and his face took the brunt of the explosion.

Heading: Legalising colonies: Sheila, Maken fight for one-upmanship - Indian Express
Content:
An assistant manager working with the Greater Noida unit of Italian multinational Graziano Transmissioni today lodged a police complaint against four dismissed employees of the company for threatening him. All four are wanted in the murder of company CEO Lalit K Choudhary.

According to the complaint lodged at Bisrakh police station, Phool Singh, an assistant manager with Graziano, was on way to attend a meeting at the company office. He said, "The four blocked my way and threatened me with dire consequences if I deposed against them in court." The incident occurred last week, Singh, a Ghaziabad resident, said.

Bisrakh police station house officer B K Sharma said, "We have registered a complaint against the four persons and are searching for them. We are yet to trace the seven absconding employees named in the FIR."

Choudhary was killed on September 22.

Heading: Jamia not using public money for legal aid to suspects, says V-C - Indian Express
Content:
When Congress president Sonia Gandhi on Saturday gifts provisional certificates of regularisation to residents of the Capital's 1,500-odd unauthorised colonies, she will have on stage at Chhatrasal stadium two of her senior party colleagues — Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and Union Minister of State for Urban Development Ajay Maken — both of whom have fought bitterly over the last two years trying to take credit for the process.

Congress sources say Maken is miffed at the way he was invited by the state, just a simple invite, not the usual formal letter by a Delhi Cabinet minister. This party member said: "Since both Maken and Union minister for Urban Development Jaipal Reddy were part of the regularisation process, the norm calls for a formal invite by one of the Delhi ministers."

Sources said a defiant Maken will surely put in an appearance at Saturday's rally, specially since Sonia Gandhi will be present. "Maken claims the Delhi government had initially dragged its feet on his initiative to regularise the colonies," the source added.

Meanwhile, members of the Dikshit camp said the Delhi government has prodded the Urban Development Ministry at every stage to regularise these colonies. "The process of regularisation was first started by Indira Gandhi in 1977. In 1993, 567 out of a total 607 colonies were regularised," said an official. In 1994, 1,071 colonies were identified for the process and the Delhi High Court issued orders to provide water and power to these colonies. In February 2004, the Urban Development Ministry ordered regularisation.

A Congress member said: "In 2004, the Sheila government asked residents' welfare associations to register for the process. We received 1,432 applications. A similar process was reinstituted in 2006. The government has already released Rs 658 crore to civic agencies out of a total budget of Rs 2,800 crore. The work on roads, water lines, sanitation, etc has begun in 728 colonies."

The state will issue certificates to an estimated 35 to 40 lakh residents who live in these colonies and who will now form a crucial vote bank in as many as 15 to 20 Assembly seats. In order to prevent Dikshit walking away with the cake, Maken went as far as attending an Assembly session on September 10 when the Delhi Assembly was to discuss the matter of unauthorised colonies and watched the proceedings from the visitors' gallery — the first time a Union minister had done so.

Focus: Jamia Nagar
Residents of 8 colonies in and around Jamia Nagar will get provisional certificates on Saturday. These are Khalilullah Masjid colony — the site close to the September 19 encounter — Jamia Nagar, Batla House, Gaffar Manzil-II, Joga Bhai, Zakir Nagar, Zakir Nagar West and Taimur Nagar extension. Parts of Abu Fazal Enclave from Block E-N will also be granted the certificate.

Heading: Court orders attachment of property of Sultanpur MLA’s public school - Indian Express
Content:
Prof Mushirul Hasan, Vice-Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia, on Friday said it is wrong to believe that the university is using tax-payers' money to provide legal and financial aid to the two Jamia students arrested for suspected links to the September 13 serial blasts.

"The public exchequer or the UGC (University Grants Commission) is not being charged for the relief, as alleged by several individuals and political parties," he said. "In Jamia, as in several other universities across the country, we have a students' aid fund. The money used in the process will be taken from this fund, which is contributed by our own students."

Prof Hasan was speaking to The Indian Express staffers as part of the weekly Idea Exchange programme; the longer version of the interaction will be published on Sunday.

He said: "Providing legal aid does not mean we intend to interfere with the legal process or defend the two; we will provide them access to justice, which is their right under the Constitution." He said the students "cannot be branded as terrorists until proven guilty — and if they are proven guilty by the court of law, not a tear will be shed by anyone."

Prof Hasan said a university's role is "like that of a parent", a view he said is shared by eminent jurists like Ram Jethmalani. He said the incidents of September 19 — the day of the encounter — are in "no way connected to the university. It is outrageous to castigate an 80-year old university on the basis of unproven charges against a couple of students."

He said, "As head of the institution, I will defend the constitutional, legal and moral rights of the university while preserving its liberal secular character."

Heading: 241 in 130: city lad whips up a ‘record’ - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Friday ordered the attachment of property of a public school in Nangloi area, run by a Congress MLA. The order came after R D Public School failed to pay a claimant his dues as accident compensation inspite of a previous court order to the effect. Noting that the school was being run by one Jai Kishen, an MLA from Sultanpur, the court directed the divisional commissioner (North-West) to make the attachment.

"It is revealed by the decree holder that the school belonged to Sultanpuri MLA Jai Kishan and therefore the officials of divisional commissioners are not effecting the attachment under his fear," said Additional District Judge Gurdeep Singh. "This infact further makes it incumbent to expedite the attachment which will only be effected through divisional commissioner Delhi," the ADJ added.

On January 29, 2004, Devi Das was seriously injured when a bus belonging to the school hit him. Das, thereafter, filed a petition in the MACT. A sum of Rs 61,213 was awarded to him as compensation by the tribunal in March 2007. It had ordered the school to pay the amount within a month from the order. With the school, however, failing to respond to the order, Das then sought an execution order from the court.

During the hearing, the SDM (Kanjhawala) informed the court though the recovery proceedings had been initiated against the school, the order could not be executed due to the ongoing farmers' stir at the divisional commissioner's office.

The court then directed the divisional commissioner to start the attachment proceedings himself and fixed the November 14 as the date for the next hearing in the case.

Heading: Police get witness, suspect Saumya knew killer - Indian Express
Content:
The white floppy hat provided just a little relief from the blazing sun. Milind Gautam looked equally nervous as any other probable lined up for the Delhi Under-19 trials at the Ferozeshah Kotla on Friday afternoon, unsure if his 'record' knock on Thursday can bargain him a place in the squad.

On Thursday, the Class XI Commerce student had scored a whopping 241 runs in an inter-school 50-over tournament — an Indian batting record awaiting official confirmation. Batting at number three for Modern School-Barakhamba Road, the 18-year old right-hander hit 11 sixes and 28 boundaries in 130 balls against Laxman Public School on home ground in the sixth SPV-GC Mittal cricket tournament.

"It took me some time to come to terms with scoring a double hundred in 50 overs," he said. "When I did, I started screaming and told everyone what I had achieved, but no one believed me — they all thought I was bluffing.

"I called up my father and he said, 'good your team scored 241, how much did you score?'. I had to repeat that I had scored all those runs myself. Only after everyone saw the official scoresheet did they believe me."

Replying to Modern School's mammoth total of 466, Laxman Public School scored 213.

The knock had the selectors talking too. National junior selector and former India paceman Sanjeev Sharma said, "It's an exceptional knock. The ground is big but to simply score that much means he's an exciting talent."

The innings, though, has just begun for the lad from Sonnet Club.

Heading: Pre-poll: BJP flouts MCD rules, frames law - Indian Express
Content:
Another witness has approached the police claiming he heard a noise similar to a bullet around the time a woman journalist of a private television channel, Saumya Vishwanathan, was shot dead four days ago. The witness told police he was passing by when he heard the sound.

Police said the witness (police has not revealed his identity) heard the noise around the time Vishwanathan's car hit the central verge on Nelson Mandela Road around 3.30 a.m.

Claiming giving away any more details "might hamper the investigations", DCP South, HGS Dhaliwal has appealed to people who had travelled on the same road the day Vishwanathan died to approach police with information.

Police officials said Vishwanathan's colleagues told them that she was a promising producer with the news channel. Before heading home, she had completed an unusually long shift at work, having stayed back to help with her channel's coverage of Gujarat and Maharashtra blasts of September 29.

She was found dead in her white Maruti Suzuki Zen car on the Nelson Mandela Road in the Vasant Kunj area around 3.30 am on Tuesday. She was headed home in Sector-C of Vasant Kunj.

An employee of Punjabi By Nature, a restaurant nearby, had noticed her car ram into the divider. He was returning home on his bicycle. He had called police after he saw Vishwanathan's head tilted on the right side of the car. The ignition, air-conditioner and headlights were on.

Police later found that she was shot in the head on the right side. "We have almost ruled out a case of a road rage, as the blue paint marks found on Vishwanathan car's was has been accounted for as having hit a signboard at the accident site," a senior police official said.

Initially, the police believed that the marks might have been due to brushing with another car.

Police said the accident took place in a span of 15-20 minutes. Sources said she had spoken to her father M K Vishwanathan at 3.10 am and she died around 3.30 am, police said.

Police said that she either might have been shot by a person sitting with her inside the car or by assailant (s) driving parallel to her car on the road after some altercation. Police suspect in either case, she must have known the killer.

Police are now filtering records of criminals who use countrymade weapons. They also studying CCTV footage obtained from the parking lot of her Jhandewalan office. It only shows her getting down the stairs, paying a coffee vendor, sitting in her car, getting out to clean her windshield and then driving away, the police said.

Heading: Puja organisers to mix revelry with charity, gather funds for flood victims - Indian Express
Content:
Section 72 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act clearly states that the first House meeting every month has to be a General House meeting. No pending agendas of the previous month can be taken up in the first meeting of the month. The decisions taken and the agendas passed in this meeting shall be treated null and void.

But with Assembly elections round the corner, it seems the BJP is not concerned following rules. In haste to allow commercial activities in the garage of DDA flats, the BJP, which holds a majority in the House, passed the resolution without hearing out the Opposition.

"The DMC Act does not allow a pending matter to be passed in the first House meeting of the month. Now when the elections are round the corner the Mayor is randomly passing one item after the other," said the MCD leader of the Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma.

The Congress has decided on sending a legal notice to the Mayor and will also write to the Lieutenant Governor. The BJP, however, denies having violating any law.

But the Municipal Secretary Office confirms that there has been a violation of the act. "The agendas passed in the house today can be declared null and void," informed the Secretary Office.

Heading: Now, another league for Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Durga Puja committees in the Capital this year are aiming to combine celebrations with charity. A number of Puja committees are trying to cut down on expenses or planning to set up special booths to collect donations for the flood victims of Bihar and Orissa.

The CR Park Kali Mandir will have a stall run by a city-based NGO to collect donations for Bihar and Orissa.

"The NGO has taken up the responsibility of raking up funds, and as organisers even we will try to pool in more money from sponsorships," said Ashish Dutta, Chairman, CR Park Kali Mandir Durga Puja committee.

The B Block Puja committee in CR Park too, has plans for gathering funds for flood victims.

"We get a lot of sponsorships and donations from companies for the Puja and this year we will try to channelise some of the funds for the flood victims. In previous years as well, we have given out a certain portion of the donations for charity," Ashim Banerjee, president of the Puja samiti.

Organisers at the CR Park Mela Ground Puja samity, have, however, tried to cut down on the expenses of pandal construction and other preparations with the aim to save money for the victims.

"Apart from the donations and contributions, we have tried to cut down on expenses to apportion a certain amount for the flood victims," said Narayan Dey, CR Park Durga Puja Samity, Mela Ground.

Heading: Life’s sweet for Metha on the football field - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when reports that Delhi might be dropped from the AFC's list of beneficiaries through the Vision India project are making the rounds, a new league comprising the best in the business in the Capital — that is, top eight of the fourteen participating clubs in the senior division DSA league — is what Delhi's soccer fans can cheer about.

Delhi Soccer Association secretary NK Bhatia says the Elite league has been planned to encourage local participation. "The top eight clubs of the senior division will play in the league which will be played from July. The last two teams will be relegated to the senior division and the toppers from the same will be promoted.

"For the vacant spots in the senior division, we can increase the number of promoted teams from A division from two to four. The AFC wants our clubs to play at least 70 to 80 matches, but our current format supports only 22 matches. The changes will be made accordingly and the clubs are also preparing for the same," says Bhatia.

But this is only the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) keeping its promise in reply to DSA's response to the constitutional reforms suggested. The DSA, however, has been lax about keeping its side and hopes to meet AFC's requirements — every club having its own fields, a permanently functioning office and a licensed referee.

"New Delhi Heroes, Shimla Youngs and Hindustan Club have already hired a few University grounds and meet other requirements as well. The rest of the clubs will also be made to do so. Depending on the success, other criteria might be enforced from the second edition," added Bhatia.

Meanwhile, Shaji Prabhakaran, director of the Vision India Project, said Delhi might not be off AFC's radar, but the Elite league is only a possibility now as the state federation has been asked to amend its constitution by December by AFC, failing which the league can't kick off as it's a part of AFC's consequent programme.

"They have to make some changes in their constitution by December like having a full-time general secretary, composition of the executive committee and so on. Otherwise there's no possibility of organising the league. Manipur got AFC's nod along with Delhi in 2005; it started there within a year," he said.

Talks on the implementation of such leagues in other states are on. "We are discussing West Bengal and Goa as the next destinations. But the formats will vary according to the requirements of these two states," added Prabhakaran.

Heading: Katara case witness arrested for abduction bid - Indian Express
Content:
Five years ago, Khramalie Metha was just another cricket-crazy boy, albeit more interested in fielding than wielding the willow or rolling over his arm.

It was this propensity to chase the ball that eventually led him to a different ball game altogether — soccer. Metha, who would otherwise stand in some corner of a cricket ground, was soon in the thick of things, becoming a striker for St. Xavier's, Kolkata.

Now a student of St. Columba's in the Capital, he made his first appearance for in the DSA 'B' division league against Victory FC at the Ambedkar Stadium on Friday, and scored a brace to ensure a winning start to his club. Metha scored both the goals scored in the match. He first struck in the 16th minute, lobbing the ball over an advancing opponent goalkeeper Rahul Kumar Singh, while his 34th minute goal came off a long ranger.

While a few of his shots came off the bar, Metha isn't too concerned. "I started playing in Kolkata, then moved to Mussoorie and now to Delhi. The basic lesson I learnt was to leave it to my instincts and not get into the technicalities too much. I don't think too much about the game and that keeps me relaxed," says Metha.

On his experience of playing in three different places, he says the Capital is best-suited for his age. "At school level, Delhi is the best place for soccer. In Kolkata, it's more of a passing game, but players are more skilled here," he says, adding, "There (in Kolkata) club soccer is more important than anywhere else in the country. I don't know too much of Indian football, but the names Mohun Bagan and East Bengal are very common."

While he feels Delhi misses the excitement and interest for the next stage, his views on taking up professional soccer are also fickle, or what he calls 'instinctive'. "I haven't seriously given it a thought. If it works out for me I might continue, but getting a college degree is my first priority. I wouldn't leave everything to play football," adds Metha. After a moment's pause, he comes up with a better reason: "I think I'm not good enough. I'm already 19."

In a Group 1 match, Shakti FC beat New Friends FC 2-1 with Samar Dass and Mohammad Atiq scoring, while Mithun scored for the losing side.

Heading: Three brothers held for credit card fraud worth Rs 1 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Ajay Katara, an eyewitness in the Nitish Katara murder case, was arrested on Friday by the Ghaziabad police after he allegedly tried to abduct the nephew of DP Yadav on Thursday evening.

According to the complaint registered by Manjula Yadav, wife of the victim, Katara forcefully entered their house in Indirapuram with four others — two police security guards, a private bodyguard and a driver, and started beating up Dharmendra Yadav. They, then forced Yadav into Ajay's car. Hearing the noise, neighbours surrounded the car and rescued Yadav," stated the complaint.

Katara, however, has alleged that it was he who was attacked. "I went to the Indirapuram police station to register a compliant against Yadav. But the police arrested me instead writing my compliant," alleged Katara.

Katara was produced in the court of Sapna Mishra Tripathi, Special Magistrate, CBI, who dismissed his bail application and sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. Ghaziabad, SSP L Ravi Kumar stated that Indirapuram police has registered a criminal case against Ajay, his private guards and the driver.

Heading: PGTI ropes in golf guru Gary Wiren - Indian Express
Content:
The South Delhi Police have arrested three brothers and their accomplice for allegedly hacking bank websites and fraudulently using credit cards. Police claim the gang withdrew close to Rs one crore from cards that were issued by the banks to their foreign customers. Police officials said the accused cheated Citi Bank, ICICI, Development Credit Bank, Singapore, and HDFC.

The police said the accused purchased gold and platinum card details of some foreign customers of the mentioned banks from online black markets. After that, they withdrew money from their accounts.

Police said the accused also hacked bank websites to obtain details of customers. According to the police, they have recovered cash worth Rs 7.5 lakh, 28 different credit cards, 13 cheque books, three card-swapping machines, one Tata Indicom smart PCO, four pan cards and three Reliance and Tata Indicom data cards.

Police said on September 30, one Harminder Singh from Citi Bank branch in Gurgaon complained to the police that in March and April this year, two men approached the bank and opened a current account in the name of Diamond Tours and Travels in Sector 31, Noida. They showed its proprietor was one Vishal Verma and deposited Rs 3 lakh and requested the issuing of an Electronic Data Capture machine (machines used in shops to swipe cards). Verma's passport copy also was deposited, which was later found to be forged. "It was later found that with the help of the said EDC machine, the accused had swapped several credit cards of different banks and cheated Citi Bank to the tune of Rs 71.5 lakh. The Citi Bank came to know about the cheating, when various customers started disputing the charges debited from their credit card accounts," DCP, South, HGS Dhaliwal said.

Police officials said the accused Vishal and Anil Verma used only the cards that were issued by different banks to foreign customers. After their arrest from Madanpur Khadar, on basis of a secret information, they confessed to their roles in the fraud, police said.

Vishal Verma, whose real name is Sajid Choudhary, disclosed to police that he and his two brothers, Shabbir Choudhary and Shahnawaz Choudhary and their accomplice, Sabir Khan, had been committing similar frauds for the past four years. Police officials said Sajid initially worked for Reliance in Mumbai and was arrested in 2005 for hacking the Reliance website.

In jail, he met with one Kamal Kumar who was behind the bars a similar offence. After coming out on bail, he was arrested by ATS, Mumbai, in January, 2008, for fraudulently withdrawing money from swapped credit cards.

"He came to Delhi in March 2008 and started working with Kamal Kumar in Diamond Tours and Travels, where they indulged in more card swapping and withdrawing money from accounts of foreign customers," DCP Dhaliwal said.

Heading: In Lucknow, ban gone with the smoke - Indian Express
Content:
Just before its second season heads to a close, the new domestic golf tour will have another first to its name.

With proper training of coaches having been a key issue for a while now, the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) has lined up PGA of America master professional and Hall of Famer Gary Wiren for a coaching seminar in the city.

Wiren, a much-in-demand golf educator who is also a former national PGA staff director as well as a past board member of the National Golf Foundation, the American Junior Golf Association and the Children's Golf Foundation, will be in the country in early November for the three-day long seminar to be held at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurgaon.

"Wiren has collaborated in the writing of the PGA Tour instruction manual, and is one of the most respected guys in America as far as the educational part of the game is concerned," PGTI tour commissioner Ajai Gupta told Sportline. "The camp is more for the benefit of golf teachers and coaches, though players are obviously welcome," Gupta said.

"On the agenda are issues on fitness, mental aspects, and of course the game itself. It'll be a combination of indoor study and discussion and outdoor practical application of theories. This comes as part of our initial goals to assist the development of the game in the country," Gupta said.

Though the final schedule has been left for Wiren to plan, Gupta says there will be six sessions of three hours each over the three days. The seminar, scheduled for November 12-14, is open free of cost to registered members of the PGTI and the Women's Golf Tour of India.

Heading: UP Technical University to form moderation board - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Union government announced a ban on smoking in public places, the smokers in the state capital merrily blew away the ban, by smoking in public places.

The ban was flouted even at places like hospitals and government buildings. No one was caught or fined. The authorities responsible for implementing the ban justified their inaction by saying: "We are waiting for formal orders."

At the Lucknow Zoo, where there were a large number of visitors on Friday owing to the Tarr Mela which is organised on day after Eid, many people were found smoking without restrictions or fines. The 'No Smoking' signs posted at various spots inside the zoo could not fail deter them.

The director of Lucknow Zoo, Renu Singh, said the authorities were trying hard to implement the ban inside the zoo campus. "We already had been asking the people not to smoke here. Now, we have the government by our side and can implement it more strictly," said Singh.

She, however, had "reasons" to explain the large number of people found smoking inside the campus. "Since it was a busy day with a large number of visitors, there are chances that our caretakers must have missed some people smoking. But we have asked them to keep a strict vigil," Singh said.

The zoo's deputy director and veterinary doctor Dr Utkarsh Shukla himself caught around six people. Singh said that they are still waiting for an order from the state government as to how much fine should be levied. "At the moment, we are just issuing warnings. As soon as the order comes, we will implement it strictly," Singh added.

The other places where The Indian Express lensman caught people smoking were the Balrampur Hospital campus, the cycle stand of the Civil Hospital and the office of the Chief Medical Officer.

But the Chief Medical Officer Dr A K Shukla said they will be implementing the ban at the earliest. "We are waiting for the detailed guidelines so we can implement the ban strictly at our hospitals," Shukla said.

When he was told that people were caught smoking right outside his office and photographs were taken, he replied, "You publish the photos. We will be able to do something strict only after we get the directives."

The secretariat, meanwhile, continued to implement its ban on smoking and eating of gutkha. Shripal Singh, the security in-charge of the secretariat building, said: "We have 'No Chewing Gutkha' signs already on the stairs where we have placed the dustbins. We have also put up "No Smoking' signs alongside."

At Jawahar Bhawan and Indira Bhawan, the two buidlings which house around 70 government offices, the employees union has already put a ban on smoking inside the central park and the union office and recreation room.

Satish Pandey, president of the employees' union, said: "Since our employees smoke in these three areas, we have put a strict ban and caught a few people today. We have already implemented a fine of Rs 50 for smoking inside the recreation room and central park, and are waiting for the formal orders from the state government."

Heading: Policemen suspended for booking youth in fake case - Indian Express
Content:
Examiners checking answer scripts can be liberal or conservative when it comes to giving marks. Recognising this, the UP Technical University has decided to review the results before making it public.

The university has decided to set up a moderation board, comprising experts of various technical subjects, that could either increase or decrease the marks, if it find necessary after reviewing the results.

The university authorities said that the modalities for constitutions of moderation board are being decided and it will start functioning from the next semester examinations for various technical courses.

About the functioning of the moderation board, Vice-Chancellor Professor Prem Vrat said: "It often happens that students score high marks in four out of the five subjects but low in one particular subject. There are possibilities that the examiner had checked the answer sheets in a strict manner. Likewise, sometimes students perform below average in various subjects but they get higher marks in one particular subject. In such cases, the examiner possibly had evaluated the answer sheets liberally. In these situations, moderation board will help in fine tuning the results."

The board will also recheck the answer sheets and go through question papers to find out if it was tough or easy for all students, the V-C said.

He added that board will also act when students of any particular technical college had performed very poor in any subject as compared to other colleges.

"During moderation, the board will decide on a factor which could either be more than '1' (positive) or less than '1' (negative), depending upon low scores or high scores respectively. For example, if the average result of university in a subject was 50 per cent while maximum number (70 per cent) students had scored less than 40 per cent, board will multiply the marks with a positive moderation factor to increase their marks," Vrat said.

In case the board feels that the marks need to be decreased, it will multiply the score with a negative factor.

Vrat said the moderation factor will provide justice to those students who lose higher rank and ultimately good jobs due to less score in one particular subject.

"This will also motivate the examiners to evaluate answer sheets properly as that could be evaluated again by moderation board members. Moderation factors would be applied both in written and practical exams," the V-C said.

"Once the results will be prepared and before releasing them, the university's examination committee will carry out review and if the members find any discrepancy, as mentioned above, it will recommend the moderation board to recheck answer sheets and moderate the marks," Vrat added.

Heading: Tarred by terror brush, Atif’s college cheers a topper set to become judge - Indian Express
Content:
As Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, who was asked about the attacks on Christians in Orissa and Karnataka during his trip to the US and France, brought up the matter at the Cabinet meeting today and sought a report from Home Minister Shivraj Patil, the Orissa police, after taking 38 days to collect the medical report confirming the rape of a nun who was later stripped and paraded, arrested four persons in connection with the case and suspended the Baliguda police station Inspector-in-charge.

Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik promised action, describing the rape of the nun as "a shameful and savage crime". Within hours of the Cabinet meeting, Patil sent Patnaik a strongly-worded letter, asking him to take effective measures and provide security to Christians.

In Kandhamal, police recovered two more bodies — one of a Christian and the other of a Hindu — from Sundipakhalo village in Tumudibandh block, taking the official death toll in the communal violence to 34.

Juria Pradhan (52), his son Kartik Pradhan (22), Biren Sahu (35) and Tapas Patnaik (26) were arrested in connection with the assault and rape of a 29-year-old Catholic nun on August 25. The case was handed over to the IG, CID.

Baliguda police station Inspector-in-charge K Narayan Rao was suspended for the "callousness" shown in investigating the case but to the people there, it was too little, too late. The rape accused and others who had participated in the attack on the Divyajyoti Pastoral Centre in Kanjimendi had been moving freely in the area all these days.

Padmacharan Nayak, a Dalit Christian of Kanjimendi, said: "People who took part in the assault were on the streets, fully aware that police would not do anything. We saw it on August 25 when the Orissa State Armed Police stood by while the pastoral centre was being burnt and the nun raped.

They did not even fire a shot, saying they had no orders."

And now a blame game of sorts is on between the doctors and police as to who was responsible for the delay in submitting the medical report confirming the rape.

In New Delhi, Information and Broadcasting Minister P R Dasmunsi told reporters: "The Cabinet took note of the latest situation prevailing in Orissa and Karnataka. The situation is very grave. The Government is quite concerned about it. Prime Minister has directed Home Minister to apprise the Cabinet about the situation."

Sources said that as soon as the Cabinet finished discussing the day's agenda, Manmohan Singh mentioned the attacks on Christians. He was quoted as having said that the attacks on Christians was being discussed abroad when he was there. Mines Minister Sis Ram Ola joined him, saying this was "harming the image of the country".

Railways Minister Lalu Prasad, Heavy Industry Minister Santosh Mohan Deb, Labour Minister Oscar Fernandes too raised the matter. Saying that the Centre must take tough measures to stop the attacks on Christians, Lalu Prasad even demanded a ban on the Bajrang Dal. Dasmunsi said "we feel strongly that the Orissa government has to do more, what it is not doing".

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Vyalar Ravi raised the issue of attacks on Christians in Left-ruled Kerala. He had even written a letter to the Prime Minister last month, suggesting the Constitution be amended to enable localised intervention by the Centre in states to protect minorities. "As the trend of different political parties coming to power in different ideology gains ground, it becomes imperative to ensure that the minorities that live in those states are adequately protected and safeguarded," he wrote.

In his letter to Patnaik, Patil stated that seeking additional forces every few days was no solution to the violence in the state. Pointing out that the Orissa government had used an Mi-17 helicopter provided to it by the Home Ministry only for reconnaissance and not for transportation of troops as was required, Patil said the state government had raised only one of the five sanctioned battalions of the India Reserve Battalion.

Heading: Arif named Saif as mastermind of court blasts, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Last month, the reputation of Azamgarh's Shibli Inter College was unexpectedly stained. Delhi Police said former student Atif Amin, killed in the Jamia Nagar encounter, was a leader of Indian Mujahideen and mastermind of the September 13 blasts.

Yesterday, the college's reputation received an unexpected boost. Former student Nusrat Khan topped the Uttaranchal Provincial Judiciary Services Exam, 2008.

For students and teachers facing endless embarrassing and intrusive questions since the Jamia Nagar encounter, a dark phase ended on Eid, and a shiny sliver of pride emerged.

Twenty-six-year-old Nusrat is one of 19 candidates who have made it in the all-India exam conducted by the Uttaranchal Public Service Commission.

Only law graduates were eligible, and despite 33 vacancies, the Commission cleared only 19.

After a year's training, the young man from Mau, a town 20 km from Azamgarh, will become a civil judge.

"At a time everybody is looking at Azamgarh in a certain way,

Nusrat has done the city and our college proud. Our alumni have cleared the judicial services exams in the past, but Nusrat is the first topper we have produced," Shibli College principal Abu Mohammad said.

He added that no college ever taught "bad things" to its students, and the college hardly deserves the blame if a student strays.

Nusrat credited his college with a crucial role in his success. "I don't know any of those whose names have cropped up in the blast cases. But as far as the college is concerned, it has played a crucial role in moulding my career. When I joined, I had no specific plan for my future. It was the college that gave me direction," he said.

After passing out of Shibli College in 1999, Nusrat went to Aligarh Muslim University for a BA, LLB and LLM. Last year, he cleared UGC's NET, and became eligible to teach undergraduate classes. "But my aim was judicial services, and I kept trying till I cleared the exam."

Heading: Cong demands dismissal of SICs - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi cops claim Atif had assigned the UP court blasts operation to Saif

The alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) activist, Mohammad Arif, has reportedly told his interrogators that Mohammad Saif — arrested by the Delhi Police after the Jamia Nagar encounter — was the mastermind of the serial court blasts in Uttar Pradesh.

Arif, who was arrested here last week and is being questioned by the Anti-Terror Squad, also said Saif stayed at the rented house his brother Shahnawaz in Hussainganj till a day after the blasts.

Others IM operatives — Atif Amin, the second in command of the group who was killed in the Delhi encounter — Junaid alias Ariz and Khalid also stayed there. Junaid is wanted for the Lucknow blasts, and Khalid is wanted for the Delhi blasts.

The Deputy Inspector General of ATS, Rajiv Krishna, said: "Though Arif Amin was there, he has specifically named Saif, saying he orchestrated the IM module involved in the court blasts in UP. It was also Saif, who had the job of purchasing bicycles and planting the timers to various IM members."

Besides Junaid, who is wanted in the Lucknow court blasts case, the other members of the module were Shadab alias Malik and Salman — wanted in the Faizabad case.

Sajid, who was killed in the Delhi encounter alongwith Atif, had placed the bombs in Varanasi, Krishna said.

Sources in the Delhi Special Cell confirmed that Atif had assigned the UP court blasts operation to Saif. Saif had corroborated this during interrogation, they said.

Arif had reportedly told the ATS that initially, he was not aware if Saif would involve him in planting the bombs. Saif and Atif had visited Arif's rented room at Daliganj a month before the court blasts.

Arif had said that he, too, used to meet them in Azamgarh or in Delhi.

The police are looking for Shahnawaz, who worked in a local hospital and has been missing since the Delhi encounter. Arif has reportedly told the ATS that he did not know if Shahnawaz was aware of IM designs.

Saif had visited Lucknow thrice in November 2007 before the blasts. He also visited Faizabad and Varanasi.

Mumbai police return after Sanajarpur raid
A four-member team of Mumbai Crime Branch raided the Sanjarpur house of an alleged Indian Mujahidin (IM) operative, Abu Rashid, on Friday morning. The accused, however, could not be traced. Police said Rashid's name was revealed by five IM members, including the outfit's chief Sadik Sheikh. Sadik and others were arrested in Mumbai on September 24 in connection with Ahmedabad serial blasts case.

Superintendent of Police (Rural) Azamgarh, S K Rana said: "A team led by me accompanied the Mumbai police in the search that began at 6 am. Rashid's father Ikhlaq Ahmed and brother, Abu Shad, were there in the house. The Mumbai police recorded statement of Ikhlaq and Shad who told that Rashid had left for Mumbai in November 2007 where he was doing a job." The team left for Mumbai later in the day after they failed to trace him.

Heading: Now, recycled plastic for building roads - Indian Express
Content:
Following the arrest of Shailendra Singh, the state Congress has decided to intensify its campaign against Chief Minister Mayawati by seeking the dismissal of four state information commissioners (SIC).

They allege that the SICs had been appointed illegally. "According to the Right To Information Act, the chief minister should appoint the commissioners after consulting the Leader of Opposition in the state Assembly and a minister of the Cabinet rank," said Singh, chairman of the right to information cell of the Congress. "But the chief minister did not adhere to the process," he said.

Singh said he will soon file a petition in the Allahabad High Court regarding this matter. Leader of Opposition Mulayam Singh Yadav, said that he was never consulted in this matter, although "it is mandatory for the chief minister to consult the Leader of the Opposition before appointing the information commissioners."

As for the Congress, Mulayam said: "Instead of creating a ruckus about this matter, they (Congress) should ask the Governor as to why he had given his assent without consulting the government."

Singh, who was the former Deputy Superintendent of Police, alleged that he was being victimised by the CM for raising issues related to the misuse of public funds in the construction of Ambedkar Memorial.

Singh was arrested on September 25 for allegedly indulging in violence at the SIC office. Later, he was released on bail. He said he would move the National Human Rights Commission regarding his arrest, which was based on fake charges.

Heading: US firm joins hand with university to begin e-courses - Indian Express
Content:
To help the carpeting of the city roads last longer and utilise plastic waste in an environment-friendly manner, Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) plans to use recycled plastic waste in the construction of roads.

Such an initiative is expected to protect roads from damage during the monsoon season. The technology, developed by the Thyagarajar College of Engineering in Madurai, has already been adopted by Tamil Nadu and Kerela.

"Deliberations are in progress with the Public Works Department (PWD) in this regard," said C S Bhatt, member secretary of UPPCB. "We are also exploring the possibility of using recycled plastic waste in some of our future road projects. The life of a road increases by one-and-a-half times with the use of this technology," PWD Engineer-in-Chief T Ram said.

Dr R Vasudevan, Dean and Professor of the Department of Chemistry at Thyagarajar College of Engineering, said: "During heavy rainfall, water seeps in and damages the bitumen. The use of recycled plastic waste as polymer modified bitumen prevents water seepage and reduces the damage."

Vasudevan added that nine tonne of bitumen and one tonne of plastic will be needed to construct one km stretch of road.

Moreover, plastic waste will reduce the usage of bitumen and lower the per km cost of construction by Rs 15,000.

"Another obvious advantage is using non-biodegradable waste material,' said G N Garg, Chief Environmental Officer of UPPCB. He added that roads constructed with plastic blended with bitumen not only have a longer life, but also perform better in hostile weather conditions.

Heading: Railways get Idea to paint Prayagraj Express yellow - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad University is all set to start e-courses in collaboration with US-based Adyana Inc on October 18.

To begin with, the university is starting courses which will help students acquire skills required by the industrial and corporate world.

After two years of planning and preparatory work, the university's state-of-art e-learning resource centre is finally ready. It is equipped with computer work stations, servers and facilities like video conferencing.

"It is a big achievement for the university to develop e-learning modules and transform the traditional campus into an e-environment campus," said Professor Rajen Harshe, Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University. He added, "Allahabad University is the first regular university in the country to start e-learning."

Initially, it is going to be a pilot project which will be followed by major expansion. The university administration is in touch with various corporate houses and reputed banks to launch industry-oriented e-courses, said Harshe.

Adyana Inc has designed and developed the work skills programme (WSP) with the sole objective of bridging the gap between formal education and employment prospects of students. The courses have been approved by the university's board of studies. Under the pilot project, 100 students will be admitted, said director of the Institute of Professional Studies Professor G K Rai.

The WSP is an online programme that could be accessed by students. "This will be an online classroom for the user. We aim to train thousands of users on their employability skills with the help of technology. AU is a pioneer in propagating this project concept to students," said Harshe.

Rai said WSP will deliver a 150 hour e-learning curriculum and the learner has maximum time window of six months to complete it. There will be nine hours of assessment. In all, there will be 14 modules. The global examination will be conducted by Adyana's assessment and certification group online.

Students will have to clear knowledge verification test, soft skill testing and simulation. Adayana is a global human capital management solutions provider that enables clients to improve their business performance through human capital development. Its clients include over 250 active customers in North America, South America, India, and Europe, said Rajiv Tandon, CEO of the company.

Heading: LDA employees go on indefinite strike - Indian Express
Content:
After Chennai's Kurkure Express and New Delhi's Airtel Rajdhani Express, it is now the turn of Allahabad's Prayagraj Express to get a brand makeover. It will be renamed "Idea Prayagraj Express" after the Idea Cellular, which has bagged an advertisement contract for three years.

It cost Idea Rs 49 lakh to bag the contract.

It will be the first train in three zones — North Central Railway (NCR), Northern Railway and North Eastern Railway, which will soon be painted yellow. All the 54 compartments of the Allahabad-New Delhi train will carry advertisements of the firm. The agreement between the NCR authorities and the advertising company was finalised on May 23.

"The interior and exterior work to display the advertisements will start within a couple of days," said an official in the Idea Cellular. The order for printing material and creative concepts has already been placed. If the experiment is a commercial success, 20 more trains of the total 165 trains of NCR could soon follow suit, a source said.

Sources said that Gareeb Rath and three Satabdi Express would also be rented out to firms within a month as talks with the same advertisement company that has bagged the contract of Prayagraj Express are in final stages.

NCR Public Relations Officer Amit Malviya said this would be a source of revenue for the Railways and it will also give a facelift to the trains. He added the advertisement company has to adhere to Railways' guidelines for the ad campaign.

Heading: NHAI asks construction firm to check quality of flyovers - Indian Express
Content:
Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) employees have gone on an indefinite strike from Friday.

They alleged that Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra had made abusive remarks against them during a function at the LDA office to observe Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary on Thursday. The employees said they will continue their protest until Mishra apologised.

"While addressing the gathering, Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra had called us dogs, stating that we are corrupt and take commission from the allottees. It was disgusting. After all, we are government employees, not his slave," said LDA employee's association president Avdhesh Kumar.

Mishra admitted that he had used the word "dogs". "But I had used it for all those who indulge in corrupt practices. I had only asked the LDA employees to do away with corruption and stop accepting bribes. I had no intention to insult anyone," he added. He maintained that he will not apologise. "No work-no pay" will apply to the protesting employees, he added.

LDA to sell land in Jankipuram
The LDA is going to sell its 21-acre plot in Sector-J, Jankipuram to private builders for developing group housing schemes. By the end of the month, an auction will be organised for this purpose. LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram said over 30 acres of land was lying unused in Jankipuram for the past few years. "Through auction, 21 acres will be provided to private builders for developing group housing scheme. On the remaining nine acres, the LDA will develop its own schemes," he said.

Heading: 'I'm thankful that I'm still getting good work' - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of the recent collapse of a section of a flyover near Lucknow, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on Friday asked the Hindustan Construction Company (HCC) to check the quality of flyover being constructed at three different sites on the road connecting Lucknow to Faizabad.

"The HCC has set up three committees to review and check the quality of construction and submit its report in three days," said M K Jain, NHAI project director. The HCC was also the agency that was responsible for the construction of the flyover that caved in last week, killing three people and leaving 11 others injured. Jain said engineers from NHAI and HCC have inspected the accident site on the Lucknow-Faizabad Road.

Heading: N-deal historic, says Bal Thackeray; praises PM - Indian Express
Content:
A career going great guns and a seemingly happy personal front, life is all roses for Sanjay Dutt. 'Kidnap', his first big film of 2008, is out, and movies like 'Blue', 'EMI' and 'Aladin', will see the light of Friday in the last quarter of the year. Dutt has also turned producer with the launch of his banner, Sanjay Dutt Productions.

Its two films — an action adventure directed by Soham Shah and another action film directed by Milan Luthria — are scheduled to hit the floors next year. Talks are also on with five more directors, which make it seven films in all. And Dutt will act in all of these. The actor is also committed to a couple of film assignments for Balaji Films. In all, the actor has almost 20 films in various stages of production.

"I'm very charged up about life and want to do a lot of good work. Thankfully, I'm still getting it," he says with characteristic nonchalance.

There are other things that Dutt is contemplating. Promoting boxing is one, ever since Vijender Singh got home a bronze from Beijing. Trying his hand in politics is also on his wish list, but that will happen, he says, when the work pressure is less.

'Kidnap', a high-action drama, has him essaying the role of a multi-millionaire whose daughter is held for ransom. The role is special for Dutt because it is for the first time that he is playing father to a teenage girl, close to his daughter's age, one of the reasons he was considered for the role. "Sanjay Gadhvi saw me with my daughter Trishala on a show and said he could think of no one but me to play the part. There are times in a person's life when all the money in the world can be of no use. Working in this intense drama between a father and a daughter was an emotional experience for me. I also enjoyed working with Imran Khan whom I found to be a very confident actor," says Dutt.

The actor hotly denies that relations between him and his daughter are strained because of his marriage to Manyata. "Trishala was with us in the Bahamas when I was shooting for Blue, and even otherwise we are on the Net everyday. She is studying forensic sciences and just the other day she called to say that there was a body with a bullet in the head lying in front of her. She was so cool about it, but it really blew my mind," he smiles indulgently.

Heading: Bal Thackeray to address Sena rally after one year - Indian Express
Content:
Describing the Indo-US civilian nuclear deal as "historic" and in "national interest", Shiv Sena Chief Bal Thackeray did not buy his ally BJP's argument that UPA government has compromised the country's sovereignty.

"I don't think there is any truth in this political criticism. The voluntary moratorium on not conducting further nuclear tests was imposed by our government," Thackeray said in an editorial in his party mouthpiece 'Saamna'.

Thackeray, however, said only voters will decide whether the Congress and Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh will derive any political benefit due to this "historic" deal. The octogenarian leader said the deal has opened horizons of nuclear trade for India.

"This deal should be viewed in this respect only. Due to the NSG waiver, India can procure reactors and nuclear technology to tackle energy shortage from various countries. American trade and commerce will get a fillip while India can provide for its energy security. Because of the NSG waiver, India can ink nuclear pacts with the member countries," he said.

Praising Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, Thackeray said he staked his integrity and honesty for the deal. "He has already clarified issues related to 123 agreement and the Hyde Act. Even though the Congress can't be trusted, the same yardstick cannot be applied to the Prime Minister," he added.

Heading: Dikshit's 'adventurous' comment 'outrageous': Advani - Indian Express
Content:
After a gap of almost a year, Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray is all set to address the party's traditional Dussehra rally on October 9. The 81-year-old Thackeray has stopped attending Sena rallies owing to ill-health since last year.

The Sena chief's video recorded message was shown at the party's foundation day and also at a gathering of veteran Shiv Sainiks earlier this year.

This would be the 43rd Dussehra rally of the Sena. The rally is being held at Shivaji Park in central Mumbai and the venue hasn't changed over the years, with the faithful cadre converging at the sprawling ground to hear the cartoonist-turned `Hinduhridaysamarat' (emperor of Hindu hearts) hold forth on a variety of issues.

Thackeray's son and Sena executive president Uddhav, who is now de facto managing the party affairs, will also address the rally, Sena sources said.

The senior Thackeray is expected to touch on the overture made by former Sena leader Chhagan Bhujbal in withdrawing a defamation case against him and also dwell on former Sena leaders Narayan Rane and Raj Thackeray, the sources said.

Rane is launching a Marathi newspaper 'Prahar' on Dussehra, in presence of NCP chief Sharad Pawar. The daily is expected to take on the Sena mouthpiece 'Saamana', which has been critical of the former Shiv sainik.

Rubbishing nephew and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena leader Raj Thackeray's "hollow sympathy" for him over the Lok Sabha's privileges committee summons issue, Thackeray had recently told his nephew that he need not bother.

"We are competent to tackle the case. You should not worry," Thackeray said after Raj threatened not to allow officials and people's representatives from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to enter Mumbai if the committee summons Thackeray in a breach of privilege case.

"The MNS people are now worrying about my age and health. But health is the same as it was when Raj left the Sena," Thackeray had said, rebuking Raj.
