Heading: City gets 2 CCTV mobile vans - Indian Express
Content:
Art finally seems to be picking up in the city with another commercial art gallery being inaugurated in the posh area of Gurdev Nagar recently.

In fact, this art gallery is just another feather in the cap of businesswoman Ranjeet Grewal, who has also been a professional golf player.

Ranjeet Grewal told Newsline, "This art gallery has been christened as Aafreen, which means to praise or to create in Persian. The idea of setting up a commercial art gallery struck my mind when we were running a restaurant earlier at this place. When that restaurant shifted elsewhere, I thought of utilising this place for some creative work. As I myself am very creative, I thought of setting up a art gallery here."

Grewal has procured over 200 paintings of various artists from all over the country and these have been displayed in the gallery for sale.

"Not only art lovers, but also students visit our gallery to get ideas for their works," she says.

Grewal has been a professional golfer and has won the national golf tournaments in 1982 and 1986 at Kolkata and Mumbai respectively and was also a member of the Indian team for the Asia-Pacific golf tournaments from 1982 to 1990.

She has always had a penchant for being the first in different fields. She is famous for having opened the first flower shop in the city in the early 1970s.

She says that her husband Gurlal Singh Grewal, who runs a steel industry, has always been supportive of all her endeavours.

Heading: Splashing joy to heal body and mind - Indian Express
Content:
To keep watch during the festive season, the Ludhiana police have deployed two CCTV mobile vans to prevent any untoward incident in the city.

At present, two CCTV mobile vans have been deployed on rotation basis but there is a proposal to increase the number vans to keep a tab on various activities in the city. "This exercise has been initiated in view of the terrorist attacks across the country. We hope to keep a check on the nefarious plans of the anti-social elements," Sandeep Sharma, DSP Control Room and PCR told Newsline.

DSP Sharma said the idea is the brainchild of SSP R K Jaiswal. "Before starting this exercise recently, SSP Jaiswal held a brainstorming session with senior police personnel," Sharma added.

"We have identified nearly one dozen vulnerable points in the city and plan to deploy more vans at such sites," he added.

Sharma said that these vans were fitted with latest equipment including night vision cameras and search lights.

"After videorecording the activities, we would make their hard discs and keep it for future reference. We will be keeping this record with us for about one and a half months so that in case of any untoward incident, we can track the culprits," he said.

DSP Sharma said that police control room will also be modernised and through satellite channels, the local police will keep an eye on crime in the country.

Heading: This Sikh calls the Ram Leela shots - Indian Express
Content:
For many homemakers life ends after marriage but not for Kavita Kansal — who is a caring wife, a loving mother of three and a doting grandmother and above all a bunch of creative energy.

Ask her and she tells you how much she loves to paint and make candles. She is in the city to put her inspired exhibits on display at Sutlej Club.

"Though I suffer from cervical pain and hypertension, painting has done wonders to my physiological and emotional wellbeing.

Whenever I feel little under the weather, I go and start painting and in no time I am as fit as a fiddle," explains Kavita. With poise, she adds, "This is just not with me. At my art classes in Panchkula, I get women in their 60s coming to me to learn art. They also feel the same way as I do. Painting has a therapeutic effect."

Armed with as MA in History of Arts from the Panjab University, Kavita has on display painting done in acrylic with some Tanjavore art thrown in. She has on display paintings depicting Hindu gods, modern art and carton characters for children. "My aim to make all genres of paintings. While I personally like modern art, I paint everything.

Kavita 's forte includes canvas painting, pot painting, Tanjore art , textile paintings and has also picked up various prizes at the Spring Festival held every year at Pinjore and the prestigious Rose Festival of Chandigarh.

Kavita, also knows the art of making floating candles, which are a big hit during Diwali.

Heading: Retrieve land from encroachers in 6 months: High Court tells MC - Indian Express
Content:
This Dussehra, this is a story to warm your heart. For the first time in the city, a Sikh is at the helm of a committee to organise the festivities. Charanjeet Singh Channi, a resident of Civil Lines, has been elected as the president of the Shri Dussehra Committee, Upkar Nagar. He won by 42 votes.

Channi, a businessman, said: "Some of the members did protest saying a Sikh could not be the president of a Dussehra committee. They wanted a Hindu at the post. But I did not back out."

He added: "I have deep regard for every religion. Serving on the committee will give me immense satisfaction and I also plan to bring about some vital changes in its functioning. We have doubled the decorations and implemented crowd control measures at the Ram Leela function. At Friday's function, we had over 10 bands playing in the scene wherein Lord Rama weds Sita. We have also displayed around 40 tableaus depicting different scenes from the Ramayana."

As every year, the Ram Leela attracts people from all religions, cast and creed. Aslam, a resident of Bhai Randhir Singh Nagar, said: "I love watching

it every year as it represents the victory of good over evil."

Karnail Singh, a farmer from Jhande village, said: "I used to perform in the Ram Leela when I was in school. Now, whenever I watch it, I am reminded of my childhood."

Heading: City parks caught in PMC, MC squabble - Indian Express
Content:
Taking strong note of the perennial problem of encroachments in Ludhiana, the Punjab and Haryana High Court today passed detailed directions to the Punjab government and Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana, to remove the encroachments within six months and take stern action against encroachers.

A division Bench comprising of Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Surya Kant today passed the judgment arising out of a suo moto notice taken by the High Court in relation with encroachments in Ludhiana.

A survey was conducted by the Punjab government and Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana, after the High Court had ordered them to do so.

On December 6, 2003, the MC informed that in a large number of cases, encroachments could not be removed due to restraint orders passed in about 200 cases pending in different civil courts at Ludhiana.

On February 10, 2004, the state government was restrained from regularising unauthorised encroachment. Few months later, the High Court was informed about 108 cases of encroachments land measuring 400 square yards. It was further informed that more than 2,42,363.14 square yards was under unauthorised possession out of which 22 encroachments involving land measuring 1,16,817.74 square yards had been made by Government institutions, such as civil hospitals.

On August 25, 2005, the government informed that 68 big encroachments had since been removed as a result of which land measuring one lakh square yards stood retrieved.

Expressing deep concern over this, the court held "It does not absolve municipal authorities from keeping vigil and introducing and effective enforcement and monitoring mechanism to prevent future recurrences and tackle to this perennial problem. It is a sad state of affair that what the municipal authorities ought to have done on their own, had to be reminded by this court through suo moto. It would thus, be too presumptuous and far from ground realities to accept that no further action is required to be taken in this regard".

The division Bench further observed that while, we are not inclined to continue monitoring the enforcement activities of the corporations indefinitely their persistent inaction in the past, warrants suitable directions to ensure that ongoing process of removal of encroachments is taken to its logical end.

The High Court has issued directions to the Punjab government and Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana, by restraining the state government from regularizing unauthorized encroachment and constructions.

Moreover, Punjab has been directed to take a conscious policy decision in accordance with law for removal of encroachments, if any, made on public lands by government hospitals, dispensaries, police stations, educational institutions not to be placed at the same pedestal as a private individual encroacher.

The High Court has also directed the civil courts to expedite cases pertaining to encroachment made within areas of Municipal Corporations of Ludhiana, Bathinda and Patiala. The MCs have been directed to retrieve the land from encroachers within a period of six months. "MCs should locate encroachment prone areas and take all necessary safeguards/preventive measures against encroachments by erecting barbed wire fencing, displaying notice boards containing statutory warning. MCs should also evolve public participation. If a person notices that encroachment is not removed in connivance with the authorities, contempt of court notices be issued".

Heading: 4 suspected dengue cases in Khanna - Indian Express
Content:
Of the total 738 parks in the city, only 324 have been handed over to the park management committees(PMCs), while the rest are being 'maintained' by the MC. Not many PMCs are also keen to take up the maintenance of the rest of the parks because most of them need civil works including making of boundary walls, proper water connection, footpath construction or garbage clearance. These civil works should be carried out by the MC, only then PMCs can think of maintaining these parks.

Moreover, the allotment of parks is a lengthy process. At the moment, nearly 40 applications are lying pending with MC authorities and they can be approved only in the MC general House meeting - the meetings are normally called after a gap of three months or even more.

The PMCs are getting payments at the rate of Rs 1 per square metre from MC for the maintenance of parks.

Apart from the city parks, even the roadside green belts have also not been allotted to anyone.

Sources also revealed that a number of mohalla societies which wanted to maintain parks were not allotted any parks this time. Instead, the favourities of councillors' got parks allotted for them. This has led to resentment brewing among a few residents in Dugri, Focal Point, Salem Tabri, Chand Cinema and many other areas.

Though a few flora lights have been installed in the shabby looking parks, little has been done to clean these parks which otherwise are full of filth and have no vegetation.

In Focal Point, a number of parks and roadside green belts have dumped flyash while a few others are barren and are used to dump industrial waste. Hence, industrialists don't seem to be very keen to maintain the green belts though time and again they have given representations to the CM about poor infrastructure in the focal points.

Sources said MC plans to redo these parks in Focal Point and will invite applications from businessmen in the area.

MC Landscaping Officer Surinder Kumar, meanwhile, said as they have more than 77-km long central verge to maintain, they want to allot 500 city parks to the PMCs.

The central verge on the main approach road is also in a bad shape and many plants have died due to lack of proper care. This was even highlighted by Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda on his surprise visit to many city roads.

Picture of neglect
Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority(GLADA) and Ludhiana Improvement Trust (LIT) have not yet allotted parks to the PMCs hence most of there parks in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, Rishi Nagar and Chandigarh Road area are in a bad shape.

Heading: ‘Education without ethics is mere information’ - Indian Express
Content:
Four suspected cases of dengue and more than 50 cases of viral and typhoid have been reported from Model Town.

Former Municipal Council president Sant Ram, who is also the resident of the area, said poor sanitation is responsible for the disease outbreak.

Sant Ram's son Harvinder Kumar is also suffering from viral fever.

Four members of the family of Jagdish Kumar (40) have been suffering from fever including two cases of suspected dengue.

Jagdish Kumar said,

"I and my son Rajan (16) were reported mild dengue and we got treatment from Chandigarh. My other son and daughter are also suffering from high fever."

Another resident Mohinder Singh said, "My uncle Charanjit Singh has been suffering from mild dengue and getting treated at Apollo Hospital in Ludhiana."

Vijay another resident of the area said, "My mother Meena Devi is also suffering from mild dengue."

Faqir Chand's whole family has been suffering from viral including him, his son, daughter-in-law, grandson, brother and sister-in-law.

Residents alleged that fogging machine was pressed into service only once and that too in June.

They also alleged that there is no arrangement to remove garbage from the area.

Sanitry Inspector Sandeep Kumar said, "We have sent fogging machine twice in the area and the garbage will be removed soon."

Municipal Council president Iqbal Singh told Newsline, "I took the charge in the first week of August and immediately directed to repair the fogging machine which was out of order.

We are using 'king fog' for fogging which is recommended by World Health Organization (WHO)."

Heading: Mohan Singh Yadgari mela to begin from Oct 18 - Indian Express
Content:
"Education does not end with mastery over a few languages or subjects, instead it means opening doors of the mind, cleansing of the soul and ultimately realisation of the self.

We Indians have a very rich spiritual heritage but it is a matter of regret that we are drifting away from it," said Swami Jitatmanand, head of the Rama Krishan Mission, Vivekanand Memorial, Kolkata, while presiding over the two-day international seminar on value-based education.

The seminar is being organised in the city by the Desh Bhagat Institute of Management and Computer Sciences, Mandi Gobindgarh.

The second in the series of international seminars, it is going to witness over seventy eminent scholars from different parts of the world participate and present papers on various topics under the umbrella of the main theme. Earlier, while welcoming delegates and guests, Professor Shalini Gupta, director general of the Desh Bhagat group quoted extensively from the Gita, Guru Granth Sahib and other ancient scriptures. She opined that value-based education was the need of the hour.

The key speaker of the inaugural session, Professor T N Pathak (former vice-chancellor of Punjab University) said that education without ethics is mere information which cannot bring any substantial change in one's approach towards life.

Others who spoke on the occasion and highlighted the relevance of social, moral and spiritual values in education included S S Sewak (CEO of Arihant Spinning Mills, Ludhiana), Prof Orger Sophie (France) and Davud Hilton (Director and Principal, Josphe International group of schools, London). Tejinder Kaur, vice-chairman of the Desh Bhagat Institute also graced the occasion.

A book Value Based Education-Dimensions and Directions comprising of selected papers to be presented during the seminar and a souvenir highlighting the main events of the seminar were also released on the occasion.

Heading: Dabur ayurvedic college to adopt senior citizens - Indian Express
Content:
The 30th International Professor Mohan Singh Yadgari mela will be organised in the Sangatpura village of Amritsar district from October 18 to 20.

The mela is being organised in collaboration by the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, Aalmi Punjabi Virasat Foundation and Jagdev Singh Jassowal Charitable Trust.

Jagdev Singh Jassowal, founder of the Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, said, "Literary and cultural competitions will be held for children. Artistes from the North Zone Cultural Centre in Patiala will perform on October 19 and seminars will also be held. On October 20, a programme on Punjabi folk songs will be held."

Nirmal Jaura, managing secretary of the foundation said, "Buta Singh Chauhan's CD of gazals will also be released on the occasion."

Dr Surjit patar, senior vice-president, and general secretary of the foundation Gubhajan Gill said, "A seminar is being held in collaboration with the Punjabi Sahit Academy in Delhi on October 17. The seminar will be presided over by Dr Satinder Singh Noor. It will be followed by Kavi darbar."

A souvenir dedicated to the eminent educationist who was also known as a 'walking encyclopedia' will also be released.

According to President of the Aalmi Punjab Virasat Foundation Bhupinder Singh Sandhu, "This year, representatives from the Pakistan citizen council and members of Parliament from Pakistan will also participate in the mela.

Heading: Seminar to facilitate safe tourism held in city - Indian Express
Content:
The Dabur Dhanwantry Ayurvedic College in Sector 46 has decided to adopt senior citizens living in Sector 46, as listed in the police records. The college has decided to appoint one student for each senior citizen to look after their medical needs.

Senior citizens living alone and incapable of moving out will be treated in the hospital as indoor patients, wherever needed, free of cost. This was announced by vice-president of the college, Dr Naresh Mittal, at the inauguration of a free seven-day medical check-up camp at the college, organised jointly with the Sai Tara Ummat Foundation.

Dr Rakesh Sharma, Director (Ayurveda), Punjab, inaugurated the camp and Dr Ashwani Kumar Sharma, Director of AYUSH, Punjab, presided over the function. About 150 patients were examined and provided free medicines during the camp. Earlier, A K Ummat, chairman of the Sai Tara Ummat Foundation, highlighted the activities of the foundation and brought out the necessity of interaction between the youth and senior citizens.

The foundation honoured five senior citizens: Maj Gen J S Bhullar (Retd), P H Vaishnav, Air Marshal K S Bhatia, Brig Keshav Anand and Dr Rajinder Kaur.

Heading: Second day of Pinjore Heritage festival draws a galaxy of craftsmen from across India - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Tourism, Chandigarh Administration, in association with the Safety Circle held a seminar — "Indispensability of Safety in Hospitality Industry" — at Hotel Chandigarh Beckons on Saturday.

The objective of the seminar was to educate hoteliers about the safety of tourists and help promote safe tourism in the city.

Manmohan Singh, president, Chandigarh Hotel Association, said: "The biggest fear with the hotel industry these days is cyber crime. Every hotelier today is worried about this particular issue as they cannot do away with the wi-fi system. We want the administration to help us."

Director Tourism, Chandigarh Administration, Vivek Atray, said "Our motto is 'Responsible Tourism' and our activities should be balanced and responsible. Tourism is increasing rapidly within India and in other countries."

Chandigarh Tourism has adopted various measures for the safety and hospitality of the national and international tourists. To facilitate their visits, the department offers brochures, key numbers, and road signs among other things. S S Srivastva, SSP (UT), said: "Chandigarh Police is associated with safety issues. The city has been safe and peaceful for the residents and tourists."

Srivastva added, "The city residents are law abiding and the Chandigarh Police enforces it if somebody tries to violate it."

BPS Bakshi (MD), Safety Circle, also provided inputs on the topic and emphasised on the safety areas and their correlation and significance with each other.

Col J S Sandhu, an expert in disaster preparedness, spoke on the "Significance of Disaster Preparedness". The seminar was attended by hoteliers and restaurant owners from the region.

Heading: High Court issues showcause notices to Bindra’s father - Indian Express
Content:
Dr A S Bindra, the managing director of the Punjab Meats Limited (PML) Industries, is in thick soup. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued showcause notices to Dr A S Bindra, father of ace shooter Abhinav Bindra, asking him to explain as to why contempt of court proceedings cannot be initiated against him.

The directions have been passed by Justice Permod Kohli on a petition filed by one Dr Joseph K Masih, a resident of Mohali. Masih, who was working with the PML Industries, moved the High Court demanding contempt of court proceedings against Bindra.

Due to certain reasons, Masih was dismissed from service. Aggrieved of this, Masih moved the court of Labour Commissioner, who passed the order in 2001 in favour of Masih and directed the company to reinstate him.

Challenging the order, the PML Industry moved the High Court which stayed the order of Labour Commissioner with the condition that the company will comply with Section 17-B of the Industrial Disputes Act.

As per Section 17-B, an employer is liable to pay monthly wages to his employee in case of a dispute. Meanwhile, the company also moved the Court of Assistant Labour Commissioner, Mohali, which was supposed to execute the order passed by the Labour Commissioner in 2001.

The company managed to stay the case in the Court of Assistant Labour Commissioner as well stating that their appeal has been stayed by the High Court. Masih then moved the High court again alleging that he has not been paid the wages and that the company has procured stay from the Court of Assistant Labour Commissioner by 'wrong statement'.

Masih alleged that the company did not bring this to the notice of Court of Assistant Labour Commissioner that the wages have not been paid to Masih.

Taking note of this, the High Court today issued showcause notices to Dr A S Bindra, MD, PML Industries Limited, Dera Bassi.

Heading: NOBODY’S BABIES - Indian Express
Content:
After over 20 dead fish surfaced at the Sukhna Lake recently, experts warn that the death toll could increase if the administration does not take any measures to remove silt from the water soon.

And they also point to another factor that contributes to the fatalities — methane gas at the bottom of the reservoir.

Professor M S Johal of the Department of Zoology at Panjab University, who had examined the dead fish, said: "Organic waste in the water produces methane, which is also a factor in the death of fish, apart from the presence of silt in Sukhna."

Professor Johal explained that a warm environment causes oxygen levels in water to decrease — "this is a direct threat to fish".

Also, the lake has overgrown varieties of fish which need to be removed immediately.

"These fish eat most of the food and hence, there arises an imbalance," added Johal.

Administration officials, meanwhile, do not admit to the presence of methane as "the lake has no organic waste".

Conservator Officer Ishwar Singh said: "We check the level of oxygen in the water at regular intervals and they are under control. Organic waste is present only at the sides of the lake and is not a cause for concern."

Johal said: "It is imperative that a panel of scientific experts be constituted and the administration implements the measures suggested by them.'

Heading: Badal follows Amarinder, lays foundation of Sutlej bridge again - Indian Express
Content:
Inspired by foreign countries, UT began several projects in the city with much fanfare. But most of them ran into trouble due to one reason or the other. With none of the officials who initiated the works at the helm any longer, no one seems to be answerable for the debacles

Officials of the UT Administration and the Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh have often been inspired by various development projects that they see on foreign shores.

They tried to replicate a number of such projects in the city. But, in most of the cases, by the time the projects saw the light of day the officials no longer held the same office.

Started with much fanfare, some of these projects ran into troubled waters. But with the officials concerned either being repatriated to their parent states or retired, there is no one to be held accountable for the debacles. Newsline takes a look at the status of these projects.

Solid waste management plant

The much-hyped, first-of-its-kind plant set up at a cost of Rs 30 crore in Dadumajra always remained mired in controversy.

Its inauguration on May 21 this year had been boycotted by Congress councillors due to non-inclusion of the name of Mayor Pardeep Chhabra on the invitation card.

The plant was later not found to be functioning satisfactorily and a notice was issued to JP Associates, the company that was given the contract to run it.

The residents of Dadumajra complained of foul smell emanating out of the dumping ground during the monsoon, with garbage not being lifted for processing.

The company said in the absence of a dryer, the wet garbage could not be processed.

A dryer was finally installed this month and work resumed.

The setting up of the plant had been preceded by a tour to Germany by the then Mayor, Surinder Singh, Municipal Commissioner P S Aujla, councillors Lalit Joshi and Subhash Chawla, along with Municipal Officer Health Dr G C Bansal and Joint Commissioner H S Kandhola.

While councillors and officials now get into heated debates on the functioning of the plant every time the House meets, none of the officials involved in getting the plant to the city are part of the MC any more.

Mechanical sweeping machines

A final word is still not out on whether the machines are capable of sweeping the city roads or not. Three such machines were bought at a cost of Rs 3 crore in May this year.

They were supposed to be used during night hours for cleaning the roads, but at present these are used during peak traffic hours, causing jams.

It is learnt that the machines are suitable for cleaning only smaller areas, like parking lots.

This is another project which has seen much debate in the House.

Similar machines have been in use in Delhi for quite some time. But, the then joint commissioner, H S Kandhola, medical officer of health Dr G C Bansal and an executive engineer had to travel all the way to Italy to inspect the machines before buying them.

With the team repatriated to Punjab, there is no one who is now answerable.

Underpasses

A team comprising the then finance secretary S K Sandhu, chief engineer V K Bhardwaj and chief architect Sunita Monga went to Belgium in August 2007 to study tunnel underpasses.

They came back with a recommendation for eight underpasses. The team also brought ideas for their maintenance.

Within a few months of the junket, Bhardwaj retired and Sandhu was repatriated to Punjab and the project was handed over to the Chandigarh Housing Board.

A final verdict on whether the proposal will finally see the light of the day is still awaited.

Fire-fighting equipment

MC teams have been on junkets to different places for buying fire-fighting equipment.

One such trip was to Finland in July last year to buy a hydraulic ladder at a cost of Rs 2.51 crore.

While the equipment is lying unused with the fire department, officials who brought it to the city are no longer with the corporation.

The team that went to Finland comprised former municipal commissioner P S Aujla, chief fire officer H S Kandhola, superintending engineer, Public Health, S R Aggarwal and sub-fire officer Sham Singh.

Aujla and Kandhola have been repatriated to Punjab. There were objections over inclusion of Aggarwal in the team as he was not the fire department.

Heading: Life term for three brothers for killing neighbour - Indian Express
Content:
Two years after former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh laid the foundation stone for the bridge over River Sutlej at Sarai Pattan, controversy sparked off on Saturday when Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal relaid the foundation stone for the same bridge.

District Congress Committee President Dr Ramesh Dutt Sharma raised strong objections over the relaying of the foundation stone saying that Badal had no "moral right" to lay the foundation stone of the bridge for the second time.

He alleged that the foundation stone was laid to get credit with the Lok Sabha elections in mind.

Amarinder Singh had already laid the foundation stone of the bridge, which was to be built at a cost of Rs 44 crore, said Dutt.

He accused the present SAD-BJP government of delaying the construction of the bridge that has caused the construction cost to escalate to Rs 56 crore.

While the assembly elections had prevented work from being undertaken, the foundation stone laid then was also damaged by some unidentified persons.

Talking about the damage, the DCC president claimed that he had lodged a complaint with the

Nurpur Bedi police station but no action had been taken so far. Dutt asserted that the construction work should have been undertaken without laying afresh the foundation stone.

Former Punjab Minister and senior BJP leader Madan Mohan Mittal was also, meanwhile, conspicuous by his absence as he alleged that he was not informed about the function in time under a deep-rooted conspiracy.

Meanwhile, with the long standing demand of the residents of the area, the government finally decided to construct the bridge with the help of the Punjab Infrastructure Development Board.

Badal also announced that he would soon take up the matter with the Centre to immediately exempt the Kandi area from the ambit of Punjab Land Preservation Act (PLPA), 1900, that had severely hit the overall development of the sub-mountainous region.

Heading: 67,67: Dengue, malaria cases shoot up in Pimpri - Indian Express
Content:
Three brothers were on Saturday sentenced to life imprisonment for killing a 42-year-old man by flinging him from a five-storey apartment in April 2007. The District and Sessions Court passed the sentence on the three residents of Parshuram Apartment in Narayan Peth for killing Mayur alias Mahesh Yeshwant Damle by pushing him from the terrace of the apartment following a minor brawl.

On April 11, 2007, Damle, who was also a resident of Parshuram Apartment, was dining with a friend, Dhirajsingh Riyat (37), on the terrace and had consumed alcohol. A liquor bottle fell down as the terrace did not have any protective wall.

Angered by the bottle landing at their place, Pandurang Shankarrao Padwal (37) and his brothers Vivek Padwal (35) and Dnyaneshwar Padwal (34) went to the terrace and thrashed Damle.

During the scuffle, the Padwals pushed him down from the terrace.

Damle died on the spot. Riyat, a private security guard, lodged a complaint with Vishrambaug police after which they were arrested on the charges of murder.

Additional sessions judge B D Kapadnis held the Padwals guilty. Public prosecutor Chandrakiran Salvi examined six witnesses in the case. The statement of Riyat proved crucial in the conviction of the trio.

Heading: Goettingen univ opens liaison office at UoP - Indian Express
Content:
Dengue and malaria cases have returned to haunt residents in Pimpri-Chinchwad. Dengue cases, especially, have seen a sudden jump in last two months. On the other hand, malaria cases have persisted right from the beginning of the year.

In September, as many as 67 dengue cases have been reported from different parts of the industrial town. In August, there were 44 dengue cases. From January to July, the town had seen 38 dengue cases. No dengue deaths had been reported so far.

Last month, 58 citizens were affected by malaria in Pimpri-Chinchwad, this month the figure has gone up to 67. July was the highest so far with 92 malaria cases reported by the medical department of the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.

"Both dengue and malaria cases have seen a jump in last couple of months. Dengue cases especially are rising rapidly," PCMC health officer Dr Milind Jawale told this paper on Saturday. "The medical department has been spreading awareness and carrying out necessary activity like fogging and spraying medicines in affected areas. But it is public participation which will help in controlling both malaria and dengue," he said. Three malaria deaths, all falcipuram ones, have been reported. In 2007, there were 655 malaria cases and three deaths.

PCMC medical director Dr Rajshekhar Iyer said despite repeated appeals to residents through advertisements in newspapers, television channels, distribution of pamphlets, the general public is apathetic towards simple steps required to keep the dangerous dengue at bay. "Dengue cases mainly breed at homes. That is because people store fresh water for more than three to four days. Not only this, but the dengue larvae are found in big numbers in flower pots, refrigerators, tyres and tubes. The medical department can do its job of spreading awareness, but the citizens at large have to act on their own," Dr Iyer said.

PCMC health department says the sudden spurt in dengue cases is worrisome. October is considered as the crucial month because last year it had seen as many as 139 cases. The year saw 409 cases. "The figures clearly reveal that dengue cases are rising. And we appeal to the general public to take necessary precautions at their end," said Dr Jawale.

Dr Iyer said malaria cases, like last year, are mostly seen in areas where construction activity is taking place on large-scale. "Suburbs like Chinchwad, Pimple Nilakh, Wakad, Gurav Pimple and Indrayaninagar are witnessing hectic construction activity. The builders are not making adequate provisions for sanitation for their workers, resulting in unhealthy conditions around the construction sites," he said.

Heading: 22-feet high Shivaji statue unveiled at Commonwealth Youth Games venue - Indian Express
Content:
The University of Goettingen, a 271-year-old German university, which produced 44 Nobel laureates, set up its first ever liaison office in a foreign country at the University of Pune on Saturday. It will work as a link between the University of Goettingen, UoP and German industries in Pune.

A delegation of officials from the state of Lower Saxony, hometown of University of Goettingen, led by chief minister of Lower Saxony Christian Wulf visited UoP. Wulf inaugurated the liaison office and the new building of the International Students Centre at the UoP along with vice-chancellor Narendra Jadhav.

UoP had signed an MoU with the University of Goettingen in March 2007. Both the universities will collaborate in areas like science and humanities. The universities will also be involved in students and faculty exchange. "The liaison office is a landmark development as it will intensify the collaborations," said Wulf.

Wulf said the state of Lower Saxony is the hometown for Volkswagen. "The Pune plant of the company will require 2500 engineers and I hope the collaboration with the UoP will be fruitful in this context also," he said. Wulf also said that the state of Lower Saxony had set up an office at Mumbai too and would like to develop relationship with Maharashtra.

Jadhav said the tie-up would give a great fillip to postgraduate students of the UoP for research. "We will be collaborating in areas like automobile engineering, library science, German literature, Geography and Biodiversity. In addition a Centre for Modern Indian Studies will be set up at the University of Goetteingen, which will give an opportunity to the faculty of the UoP to go there and teach some subjects," he said.

"The University of Goetteingen is a great place to do research as it provides right kind of environment and degree of freedom for research," said Kurt von Figura, president of University of Goettingen.

Heading: 63-yr-old gets 10-yr RI for raping minor - Indian Express
Content:
Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur and Chhatrapati Udayan Raje Bhosale of Satara on Saturday unveiled the 22-feet tall statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji at the Balewadi Sports Complex, the venue of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG).

Congress MP Suresh Kalmadi, state education and sports minister Vasant Purke and director of sports Laxmikant Deshmukh were present during the occassion.

However, mayors of Pune as well as Pimpri-Chinchwad, had not been invited.

While unveiling the statue, Shahu Maharaj said, "The word 'commonwealth' symbolises slavery, hence, India should take a lead in changing the name." adding that in sports, people come together irrespective of their caste and creed.

He expressed hope that Balewadi sports complex will produce more and more sportsmen in future. The guests were given a warm welcome to the accompaniment of the music at the venue. Traditional martial arts were also performed.

Heading: Joy to the World - Indian Express
Content:
Additional sessions judge S S Phansalkar Joshi on Saturday sentenced 63-year-old Bhimrao Shankarrao Gaikwad of Laxmi Nagar in Yerwada to ten-year rigorous imprisonment and also slapped a fine of Rs 6,000 for raping an eight-year-old girl about three years ago.

On May 30, 2005, Gaikwad asked the victim, his neighbour, to purchase a cigarette for him.

When the girl returned with the cigarettes, he took her inside his house and raped her. Gaikwad gave Rs 3 to the girl and threatened to beat her if she mentioned the incident to anyone.

The girl told the incident to her mother who then lodged a complaint with Yerwada police station.

The defence counsel argued that the court should consider the age of the accused while awarding the sentence. To this, Judge Joshi said that the crime that the accused committed was heinous.

Public prosecutor Vikas Shah examined five witnesses.

Heading: The Mahacelebration - Indian Express
Content:
It will be a moment of joy, celebration and pride for the entire nation as sister Alphonsa gets canonised on October 12. With this, she would be the first woman from India to be declared a saint by his Holiness Benedict XVI in Rome.

On this occasion, the Blessed Alphonsa church in Kalewadi, Pune will be renamed as Saint Alphonsa church. According to father Benny T, parish priest, Alphonsa church, "This is a historic moment and we are proud that we are a part of it. We have got the remains of sister Alphonsa from Kerala and it has been instituted here by the bishop of Kalyan."

Sister Alphonsa was born on August 19, 1910 in a poor family. Though she taught in a school for a short period, sister Alphonsa had to give up her job due to illness. She spent most of her life in the sick room of the convent and she became known as the suffering servant . The title was more of a tribute to her for the way she accepted all the sufferings in her life, saying that it was a gift for her from her loving Lord. She was buried in Bharananganam, Kerala on July 28, 1946. She was declared blessed on February 8, 1986 by his holiness John Paul on his visit to Kerala.

According to George Velloor, trusty, Alphonsa church, "The canonisation that will take place in Rome at 10 am in the morning will include holy mass presided over by the Pope and supported by hierarchy of priests from Kerala. Over 3000 devotees from Kerala are expected to attend the canonisation ceremony."

"One of the basic prerequisites for declaring a person saint is that after his or her death, some miracle has to take place in his or her name. This miracle, mostly related to healing needs to be reported and certified by the doctors as a phenomenon beyond the capabilities of medical science. Other than this, the person has to have led a good, clean life," adds C P Varkey, committee member, Alphonsa church.

Such a miracle took place in case of sister Alphonsa not once but twice. "In the year 1947, a person named Kunju was born in Kerala with a twisted leg. He prayed to sister Alphonsa and was miraculously cured. This was the incident that got sister Alphonsa declared as blessed. A similar phenomenon was repeated in 1999 when Jinil, a small boy in Kerala, born with two twisted legs was cured by praying to her. This miracle played a crucial role in making her a saint," adds father Benny.

The declaration has sent a wave of happiness amongst the Keralite Catholics. The Alphonsa church will be celebrating the event for two days. "Various events like social activities and blood donation camps have been organised. We will also be sponsoring one-day meals for five old age homes in the city. The event will also include flag hoisting and a feast," says father Benny.

Heading: Film review - Indian Express
Content:
Durga Puja celebration by city-based Bengali Durga Puja samitis offers a peek into Bengal's rich culture

From bringing the bodhan to Sindoor Khela, the Bengali way of Durag Puja has always been enormous, every day, prefixed with maha corroborates the fact. Come mahashasthi the festivities will be in full swing with various puja samitis coming up with pandals and arrangements that would prove to be a peek into Bengal's biggest festival and grandeur associated with it.

"Staying out of Kolkata we miss on so many things of Bengal, Durga puja gives an opportunity to feel close to Kolkata once again," says Amrita Banerjee, HR consultant in a firm.

Giving some details about the puja, she says that the goddess is welcomed on mahashasthi, and on Bijoyadashmi devotees bid adieu to her. The celebration continues even after the tenth day, that is Bijoya. "Mahasthami is the most important day. The celebration being a more common one gives us an opportunity to interact fellow Bengalis in Pune," adds Banerjee.

The main attraction of the celebration is the Dhak, a special drum that is played on all four days and Dhunuchi naach that is done during the aarti of the goddess in the evening. Famous for their love for food, Bengalis have khichuri, chorchori and payesh (termed as Bhog) as offering to the goddess.

The Bangiya Sanskriti Samsad, Pune has organised a five-day festivity to rejoice the occasion of Durga Puja at the Congress Bhavan near Shivaji Nagar, "Different competitions are held and various food stalls are put where we relish the scrumptious snacks and delicacies of Bengali sweets," says Samiran Bhowmik, trustee of the organisation. "Every year we have singers from Kolkata coming down for the event. There is a recital of the holy books and a programme on Rabindra Sangeet," says Indraniel Sen, who visits the event every year.

The celebrations of Navratri have already geared up at the Kali Bari Samiti in Khadki, where events have been lined up from October 4. Various cultural programmes like milan mela, puspanjali, sindoor utsav and many other musical programmes will be held.

Heading: WiFi plan: hotspots at kiosks - Indian Express
Content:
A gift on Eid
Movie Name: Ramchand Pakistani
Directed by : Mehreen Jabbar
Cast: Nandita Das, Rashid Farooqui, Fazal Hussain
Showing at: City Pride Satara Road, INOX
Seven-year-old Ramchand crosses the border, from Pakistan to India, without knowing that his straying steps are taking him to a place from where there is no return. Both the boy and his father, who runs after him, are arrested. Ramchand Pakistani, based on a true story, tells it like it is, without embroidery or excess.
And that is debutant director Mehreen Jabbar's film's real strength. The village in which Ramchand (Syed Fazal Hussain) lives with his father Shankar (Rashid Farooqui) and mother Champa (Nandita Das) is all mud huts and abject poverty. Being Hindu and Dalit is a double burden: They are treated as outcasts in their own country, as well as the one that lies across the border, separated by a small strip of sand.
The lady officer in the Indian camp which houses prisoners like Ramchand epitomises the divide beautifully: She is willing to teach him what she can, but he is not allowed to touch her utensils because he is achhoot. Her change of heart is one of the high points of the film. So is Syed Fazal Hussain's affecting, natural performance as Ramchand? Child actors in Hindi cinema can learn a thing or two from their counterparts in Pakistan.
What happens with Ramchand and Shankar is not just the story of that father and son, but of countless ordinary individuals from both countries, who become victims of politics and animosity.
The film was meant to be a simultaneous release in both countries, but it opened in Pakistan a couple of months earlier. It's good timing, regardless: A good Eid present, as well as a pointer on Mahatma Gandhi's birthday, towards peace and goodwill between countries which have been struggling these past decades to reach accommodation.
Well worth your time.

Wild goose chase
Movie Name: Kidnap
Directed by: Sanjay Gadhvi
Cast: Sanjay Dutt, Imran Khan, Minissha Lamba, Vijay Malvade
Showing at: City Pride Kothrud, City Pride Satara Road, Fame Akurdi, Gold Adlabs, Mangala, Inox
CAN clean-cut Imran Khan, after playing good so well, go bad with equal felicity? Not, if his director is Sanjay Gadhvi.
Curvy lass Sonia (Minissha Lamba) has an altercation with equally curvy mom (Vidya Malvade). Off she goes for a dip in the sea, all the better for us to see some more of her waist-to-hip ratio. Next thing, she wakes up in a strange house, with a strange guy (Imran Khan), with his back to her, making tea at a stove. "This is a kidnap", strange guy intones, and keeps stirring the pot. Out pops protective pa (Sanjay Dutt) on a rescue mission, which consists of a series of lax wild goose chases all over Mumbai.
Clearly, all ideas of knife-edge suspense and adrenalin rushes were very far from the director's mind when he dreamt up this long-drawn plot which mixes childhood trauma, revenge, and unhappy marriages, with less than average results.
Sanjay Dutt is a dab hand at revenge sagas, having done so many before. And Imran had shown his ability to do a superb character read in Jaane Tu…Ya Jaane Na: Gadhvi, who had created dhoom with both the Dhoom movies, swings unconvincingly between suspense and song, and gets neither right.
The overhang is evident in Lamba's bikinis and tankinis She is also plonked under a waterfall in a transparent white shift, with Imran brooding by the side. Don't say we didn't warn you.

Magic-less
Movie Name: Drona
Directed by: Goldie Bhel
Cast: Abishek Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra, Kay Kay Menon, Jaya Bachchan
Showing at: City pride Kothrud, City Pride Satara Road, Fame Akurdi, Gold Adlabs, Mangala
SUPERHEROES who save the world are still, despite Hrithik Roshan, a Western concept. The Roshan lad wore a zigzag mask, which hid half his face, and a flowing cape: He spoke Hindi and romanced Priyanka Chopra, but he looked faintly like Superman. Abhishek Bachchan takes on the mantle of the next Bollywood superhero-a totally desi mahapurushr—in a white tunic embossed with golden stars. He also speaks Hindi and romances Priyanka, but looks nothing like Superman. He doesn't even, sigh, have a mask.
What he does have is a nasty mother-and-son duo, making his life miserable. Every so often a blue rose petal floats in to comfort him. And then, one day, he acquires, in rapid succession, a gem-studded bracelet, a gorgeous bodyguard (Priyanka), the knowledge that his own mother Rani Jayati Devi (Jaya Bachchan) abandoned him when he was a young child, and that he is not an ordinary mortal, but a Drona, keeper of the faith that he has to save from the evil jaadugar Riz Raizada (Kay Kay Menon).
Oh, this could have been such a wonderful fantasy, harking back to ancient Indian tales of intrigue and mystery, full of tilasmi nagris, and jaadui talwaars. The special effects are absolutely fabulous; the top-notch quality is a first for Indian cinema. But the plot's ludicrous. Goldie Behl filches from here and there (Harry Potter, The Lord Of The Rings come instantly to mind), and gives us a slow, slack story.
Fairy tales work only when the strange and fantastical are buoyed by credible characters, not by poor, misguided actors, looking as if they had strolled out in fancy dress. Abhishek can't lift his turgid Adi aka Drona off the ground, Priyanka's martial arts moves are buried under the cleavage-flashing red and yellow billowing shifts. Only Kay Kay, the black-hearted magician, carries off a gelled Mohawk and a curved silver hook on his forefinger with élan.
If only his magic had spilled over to the movie.

Heading: Traffic cops now hit back, with dacoity charges - Indian Express
Content:
Although it's difficult to predict when the Pune Municipal Corporation will cover the whole city under its 'Unwired Pune' project, it's ready with a WiFi plan.

The plan is to install WiFi hotspots at Citizen Facilitation Centre (CFC) kiosks being set up at 144 places. People can buy coupons and enjoy WiFi connectivity in the vicinity of the hotspots.

The IT department of the PMC, the kiosk operator and Internet service providers are holding talks in this direction.

The PMC is in the process of setting up CFCs in each of its 144 wards and so far about 70 have been set up. If the new plan is implemented, the kiosks will enable citizens to use the WiFi network in addition to existing services like payment of property tax, telephone bills and electricity bills. "Since CFCs are spread across the city, we are aiming at turning them into WiFi hotspots. If this happens, people can easily access WiFi," said Anupam Saraph, chief information officer of the PMC.

Rohan Dudhedia, an official of Vansh Infotech, which has been given the task of running the kiosks, said, "We held a couple of meetings to discuss the nitty-gritty of the plan and it is up to the Internet service providers to see whether it is feasible for them or not. If they think it is, we can start the project." At present, two private firms are providing Internet connectivity to the CFC kiosks.

Saraph added that if the idea clicks, then it would strengthen the WiFi network in the city. "We can keep coupons for sale. Citizens can buy them and use the WiFi network."

Heading: CYG effect: fuel outlets brace for demand hike - Indian Express
Content:
Dacoity case against 10 after manhandling cop; lawyer for theft charges against cops instead

The traffic police on Saturday got even with those who had manhandled their men. They lodged a complaint against 10 persons and had them arrested for allegedly manhandling a traffic police constable and pelting stones at a towing vehicle on duty at Kunte chowk on Friday evening.

Strangely, the police have charged them with dacoity, claiming they snatched away a two-wheeler being towed away from the no-parking area.

Constable V M Jagtap attached to the Faraskhana division of traffic control branch lodged a complaint with the Vishrambaug police station. The arrested said a false case was filed against them when they questioned the constable after the towing vehicle hit a citizen.

Jagtap was heading the van on Laxmi Road. The staff on the van picked up a few two-wheelers in the no-parking zone at Kunte chowk. Owners of the two-wheelers rushed towards the towing van. According to the police, one of them was injured as he fell down while trying to enter the driver's cabin.

Soon a mob gathered and thrashed the staff and the van driver and manhandled the constable. Some pelted stones at the van, causing a damage of Rs 20,000, the police said.

Police arrested 10 persons identified as Anil Mahadev Jagtap (48), Naviel Tushar Gogri (27), Brijan Gogari (32), Duttatraya Jagtap (35), Sanjay Hanumant Musappa (35), Kishor Kamlakar Kurvalkar (30), Vitthal Mahadev Modkale (20), Sagar Chillal (30), Tushar Devchand Gogri (57) and Arun Rasiklal Shah (55), all residents of Kunte chowk.

Interestingly, police had initially booked them for obstructing government work, illegal assembly and manhandling a traffic policeman on duty. Later, the police also applied Section 395 (dacoity) of the Indian Penal Code. Senior inspector C D Jadhav justified the dacoity charges saying the accused snatched the vehicle picked from the no-parking zone. He said the person injured in the incident had himself to blame. Jadhav produced them in Shivajinagar court on Saturday. They were remanded to police custody for one day.

Relatives of the accused told mediapersons that the police van had hit a citizen. "We would be filing a counter complaint against the constable and van driver," a relative said.

Criminal lawyer Sushil Mancharkar said it was shocking to see the level to which police were stooping. "In this case, a dacoity case cannot be applied because there is no motive, intention or preparation behind commission of the offence and the property belongs to the accused themselves. Every citizen is duty-bound by law to protect his propery, his body and also of others. So it is mandatory provision on the part of the police to intimate and file necessary complaints before the Motor Vehicle court." Mancharkar said taking away the property of the citizen without any intimation is itself an offence of theft under Section 379 of the IPC. "Section 379 says whoever removes the property of any person without his consent and knowledge is said to have committed theft," he said.

In the wake of an increase in attacks on traffic cops, top officers of the Pune city police had conducted a meeting last week and decided to take stern action against those who manhandle traffic cops on duty.

Heading: Villagers game, call off strike over grazing land - Indian Express
Content:
Expecting a surge in fuel demand during the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), the Petrol Pump Dealers Association is seeking an increase in supply from oil companies.

This is in view of the large number of people from outside expected to turn up during the games, said Baba Dhumal, president of the Pune Petrol Pump Dealers Association.

But he does not have to worry. Officials at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) terminal at Loni, which supplies the bulk of fuel in the district, said they were ready. "There could be a rise by 10-15 per cent in demand for petrol. We are confident of meeting it. We have sufficient stock to meet any increase in the demand for petrol and diesel," said V K Goel, chief terminal manager at Loni for HPCL.

A senior official from the Indian Oil Corporation Limited also said additional fuel for vehicles would pose no problem. "There is no restriction on fuel for transport and agriculture. At present, we are restricting diesel supply for power generation for the industries. We will be able to supply fuel consistently whatever the demand," he said.

Unlike a few months ago, petrol pump owners are not reporting an acute diesel shortage either. But on Friday, the HPCL Loni server developed a technical snag because of which fuelling of oil tankers was stopped for four hours. To make good the lost time, HPCL Loni officers worked till 5 in the morning and filled around 281 tankers.

"Since fuelling is an automated process, it has to be stopped if the server develops a problem. We cannot issue invoices either," Goel said. About a month ago, the terminal had faced a similar disruption in server connectivity, which lasted a day.

A few months ago, the diesel shortage was more acute given the unprecedented load-shedding in Pune, which drove up demand for diesel to be used in generators for commercial purposes.

Heading: Court admits Anandsen’s narco report as evidence - Indian Express
Content:
Villagers of Balewadi and Mhalunge have withdrawn their proposed three-day strike after a request from the police department.

Around 100 villagers were agitating against the sports department for not providing jobs in accordance with a Bombay High Court order of 1998.

Director of sports Laxmikant Deshmukh had assured them that he would take up their grievances with the government and declared that no new appointments had been made since 1994.

The villagers said they were "withdrawing the strike temporarily.'' Ajay Kamble from Balewadi village said, "We have given a contempt notice to the sports authority. This being a mega event, the police department requested us to withdraw the strike. We did not want to disrupt it."

In 1992, the gram panchayats of Balewadi and Mhalunge gave up 165 acre of grazing land to allow the construction of the Shri Shiv Chhatrapati Sports City at Balewadi. In 1998, the court ruled that whenever work came up, the state sports department would give first preference to the 100-odd affected villagers.

When contacted, Deshmukh told The Indian Express, "As of now we have 70 employees in the class-four category. Right now we have no job positions.''

Meanwhile, advocate Vaishali Sarin said they would pursue the case legally. "We are hoping these villagers get relief after their decade-long struggle,'' she said.

Heading: Fake currency case: role of senior SBI officials under scanner - Indian Express
Content:
Admitting the report of the narco test that was conducted on former BSP legislator Anandsen Yadav as "important evidence", the additional district judge of Faizabad court on Saturday rejected the legislator's bail plea in connection with the Shashi murder case.

While rejecting Anandsen's bail plea, which was moved by his lawyer Avadhesh Yadav, the special judge (SC /ST Act) Vimal Chand in his order accepted the forensic report as true and made it the basis of the case.

Advocate Saeed Khan, who represent the prosecution's side, told The Sunday Express that the court in its order had mentioned: "As per a ruling of the Supreme Court, narco test reports cannot be admissible in the court. But in this particular murder case, the court has acknowledged that the narco test report is important evidence and a legal part of the case."

Anandsen underwent a narco test in January this year. In the report that was submitted to the court, it was stated that the legislator knew Shashi and used to visit her residence. During the narco test, Anandsen also admitted that Shashi had helped him during the elections.

During today's hearing, the court also took cognizance of the fact that by using his political stature, the accused may tamper with the evidence or harm the witnesses or he even might influence and pressurise them.

Twelve criminal cases of serious nature are pending against Anandsen. This was cited as one of the reason by the prosecutor not to grant him the bail.

Anandsen's counsel while reacting to court's judgment said that he would move the High Court or the district court for relief. Anandsen's father Mitra Sen Yadav is BSP's sitting member of parliament from Faizabad Lok Sabha constituency.

Heading: Graft case filed against 3 former V-Cs - Indian Express
Content:
Senior officials of the State Bank of India may also land in trouble in the case of recovery of fake Indian currency notes from the bank's chest at Dumariyaganj branch in Sidhhartha Nagar district.

A Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)team from New Delhi has been camping in Sidhhartha Nagar for the last 15 days to probe the circulation of counterfeit notes across Uttar Pradesh.

Sources in the CBI revealed that the departmental inquiry conducted by the SBI authorities had held some senior officials responsible for the recovery. These officials were supposed to look after the transaction in the currency chest and ensure frequent inspection.

The CBI team has served notices to all these officials for interrogation. The investigating agency has also been quizzing the bank staff at Dumariyaganj regarding the case.

A team of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials had recovered fake notes of face value of Rs 4.20 crore after scanning Rs 1.84 crore in the bank's chest in August. A cashier, Sudhakar Tripathi, and two other employees, Ramesh and Rajaram, of the same branch have been arrested for their alleged involvement in the racket on July 28, September 1 and 4, respectively.

Heading: Half of Muslim population does not have access to doctors in UP: survey - Indian Express
Content:
On charges of corruption, fraud and amassing wealth through illegal means, Vice-Chancellor of Chandra Sekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSA) V K Suri has registered a case against former V-C P K Singh with the Nawabganj police station.

Following a complaint lodged by Suri, a case under section 419, 420 of the IPC and 7/13 of the Anti Corruption Act has been registered against the former V-C. Similar cases have also been registered against the former V-C of Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, B B Singh, and former V-C of Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel University of Agriculture and Technology, P P Singh, in Faizabad and Meerut respectively.

The three former V-Cs have been charged for corruption in the Distance Education Programme course during 2004.

The inquiry into the matter was headed by the then state Principal Secretary Agriculture Education and Research Department G Patnaik, who found that the

V-Cs did not take permission from the All India Council for Distance Education before starting the Distance Education course.

"After the completion of investigation by a state level committee, we received instructions from state Special Secretary Dheeraj Sahu, following which the case has been registered against the former V-C," Suri told The Sunday Express.

"At prima facie, the report prepared by Patnaik finds the V-C guilty," added Suri.

Heading: Govt suspends BPL survey as BJP alleges irregularities - Indian Express
Content:
Only 48.2 per cent of Muslim women have access to doctors for antenatal care, while the percentage of women having access to Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)and support of anganwadi workers for fulfilling their nutritional requirements is 21.3 per cent and 0.5 per cent respectively. These are the findings of National Family Health Survey III.

According to the survey, only 21 per cent of Muslim couples in UP and Uttarakhand are using contraceptives and only 32 per cent of them are aware about modern contraceptive methods.

Although the United Nations recognises India as one of the key countries for achieving its Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), Muslims in India are still a forgotten lot.

According to New Delhi-based Tehreek-E-Pasmanda Muslim Samaj and National Conference of Dalit Organisations Muslims continue to live as a marginalised community in U, despite the findings of the Sachchar Committee,. The organisations presented their report on "MDGs and Muslims in India" on Saturday and will organise a conference on the issue today.

Speaking on the report, president of Tehreek-E-Pasmanda Muslims Sardar Anwar said the Sachchar Committee report had assessed the real conditions of Muslims in India, but it could not attract any major policy interventions on the matter.

"There are a number of programmes like the National Rural Health Mission and the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme for poverty eradication and better health services for the poor, but no special provisions were made for minorities. The condition of Muslims, especially in UP, is still not good." Anwar said the government has launched many programmes for the community since 2000, but being the fourth largest state in terms of Muslim population, UP stands at 11th position so far as achieving MDGs are concerned.

Ashish Awasthi of the Student and Youth for Radical Practices said there is a need for a policy change if government wants to develop minorities.

Heading: One killed by tiger at Katernia sanctuary - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the BJP accused ruling Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) of aiding and abetting mass scale irregularities in the identification of people living below the poverty line (BPL), Chief Minister Mayawati on Saturday ordered suspension of the BPL survey currently underway in the state.

The state government had ordered a fresh survey of BPL in September 2007.

On Friday, BJP vice president and state spokesman H N Dikshit had alleged that under the cover of BPL survey, names of poor landless and homeless among the upper castes and OBCs have been deleted from the list. Dikshit had also alleged that the staff of the revenue and panchayat departments were being forced to prepare the revised list.

The party alleged that BSP government had commissioned the survey to benefit a particular group of caste, who were committed supporters of the ruling party.

The government has amended the minimum standards for including people in the BPL category, Dikshit alleged, adding that BSP coordinators and party's district leaders were instrumental in executing the fraud.

During 1995, Dikshit had served as parliamentary affairs minister in the first Mayawati-led government that was formed with the support of the BJP.

As per the official statement released today, the survey has been suspended till the minimum standards for inclusion in the BPL category are not revised by the Centre. The Centre has already set up a committee to look into the issue, Mayawati said.

She has also directed the district magistrates to delete the names of those person included in the BPL list, who do not qualify the minimum standards and norms laid down by the Centre.

According to the release, the norms for the inclusion in the BPL category have been formulated by the Centre and it was beyond the purview of the state government to amend the norms.

It states that the chief minister has also sent a letter to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh seeking increase in number of the BPL in Uttar Pradesh. At present, the number of BPL in the state is 99 lakh, which was ascertained in 2002. The statement added that this figure needs to be revised.

Heading: Cong leaders resign en masse in Pratapgarh - Indian Express
Content:
A railway employee died after he was mauled by a tiger at Katernia Wildlife Division in Bahraich district on Saturday morning. Gangman Ram Naresh Yadav (24) was attacked by the maneater while he was cutting grass near Nishant Ghera railway station. The tiger caught Yadav by throat and dragged him 15 metres before other three employees at the scene could react.

Divisional forest officer, Katernia Wildlife Division, R K Singh said, "When we received information about the attack, we immediately rushed to the spot and identified pugmarks belonging to a tiger." This division has had previous incidents of wild animal attacks but this is the first time that a male tiger has attacked a person. The previous attacks were by leopards and a tigress.

In the past three months, two people have died and five others injured by wild animals in the sanctuary. "We have set up a team to monitor the tiger's movements. We have warned railway employees, passengers and villagers. We have advised them to move in groups and make noise to scare away animals," Singh said.

Recently, the forest department caught two leopards. While one was sent to a zoo, the other was released back into the sanctuary.

Heading: Farmers sow seeds of protest at Sonia rally - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 29 leaders of Congress party in Pratapgarh district resigned en masse from the party's primary membership on Saturday accusing senior leaders of ignoring them, sources in the party said.

The leaders accused Congress party legislator Pramod Tiwari, who has been winning assembly elections since 1980, of undermining their efforts and neglecting them. "In this regard, we have sent a letter to Congress president Sonia Gandhi and general secretary Rahul Gandhi," party's district general secretary Rajendra Singh told a news agency over phone from Pratapgarh. Those who resigned include party's former state secretary Om Prakash, members of the district Congress committee and those associated with the party's front organisations.

Heading: Churches attacked in city, cops says under control - Indian Express
Content:
Kanjhawala farmers direct barbs at UPA chief, Sheila as Cong distributes certificates to unauthorised colonies

Disgruntled with their compensation for land acquired by the government a group of farmers from Kanjhawala disrupted UPA chief Sonia Gandhi's address during a rally organised by Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit at Chhatrasal Stadium on Saturday.

The rally was meant to kickstart the Congress party's campaign for the forthcoming Assembly elections. It was earlier scheduled for September 17 but was cancelled after the September 13 serial blasts.

On Saturday, Gandhi distributed 11 certificates to members of unauthorised colonies such as Palam Kunj, Nangli Vihar in Najafgarh, Sangam Vihar and Prem Nagar. Soon, some 30 or so farmers from Kanjhawala village in Northwest Delhi started raising slogans against Gandhi and Dikshit just as the former started underlining the UPA government's initiatives for the welfare of farmers and the nuclear deal that she said would accelerate the pace of development for both farmers and industrialists.

Unfazed, Gandhi continued. But her speech was almost inaudible amid slogans by Congress supporters and the farmers and women from Kanjhawala. The protestors demanded de-notification of their land acquired for industrial development and low-cost housing projects. They claimed that the acquired land's market price is 15 times more than the package offered by the government.

Today's rally was meant as a show of strength in the aftermath of the successful nuclear deal, and the Centre's initiatives to regularise unauthorised colonies in the Capital while notifying Masterplan 2021 in February 2007.

Meanwhile, taking a tough stand on terror, Gandhi said: "Some people are using terror incidents for political mileage and dividing our society. Due to the acts of some, these elements create doubt in the minds of common people and try to blame the entire community. This is wrong."

Ostensibly referring to recent attacks against Christians in Orissa and Karnataka and acts of violence against other weaker sections, she said, "Enemies of the country also want this along with those indulging in politics of vested interests. We have to be careful of their designs." Area MP Jagdish Tytler and Union Minister of State for Urban Development Ajay Maken were also present at the event to show unity with Dikshit ahead of the Assembly elections.

While Maken did not address the rally, Union Urban Development Minister Jaipal Reddy said, "Along with Maken-ji, I am proud to say that this government has put an end to the terrible times of sealing and demolition in the city by deciding to notify 1,500 unauthorised colonies, which will benefit over 40 lakh people."

Diskhit said, "For the first time in 30 years we have taken a step to initiate development in unauthorised colonies. The government has decided to spend Rs 2,800 crore for bijli, paani and sadak in these colonies."

Heading: Amar: I am from Azamgarh, will they target me next? - Indian Express
Content:
Incidents not related to attacks elsewhere in country, say police

While protesters rallying against attacks on Christians in Orissa say churches have come under attack in the Capital of late, the police call it only a coincidence that these incidents in Delhi have taken place at the same time.

According to locals and church officials, a mob at the Punjabi refugee colony in Peeragarhi attacked the church being constructed in their locality on September 9. Residents blame the church priest for allegedly encroaching on public land, and the attempts to convert people.

But Joint Commissioner of Police (Southern range) Ajay Kashyap says: "In Punjabi refugee colony, where people do not let even neighbours raise a concrete structure, how could they let an outsider (church) do it? People in Peeragarhi and Trilokpuri are probably not even aware of what is happening in Orissa and Karnataka." The police, he says, are "alert and doing their best to maintain peace in the city".

Newsline looks at some churches allegedly attacked:

PEERAGARHI

Subhash Chandar and Surinder Kaur say their son Raju, baptised in 2005, died in an accident the following year. A month later, their daughter-in-law died, and their younger son met the same fate within days, the couple says. They blame the bad omen on the family following Raju's baptism. Raju is survived by a son, 5, and daughter, 4.

Raju's last rites were performed as per Christian rituals, Chandra says, "and church people took his body. But they said they did not have space for our daughter-in-law. So we cremated her according to Hindu rites."

Kaur claims the church gave Raju Rs 2 lakh for converting and assured him that they would take care of his children's education and other needs. "But everything just got over after his death," she alleges.

Residents, who do not want to be named, say they attacked the church following this. They say locals in the refugee colony live in tents and that making concrete structures is not allowed. "We are not allowed to make concrete roofs; how can the church do that?" local leader Radha Krishan Mahajan asks. "Besides, the church was also trying to encroach public land."

Another resident says: "We do not want these people here. They will ruin more families."

No one from the church has visited the area since the incident, locals say. Church representatives, however, deny any conversion took place in lieu of money.

TRILOKPURI

On September 14, some residents of block-13 in Trilokpuri put up an idol of Shiva and Hanuman on walls of the local church. For two days women of the neighbourhood prayed at this "open temple". The makeshift temple was removed on the third day.

"We knew it would create a tussle between the church and locals over time. So we called the SHO and got the temple removed," Father Peter Emmanuel of the church says.

And just a day after the idols were removed, some 15 people locals broke open the gate and entered the church lawn, says church caretaker Rajesh, present when the incident took place. Locals contend they are at no fault, for the lawn is built on public land.

Emmanuel says, "The plot was lying vacant and people used it to dump garbage. The church took it over to maintain it — it is government land and they can make anything on it."

Two policemen have now been deployed in the church.

Locals, though, say nothing of the sort happened. Prem Chand, an area resident, says, "We go out for work the whole day and our women are at home. We don't know about any protest."

PITAMPURA church, opposite New Academy School Construction of this church begun six months ago, and church officials say locals manhandled construction workers while work was on. "Residents said they did not want a church here," Father Santosh from the church says. After the reported ruckus, construction work was stopped temporarily but the church was attacked again in July. This time, they called the police.

Heading: 3rd witness surfaces in Soumya case - Indian Express
Content:
More than a fortnight after the encounter, Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh arrived in Jamia Nagar with Member of Parliament Jayaprada to lend support of local Muslim party leaders demanding a judicial inquiry.

Singh met the people of the area near Khalilulla mosque and gave a patient hearing to local Muslim leaders criticising the government and the Delhi Police for 'victimising' the community.

Singh said, "The Government always targets Azamgarh following any blast and for any incidents in any state of India, alleging that the masterminds are from the place. I am also from Azamgarh, does this mean that they will target me next?" he asked.

Singh said, "We are demanding the setting up of a judicial committee to inquire into the cases and reveal the truth behind this so-called Jamia encounter."

He also pointed out, "When the authorities had decided five days before the 'encounter' that Inspector M C Sharma was to be transferred, was he sent just to gamble away his life?"

Singh promised to raise the issue in the Parliament and to appeal to the Delhi government to include Muslims in Delhi Police.

Heading: Competition for DDA: More affordable houses to come up in Delhi, NCR - Indian Express
Content:
An eyewitness who had approached the police on Friday, in connection with the murder of Headlines Today journalist Soumya Vishwanathan on Tuesday, was identified as Shri Bhagwan.

During questioning, he said the first witness, Anil, who had seen Soumya's car crash against the road divider, had flagged him down and urged him to call the police. He had not seen or heard anything and stopped only because Anil desperately waved at him.

Soumya was shot dead while she was driving back home to Vasant Kunj on Tuesday night; the incident occurred at 3.35 am.

The police said they also interrogated Anil Singh, who works with the restaurant Punjabi by Nature, after he returned to duty on Friday. "Anil told us he saw Soumya lying in a pool of blood. But he said he did not know anything about what had happened," a senior officer said.

He stopped Shri Bhagwan as he did not have a mobile. When asked why did not report to work for two days after the incident, Anil said he was unwell.

"It is still a blind case and we have not been able to figure out the murder motive," a senior police officer said.

Heading: Delhi blasts: Five suspects sent to 12 days in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
After launching its first residential real estate project in Kolkata, called NBCC Vibgyor Towers, the National Building Construction Corporation (NBCC) is all set to launch its first residential project in Delhi and NCR by the end of this year. In Delhi, the project is likely to take shape near the Chhattarpur Mandir near Mehrauli.

"At NBCC, we believe in constructing houses at affordable prices. Our approach is not going to be like the private sector, where profit is the only motive. We expect to sell these properties at cheaper rates than the private sector builders at the same locations," said Ajay Garg, Director (Finance), NBCC.

According to officials, the procurement process for the residential project for Delhi and NCR is underway. "We will be in a position to state the site for the project in Delhi in the next two months. We are also in an advanced stage of land procurement in Gurgaon and Noida," Garg said.

Company sources said the houses in Delhi are expected to cost between Rs 20-40 lakh. "While our priority is to provide quality houses at affordable prices, the cost will depend on factors like the cost of land. Though we don't strive for huge profits, we will keep the costs sustainable," Garg said.

Initial estimates suggest a two-bedroom flat will cost around Rs 20 lakh, a three-bedroom flat around Rs 30 lakh, and a four-bedroom flat around Rs 40 lakh. "Though these are not the final prices, our aim will be keep prices as close as possible to the given estimate. The final cost will depend on several other factors," Garg said.

According to company officials, all the upcoming housing projects will have a mix of commercial and residential properties. "This will help in cross subsidising housing units," said a senior official. NBCC has already acquired 8,597 sq mt. land in Okhla for commercial development. "We are in the process of acquiring land near Chhattarpur for residential development," said the official.

Heading: Journalists take up cudgels for Soumya, start campaign for justice - Indian Express
Content:
Five suspected men allegedly involved in September 13 serial blasts were on Saturday remanded to 12 days' police custody by a court here.
