Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan, Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saqib Nissar were produced before Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sanjeev Jain who sent them to police custody till October 16.

Saif was arrested immediately after the September 19 encounter in Jamia Nagar in South Delhi while Zeeshan was arrested the same evening from Jhandewalan area in Central Delhi where he had gone to give an interview to a private TV channel.

Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saqib Nissar were arrested the next day from South Delhi and produced in court in connection with the blast at Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh on September 13.

Saif and Zeeshan have been named accused for their alleged involvement in the blasts Greater Kailash-I on the same day.

The September 13 serial blasts which rocked Connaught Place, Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh in Central Delhi and the M-Block market in Greater Kailash left 21 people dead and several others injured.

Heading: Sanjeev Nanda denied bail by HC - Indian Express
Content:
Over 100 journalists from across the Capital participated in the launch of 'Justice for Soumya' campaign, organised here on Saturday. Rahul Kanwal of the Headlines Today described the campaign as a crusade that will not end until Soumya Vishwanathan's killers were caught.

"We have launched campaigns for justice in cases like that of Jessica Lal and Priyadarshini Mattoo. This time it is for someone who was one of us. Soumya was a hard-working professional and a lovely person, who never hesitated to help when the need arose. It's our turn now," Kanwal said.

Vishwanathan, 25, was found dead in her car in Vasant Kunj area around 3.30 am on Tuesday while returning home from work. She was killed by a bullet in her head. While police are

investigating the case, they have no clues yet.

Radhika, a journalism teacher at the Kamla Nehru College, where Soumya studied, described her killing as 'a sad reminder of the insecurity of our times'. "In the college, we ask young women to be fearless and honest journalists. Soumya was all that we wanted our students to be, yet look at what happened to her. This is a sad reminder of the insecurity in our lives," Radhika said.

A petition demanding justice for Vishwanathan and safety for all, signed by all present, will be submitted to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi and Home Minister Shivraj Patil.

This apart, an online campaign and communities in social networking sites like Orkut and Facebook have been created to keep alive the crusade for justice.

Rajyalakshmi Rao, a senior journalist, said Soumya's death was a signal for people to put the onus on employers and organisations to ensure safety of women employees. "While the state is accountable for the safety of its citizens, we should also put pressure on employers to take the responsibility for ensuring safety of women employees. There should be a mandatory cab service to drop employees home at night, especially women," she said.

Heading: At Nigam Bodh, VIPs cremated on raised platform; MCD says no bias - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Saturday denied bail to Sanjeev Nanda, who has been sentenced to five years' rigorous imprisonment for running over six people with his BMW in 1999.

"I am of the view that the applicant (Nanda) does not deserve suspension of sentence during the pendency of the case," Justice Kailash Gambhir said. The court, however, was of the opinion that Nanda's appeal challenging his conviction and quantum of sentence be heard on a day-to-day basis for an early disposal of the case.

Nanda, grandson of former naval chief S M Nanda, filed the bail plea in the High Court along with an appeal following his conviction by a trial court on September 5. In his appeal, Nanda contended the court had found him guilty despite not having any incriminating evidence against him. Justice Gambhir had at the time refused to grant any interim relief to Nanda, noting that the accident was indeed a "serious" offence.

Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Nanda, contended that the trial court had wrongly convicted him due to publicity in the media and he should not be given more than two years of imprisonment.

Nanda also criticised the trial court's "implicit reliance" on the testimony given by witness Sunil Kulkarni, even though the defence had produced enough evidence to show that Kulkarni was "in Mumbai on the date of the accident". Kulkarni, the appeal submits, had "categorically stated that Nanda was not the driver of the car". Nanda stated that he paid a total compensation of Rs 65 lakh to victims and their families was also ignored by the court. He said he had shown good conduct during the trial, again not considered by the judge.

Heading: Sterilisation drive for dogs on city campuses - Indian Express
Content:
At Nigam Bodh Ghat on the banks of Yamuna, VVIP and VIP pyre platforms maintain a distance and stand a couple of heads higher than the general crematorium.

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) claims the arrangement is a security measure, and an afterthought to avoid disturbance for "other mourners" caused by large crowds gathered for cremation of VIPs.

On October 1, the civic agency urged the Central Information Commission (CIC) that the raised VVIP and three semi-VIP pyre altars were meant for "public benefit" — even the common man can book them with through a phone call or a letter sent well in advance.

But that being so, the MCD also nudges in a rider: cremation at these pyre platforms would depend on their "availability".

"There are no written conditions regarding booking of VIP or semi-VIP platforms," the MCD maintained before Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah. "However, in case of death of some prominent leader/official/citizen, keeping in view possible number of persons likely to attend cremation, use of VIP/semi-VIP platform constructed away from common cremation area is allowed to avoid inconvenience to other mourners and for security reasons."

To a query if it was fair to discriminate "even in cremation after deaths of ordinary and influential persons", pat came the MCD reply: "VIP pyre platforms are for public benefit. There is no discrimination. Everyone can use ordinary as well as VIP platforms subject to its availability."

The hearing was on the basis of a Right to Information (RTI) appeal filed by S C Aggarwal in August. Aggarwal sought a

three-point information on reasons for construction of the VVIP/VIP platforms; the procedure to book them for a cremation; and whether "influential" persons paid "high charges" to use them.

Submitting that a "separate grilled block" distinguished the three VIP pyre platforms, Aggarwal asked: "Considering approaches and influences from rich and influential families, will the Corporation consider some high charges for allowing cremation on this VVIP platform?"

The MCD clarified that the platforms were built 25 years ago, and that the civic agency does not have any intention to fix "high charges" or build another VVIP platform at the crematorium.

To further its case for the common man, the civic agency said it had spent over Rs 2 crore to install CNG cremation plants at Nigam Bodh Ghat. The MCD claims the CNG cremation plants are "already functional".

Heading: Calls to clips, cops pool blast evidence - Indian Express
Content:
An animal birth control exercise has been going on quietly on the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) campus for the past four months.

And the exercise, experts revealed, is being carried out on a massive scale, as closed campuses like JNU and the Indian Institute of Technology in the city spawn huge numbers of dogs.

The Sonadi Charitable Trust, based in Dwarka, has sterilised more than 80 dogs in JNU over the past four months. And there's more. "It's near impossible to count the actual number of dogs in JNU. We don't have the resources for such a count and no one from the JNU administration is actually interested in the birth control exercise. It's the Municipal Corporation of Delhi that commissioned us to perform the sterilisation. Many dogs are, however, yet to be sterilised. It is imperative to perform the exercise before the breeding season begins. We shall also do a weekly check on the dog population on all campuses similar to JNU," Bandana Sen, of Sonadi Charitable Trust, said.

Closed areas with a regular food supply help burgeoning dog populations. "We also carried out a similar drive in St Stephen's College, where there were a large number of dogs. Areas within certain enclosures, including even the Walled City, are more prone to have a growing dog population. Sterilisation is the only way forward. During sterilisation, dogs will also be given anti rabies shots," Gautam Grover, of Animal Saviour, said.

Animal shelter Friendicoes has been carrying out the sterilisation of dogs in IIT for the past ten years. The problem of a growing canine population here is more pronounced, as dogs come in from adjoining areas."On an average, we sterilise around 100 dogs a year in IIT. The number of dogs there, however, does not seem to be coming down as dogs come in from the nearby slum areas," Geeta Seshamani, of Friendicoes, said.

The municipal corporation pays Rs 445 per dog to NGOs for sterilisation. However, the corporation's much publicised plan to free the city of unwanted dogs has failed to take off in most areas. Dogs that will no longer breed can be identified by a nick on the ear.

Heading: Sewage line across Old Delhi-Gurgaon Road makes it unsafe - Indian Express
Content:
On a day five suspected militants accused of carrying out the recent blasts were remanded to 12 days' police custody by a city court, police sources on Saturday claimed to have gathered substantial evidence against Atif Ameen and his module. Delhi Police claims this module of the Indian Mujaheedin carried out the serial blasts on September 13.

Newsline collates evidence gathered by the Special Cell, confirmed by Joint Commissioner (Special Cell) Karnal Singh.

Clips: From Atif's mobile phone and laptop, the police have recovered five clips of Gujarat blasts, one clip of Delhi blast, and one clip of Jaipur blast. Atif reportedly photographed all the blast sites before planting bombs. Some of the clips have been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for further examination. Officials say these clips would work as circumstantial evidence.

Account details: Bank accounts of the alleged militants killed in September 19 (Atif and Sajid) and the three suspects arrested (Zia-ur-Rehman, Saqib Nisar and Shakil) have been scanned. Police have found there were not many transactions in most of these accounts; approximately Rs 30,000 has been found in Atif's account. Officials are looking for a hawala trader, one Hakim, who may provide details of money transactions. Officials say there is enough time left for the 90-day period to file a chargesheet. Account transactions would be linked by then, they say.

Seven suspects are still on the run, police say, and their account details would also provide leads.

Call details: Police have call detail records of all the accused which show frequent calls made to Mumbai and UP before and after the blasts.

Travel records: The police have reportedly found all journey tickets in the name of Atif and Mohammad Saif (under aliases Rahul Sharma and Pankaj Kumar, respectively) to Jaipur, Ahmedabad and Udupi in Karnataka.

Record of stay in Udupi: Police claim to have found record of Mohammad Saif staying at Hotel Broadway in Udupi, under the assumed name of Rahul Sharma. An identity card in Sharma's name has also been found from L-18, Jamia Nagar, where the encounter took place. Calls made from a PCO near the Udupi hotel have also been identified, sources say.

Bag carrying explosives: Police claim to have found a black bag which they say Saif and Atif used to bring explosives from Karnataka a few days before the September 13 blasts in Delhi. It is being seen as material evidence.

Bucket: Police say they recovered a bucket, used by the alleged militants to store explosives, in the Jamia Nagar flat.

Adhesive tapes: These were allegedly used to attach clocks to the explosives. The tape has been matched with the defused bombs and has been sent to FSL for further verification.

Clues from defused bombs: Officials have not disclosed the number of fingerprints found on defused bombs but expect to get their hands on more evidence when the report comes from the Chandigarh lab.

Confessions: All five arrested have reportedly confessed to having planted bombs.

Weapons: One AK-47 and two pistols recovered from flat.

Heading: First community radio in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
It seems civic authorities in Gurgaon have learnt little from past mistakes. A sewage line laid right across the Old Delhi-Gurgaon Road near old DLF colony poses a serious hazard to residents and commuters alike.

The work, according to officials, started in August this year. "This stretch of the road is a major traffic obstruction since one side of it is dug right across and causes massive pile-ups especially during office hours and in afternoons when schoolbuses ply on it," said the traffic policeman who has been on duty. Officials added the manner in which work was carried out was irregular as labourers skip days in between work.

The dug-up portion has no barricades to caution motorists or pedestrians. Poor street lighting is another major concern among most residents in the area. "The road is like a trap and if the matter is not considered seriously, it is a mishap in the making," said a worried Bhawani Shankar Tripathy, who lives in the neighbourhood.

With a school right across the street, parents express concern over iron rods jutting out precariously in the middle of the road.

"I am worried about my son who rides a cycle to school. Any two-wheeler, be it a bike or a cycle, can skid on the pebbles scattered on the road and can land on these rods. This happened to a labourer here a few days ago," said a Sunita Narang, a resident of Old Gurgaon.

Heading: 141 people fined for smoking in public - Indian Express
Content:
Community awareness on issues like health, law and order, development and social issues will soon have a voice in Noida. The city is set to unveil its own first community radio. The licence for starting community radio has been granted to the Institute of Management Studies by the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The community radio will be named Salaam Namaste CRS 90.4 FM and journalism students of the management institute will host programmes.

"On September 16, 2008 we have received the grant of permission from Information and Broadcasting ministry which is a license to make the radio functional," said Sanjay Kumar, head of admission and public relations department at IMS.

While welcoming the inauguration of the first-ever community radio station in the city, District Magistrate, Gautam Budh Nagar, Shravan Kumar, said the services of Salaam Namaste could be used for creating public awareness regarding ongoing issues. "Community radio will be beneficial for the city as issues pertaining to the grassroots level would be discussed by the people," said the DM.

It will run programmes related to various issues like health, crime, education, law and order and industries for eight hours every day. "Students will host the programmes. Community radio will provide a platform for the people to come and share their views," said Kumar.

Students of the Institute of Management Studies have decided to discuss the city and its problems with the people who are affected. Community radio will also run health programmes and invite doctors and consultants for the benefit of people.

Community radio will be inaugurated on October 12 and also serve as a guide for cultural activities in the city. Kumar said, "We will have a section where all major events and festivities will be reported. Noida has seen industrial unrest, the radio will also provide a platform for those who were unheard and for the industrialists who face major problems in the region." The institute is performing a trial run till October 12.

"The radio will cover area of 10 km which will cover Mayur Vihar phase III, Noida and DND flyover," added Kumar.

Heading: Annual day celebrated at Convent of Rani Jhansi - Indian Express
Content:
In the last two days, since the nation-wide ban on smoking in public places has come into effect, only 141 people have been challaned in Delhi. The bounty collected: a meager Rs 7,080.

Authorities in the Capital have carried out raids in 56 public places and 388 buses, and 55 people were challaned in public places and six in buses, R P Vashishtha, head of the Delhi Tobacco Control department, said. "The Delhi government is conducting raids and has already fined 141 people," Vashishtha said.

Anirudh Kaushal, a chartered accountant, said: "I work on the eighth floor and find it inconvenient to go down to the road and smoke every half hour. The ban has definitely reduced my smoking breaks."

The ban covers hotels, restaurants, pubs, offices and even international airports. Pub and restaurant owners in the Capital, however, feel the government did not give them enough time to arrange space for "smoking zones".

Heading: Urban frames - Indian Express
Content: 'Splendour', the annual day function of the Convent of Rani Jhansi in R K Puram, the junior branch of the Manav Sthali School, was held on Saturday at the auditorium of Manav Sthali School in Rajendra Nagar. A cultural programme was organised by students from nursery to Class VII. Dances, plays and group song performances celebrating life and friendship were held. The highlight of the event was an enactment of Rabindranath Tagore's Phalguni by middle school students. The highlight of the event were the special awards given to children from various classes, in especially created categories celebrating achievements not just in academics but also music, oratory, dance, sports, social behaviour, artistic skills, and computer skills. "It feels additionally special to receive the 'humble achiever' award for being adept in social graces," Supriya, a class VI student and award winner, said. Parents too were appreciative of the event. "It was remarkable to see every child being given a chance to perform onstage," Sakshi Pahuja, whose five-year-old daughter participated in the Bharatnatyam performance, said.

Heading: Master of spices - Indian Express
Content:
Environmentalist Ravi Agarwal trains his lens on the rapidly changing cityscape

If in 2006, he shocked Delhi with visuals of the Yamuna that featured in his book Immersion.Emergence, in his current exhibition titled 'An Other Place', Ravi Agarwal has moved beyond the riverbed to capture the rapidly changing cityscape. With urban development as his focus, he zooms in on innumerable locations in the Capital, from crumbing buildings to long forgotten green patches.

The photographs may not indicative of the vicinity but that was not Agarwal's intention either. The absence of particulars, in fact, is what lends universality to the prints. "For me this is a personal documentation of spaces that I grew up seeing and the changes that are occurring," says Agarwal, as he looks at a photograph that has the image of a white mannequin—he bought it at Jamia—superimposed on brick coloured quarters in Lodhi Colony. "These will soon be pulled down to make space for new constructions," says Agarwal. They may soon disappear but the environmentalist working with the non-governmental organisation Toxics Link, has given them permanence in his photographs—they feature in the series 'Mechanical Man', which is a part of the display at Gallery Espace. Shot in the last two years and neatly divided into four categories, the photographs have been digitally altered. Several photographs have been merged to form one complete image representative of urban development. While the series titled 'Urbanscape' has unfinished buildings juxtaposed with lush green trees and flowerbeds, the series 'Machine Man' has Agarwal in front of the camera. His body covered with oil, he works with machines to show the effort a labourer puts in, reminiscent of his previous series (1997-2000) titled 'Down and Out: Labouring under Global Capitalism', that featured working people from the informal sector of Indian economy.

Apart from still images, a two-channel, two-minute video titled 'Oil is not Water', also features in the exhibition. "It depicts the futile attempt of mixing oil and water and is also an offshoot of the rising oil prices. Water may be free and people may be worried about the shortage of oil, but the video reflects on the fact that water will be more scarce than oil in a few years," says Agarwal, who has represented India at forums like the acclaimed 'Documenta' exhibition of modern and contemporary art with his images. "Fortunately photography is gradually becoming part of mainstream art in India. The acceptance does pose its set of challenges though. It will not be viewed in isolation from other mediums and one needs to be ready for comparisons," adds Agarwal. As he looks at a photograph of the now shut Rabindra Rangshala, the reality may appear grim but the larger picture represents development. Negotiation, according to Agarwal, will be the keyword—in urban development and world of photography.

Ravi Agarwal's exhibition is on at Gallery Espace

Heading: Classroom experiment - Indian Express
Content:
A combination of 21 spices goes into the biryani served by Rahid and Farid Khan

It is a family secret. We can't disclose the recipe," says Rahid Khan, 35, an Old Delhi chef who specialises in biryanis. Rahid belongs to a family of cooks whose roots can be traced back to the times of Shah Jahan. He has been living in the Churi Walan area of Old Delhi for the past 16 years, preparing biryanis for parties and religious events. "I make good money serving biryani to patrons 10 days after the start of Ramzan," explains Rahid who hosted a biryani festival in a restaurant in Greater Kailash-I.

Before Eid, Khan and his associates were fasting and so couldn't taste the food they had prepared—a must at other times. "By now I am habitual to making biryanis and can decipher the exact proportion of ingredients needed to make a dish," he laughs. During Ramzan, Rahid is assisted by his friend Farid Khan, 40, also a resident of Churi Walaan. His ustad was Swahlin bawarchi, a third generation cook belonging to the famous Yasin dynasty, known in Old Delhi for its biryanis. There is something unique about biryanis in Old Delhi, claim both Khans.

"Although the style of cooking biryanis in a copper handi in dum style is common across all regions, the proportion of the spices varies from place to place. And for thousands of years, a section of cooks in Old Delhi have been making it in the same manner," explains Farid, who says he uses a combination of 21 garam masalas to cook biryani. But they are willing to let out the name of a few spices: ahar shinghar flower, aloo bukhara and javitri (mace).

"I was fond of qormas, biryanis and mutton burras since childhood. So I would assist my father in the kitchen, bringing him water, washing utensils and cutting vegetables. Seeing my interest in cooking, my father taught me further," says Rahid, recalling that the first biryani he made was for a gathering of over 100 people. "My uncle was out and had asked me to prepare a chicken zaffrani biryani by the time he returned. I was nervous but fortunately my uncle liked it—though he never praised me. He felt praises would give us false hopes," explains Rahid. The appreciation showered on him by the guests was a consolation though. But their teachers were not that kind to them if they slipped up.

"I remember getting beaten with a handi (copper bowl), karchi (a ladle with a long handle) for not making good biryanis or for being careless," says Farid. "While I was in my twenties and unemployed, I took up this profession under the tutelage of Ahmad Hussain (founder of Connaught Place restaurant Host)," he says, adding that their skills may die out with them. Farid has three children but is not keen that any of them follow in his footsteps. "There are so many options nowadays," he says.

Heading: Divine image - Indian Express
Content:
Business studies teacher Rajni Rawal received the National Award this year for her innovative teaching methods

If Ram Nikumbh, the committed teacher played by Aamir Khan in Taare Zameen Par, awed you with the innovative ways he educated a dyslexic child, meet Rajni Rawal, a business studies teacher who was honoured with the National Award by President Pratibha Patil recently.

Rawal, who has been teaching Class XI and XII students at government schools for over 25 years, has been awarded thrice by the NCERT (2002, 2004 and 2007) for her experimental methods. "My classroom should be filled with not just my voice. It should have the voices of my students as well," says Rawal, who began her "journey of novelty" in 1986, when the National Policy on Education stressed on the individuality of students and advocated that they be recognised as active partners in education.

"The policy offered the perfect solution to my frustration in trying to get students interested in my subject—perceived by most to be dull," she says. And so she decided to look beyond the textbook. She began with cutting out political cartoons published in newspapers and placing them in the context of business management. One such cartoon dates to 1997 and shows Congress leaders in a ship that's sinking and cracking open. While the Congressmen in it are all falling over each other, Sonia Gandhi stands tall and looks far ahead through binoculars.

"I used this comic strip as a management lesson. If a firm has no clear leadership and is overtaken by chaos in its management system, it will fail to achieve its objective," says Rawal, most of whose students come from low-income households living in slums. "These students are too bogged down by domestic issues to concentrate on a lecture. When you give them some activity like drawing a sketch on what's being taught, they'll be able to concentrate and retain what they've learnt," she says.

Come 2000 and Rawal took another cue to innovate from the first edition of Kaun Banega Crorepati. She organised a classroom version of the reality show —'Kaun Banega Safal Prabandhak'. While she played the host, the student scoring the highest in the fastest-finger-first round occupied the hot seat. "It was a hit among my students and they were motivated to work hard on their subject," she says. She has also developed a digital version of the game on Microsoft Powerpoint which students can self-play as revision of their lessons.

Last year, even as SRK was regaling TV audiences with his wisecracks on Kya Aap Panchvi Paas Se Tez Hain, Rawal was educating her students with 'Kya Aap Prabandhan Mein Tez Hain'. She had also made a classroom edition of Janata ki Adalat, calling it 'Accountant Baba Ki Adalat'.

Technology has opened up more ideas for Rawal, who did not know how to operate a computer till she enrolled for a program that NCERT had started in collaboration with Intel for teachers in 2003. Intel's website has included Rawal's technology-aided learning techniques among its stories on how teachers all over the world are using computers to educate. NCERT's Class XII Business Studies textbook, too, includes some of her innovation such as the business crossword puzzle.

So, what is Rawal working on now? "Now that I am an administrator (vice-principal at Rajkiya Pratibha Vikas Vidyalay), I better apply the management lessons I taught my kids and perhaps innovate there too."

Heading: Stealing the Show - Indian Express
Content:
As Durga Puja starts today, Nalinikanta Nath, who settled in Delhi 40 years ago, and his son are busy giving final touches to clay idols

Deft fingers are busy giving shape to clay idols—there's not much time left, but there's a lot to do. Understandably, Nalinikanta Nath, the chief idol-maker, is in no mood to talk to strangers. "He would rather concentrate on his work and guide the rest of us," says his son Gobind Nath, who recounts how Nalinikanta migrated from Jagannathpur in 24 Paraganas, West Bengal, 40 years ago and settled down in Delhi's Govindpuri, an area close to Chittaranjan Park, fondly called Delhi's Mini Calcutta.

Initially, Nalinikanta had a modest workshop in one of the markets in Chittaranjan Park. Then it shifted to a more appropriate place—the Kali Mandir complex in the locality. Here, one can see the entire Nath family and their 12 assistants work on 26 idols. Though it is considered a single entity, one idol or thakur is at least 11 figures: the idols of Durga, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Ganesh, Kartik, their vehicles lion, owl, swan, mouse, peacock, respectively, and of course, the demon Mahishasur. "This year, bad weather didn't allow us to take more orders. At times, we make more than 35 idols and some of those are meant for clients based abroad," says Gobind.

Nalinikanta's entire family works in Delhi. All his four sons, except his second son, Gobind, work for various companies. However, he made sure that one of his sons turns a full-time kumor or potter. "Father started making idols at a very tender age and since he found a potential clientele in Delhi, he came here in search of work. Gradually, all of us shifted base. I am a Dilliwalla. After completing my primary education in Kolkata, I joined my father," smiles Gobind.

The family maintains that though it's only Gobind who has taken up the family profession, come Durga puja and all of them get involved in the making of pratima or idols. And as Nalinikanta's other son Shantanu says, the family ensures that the children get initiated in the art of idol-making at a young age and at least one of them carries forward the tradition.

Every year, around June, Durga puja committees start placing orders and the Naths begin their work on the Rathayatra day in July-August. Their work continues till February.

"Around June, we go to Krishnanagar in West Bengal scouting for people who can act as skillful assistants. Idols are required by people organising Vishwakarma puja, which is generally a month before the Durga puja. Then there's Lakshmi puja, followed by Jagadhatri puja, Kali puja. Later in January-February, idols are in demand for Saraswati puja. While demand is less for Jagadhatri puja, for Lakshmi and Saraswati puja, the demand is for smaller idols, as these festivals are mostly celebrated at homes. For an idol-maker, there's nothing like Durga puja. We wait for this festival the entire year," says Gobind. That's evident as one takes a look at the various idols standing in his workshop.

Today, on Shashthi day as Bengali households hum agomoni songs invoking the Mother Goddess, mere mortal hands would give final shape to divinity.

Heading: Self Involved - Indian Express
Content:
Trendy banqueting venues have sprouted in south Delhi as wedding spots and stylish replacements for farmhouses

Not too long ago, the plush farmhouses lacing the Mehrauli-Gurgaon road made for an idyllic spot where grooms galloped in to make promises of a lifetime. But after the MCD's strict regulations, wedding venues have undergone a serious makeover. This year, too, the Mehrauli-Gurgaon belt remains a hot spot for wedding bashes, with added chaos caused by the construction of the Metro. But what has added a zing to its dusty bylanes is the entry of hotel-cum-banqueting venues that have been stationed strategically next to farmhouses and have brought along a slew of facilities, including stylish lodging.

If you cruise down the road around dinnertime, it is easy to spot three, if not more, party venues decked up in ferry lights and with guests steering into the driveway. The latest to join the plush venues is Vista Delhi that opened its jumbo metallic doors last month and has been busy hosting a series of parties. Aya Nagar, close to Gurgaon border, got its first hotel-cum-convention centre with Claremont, followed by Lutyens on MG Road. While the officials at most of these posh venues insist that they are mostly booked for corporate events and product-launch parties, people, especially from south Delhi, have often donned their gold and glittering gems to attend wedding bashes there.

Sanam Ahuja of Vista Delhi says, "With our proximity to south Delhi and Gurgaon, the bookings are a mix of events. A lot of private corporate events take place here, especially if the company plans to have over 100 guests." Ahuja says the venue is booked for 15 days in November when the wedding season peaks. On offer are 20 rooms and a banquet hall so far. Within a month, a pub called Sundowner and a 24x7 coffee shop called Fork It will be launched. "There are over a lakh commuters that take the MG Road, so it is important to offer eating joints," he adds.

Cappuccino may be affordable there, but hosting a party is not. If you choose from their pre-designed menus, the rates for a non-vegetarian meal varies between Rs 950 and Rs 1,200 per head. Add-ons come with extra charges. Also, if you want some drinks to go, the rates tend to vary between Rs 1,200 and Rs 5,500 per head for foreign brands to keep flowing for a three-hour serving. "People prefer venues like ours because we offer well-appointed rooms, specialty restaurants and neatly landscaped gardens," says Ahuja.

Apart from two banquet halls, the poolside at Claremont can easily accommodate 70 guests for a private party. A few blocks away, Tivoli Garden in Chhattarpur is booked for the next month. "Hosts look for a venue where they can spend time with their relatives. Our banquets are packed between November 18 and 26, with three functions lined up everyday," says Rohit Gupta, chairman, Tivoli Group. The Daffodils hotel, Tivoli's another venture in the neighbourhood, too, is choc-a-bloc with sangeet, bachelor's nights and reception parties, adds Gupta. "There is a scarcity of wedding venues in the city. More and more people are opting for motels and convention halls in the suburbs," he says. The unique selling points of the venue are the two rail coaches bought from the Railway Board. Now, experiments are under way to convert a double-decker bus into a double-occupancy room.

Well, as usual, the traffic might get nightmarish when the shehnai plays, but then Delhi pulls out all the stops when it comes to wedding in style.

Heading: This Puja pandal will bring nature to life - Indian Express
Content:
There are unapologetic undercurrents of homoerotism and sadomasochism in the works of Abir Karmakar displayed at the exhibition "Within the Walls" at Gallery Espace. Though the 30-year-old, Vadodara-based artist demurs that he is fascinated by the male body, the 12 large-scale oils on canvases have him trussed in a lurid position on a bed in a posh hotel room, crouched naked in a small passageway and huddled in a washroom, fenced off by a washbasin. And, in all the works, Karmakar has used himself as an androgynous subject.

"The journey started four years back," says the diminutive Karmakar, whose works created a lot of interest among artists like Vivan Sundaram, Bharti Kher, Subodh Gupta and Gopi Gajwani who were seen eulogizing over the nude male tromping about the room with almost a sadomasochistic glee.

Even in the 2005 exhibition "From My Photo Album", Karmakar had shown images of a drag queen, with his face superimposed over the lithe female body. Ask whether he is trying to depict himself, and he says, "I am filling the grey areas between male and female. To call the works homoerotic would be like trapping them."

The choice of environment, cloistered rooms, he points out, is "to create another layer". "The rooms become an extension of the body," he says. And as art critic Gayatri Sinha says in her essay, "The imperfect body gains attention." It is the unremarkable body of Karmakar that is deified as a celebrity. The price of the works begins at a forbidding Rs 18 lakh and goes up to Rs 75 lakh.

The exhibition is on till October 21. For details call 26326267

Heading: An hour from Singur, a Tata story — just the opposite - Indian Express
Content:
Way back in 1931, Abanindranath Tagore found a semblance of human creativity in nature. And he decided to call the phenomenon 'Katum Kutum'.

The poet-artiste, in the twilight of his life, found how roots, stems, leaves and plants grew into interesting shapes that often looked like artistic representations of living forms. Since then, several have regaled in Tagore's discovery and have also tried, following his example, locating interesting natural forms that can well qualify as high art. Seventy-seven years after Tagore's discovery, a corner of Kolkata has come alive to his theory, thanks to 51-year-old Sorab Sardar.

Sardar had never seen a city skyline before his tryst with the 41 Pally Puja at Haridevpur this year. Sardar, who had painstakingly collected at least 60,000 pieces of stems, trunks, bark of trees and branches, apart from the nests of humming birds, has come down to the city to exhibit them in the 41 Pally Pujas. The pandal has been tastefully decorated by a display of his finds.

"It all started when I was a kid in Radhaballabhpur village in Joynagar district. Thunder-showers then used to be occasions of great excitement as mangoes and nests of humming birds used to fall off trees. I started collecting nests since then," Sardar said. Soon, interest in quaint bird nests expanded into all

forms of nature — especially trees. And over 40 years, his collection boasts of an eclectic mix of forms that range from branches that resemble chameleons to roots that resemble turtles.

Sardar's show is not just an exhibition of a personal passion. "Now that I have come to the city, I realise that people here are so removed from nature — animals, trees and birds. I hope they understand the importance of conserving nature from my exhibits," he added.

The nature lover owns woodwork from at least 100 variety of trees ranging from the popular neem, mango, apple trees to local ones like goran, champa etc. Sardar meticulously avoids the use of chemicals to preserve the pieces of wood, bee hives etc.

"I first wash the pieces with hot water and then leave them immersed in pond water for 14 days. Over this time, the piece loses its juices and becomes more of a collection of dead cells. Then, it becomes easy to preserve them," explains Sardar.

The proof of the method's success is an interesting form that very closely resembles a turtle. Sardar says it is the root of the Sirish tree that had been chopped down 14 years ago. Similarly interesting are the forms of fox, jackals, hedge hogs and ducks that have been found in roots of trees and bamboos even. Stems and branches shaped like baby elephants, deer, owls, cats and pigs are also eye-catching. In the meantime, Sardar held up a dried bark of a papaya tree explained how easy it was for our forefathers to drape themselves in the glossy, firm material, though we can't make out how.

"I have also superimposed different pieces of wood which don't say much individually, but when put together they convey interesting pictures," Sardar added. As proof, he held two branches on top of each other — the end form resembles a mother bird feeding a blind offspring.

If you ask Sardar why he never planned to sell the interesting art forms, pat comes the reply: "These pieces might fetch me some money, but I am sure I can't find their replacements in a lifetime. Then, I won't be able to show a generation the beauty of nature."

Dipankar Chatterjee, chief coordinator of the Puja, found Sardar when he went on duty to erect a mobile network tower in Joynagar. And the 41 Pally Puja must be thanking its stars for the trip.

Heading: Nano splits Singur wide open - Indian Express
Content:
No hitch in the 1,251-acre Tata Telcon-Hitachi JV to make earth-movers; over 700 acres of farmland acquired. Officials explain: Singur is Trinamool area, Nano was too high-profile, too close to Kolkata

Announcing the Nano pull-out from West Bengal, Ratan Tata referred to the Tata Cancer Centre coming up in the Rajarhat township, on the outskirts of Kolkata, as the bridge that remains between the group and the government of Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. That hospital is spread over just 13.40 acres of Government land but there is another Tata project on a scale as big as the Nano — and which is moving quietly ahead as per script.

Barely an hour's drive from Singur, the Tata Telcon project in Kharagpur, a joint venture with Hitachi for making heavy earth-moving vehicles, also involved acquisition of agricultural land by the government right next to National Highway 6 (Kolkata-Mumbai highway).

Land acquisition began in June-July 2006 almost simultaneously with the Nano project in Singur. The Tata Telcon project envisages an industrial park of 1251.49 acres — Nano's was 997 acres — of which the state government's West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation has already acquired 967.96 acres. An estimated 80 per cent of this is agricultural. To date, Rs 63 crore has been paid as compensation to farmers and landholders. There are no "unwilling farmers" so far.

The main Tata factory here will cover 562 acres — the equivalent in Singur was about 650 acres — and the total investment in the project, including that by vendors, is expected to be around Rs 2000 crore. Like Singur, besides the main plant, several vendors form part of the project. The state government and WBIDC have successfully acquired and allotted land to key vendors.

Consider the following:

* Telcon has its own vendor unit spread over 250 acres and will invest over Rs 500 crore.

* Tractors India has got 50 acres and will invest Rs 220 crore

* Arcon, a Canada-based vendor, has got 12 acres and is estimated to invest Rs 120 crore.

* York Consultant, a Tata holding company based in Singapore, has got 40 acres and is estimated to invest Rs 80 crore.

* US-based vendor P and H, specialising in coal mining equipment, has got 20 acres and is estimated to invest around Rs 60 crore.

"The Tata Telcon project is running smoothly. We have acquired land for the company and construction work has started recently," said Subrata Gupta, MD, WBIDC. So why was land acquisition here smoother? The answers, officials admit, are hard to find. "Our compensation package was the normal one — Rs 8 lakh-Rs 11 lakh per acre, depending on the crop pattern on the land, which is primarily agricultural. (For Nano, the rates were Rs 9 -12 lakh). Just like in Singur, we held a regular dialogue at the grassroots level. We paid 25 per cent of the land price to recorded bargadars, which is also what was done in Singur," said N S Nigam, District Magistrate, West Midnapore, in which the project falls. "Everyone cooperated, including the Opposition Trinamool Congress," said Nigam. Asked why, Nigam said: "There was more attention on Singur. Maybe the stakes were higher given the publicity over Nano, the world's cheapest car, and the firm deadline. Kharagpur was in the backyard and things proceeded here quietly from the spotlight." In fact, an official said that Singur's proximity to Kolkata — a mere 40-minute drive away — made it easier as a target since protesters had easy access to it. The area, dominated by the CPM, has a strong Trinamool and Congress base. A portion of the industrial park falls under Congress MLA Gyan Singh Sohon Pal's Assembly constituency and the Lok Sabha seat falls under Probodh Panda of CPI. Said Partho Chatterjee, TMC leader and leader of the Opposition: "The right political atmosphere has been created there so therefore we did not protest. But Singur is different."

Asked to explain what he meant by the right "atmosphere," Chatterjee declined to comment. There may not be clear-cut answers as to why this is different from Nano but one thing is clear: no one in the government is complaining.

Heading: Mamata back in agitation mode - Indian Express
Content:
Since Friday evening when residents of Singur saw on their television sets Tata chairman Ratan Tata announcing his decision to pull out his Nano car factory from there, tension has only mounted.

A CPM worker was allegedly beaten up by Trinamool Congress supporters in Beraberi village market on Friday night. This was followed by a Trinamool supporter being allegedly roughed up by CPM workers at Joymollah village on Saturday morning.

At the National Highway No. 2 tyres were burnt throughout Friday night and Saturday morning by pro-Tata factory supporters. They also blocked the Durgapur Expressway that left thousands of trucks stranded. CPM supporters also tried to block trains at Kamarkundu. Amid this, the 12-hour bandh called by district CPM of Hooghly passed off peacefully.

Residents of Madhyapara area of Beraberi village that lies next to Tata Motors' small car factory are angry. Many of them had given up their land in the hope of a better living. Now, they are left with nothing. No sooner, Tata made the announcement, villagers gathered at the village 'manasatala'.

Many of them quickly suggested that the national highway should be blocked. Others added that the kuccha road — connecting the village to the highway which also happens to be the lifeline — be dug so that local Trinamool men cannot stop them from reaching the expressway. This was a complete rerun of what had happened in Nandigram in December 2006 during Trinamool's agitation.

"My brother got a job as an apprentice in the factory. This had improved our economic condition after we had given up land willingly for the factory. Now, we have lost our land as well as our livelihood," rued Akul Ruidas, a youth from Beraberi Madhyapara. Dipali Mondal of Singherbheri village has also her livelihood.

She used to work at the canteen of the Tata Motors factory till Friday after her family had given up the land and accepted money. Today, Dipali seemed speechless. "We have stopped construction of our house. We now have to save money for the future. The land is gone, so has the livelihood," said Dipali. She, along with 22 other women who worked in the canteen, has stopped going to work.

On Saturday, residents of various villages of Singur were clearly divided — those who wanted the Tatas to return and those who wanted their land back.

"There is tension in the villages. We are keeping a tight vigil," said an officer of Singur police station. Police also carried out a flag march in Beraberi village on Saturday morning, according to locals.

"Till Friday, the CPM had been patient. Now tension is running high and anything can happen," said a resident of Gopalnagar village.

Villagers, belonging to the material supply syndicate of the Tata factory, meanwhile, blocked the highway. Sporting sun glasses and T-shirts, some of them burnt tyres and stopped traffic till 3 pm on Saturday. Kalyan De, one of the protesting youth, claimed that more than Rs 200 crore was invested by them in the plant and they would all be ruined if the factory closed down.

Biman slams Governor
Left Front chairman and CPM politburo member Biman Bose on Saturday urged the people of West Bengal to play a pro-active role in helping the government to implement the ongoing industrial projects such as the proposed chemical hub at Nayachar.
Bose trained his guns at Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, stating that he has overstepped his duty in communicating with the Tatas. "A Governor should stick to his job. He cannot write letters to a company like Tata. That is not his job. We have never seen a Governor writing letter to a private company," he said.
"I request the government not to give up their idea of developing Singur as an industrial zone. I hope the government will take initiative to help those Singur youths who got training at the car factory to get employment," Bose told the media at the CPM headquarters on Alimuddin Street. He, however, ruled out the possibility of returning land which was leased out to the Tata Motors for 99 years.
— ENS

Heading: Police ready with loads of arrangements - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-four hours after Ratan Tata announced the decision to pull out the small car project from Bengal, Trinamool Congress leader Mamata Banerjee reiterated her demand that the government return the farmland of the unwilling farmers of Singur. She termed the leaving of the Tatas from Singur as a victory and vowed to renew her agitation for getting back land.

On Friday Banerjee had said that the pull out of the Tatas from Singur was a conspiracy hatched by the CPM and the Tatas. A day later, she again went back to her old demand. "We want the state government to remain steady on its commitment and give land back to the unwilling farmers," Banerjee said. "We will begin a fresh agitation after the Pujas," she added.

She said "this was a victory for Ma, Mati, Manush (mother, land, people)". She added that the state government should take a lesson from the entire episode before acquiring land in the future.

She, however, maintained that the Trinamool would have no qualms if any other industry was set up at the site provided that the land of the unwilling farmers was returned. "We have always said that we want both industry and agriculture," she said.

The Trinamool leader announced that she plans to meet the President and the Prime Minister between October 13 and 15.

Heading: Security rules dandiya venues - Indian Express
Content:
As instances of terrorists striking crowded places continue unabated all over the country, the Kolkata Police has dissuaded the public from using bicycles and asked them to avoid carrying polythene bags during the Puja.

"We are not apprehending any untoward incident but we cannot be complacent," said Commisoner of Police Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti at a press conference on Saturday. The commissioner said 20 per cent of uniformed 14,000 police personnel will be deployed to keep a vigil on the movements of people in the city.

The police have decided to keep a contingent of force at the Tollygunge police station in south Kolkata and the Office of DC, North, so that in case of any emergency the force can be mobilised to any location quickly.

Twenty vehicles will be located at various places in the city equipped with bomb detection equipment and members of the bomb squad so that they can reach any place immediately in case of an emergency.

The police plan to install CCTVs at 200 important intersections in the city. According to the police, so far, they have installed CCTVs at 53 locations. The commissioner also said 21 watch towers will be set up in various parts of the city.

Kolkata Police will also deploy 25 mobile ambulances and six mobile missing sqauds that can help people in locating children if they are lost.

"We will request the people to avoid using bags. However, if they carry bags we will have to check them at the pandal entrance," said DC DD Jawed Shamim.

Instructions issued by the Kolkata Police

* Do not carry bags, boxes and polythene bags during pandal hopping
* Do not park two wheelers and cars at any place other than parking lots. Stick a label with the name and contact number of the owner of the vehicle on the wind screen
* Do not use bicycles during the Pujas. Also, do not park them anywhere near pandals
* On finding a suspicious-looking object, do not touch, move or lift it. Call 100 for emergency, 1090 for giving any information to the police and 1073 for any unclaimed object
* Do not keep bags and belongings of unknown people with you

Heading: Left-backed teachers’ bodies hail pay panel recommendations - Indian Express
Content:
With dandiya organisers booking many big venues of the city for Navratras and celebrities from Mumbai are expected to descend on the city, no stone have been left unturned to ensure fool-proof security arrangements.

At the Netaji Indoor Stadium, apart from CCTVs, 250 guards from a private agency will be deployed to ensure security.

"Every year, we deploy around 150 security guards, but this year we have decided to increase their number to 250. Besides, there will be 50 police-approved armed guards to patrol the venue," said Tushar Doshi, organiser of the Navratri Dandia Mahotsav.

Apart from CCTVs, the VIP enclosure will be fitted with a special cameras. "We have already sold around 7,500 passes in the last four days. Hence, we are not taking any chances with security this year," Doshi added.

CCTVs have emerged as the obvious choice to man the dance venues. Swabhumi will have six CCTVs, besides, 35 bouncers and 20 guards deployed at various places.

"It is for the first time that we are going to install CCTVs at the dance venue. We have also installed metal detectors at various entry points and will have sniffer dogs in the parking lot," event manager Sandip Sharma said.

Tight security arrangements have also been made by the organisers at Nicco Park. Metal detectors, a bomb detection squad of Gorkha Regiment, sniffer dogs, 80 black cat commandos, will look after the security at the venue.

Heading: One more elephant hit by train, dead - Indian Express
Content:
The Left-backed teachers' organisations, who were up in arms against the G K Chaddha Pay Review Committee after it failed to submit its report last month, have hailed its recommendations as path-breaking. With 60-80 per cent pay hike being recommended by the committee, the teachers were all praise for it. "The committee has submitted its report in a record time of one year and one month," said Ashok Burman, general secretary of the All India Federation of University and College Teachers Organisation.

"Certain recommendations of the committee are path-breaking like the starting salary of college and university teachers will now be more than those of IAS officers. The Central government will take full responsibility for the salary of college and university teachers for the first five years," he added.

Earlier, the teachers were planning to launch movements across the country as the pay panel had failed to submit its report in time.

"We welcome the committee's recommendations of 60-80 per cent pay hike and the decision to increase the retirement age of teachers to 65 years," said Tarun Kanti Naskar, general secretary of the All Bengal University Teachers Association. "But the state government should also implement the recommendations in totality," Naskar added.

Heading: Multiplex collapse: Supervisor detained - Indian Express
Content:
One more elephant was mowed down by a goods train in West Bengal's Buxa Tiger Reserve at Alipurduar on Saturday morning.

The female elephant was crushed to death at the Rajabhatkhawa crossing by a goods train coming from Siliguri.

The incident occurred at 3 am. With this, the total number of elephant deaths due to collision with speeding trains reached five in the past two years.

"The accident took place when a speeding goods train hit an elephant at the Rajabhatkhawa crossing. An investigation will take place and an inquiry will be held to ascertain whether the driver of the goods train had been careless," said L G Lepcha, field director, Buxa Tiger Reserve.

Despite areas on the stretch being identified as elephant corridors and a few zones being declared as vulnerable, the stretch still remains a high risk zone for animals many of whom fall victim to speeding trains.

Heading: Terror trail catches up with former chief of fisheries board - Indian Express
Content:
Police have detained one of the supervisors of the Baguihati multiplex, a portion of which collapsed on Friday evening, critically injuring 11 construction workers.

An FIR was lodged against the builder and the contractor. "The police will take legal actions against the guilty. We have cancelled the licence of the multiplex," chairman of the Rajarhat municipality Tapas Chatterjee said.

The police have also started a probe into the incident. The multiplex on VIP road opposite Big Bazar caved in on Friday.

"Besides inferior quality of building materials, we found several cracks in the building. Had the multiplex been opened for the general public, it would have been a disaster," director of fire services Gopal Bhattacharya said.

Construction of the five-storey multiplex was almost over and the ill-fated labourers were giving finishing touches to the casting work on the top floor.

Heading: Modi keen on taking Nano ride - Indian Express
Content:
16 years after blast in Surat, court convicts 13 people; 7 get 20 yrs in jail, 6 others get off with 10 yrs RI

The Additional and Sessions Court on Saturday convicted former State Fisheries Board Chairman Mohammed Gulam Surti and 12 others in two terror attack cases that had happened 16 years ago.

As per the verdict, Mohammed Hussain Shaikh, Ikbal Wadiwala, Mohammed Gulam Surti, Mustak Patel, Salim Chawal, Ehshan Patel, Yusuf Patel alias Yusuf Dadu, are guilty and will spend 20 years in prison and pay a penalty of Rs. 2 lakh each. Aziz Patel, Abdul Khalid Shaikh, Mehmud Master, Fazal Nagori, Saeed Nadi and Ejaz Patel will undergo 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and pay Rs 20,000 as penalty. Asif Shaikh, another accused, has been acquitted. The District Judge R P Dholaria pronounced the verdict amid the presence of the kin of the accused.

Surti and five of his accomplices had exploded a hand grenade at Mini Bazaar in Varachha on January 28, 1993, in which a minor girl was killed and 11 people were injured. This was a revenge attack after communal violence had flared up in the aftermath of the Babri Masjid demolition.

The accused had then thrown grenades at the Surat railway station on April 22, 1993, in which 37 people were injured and the railway premises was badly damaged.

In the police action that followed, one Mustak Patel of Varachha was arrested from the Dumas area in Surat on March 5, 1995 and a revolver was found in his possession. During interrogation, Mustak disclosed the names of those involved in both the bomb blasts. Acting on the information, the police had arrested many others from different places and recovered two AK-47 rifles with several cartridges and 10 hand grenades. All the arrested were booked under TADA. Several others including the son of Mohammed Surti were declared wanted by the police.

Mohammed Hussain Shaikh, Ikbal Wadiwala, Mohammed Gulam Surti, Mustak Patel, Salim Chawal, Ehsan Patel, Asif Shaikh, Aziz Patel, Abdul Khalid Shaikh, Mehmud Master, Fazal Nagori, Saeed Nadi, Yusuf Patel alias Yusuf Dadu and Ejaz Patel, all residents of Surat, were booked under TADA in the Varachha blast case. Barring Asif Shaikh and Ehshan Patel, all the remaining accused were also found to be involved in the Surat blast incident. All the 14 accused spent six-and-a-half years in prison and were later released on bail.

Heading: Advani to Condi: Why no visa for Modi? - Indian Express
Content:
Will Bengal's loss be Gujarat's gain? Govt in top gear to drive home the small car

Even as speculations are rife about the Tatas evincing a keen interest in relocating the prestigious Nano car project to Gujarat, the Narendra Modi government is learnt to have mounted concerted efforts to bring the small car project to the state.

Sources in the Sachivalaya said on Saturday that since the day Ratan Tata announced his decision of reversing the car project from Singur in West Bengal, Modi had been showing a keen interest in Nano's next destination. "The CM has directed senior officials of the state Industries Department, particularly its Principal Secretary Gauri Kumar, to establish a direct contact with senior executives of Tata Motors and convince them about the positives of the industries-friendly Gujarat," a senior official told Newsline on Saturday. In fact, Gauri Kumar is learnt to have met some top Tata Motors executives last week in this connection. However, senior state government officials as well as ministers concerned are tightlipped about the Nano's possible entry into Gujarat. "We don't want to reveal anything at this stage, otherwise there are chances of our efforts getting sabotaged," said the official.

She said teams from Tata had been surveying different areas of Gujarat including Abdasa and Mundra in Kutch and Sanand talukas in Ahmedabad to find a suitable site for the Nano project. When contacted over the phone on Saturday, Kutch District Collector R R Varsani said, "Tata teams have already visited various parts of the border district. But it's difficult for me to say anything about the relocation at this stage." Parrying a question if her department had offered over 1,000 acres of land to the Tata Motors at Chharodi and Charal villages in Sanand taluka for the Nano project, state Revenue Minister Anandiben Patel said, "A proper person (read Modi) will make an announcement about the Nano project at the right time."

Sachivalaya sources, however, suggest that the Tata Motors may zero in on Kutch keeping in view various factors such as cheaper land, industrial peace, no history of communal violence, besides the existence of Kandla and Mundra ports in the district. The fact that 30 per cent of the spareparts/components to be required for manufacturing Nano cars are being produced by auto ancillary units in Rajkot may also encourage the Tatas to zero in on Kutch as a suitable destination for the relocation, said an official.

Heading: ‘Phoney’ facts: Holes galore in chargesheet filed by DCB - Indian Express
Content:
Senior BJP leader L K Advani today raised the issue of USA's visa denial to Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi during his meeting with US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice.

BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar said Advani asked Rice how the US State Department had issued a clarification that Modi will not be given visa without the latter even applying for it. "Though granting visa is the right of any sovereign nation, it should not ban the entry of any elected chief minister of a democratic country," Advani was quoted as telling Rice.

To this, Rice asked the officials accompanying her to get further details on the issue, said Javadekar. The clarification was issued by the US after an American leader had sought the government's position on the issue last month.

Modi was reportedly denied visa for his alleged role in the Gujarat riots of 2002. Several human rights groups and sections of the media have accused Modi of inaction when communal riots broke out after the Godhra carnage. — PTI

Heading: Petro push: RIL to put state on world refinery map - Indian Express
Content:
The chargesheet filed by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) in the Sabarmati Jail mobile phone case has left many important questions unanswered.

The DCB had filed the chargesheet in the Metropolitan Court on Friday in a case involving Shahnawaz Hussain Bhatti, a convicted terrorist, and five other accused, who were all found with a mobile phone, charger and SIM cards inside the jail during a raid on May 18.

The raid was conducted just four days after the Jaipur serial blasts. During the raid, the DCB had recovered a mobile phone, four SIM cards, a charger, Rs 4,400 in cash and some DVDs from their possession. One of the SIM cards was reportedly being used by Bhatti, a Pakistani national, who is serving a life sentence under POTA for smuggling 24 kg RDX into the country for terrorist activity. He was arrested in 2001 from Bhuj and reportedly used the phone to communicate with his Pakistani connections.

The chargesheet filed by the DCB is, however, totally silent on the use of mobile phones for any such purpose. In fact, the chargesheet makes no mention about the call data from the SIM cards recovered during the raid. Not a single phone number called from the SIM cards is mentioned in the chargesheet.

The chargesheet also does not mention whether Bhatti made any calls to Pakistan. But three Pakistani nationals allegedly involved in the case have been made the accused and shown as 'wanted' in the chargesheet.

The chargesheet also names a few unnamed persons as accused. They are all Sabarmati Jail staffers who helped in supplying the mobile phones to the accused. The chargesheet says they will be named soon after the police finds them.

Interestingly, the chargesheet does not mention how the mobile phones reached the jail in Continued on page 5 Kin allege ill-treatment, refuse to bury Godhra accused(Page 5)

Heading: City slums under SNP unhappy with roads, streetlights - Indian Express
Content:
By 2009, Jamnagar will be a major supplier of Euro IV, Euro V fuel to the European market

By 2009, many automobiles in Europe will be running on fuel exported from Gujarat. The state is set to become the supplier for meeting the growing demand for Euro IV and Euro V standard fuel in the UK and other Western countries. The new Reliance Petroleum Limited refinery coming up at Jamnagar is set to begin operations very soon, ahead of its December 2008 deadline.

Reliance Industries Limited president (refinery) P Raghvendra has said that the refinery is set to begin operations shortly, setting a record of building a new refinery in less than 36 months. The combined output from the new 6-billion dollar refinery and the existing refinery at Moti Khavdi — which has a capacity of 66 million barrels per day — will touch a figure of 1.2 million barrels per day, which is like meeting 50 per cent of the global oil demand increment by the coming year. The refinery is expected to supply 10 million tonnes of petrol and 20 million tonnes of diesel every year.

This will also make Jamnagar the refinery capital of the world. Despite negligible crude production, India will emerge as a prominent player in refining petroleum products.

Along with the quantity, the quality of the products will also give the RPL refinery an edge over the refineries in the Middle East. It will be one of the most complex refineries in the world with a Nelson Complexity Index (NCI) of 14.0. NCI is a measure of the secondary conversion capacity of a petroleum refinery relative to the primary distillation capacity, which assures quality of the by-products like petroleum and diesel of Euro IV and Euro V standard. Even the existing refinery has an NCI of 11.

Heading: Guru Cool: Gujarati parents send their children back to gurukul - Indian Express
Content:
The Slum Networking Programme (SNP) of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) ensures that the slums have streetlights and paved roads. The programme also provides for the construction of internal roads in the slum pockets. However, those slums benefited by the programme are not fully satisfied with the development.

Before the SNP was implemented, the condition of the kachcha lanes and by-lanes was miserable. After it was implemented, things changed for the better but not entirely. Although concrete pavements came up as promised outside the hutments, the condition of internal roads is still in a poor condition. Some slums have concrete roads while others have concrete pavements.

"The internal roads were laid a few years ago, albeit poorly, without studying the slopes. There is always a puddle of water in front of our houses. The AMC officials had only cemented the roads to make them pucca; there was absolutely no effort to lay roads efficiently," says Sanjay Parmar of Guptanagar.

The slums of Narsinhji na Chapra and Jadibanagar face similar problems. The internal road links to the main road are in a bad shape. In some areas, the slabs put in front of the hutments are in a broken condition while in others there are huge pits on the roads.

"We had sent many applications to the AMC, but none were attended to. The pits in front of our hutments become a cesspool of dirty water and filth. They just laid the roads and made no effort to maintain them," says a resident of Pravinnagar.

The roads near Narinhji na Chapra are dotted with huge pits and filth, due to which the internal concrete pavements serve no purpose.

"The main roads near the slums fall under the purview of the AMC. There is no specific initiative only for the slum roads," says Anand Patel, Additional Chief City Engineer of SNP.

Under SNP, the government has installed streetlights in the narrow by lanes of the slums. There is one streetlight after every 7th house. "About 8 streetlights have not been functioning for the last four months. We are waiting for the AMC to come and repair them but nothing has been done yet," says a Jadibanagar resident.

In slum pockets of Chamundanagar, a similar problem was witnessed. The non-functioning of the streetlights is a common complaint in this slum, which has about 1200 hutments. Jagruti Parmar of Chamundanagar says: "The AMC officials removed a faulty streetlight outside our house after we complained, but didn't install a new one."

Heading: Will Ghuma, Sanand meet the same fate as Bopal? - Indian Express
Content:
State witnesses a mushrooming of residential schools offering a mix of religious and contemporary education

Gurukuls have caught the fancy of a large number of parents in Gujarat. These new-age gurukuls impart a mix of religious and contemporary education.

With the rise of spiritualism in the state, the number of ashrams and gurukuls has also multiplied. The students are admitted to the gurukul and they stay in the ashram till their training is over. There are about 95 gurukuls of various spiritual leaders in Gujarat. In Ahmedabad alone, there are about 10 residential gurukuls.

Jridip Surud, an educationist said: "The rise of Hindutva coincided with the emergence of the new middle-class in the state. With this, the need for a non-convent, non-Jesuit culture also gained ground. Parents wanted educational institutions that could inculcate Indian cultural ethos and values in their children. The new gurukuls have now become modern institutes that impart these values."

The Swaminarayan Sampradaya and the Asaram Ashram have the maximum number of gurukuls in Gujarat, followed by the Jain gurukuls. The students in these gurukuls are imparted Vedic, spiritual and modern education. Students not only learn the scriptures and Vedic philosophy, but also horse riding, sports, music and arts.

The curriculum is approved by the Gujarat State Board and only teachers with good qualification are taken in the gurukul pathshaalas. In order to have a better student-teacher relation, the teachers are also given training in child behaviour.

Ravjirai Akbari, the manager at the Swaminarayan Gurukul in Rajkot said: "Every year, the number of students taking admission here doubles. At present, we have 800 students. We have students from Class I to X. For their Class XII education, the students move to Ahmedabad. Students are charged Rs 6,000 per annum as fees."

At the Swaminarayan Gurukul, the students start their day with daily prayers. The classes are held in the campus. Prayers are held three times a day and the students are taught meditation and yoga for inner growth. Suitable infrastructure is also provided for the students on the campus so that they do not need feel the need of going out.

But it is not only Vedic education that is provided to the students. According to Ravinder Kaur, a teacher at the Mahatma Gandhi International School, the students are also given technical training to be on par with their counterparts from regular schools.

Few gurukuls have also become a refuge for the poor kids from the villages, where they are provided with all the amenities at a nominal fee. At the Asaram Ashram in Ahmedabad, there are about 250 students studying in the gurukul. The Ashram charges about Rs 29,000 per annum for boarding, tuition and other facilities. The paathshala charges about 200 per month.

Uday Sangani, spokesperson of Asaram Ashram in Ahmedabad, said: "We believe in this system of education, as it not only educates the students, but also instils true Indian cultural values in them. They are taught the Vedas, shlokas and yogic exercises to help in their mental and physical growth."

The system has also found favour with a large number of Non-Resident Indians (NRI) from the state.

Jatin Shukla, an NRI, said his son studied in the gurukul method, as he wanted him to remain close to Indian culture. "There are many parents who believe that the gurukul system can discipline their children," he said.

There are also some gurukuls like Sandipani Gurukul of Porbandar where children are admitted at the kindergarten stage. The school admits 30-40 students every year from the kindergarten stage to Class X. The school charges Rs 20,000 per annum for boarding and anything between Rs 3,000 and 5,000 as tuition fees.

Hitendra Vyas, the principal of Bhagwad Vidyapeeth, which is the only gurukul having a sanskritised education system, further said that his students fare well in the outside world.

"There are many students who go to the IITs and the IIMs, but they do not know that no book can teach better management skills than the Bhagvad Gita. Our scriptures have a solution to everything, and our students, who are MA in Sanskrit, can easily get any job they want like their English medium counterparts," Vyas said.

Heading: Terror drives garba lovers into closed confines - Indian Express
Content:
With a High Court stay on sale of non-agricultural land and AUDA cap on construction in Bopal, builders and buyers are moving to neighbouring suburbs

Ghuma and Sanand areas of Ahmedabad are the latest victims of unregulated construction.

With the High Court putting a stay on the sale of non-agricultural land in Bopal on Ahmedabad's suburbs, and the Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority's (AUDA) deciding to stop all construction in the said area till the infrastructure and drainage is improved, builders are making a beeline to the neighbouring suburbs of Ghuma and Sanand.

A prominent developer of the state said: "Bopal's affordable housing makes it the ideal choice of our middle-class clientele. But now, with constructions having been stalled here since long, many developers are moving to Ghuma and Sanand."

Buyers, however, are sceptical about this unregulated construction. They believe that unless AUDA, which, at present, is keen to get the government's nod for its Town Planning Schemes in Bopal area, concentrates on Ghuma and Sanand as well, these areas might meet with the same fate as the former.

Builders too believe the same. "Once AUDA wraps up the Bopal Town Planning schemes, it will have to concentrate on Ghuma and Sanand, where already enough houses have come up and that too without adequate infrastructure and drainage," said a builder, adding that under these circumstances, the Bopal experience was likely to be repeated in these areas as well.

AUDA too admitted to the same, but promised to look into these concerns. "With a stay on constructions in Bopal, unregulated constructions have come up in a big way in Ghuma and Sanand. But we hope to resolve Bopal's problems soon, and in all likelihood, constructions will begin there in a couple of months," said Senior Town Planner N M Munshi.

Builders, meanwhile, who had invested large sums of money in Bopal, are anxiously waiting for the HC to lift the ban on construction. "Though we had acquired 80 acres of land in Bopal, we could not begin construction," said Vishal Ditha from Safal Infrastructure, a leading developer in the country. "We are waiting for the authorities to lift the stay on construction," he added. A big project in Bopal has been held up midway, said Jatin Gupta, Director, ISCON Developers, a prominent real estate group in Ahmedabad. AUDA too has indicated that it would formulate a proposal for the expansion of this area soon and send it for the government's approval.

Heading: Boycott of Dalits: 19 held, released on bail - Indian Express
Content:
This Navratri, enthusiasts show a preference for smaller venues in their vicinity

The tradition of sheri garba seems to have bounced back to the centre-stage this Navratri season. With the July 26 serial bomb blasts in Ahmedabad, the subsequent recovery of bombs and explosives in Surat and the recent bomb blast in Modasa town of north Gujarat, still fresh in the public memory, garba enthusiasts prefer doing the sheri garba in their respective housing societies instead of thronging the big, commercial garba grounds.

Organisers of sheri garbas said that as compared to previous years, the number of people visiting their garba venues is huge this time. This is mainly due to security related issues at the commercial garba venues.

The Fatehganj Main Road Yuvak Mandal in Vadodara has been organising sheri garbas in Fatehganj area for many years now. Manhar Rajput, Vice President of the mandal, said: "Earlier, our grounds used to be almost deserted, with just about 100 people playing garba. But this year, we witnessed a crowd of around 3,000 people on the second day itself. This is unprecedented."

According to Rajput, people have re-embraced the sheri garba following the blasts in Ahmedabad and Modasa and other parts of the country. The commercial garba organisers have introduced very strict security arrangements this year, which include asking people to park their vehicles far away from the garba venue. Such things, coupled with other issues, are making people stay hooked to sheri garbas, which are closer to their homes.

The new development has its commercial implications too. Mahesh Rana, who provides sound systems to garba organisers, said: "The sheri garbas are booming this year due to the recent terror wave in the state. I had to supply additional sound systems on the second and third days of Navratri at many sheri garba venues to match the unexpected crowd inflow."

Alpa Shah, one of the organisers of sheri garba at Dharmendra Society in Nehrunagar area of Ahmedabad, said: "People, especially parents, are very scared this year. They are not willing to allow their children to play garba in the commercial grounds that face terror threats."

She added: "Young girls, who have been prohibited from playing garba in big clubs due to security reasons, have also turned to sheri garba."

Anand Parekh of Rudra Charitable Trust that organises garba in Paldi area of Ahmedabad said: "Not only girls, boys too have shunned clubs and commercial venues and are sticking to sheri garbas. Safety and security is the topmost priority for everyone."

Heading: Six-year-old raped on outskirts of Junagadh - Indian Express
Content:
Dalit leaders return to Nesda; visit shops, but under police protection, to purchase basic necessities

The Tankara police on Friday arrested 19 people in connection with the FIR over the social boycott of Dalits in this Rajkot district village on Monday. They were later released on bail.

Meanwhile, the Dalit leaders from the village, who were camping at Tankara for registering the FIR, went back to Nesda on Saturday under police protection. With the social boycott still on, the Dalits went to the village shops under police protection to purchase some basic necessities.

Dana Parmar, a Dalit villager said: "We were camping at Tankara for the last 18 days to get the FIR registered. With the FIR registered, we wanted to return to the village, but we feared some backlash, and requested for police protection. We came to Nesda with the police today. We procured whatever we required, from the grocer."

Sub-Inspector R B Rana from the Tankara police station, said: "We sent our personnel to accompany them to the grocers' shop. We have already arranged for a police bandobast there."
