Heading: After bailout, the hard part - Indian Express
Content:
The Steel Ministry today asked producers to refrain from having multiple pricing of their produce and directed that they must have a single-pricing mechanism and publicise it for the benefit of their consumers.

The directive comes amid reports that end users were paying much higher than the factory price of various steel products.

"In the past 2-3 months, allegations have been made that there are multiple prices of a product. For example the price mutually-agreed between the buyer and the seller was one while those products being sold through the retailers were differently priced," Steel Minister Ram Vilas Paswan said. He pointed out that owing to a demand-supply mismatch of nearly 12 per cent, the country had to import about 2.1 million tonnes of steel in the last fiscal.

Heading: Mumbai Metro achieves financial closure - Indian Express
Content:
It will be one of the world's largest asset management firms with an impressive $700 billion war chest. Nothing short of the global economy depends on its success. And the Treasury Department has barely a month to get it up and running.

The bailout bill that President Bush quickly signed into law on Friday must do what financial experts have been unable to do for the last year — put a dollar value on mortgage-related assets that no one wants, move them off the books of ailing banks and unlock the frozen credit markets.

In signing the measure, Bush warned Americans not to expect instant results. "This will be done as expeditiously as possible, but it cannot be accomplished overnight. We'll take the time necessary to design an effective program that achieves its objectives — and does not waste taxpayer dollars." Even after working feverishly over the last two weeks, the Treasury will not buy its first distressed asset from a bank for roughly six weeks, and almost certainly not until after the Nov. 4 elections.

Treasury officials do not plan to manage the mortgage assets on their own. Instead, they will outsource nearly all of the work to professionals, who will oversee huge portfolios of bonds and other securities for a management fee.

The Treasury is expected to name a senior official to supervise the program. For now, various working groups creating the program are reporting directly to Henry M Paulson Jr, the Treasury secretary.

Paulson has recruited several former colleagues from Goldman Sachs to advise him, though administration officials took pains to say that they were not dominating the process, pointing to other Treasury employees who were playing major roles.

"We will move rapidly to implement the new authorities, but we will also move methodically," Paulson said.

Heading: Tata move may affect growth, feels industry - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL), a joint venture between Reliance Infrastructure, France's Veolia Transport and Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA), has signed the loan agreements to raise debts totaling Rs 1,194 crore, and achieved the financial closure for the first line of Mumbai Metro Varsova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor.

In a uniquely structured project financing model, MMOPL has raised this debt from a group of banks led by IDBI, Corporation Bank, Karur Vyasa bank, Canara Bank, Indian Bank and Oriental Bank of Commerce. IIFCL (UK) is providing the foreign currency loan for the project.

The project being built at a cost of Rs 2,356 crore will have debt component of Rs 1,194 crore, while the equity is Rs 512 crore while, MMRDA, the concessioning authority will provide a capital grant Rs 650 crore.

The cost of borrowing for the rupee component, which constitutes about 75 per cent of the total debt, will be 12.25 per cent, while the foreign currency loan will be at 3.5 per cent above LIBOR. The debt has been raised amidst a tight global liquidity position, based on a unique funding model, where the only recourse available to the lenders is to the cash flow generated from the project instead of the project assets.

"Institutional funding of a metro project is new as it involves interactions with different agencies including rolling stock, power supply, signaling, engineering and other such functions. The repayment model is also unique as for the first time the project's assets are not charged to the lender as security," said K P Maheshwari, Director MMOPL.

The project is ahead of schedule and is slated to be complete by July 2010.

Heading: Seminar to keep experts abreast with new AIDS researches - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: SVIT students celebrate Vision 2008 - Indian Express
Content:
The AIDS Society of India organised a special seminar here on Sunday to update medical experts about the new drugs that help boost the immunity level of patients with HIV/AIDS.

More than 180 medical experts from within and outside the city attended the seminar. Dr I S Gilada, secretary general, AIDS Society of India, said that Anti Retroviral drugs are available free of cost to HIV/AIDS patients.

However, the liver tests which are a necessity with these drugs are hardly offered by the civil hospitals.

Dr Keyur Shah, organising committee member of the society, said: "AIDS

Society of India is a non-profit organisation primarily involved in keeping medical experts up to date about various forays, researches and drugs in the field of HIV/AIDS."

He added that awareness about various diagnostic techniques needs to be increased in order to reduce the rising cases of HIV/AIDS.

Dr Shah further said that although the drugs are available for HIV/AIDS patients in government hospitals, a strong foundation is required to battle the issue.

Heading: CBI probe sought into Continuing Education Programme - Indian Express
Content:
More than 1,200 students took part in Vision 2008, an inter-departmental technical symposium organised by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Institute of Technology in Vasad on Friday.

The event was conducted under the Indian Students Chapter of Technical Education for the second consecutive year.

According to a press release issued by the institute, about 35 technical events such as poster presentation, technical group discussion and electronic circuit analysis were organised on the occasion.

Pankit Pandya, one of the students in the organising committee, said the aim of Vision 2008 was to make prospective engineers technically and conceptually strong and give them an edge over others in the professional world.

"We believe that education without character development is meaningless. That is the motto of our institute," Pandya said.

In addition, Kartavya, a students' organisation formed by the alumni of Indian School of Mines University, Dhanbad, inaugurated its first centre in Gujarat at SVIT.

The students' organisation is dedicated to improve the future of underprivileged children.

It already has other branches at various premier institutes all over India.

Heading: ‘Open’ secret: Slums under SNP devoid of greenery - Indian Express
Content:
In a letter to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee spokesman Jayantilal Parmar has sought a CBI inquiry into the Continuing Education Programme (CEP) under Union government's Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, alleging serious financial and administrative irregularities.

In his letter, Parmar levelled 18 charges, ranging from diversion of funds to misuse of money. He also alleged that nearly 2,800 motivators (prerak) working under the CEP have not been paid honorarium for the last 18 months.

According to him, ever since the central grants flow stopped as per the provisions of the scheme, no salary was paid to motivators at various levels. Parmar also wanted to know where the money meant for motivator training went when there was no training at all. He also accused Ahmedabad Mahanagar Saksharta Samiti, a registered trust that implements CEP, of not providing bicycles to nodal motivators despite receiving grants amounting to Rs 17.25 lakh.

Heading: University panel fails to reach a conclusion on CCTV issueEXPRESS NEWS SERVICE - Indian Express
Content:
Although landscaping is part of the project, it is unknown in the slums

"We want our surroundings to be clean and green, but how can that happen when the municipality is nonchalant?" says Bina Patni of Hanuman Nagar slums.

The Slum Networking Programme (SNP) provides for landscaping in the slums. As per it, open spaces are developed and trees are planted in the slums. Sadly, however, more than 90 per cent of the slums do not have these open spaces and trees.

"To have greenery around us is a far-fetched dream. We only wish the AMC showed more concern and kept a regular check on the roads, drainage and water supply," adds Patni.

In Sanjay Nagar (first project under SNP), some hutments were pulled down and reconstructed to develop open spaces and wider internal lanes. But other slums have not been that lucky.

Most of the slums have narrow by-lanes with substandard infrastructure where sewerage and water supply continues to be a persistent problem. A two-wheeler can hardly pass through the by-lanes. Most of the land is used for solid waste disposal or cesspools.

Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation's (AMC) landscaping includes the upliftment of the nearby areas of the slums. The programme encourages developing gardens and parks for the slum-dwellers.

In slums like Pravinnagar, Guptanagar and Azad Nagar, trees were planted as part of the landscaping chapter. In other slums, the residents themselves had planted trees, years before the SNP was introduced. But in all the 45 slums that are under SNP, parks and gardens are totally absent.

Many slum residents are not even aware of landscaping being a part of the facilities under SNP. "We had trees in our area for a long time. Nobody had come to plant trees here. When we hardly have any space in the narrow by-lanes, where can we find open spaces? Even the area surrounding our chawl is in bad shape. Where will they construct parks and gardens for us?" says a visibly upset resident of Narsinhji na Chapra.

According to Ramesh Vaghela of Pravinnagar, the AMC officials had planted a few trees there.

"The slum-residents have to take care of the trees. During rains, if the trees need to be chopped, nobody attends our call. We do not have enough water supply, how can we water the trees?"

he said.

Heading: Cong leader questions Modi govt’s tech frenzy with employees - Indian Express
Content:
The special committee formed on September 28 to look into the complaints by the women non-teaching staff of Gujarat University (GU) against Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Parimal Trivedi, over the installation of CCTV cameras in the women's toilets, failed to reach any conclusion in their meeting on Sunday.

After the meeting, members of the special committee and the complainants refused to make any comments to the media. The three-member special committee of Sudhir Nanavati, Rajshree Bhatt and Mukul Shah listened to all the complaints for more than two hours, but did not declare their decision. The committee members will submit their report to the Executive Council (EC) of the GU.

"There is a strong possibility that this matter will be resolved soon as no one wants to stretch this issue. The committee and women complainants seem positive and do not want to spoil GU's image," a source said. The special committee listened to all the complaints for more than three hours on October 3 and decided to meet again on Sunday afternoon.

On September 25, the women non-teaching staff had given a written complaint to the Women Development Cell (WDC) of the GU over the CCTV issue.

The special committee was formed on September 28 at the previous Executive Council (EC) meeting.

Heading: Shaping future engineers: city gets robotics centre for kids - Indian Express
Content:
Questioning the state government's "wisdom" in making it mandatory for all its employees to pass CCC and CCC+ computer exams, Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee executive president Kunvarji Bavalia has said that this would pave way for private institutions to thrive on employees' plight. In a statement issued on Monday, he has claimed that the move would only benefit private computer training institutes.

Not only that, some ITI instructors are also involved in making money by indulging in corrupt practices in connivance with these computer institutes, alleged Bavalia. He said that instead of releasing the seven per cent dearness allowance instalments and not paying arrears under the Sixth Pay Commission report, the government is exploiting its own employees.

"The government has given a 45-hour syllabus of computer training to its employees and expects them to clear the tests, which they cannot. Increments, promotions and other benefits have been linked with this. This forces them to bribe training institutes for getting passing certificates," Bavalia said. He added that despite thousands of employees paying their examination fees at Sardar Patel Institute of Public Administration, Ahmedabad, the exams have not been conducted, which has resulted in long waiting lists. To jump the ladder, such waitlisted employees pay Rs 300-400 to the institute staff concerned.

The government has indulged in all this just to show on paper that all of its employees are computer literate, Bavalia said, adding, "There are only 50 exam centres and one centre would accommodate only 30 to 40 candidates. But when will it achieve this when there are lakhs of government employees who are supposed to clear the exam?"

He has further alleged that ITI instructors are running private institutes in the name of their relatives. According to him, this menace must be investigated and the role of institutes must be limited to training only. Computer training need not be a must for all and sundry, he said. For example, policemen are required to learn techniques to fight terror rather than learn CCC or CCC+, he said. He also said there is no justification for forcing all teachers and talatis to learn computers.

Heading: ‘No new Primary Training Colleges in 2009-10’ - Indian Express
Content:
Now, tech-savvy kids in the city have a reason to rejoice, thanks to a city-based private educational organisation, which has started a first-of-its-kind centre for children to learn basic and advanced robotics and electronics.

The centre, which was started a few months ago in Jodhpur area, has been providing training to kids in the age group of 8-14 through a four-level curriculum, spanning two years.

While the first two levels include training in basic robotics and basic electronics, the third and fourth levels include training in advanced robotics and basic electronics.

Sagar Vyas who is heading the centre said: "The main aim of this course is to motivate kids to develop the hobby of making robotic and electronic models. In the long run, it may help them in choosing the kind of career they want to pursue after Class X and Class XII."

Vyas added that the course is getting a good response. Nearly 18 students have already enrolled for the course and the number is increasing every week. In addition, the centre is on the verge of finalising a deal with a reputed school in the city to teach robotics and electronics to the students.

Vyas took the franchise of the centre from a Bangalore-based company, Silicon Kids, which is already running similar programs in other parts of the country.

Heading: Pay panel recommendation: Govt staff threaten stir - Indian Express
Content:
The National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE) has decided not to open any new Primary Training Colleges (PTC) for the academic year 2009-10.

The decision comes after an unbelievable drop in the number of students taking admission in PTCs as well as Bachelors of Education (B.Ed) colleges.

There are around 450 PTCs and 140 B.Ed colleges in the state and about 45 per cent of them do not have sufficient number of students.

In the last two academic years, there was a sudden growth in the number of PTCs in Gujarat. It has gone up to 450 from 200, said a senior official from the State Education Department on condition of anonymity.

The official added that around 80 per cent of these colleges will have to be shut down by the end of this academic year if proper steps are not taken to improve their situation.

Moreover, around 90 per cent of these colleges, which are affiliated to Gujarat University (GU) are not in good shape.

Sudhir Nanavati, President of the Association of B.Ed Colleges told Newsline: "Many students who have completed their B.Ed from these colleges complain that the placement is not up to the mark. Even the quality has been affected. So, there is an urgent need to stop opening such colleges any more."

"About 30 B.Ed colleges in the state are on the verge of closure due to insufficient number of students. The other 25 per cent might have to be shut down due to new rules and regulations, which have been framed to run such colleges," added Nanavati.

He further said, "This is a good decision by the NCTE."

D G Gohil, Managing Trustee of the Vision Education Trust, Ahmedabad, said that the situation of B.Ed colleges in the state is poor.

"The average salary of a trained student is Rs 4,500 per month, which remains the same for five years. One can not survive and support the family with this salary," he said.

Ravindra Khatri, Principal of Shri S G Roa College of Teacher Education of Veda, Mansa Taluka, Gandhinagar district, added: "There are few quality PTCs in the state. Although many PTCs have come up, they lack excellence."

Heading: Indian Airlines bus mows down airport employee - Indian Express
Content:
The state government employees are up in arms against the government over the issue of implementing the Sixth Pay Commission recommendations to hike their salaries. To register their protest, the employees carried out a huge rally in Ahmedabad on Sunday afternoon.

Other protest programmes such as going on a Mass Casual Leave and calling an indefinite strike are also on the cards if the government does not pay heed to their demand. The agitating employees have also threatened that the BJP government's delaying the pay-hike might cost the party dear in the upcoming Lok Sabha election.

The rally was carried out by different associations and federations of the state government employees under the umbrella of Guajrat Rajya Karmachari Sankalan Samiti (Gujarat State Employees Co-Ordination Committee) and was attended by thousands of state government employees.

Gujarat State Panchayat Employees Federation, Gujarat State Primary Teachers' Federation, Gujarat State Officers' Federation and Gujarat State Board Nigam Employees Federation are some of the notable organisations that took part in the rally.

Chairman of Gujarat State Employees Co-Ordination Committee, Vishnu Patel, told Newsline: "The state government had announced the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission in its manifesto, but it has been delaying it on the pretext of putting it for review by a committee. We outrightly condemn the formation of the committee to examine the pay commission's recommendation. We demand pay hike at the earliest."

Patel also said that the BJP's good performance in the coming Lok Sabha election maybe doubtful. "The total voting heads of the state government employees and their families come to almost a crore. If the government does not give them their right, it may prove costly for them in the election," he said.

Patel also announced that all state government employees would go on a Mass Casual Leave on November 5 if their demands were not accepted by then.

Joint General Secretary of the Co-Ordination Committee Harshad Raval said, "State governments of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan have already implemented the pay commission's recommendations. So, it is high time Gujarat government heard our demands."

President of the Gujarat State Officers' Federation Vivek Kapadiya said: "The state government has an inclination of not paying enough to its employees, as it believes it is already paying them enough. Apart from that, it also has a tendency to outsource all the work. That is why it has not been recruiting people. To attain their goal, they are forcing the people to leave their jobs."

Kapadiya added that the state government might have served five years in the state but the cost of their deeds might have to be borne by the central BJP leadership in the next Lok Sabha election.

Heading: Finally, Gujarat Police have proof of Lashkar’s involvement in Ahmedabad blasts - Indian Express
Content:
An Indian Airlines bus ran over a 35-year-old air catering service employee on the premises of Sardar Patel International Airport on Sunday morning. The victim, Narayan Vaghela, was rushed to the Rajasthan Hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

The Indian Airlines authorities have refused to take responsibility for the mishap. "The bus as well as the driver were employed by a private contractor and the Indian Airlines cannot be blamed for the accident," said an official of the National Aviation Company of India Ltd (NACIL) in Ahmedabad.

The incident took place near the Air Traffic Control (ATC) tower in the domestic terminal of the airport around 8.30 am. Vaghela, who worked for Conwood Inflight Catering Service, was getting out of the airport from a VIP gate after completing his night shift. Around the same time, Mohanlal Parmar, the driver of an Indian Airlines passenger bus was driving the bus out of the airport premises for servicing. When he reached close to the VIP gate, Parmar 'accidentally' pressed the accelerator of the vehicle instead of the brakes, the police said.

The bus rammed into the gate, which was flung open upon impact. It then headed towards Vaghela, who had walked a distance of more than 10 feet towards another gate near the ATC tower. But before he could save himself, the bus hit him, police added.

Sardarnagar police have arrested Parmar on charges of rash driving and causing death by negligence. "In his statement, Parmar has told us that there was a technical glitch in the brake shoe because of which the vehicle did not stop on time. We are, however, waiting for the reports of the experts examining the bus before ascertaining anything. Our investigation is on," said Inspector A S Rathod.

Incidentally, before being employed on a contract basis by the NACIL about a year ago, Parmar (61) was a driver with the Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Corporation (AMTS), whose drivers are notorious for rash driving.

A resident of Meghaninagar, Vaghela was the sole breadwinner in his family. He is survived by his wife and five children. Like other airlines, the NACIL hires private buses to be used as passenger vehicles on the airport premises. The drivers are employed on a contract basis. Air India has a total of ten such buses in Ahmedabad airport. Airport Director D P Bhagat did not answer calls by the media.

Heading: BJP legislator gives IIM-A students tips on constituency management - Indian Express
Content:
'Lashkar-e-Toiba operative Nasir Raziuddin has confessed to his role in July 26 blasts,' say cops

Nasir Raziuddin, who was arrested in connection with the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts, has reportedly confessed to his involvement in the conspiracy during interrogation. Investigating officers have said that for the first time they have clear leads to establish the direct involvement of Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) in the Gujarat blasts.

An alleged militant having links with LeT and Huji, Nasir, at present, is in the custody of the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB). Sources said that he is likely to be named as one of the key conspirators in the Ahmedabad serial blasts soon.

"Nasir has confessed to having taught the youths from Gujarat in the SIMI training camps, bomb-making with ammonium nitrate, ball bearings and other locally available materials. He has also confessed to having conspired with others to trigger blasts in Gujarat. His interrogation has given us some more leads that establish LeT's direct involvement in the recent blasts," a senior DCB officer said.

Son of Maulana Naseeruddin, who is one of the accused in the assassination of former Gujarat home minister, Haren Pandya, Nasir was recently brought to Ahmedabad in connection with the July 26 serial blasts. Until then, he was lodged in Belgaum Jail in Karnataka on charges of waging war against the nation.

"Nasir's role in the Ahmedabad serial blasts surfaced following the confessions of Abbas Sameja and Javed Ahmed Sheikh. Sameja and Sheikh had attended training camps in Halol and Kerala, where they had met Nasir and got trained by him," the officer added.

According to the DCB, although Nasir was in Belgaum Jail when Ahmedabad blasts took place and was not involved in the execution of the blasts, he was very much involved in the conspiracy.

They also said that they are in the process of bringing those arrested from Mumbai and Mangalore to Ahmedabad. Mohammed Ali, Javed Ali, Naushad, and Ahmed Bava—all associates of LeT's Riyaz Batkal—had been arrested in Mangalore, while Mohammed Zakir Shaikh, Afzal Usmani, Mohammed Sadiq Ahmed, Aman Arif Shaikh and Shaikh Mohammed Ansar were arrested in Mumbai.

"We want to corroborate what Nasir has told us about LeT's involvement in the blasts in the city and across the country," an investigating officer said.

Heading: Christians on protest march to grab Centre’s attention - Indian Express
Content:
At the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, there was brainstorming of a different kind on Sunday. There were no boardroom battles, nor were there long discussions on the treacherous ways of demand and supply in marketing and finance sectors. Instead, a thought was being given to the gap created between 'need' and 'policy' in public policies.

Helping the seven students of Public Policy Group (PPG) course formulate a framework for the Constituency Management Programme was Harin Pathak — five-time BJP Parliamentarian from Ahmedabad.

In an interaction that lasted close to three hours, Pathak discussed with the students areas that they should identify and work on, the framework of the programme and how it could benefit policy-makers.

"I had a wonderful session with the students. It was about helping them identify issues at the grassroots level and the methods in which they can be resolved by a legislator," said Pathak.

After getting the basics of constituency management, the students will now apply them in Pathak's constituency.

Srijan Pal Singh, coordinator of the course said: "We will start working in Ahmedabad Lok Sabha constituency. It will be a grassroots project that will focus on people's needs and the way they are resolved. For example, is there a policy solution for every need of the people? Or, are they even aware of the things they should demand from their leaders?"

Interacting with the students, Pathak said that each time there are elections, and a new Parliament is formed, people get to see new faces. Most of the time, 50 per cent of the MPs are new, he said. It is, therefore, imperative to reach the grassroots level. The high attrition rate among MPs, he said, could be avoided if better constituency management practices were employed.

Rajat Sarkar, who attended the session, said: "It was very motivating. He gave us a deep insight into the way politicians think about constituency management."

Pathak said that he was pleased when students said they wanted to contribute to policy-making. "I told them that they couldn't contribute much from outside. Join the civil services, politics and make a difference. One can't stay out and say that our leaders are not doing anything."

Congress MP Madhusudhan Mistry and CPI MP Sitaram Yechury are other leaders who are likely to interact with the IIM-A students as part of the PPG programme.

Heading: No entry: CEPT, NID flash red signal to outsiders - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to draw the Centre's attention and sentitise people, hundreds of Christians from across the city gathered in Bandra on Sunday, as Orissa continues to grab headlines for continuous violence against Christians. "My house at Kandhamal was burnt down by some political groups last month. Though we were lucky not to have got burnt, the fear is still there. My father-in-law cannot speak about the incident. We moved to the city, thanks to various NGOs helping the victims there. I want people in this city to know more about our problems," said Solomon Cecil.

Many such victims who moved along with their friends and relatives to Mumbai, were led by the Catholic Secular Forum (CSF) and the Indian Christian Voice (ICV) who conducted a prayer-protest march from St. Peters Church to Mount Mary in Hill Road on Sunday evening. Interestingly, the march culminated with an enactment of 'Passion of Christ'.

"The act sends across an important point. Jesus was persecuted in his own land by his own people. What Christians are facing in Orissa is something similar to that. The sad thing is that people are still unaware of the issue, so we chose to enact this to sensitise people," said Alan D' Souza, a resident of Santacruz who played the role of Jesus.

The two groups have been conducting such protest marches throughout the country for the past 40 days. Earlier, they conducted a protest march in Hyderabad and one in Chennai. "This is the first time since independence that Christians are being targeted in such huge number. This is purely a political move by Hindu fundamentalist groups. If the Centre can ban groups like SIMI then they should also ban the VHP and the Bajrang Dal. They are spilling Christian blood for political expediency," said vice-chairman of State Minorities Commission and president of ICV Dr Abraham Mathai.

While there has been widespread violence for a while now, the situation drew the Centre's attention only last week when the issue was brought up when the Prime Minister was on a visit to France. "Our main grouse with the Centre is that they have been sleeping on the issue for a very long time now. So many lives have been lost and so many families destroyed. But the Centre woke up only after the Prime Minister was questioned by world leaders during his visit," said Dr Mathai.

Dodging allegations of large-scale conversions by Christian missionary groups in the state, Dr Mathai said that anti-conversion laws in the country are 'draconian'. "Allegations of conversion are baseless. How can anybody convert people in this country, we have such draconian laws. None of these allegations have been proved yet," said Mathai.

After conducting such protest marches in the city, the group also plans to seek international help. "We will take every step to internationalise the issue. We will ask foreign groups to stop funding fundamentalist groups. We also want President's rule to be imposed in Orissa as soon as possible. We have also moved the UN to look into the matter and take necessary steps immediately," said member of the District Minorities Welfare Committee and general secretary of CSF, Joseph Dias.

"Minority rights should be saved no matter what. We will take every step possible to pressurise the Centre to take concrete action against any person or group spreading communalism in the country," added Dias.

Heading: Garba cancelled due to rains - Indian Express
Content:
In wake of the recent bomb blasts that rocked the country, Centre for Environmental Planning and Technology (CEPT) University and National Institute of Design (NID) have decided to ban entry of outsiders into their campus during the Navratri celebrations this year.

The students even came forward to bear the entire expense of the event, which runs into lakhs. However, the administration has agreed to share a part of the expense.

A number of CCTV cameras have been installed in the campus and all activity is monitored from time to time to keep any nuisance at bay.

Chirag Rangholia, president of the student council of the School of Architecture, CEPT University, said: "Till last year, it was possible for outsiders to buy passes and enjoy garba in our campus. We used to generate around Rs 6 lakh by selling these passes. But this time, we have kept it a strictly in-house affair and have invited our alumni to participate in the celebrations. But we have made provisions to allow students from other institutions to come in on particular days."

Varun Shah, president of the student council of the School of Interior Design, CEPT University, told Newsline, "We have had some bad experiences in the past and so we have planned not to allow outsiders inside the campus this year."

Ankur Mehra, president of the Student Activity Council (SAC), NID, said: "The passes distributed among students were even sold, which blemished the reputation of the college. So, this year, we have no passes. Instead, the students will be allowed to bring their family on the basis of their identity cards."

Mehra added: "The students are happy with the decision and this will allow us to minimise any trouble during the celebrations."

Heading: 2 more genetic diagnostic centres in the offing - Indian Express
Content: Sudden rains in Narmada district and Pavi Jetpur taluka in Vadodara district played spoilsport for Navratri enthusiasts on Sunday evening. Considering bad weather, all the organisers cancelled their programmes. Maximum rain recorded in Narmada district was 9 mm in Sagbara taluka and 12 mm in Pavi Jetpur. Officials at Pavi Jetpur flood control room said that there was no rainfall in Bodeli and Sukhi dam areas. However, there was drizzle in Pavi Jetpur.

Heading: Re-poll in 3 Bhavnagar University faculties - Indian Express
Content:
Centres to be set up at Rajkot and Bhavnagar civil hospitals

The way genetic diseases and conditions are diagnosed is set to change drastically in the state, with the launch of two new genetic diagnostic centres shortly. The centres, which will be set up at Rajkot and Bhavnagar civil hospitals, will function as complete genetic diagnostic centres with facilities ranging from research and training to detection.

At present, Gujarat has a total of four such centres, including one private and three government laboratories. However, the three government centres have been carrying out research and diagnosis on specific disorders.

For example, the Zoology Department at Gujarat University looks at male infertility; the Cancer Hospital in Ahmedabad focuses on cancer; and the Foundation for Research in Genetic and Endocrinology in Ahmedabad studies chromosome analysis. The new centres, however, are the first two government centres in the state that will provide treatment for all genetic diseases and conditions.

The resources for the new centres will come from Gujarat State Biotechnology Venture Fund. The training and expertise will be provided by the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM), a wing of the state Department of Science and Bio-Technology.

Apart from diagnosis, the two centres will help the state government in building data to conduct research on specific and special disorders.

"The existing government and private diagnostic centres cater to specific disorders. But the two new centres would provide diagnosis for all genetic disorder cases," said GSBTM Director Akshaykumar Saxena. He added: "These centres will prove very useful in carrying out research in general as well as on specific disorders."

While the new centres have begun the process of installing equipment required for conducting a range of tests for gene and molecular analysis, the GSBTM has commenced the training modules for staff members. "Two batches, each consisting of 30 qualified members, have been imparted the required training," said Madhvi Joshi, GSBTM Sector Specialist for Pharma and Health Care.

Existing centres

* Zoology Department, School of Sciences, Gujarat University, Ahmedabad — This department has been running the Clinic for Genetic Diagnostics since 1979. The main focus is on congenital disorders like infertility.

* Gujarat Cancer & Research Institute, M P Shah Cancer Hospital, Ahmedabad — Established in 1972, GCRI is a functional autonomous body jointly managed by Govt. of Gujarat and Gujarat Cancer Research Society. The Institute is actively involved in Cancer cytogenetics to provide services for patients with leukaemia, including karyotyping and FISH analysis in various blood cancers to help in diagnosis and prognosis.

* Foundation for Research in Genetics and Endocrinology (FRIGE) — Since 2005, the centre is involved in providing diagnosis service in genetics and endocrinology and other R&D activities with facilities of Chromosome analysis, FISH studies, Fragile X studies and other molecular analysis.

Heading: Threat mails: SOG keeps a close watch on bookshops - Indian Express
Content:
Two senate members and a principal accused of issuing duplicate cards and bringing dummy voters

Bhavnagar University has announced re-polling in three out of six faculties for posts in the senate. The decision was taken after the university Vice-Chancellor (V-C) was informed that duplicate cards and dummy voters were involved in the September-28 elections.

Polling in Commerce, Law and Education faculties have been declared null and void, and re-election will be held on November 10, said H C Trivedi, V-C of Bhavnagar University. Counting of votes in the remaining three faculties will start from October 10.

"Police have identified three people who are allegedly involved in issuing duplicate cards and bringing in dummy voters. We have already given our takes and statements on them to the police. They will investigate the matter and punish the guilty," Trivedi added.

Two senate members of Bhavnagar University and a school principal have been accused of being involved in the cheating case.

Of the three, Rajesh Joshi (appointed by the Chancellor) and Upendrasinh Rana (elected Graduates Science Faculty) are senate members. The third, H V Gardi, is the principal of a local school in Vavdi village.

"Probe is on. Till now, we have found three people who are possibly involved in the matter," said Inspector M S Adyaru of A-Division, Bhavnagar City.

Heading: Woman arrested for forging bank documents - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Operation Group (SOG) is tightening its noose around offenders sending threat mails to educational institutions and shrines.

The group is keeping a close watch on stationery shops and book shops. It is also consulting the railway department and psychiatrists to nail down the perpetrators of the crime.

Speaking to Newsline, Police Inspector K M Polra said: "There is an interesting pattern in which the letters are written. Of late, the offenders have started using stamps and issuing bogus signatures." This is a prominent change, he said.

The SOG has alerted all the stationery shop owners in the area from where the letters are suspected to have been mailed.

"We have asked owners of stationery shops to keep a tab on those who purchase stamps and those who frequently buy envelops," Polra said.

"After the instructions, each shop owner has started maintaining a record of those who purchase envelops and stamps," he said.

Heading: LPG shortage is sign of rapid industrial growth: Deora - Indian Express
Content:
Makarpura police has obtained a two-day remand order for a woman accused of procuring a chequebook from the Bank of Baroda by forging the documents of her old customer.

According to investigating officer K B Damor, the incident came to light on Saturday at around 3.30 pm when bank officials found variations in the signature of the account holder and the application form for the new chequebook.

Police said the accused, Reshma Multani, a resident of Karelibag, possessed important documents of the complainant, Motibhai Patel, since she was an insurance agent at that time.

Multani hatched a plan to withdraw money from Patel's account and used the same documents to procure the new chequebook from the bank. She produced a fake letterhead of Makarpura Saw Mill, which belonged to Patel and put a stamp on it. She produced it in the bank along with other supporting documents to get a chequebook.

"Patel was totally unaware about it as he had given the documents to Multani to get an insurance policy. Multani, however, used the documents to procure Patel's chequebook. But the bank officials found variations in the signatures and called up Patel to ask him whether he had authorised anyone or submitted any application to get a fresh chequebook. Patel denied issuing any authority letter to get the chequebook. We arrested Multani when she came to the bank," Damor told Newsline.

He added that the police are now investigating the matter in detail and are trying to find out whether Multani had swindled money from other accounts using the same trick. "We have got a two-day remand order to interrogate Multani. We are trying to find out whether she has duped others or not," Damor said.

Heading: Delegation to visit Pakistan to seek fishermen’s release - Indian Express
Content:
Shortage of Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) in small-scale industries signifies rapid growth of industries in Gujarat, said Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Murli Deora at a review meet of oil and natural gas, organised here on Sunday.

The demand for LPG was because of the new projects coming up at the Krishna Godavri Basin, he said.

"Total availability of LPG is about nine per cent in Gujarat, but the requirement is about 33 per cent. The project of Krishna Godavri Basin is in good progress and the pipeline will be installed soon," he said.

Issues such as discontinuing of the Jan Kerosene Pariyojana (JKP) were also discussed in the meeting. Representative of a kerosene dealers' association pointed out that local level gram panchayat was involved in the JKP, and it could easily be revoked. He also suggested that coupon system could be introduced so that everyone could get kerosene at subsidised rate.

Commenting on the price of crude oil, Deora said the price is decreasing and the situation will be stabilised.

Before the meeting, Deora was at Lunej, in Khambhat, to attend the function organised by ONGC to mark 50 years of oil production in India. Several representatives of small-scale industries and kerosene dealers' association also attended programme.

Meeting's highlights

* Total LPG auto retail outlets in Gujarat: 27 at present, and 18 more likely to come up

* CNG retail outlets: 62 at present, and 31 planned

* LPG bottling plant to come up on the outskirtsof Vadodara

* Retail outlets to be upgraded

Heading: Talking point : With iqbal khan - Indian Express
Content:
A seven-member delegation, including fishermen, will leave for Pakistan on October 13 to seek release of 434 fishermen and 379 boats from Pakistani custody, an Indian Fishermen Association (IFA) official said.

The delegation has been given a 21-day visa to visit Karachi and Islamabad, IFA president Veljibhai Masani said on Sunday.

The proposed visit follows a communication from Pakistani authorities that they would auction the seized Indian boats if there was no response from their side before October 30, Masani, a member of the delegation, said.

The delegation also hopes to meet Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari to seek immediate release of the captured fishermen who belong to various parts of Gujarat, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, he said.

"We hope to seek the release of the fishermen in time for them to celebrate Diwali with their family members."

Chief Minister Narendra Modi too, was worried about the issue and had taken up the matter with the Centre, official sources said. Six fishermen have committed suicide in the past three years after failing to repay their loans and due to deteriorating financial condition, Masani said.

The Centre, realising the gravity of the situation, had asked the state government to submit a list of people to be sent as part of the delegation to Pakistan, sources said.

Modi and State Fisheries and Agriculture Minister Dilip Sanghani had sent a list of 13 people to the Union Government, of which seven names were approved in a span of one-and-half months, Masani said.

Earlier, Modi had said Pakistani authorities had stopped releasing Indian boats from custody since 2003, which had aggravated the problems of fishermen, Masani said.

Heading: Ballroom dancing - Indian Express
Content:
What is the concept of your new show Sambhav Kya?

The show is based on supernatural and unusual happenings. There will be two or three stories per episode. The stories have a kernel of truth in them, meaning that they're based on fact. They're not just ghost stories; for instance, there could be a story about a lady who, when she goes for an ultrasound, is told that she's carrying twins. But when she gives birth, it's just one child. That may have happened because the lady prayed that she doesn't want two children since she can't afford to take care of them both.

Ques. What attracted you to this show?

I always thought that if I were to host a television show, it would be something different. I didn't want to do the same old type of reality show where everyone is dancing and singing.

Ques. Do you believe in the supernatural?

I don't believe in ghosts, but I do believe in some things, like the power of prayer. I believe that there are some things which are unusual and which cannot be explained.

Ques. Are you superstitious in real life?

No, not at all.

Ques. You've been called the Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan of Indian television. How do you react to compliments like that?

I think it would be a real compliment if someone was called the Iqbal Khan of Indian movies.

Ques. You've been a model, a movie actor, an extremely successful television actor and now you're a TV show host. What's next on your agenda?

I'll take things as they come. I believe in doing one thing at a time. Right now I'm in a show called Waaris on Zee. Sambhav Kya takes up 3-4 days in a month, so I have plenty of leisure time.

Ques. Your show Waaris has been launched in other countries like the UK and the USA. What does that say about the success of the show?

It shows that serials with a different storyline, unlike like other regular shows, do work well.

Ques. How did you celebrate Eid?

I did not work on that day. The day started with the morning prayers. Then, after one month of no lunch at home, there was a grand meal. In the evening, we went out for dinner.

Heading: Chatter Box - Indian Express
Content:
Ek Khiladi Ek Haseena

Colors

Friday to Saturday, 9 pm

Rating**1/2

What's it about? Cricket is religion in India and reality shows have been a craze for some time now. When the two meet, what you get is great entertainment. Indian television actresses and famous cricketers will come into your drawing rooms every week and entertain you with their moves. The game only requires you to be a good dancer and whichever pair fails to grasp the attention of the judges and the viewers is eliminated.

Who's in it? The competition will have six pairs coupling an actress and a cricketer. The pairs are: S Sreesanth and Surveen Chawla; Harbhajan Singh and Mona Singh; Irfan Pathan and Ashima Bhalla; Dinesh Karthik and Nigar Z Khan; Nikhil Chopra and Barkha Bisht; and Vinod Kambli and Shama Sikander. Colors has roped in ex-Miss Universe Sushmita Sen and ex-Pakistani skipper Wasim Akram to judge the show. Sandhya Mridul who has made a comeback on television after quite long has been roped in to anchor the show.

What's hot? This may not be first time that we are seeing cricketers participate in a dance reality show (Remember, Ajay Jadeja in Jhalak Dikhla Ja) but for ardent cricket fans it is a delight to watch six of your favourite cricketers dance to the most popular film numbers. Kambli and Harbhajan with their sense of humour and lively attitude are an absolute delight on stage. Among the girls, Chawla and Mona Singh look well-trained for the job. And the chemistry between the 'Mallu superstar' Sreesanth and Chawla is eye-catching. Sen does a good job of commenting on the performance, while Akram has a wide grin pasted on his face. Nevertheless, both of them seem to be having a good time in each others company.

What's not? While most actresses come across as good dancers, it is the men in blue who disappoint a bit. While Pathan dances in a Robot mode (reminds us of Harman Baweja from Love Story 2050), Nikhil Chopra simply cannot get out of his bowling shoes. But Dinesh Karthik is by far the worst dancer and looks like he has at least three left feet. Although the concept is novel, there is nothing new in terms of strategy and set design. Dimly lit centre stage and tacky costumes take away from the freshness of the show.

Should you be watching it?After the Slapgate controversy, it is for the first time that Bhajji and Sreesanth will be facing each other. And this is a battle worth watching for cricket lovers. For the rest, it is an opportunity to witness a new game. On a different pitch, of course.

Heading: Mehrauli blast victim loses battle for life - Indian Express
Content:
TLC for Priya

Reality shows sure can be demanding. Priya Bhatija of Kasahm Se fame, who is to appear with boyfriend Jatin Shah, popular as Ronak of Kasturi, on Nach Baliye 4, fell sick during the promo shoot. She'd been diagnosed with malaria just a few days before and had also been admitted to hospital. But the brave girl still shot and danced for the entire day. But the gruelling session took its toll on her as she realised how important the show was and she broke down under the pressure. Luckily, Jatin was around to give support and some of her favourite chocolates. His love and care managed to calm Priya and she finished the shoot.

Strike again

Swapnil Joshi's loss was Annu Kapoor's gain. Due to the federation strike, the shoot of Chota Packet Bada Dhamaka had to be advanced. This led to a lot of last minute reshuffle in the schedule of the judges and host. While Annu, Kunal Kohli and Rakhi Sawant managed to make it for the shoot, Swapnil, who is the sutradhaar of the show, remained untraceable. While the production house was wondering who a replacement could be, Annu entered the sets. He immediately jumped to the thought of going back to his first love, anchoring.

Star power

Rakhi Sawant is such a strong believer in astrology that she has appointed a personal astrologer, Sri Acharya Hari Govind Tripathi, who is with her for all the shoots of Zee's Chhota Packet Bada Dhamaka. We have heard celebrities asking about their future, new ventures and films. But, Rakhi consults him for each and every scene that she is about to enact. From suggesting which outfits she should be wearing to the colour of the dresses for the particular shot to dialogue delivery, he advices her on everything. So now you know who is behind her success.

Negative is positive

Indu Verma aka Chanchal of Rajshri's Main Teri Parchhain Hoon is loving her character in the daily soap on NDTV Imagine. So what if it's a negative character. The actor is enjoying what she is doing. "I am playing a negative role for the first time and I am thoroughly enjoying it since it contradicts my real image." The NSD graduate started her small screen career with Achanak 37 Saal Baad and went on to do Awaz Dil se Dil Tak, Kabhie Aaye Na Judaai and Siddhant.

Heading: Delhi to help Himachal build three new dams - Indian Express
Content:
Three months ago, 24-year-old Ishtiaq Ansari came to Delhi from the small village of Sonadi in Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, with hopes of getting an MBA degree.

The first in his family to go to college — the youngster, who was injured in the Mehrauli blast, lost his battle for life on Sunday morning at AIIMS Trauma Centre.

Ansari's death takes the toll of the Mehrauli blast to three. While Santosh (9) had lost his life on the spot, Dipu (23) had succumbed to his injuries on Friday morning.

On the day of the blast, Ansari, along with friends Shyam Bahadur and Satyajeet Chaudhari, had gone to Mehrauli to shop for Eid. All three were first year students of Integrated Management College in Saket. The blast occurred as they were crossing the street near the Sarai Electronic Market.

Though all three were injured, Ansari's injuries turned out to be fatal. "He was almost dead when he was bought to the Trauma Centre," said Dr MC Mishra, Director, AIIMS Trauma Centre. He had suffered extensive head and abdomen injuries. "We operated upon him immediately. But the damage to his brain and kidneys was irreparable. The chances of his survival were very bleak," he added.

Son of a small trader, Ansari had come to Delhi after getting his BCom degree from Allahabad.

"My brother always wanted to study and do well. I still can't believe that he lost his life in a terror attack," said a shaken Saddam Hussein, Ansari's 17-year-old brother.

Upon hearing the news of the blast, Ansari's father Imtiaz Ansari had come to Delhi with his wife Ummat Begum. On Sunday, they headed back to Sonadi with their son's body.

"My parents are still in shock. They can't believe that their eldest son is gone, it will take some time for them to accept this fact," said Hussein.

As the news spread, Ansari's friends and professors assembled at AIIMS. "He was a good student, keen to learn and grow. Despite coming from a small town, he adjusted well to life in Delhi and would have surely gone on to do well," said his IT professor Raman Nath.

Ansari's friends described him as popular and kind. "It has just been three months since college started, but he was already one of the most popular juniors. He was always ready to lend a helping hand and had managed to integrate himself to college life," said Sujit Kumar, one of the senior students of the college.

Heading: Sharma’s death to hamper key cases in court - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to solve the city's water problems, the Delhi government has tied up with the Himachal Pradesh government to construct three dams in the Upper Yamuna.

The government has lobbied for three projects — the Renuka, Khishau and Lakhawar-Vyasi dams — that have been lying unimplmented with the Himachal Pradesh government .

Last week, the government sent Himachal Rs 200 crore as the first tranche of funds for the projects, which are to provide Delhi with over 400 Million Gallons per Day (MGD) water, said Delhi government officials. The funds are meant expressly for land acquisition.

"We needed the supply as the estimated population for the city is 24 million by the year 2012. Already, the present supply of water is inadequate," said Chief Secretary Delhi Rakesh Mehta.

Currently, Delhi consumes around 900 MGD — the figure is only bound to increase. Delhi is to receive 23,000 litres every second from this scheme through a gravity pipeline that would cross through Haryana. Experts estimate that over 24 hours, the city will get nearly 20 crore litres of additional drinking water from this scheme.

"We met the Himachal Pradesh Chief Secretary last month and all the plans were finalised then," Mehta said. The water will be brought directly to the Sonia Vihar treatment plant and be redistributed from there.

All three dams are to be undertaken by the Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL), an undertaking of the Himachal Pradesh government.

The dams were conceptualised and a plan was drawn up as far back as 1994. But the projects have been in cold storage for years.

"Intermittent attempts have been made to revive them. But the urgency came home with the impending Commonwealth Games. We have been lobbying to expedite the work and began the process seven months ago," said a senior government official.

"The Himachal government is currently working out the relief and rehabilitation packages for those who will be affected by the construction," said an official.

The Renuka Dam, located in Himachal Pradesh on the Giri river, will offer a storage capacity of 542 million cubic metres of water and an installed capacity of 40 MW of power. Of the three dams, Renuka has been expressly expedited for the Commonwealth Games. But there is no way it will be up and running before the Games begin, officials say. It would take at least five years to be operational.

Heading: After a 33-yr trial, man convicted at the age of 94 for cheating - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Cell of the Delhi Police will not feel the absence of Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma — who died recently in the Jamia Nagar encounter — where investigations are concerned alone, but also for several cases pending in courts which required his expertise. There are nearly 25 cases related to terrorism alone that are pending for trial. Newsline takes a look at a few of the cases that are at a crucial stage:

Diwali blasts

(October 29, 2005):

Three blasts had rocked Delhi — at Sarojini Nagar market, Paharganj and Kalkaji — killing 62 people and injuring 104. Based on phone intercepts collected by Sharma's team — the calls being made on November 1 and November 4 — one Tariq Ahmed Dar was arrested on November 10. On November 22, Mohammad Fazili and Mohmmad Rafiq Shah were arrested. The Special Cell claimed that Dar was the financier of the entire operation. Sharma's departure comes at a time when the prosecution is presenting evidence in the court. "It is the most crucial time. He (Sharma) used to follow the case closely, providing critical inputs to the prosecution lawyers," said an officer who was part of his team.

Arrest of Parvez Ahmed Radoo

(October 15, 2006)

One of the controversial cases, Radoo, a PhD student of Pune, was arrested. Three kilograms of RDX, Rs 10 lakh in cash and a communication code were recovered from him. According to the Special Cell, he was an operative of Jaish-e-Mohammed. The finance expert of the module, he was facilitating the transfer of money and explosives. Months after his arrest, Radoo sent a letter to the chief metropolitan magistrate, claiming that he was innocent. He also alleged that the Special Cell had detained him for over a month and tortured him. The case is currently being heard.

Murder of Arun Gupta (April 7, 2008)

Around 10.30 am, three men on a bike shot Arun Gupta in Kalkaji. Gupta's mother-in-law Kanta Devi Mittal was the owner of Mittal Garden, which Gupta had been trying to sell. The case was transferred to the Special Cell on April 10. Sharma's team cracked the case in a record three days and arrested Gupta's brother-in-law D K Mittal. On April 11, the team managed to trace calls that indicated that the accused were in Jamia. On April 13, the officers arrested Mittal. The men who had shot Gupta were Junaid, Zar and Shakeel. A chargesheet has been filed and the Cell was planning to file a supplementary chargesheet.

Arrest of Abdul Rehman alias Mohammad Iqbal (May 23, 2008):

Allegedly a Pak-trained HUJI militant, Mohd Iqbal alias Abdur Rehman was arrested from the New Delhi Railway Station. Rehman has been accused of harbouring Babu Bhai, who had been arrested by the Special Task Force of Uttar Pradesh for being an explosive supplier. Rehman had provided shelter to other key HUJI terrorists as well when he was a maulana at a mosque in south-west Delhi. The police also recovered 3 kg RDX, a timer device and five electronic detonators from Janakpuri's D-Block. The RDX, according to the police, had been buried. But questions were raised subsequently regarding the arrest and the recovery and the Special Cell had some tough questions to answer in the court. Rehman's family,

too, had questioned the entire operation.

Amar Singh's phone tapping case

(January 2006)

Sharma's team was assigned the sensational case of Amar Singh's phone tapping, which had created a political storm. On January 6, days after the complaint was filed, the team arrested Anurag Singh, an expert hacker, who held an MBBS degree. Anurag, who was running a detective agency, had allegedly tapped Amar Singh's phone. Police said Bhupender, the co-owner of the agency, was his aide. Together, they were planning to sell the tapes at a high price to Singh's political opponents. Kuldeep, a dispatch rider of Reliance Infocom, was also arrested. Trial in the case is pending.

Heading: Prankster cries ‘bomb’ at Gurgaon’s Ambience Mall - Indian Express
Content:
It was the last appearance of 94-year-old Hemchand Jain in court. His 33-year ordeal finally came to an end as a city court found him and his accomplice guilty in connection with a cheating case registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in 1978.

Brought to the courtroom in a stretcher owing to his inability to walk, Jain was sentenced to confinement till the court finished work for the day, along with his 75-year-old associate Rajkumar Jain.

The conviction came as the prosecution proved that the two defrauded the Delhi State Industrial Development Corporation (DSIDC). According to the CBI, they had received underhand commission from various cloth dealers by acting as purchase agents of the DSIDC.

With the trial dragging on, Hemchand and Rajkumar had recently pleaded guilty, so they could see the last of the case.

Handing down the sentence on September 17, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Kanwaljeet Arora held that there was "no justification" in imposing substantive punishment of a jail term for the two accused, who had reached at this stage "after traversing the tedious path of trial" after three decades.

"I am of the opinion that after undergoing this long-drawn ordeal, none of them will ever think of repeating the offence in future," he said.

Granting them respite based on modern criminal jurisprudence advocating the theory of reformation in certain cases, the court found substance in their plea regarding clean antecedents.

The court, however, struck a balance between reformation and deterrence, saying that though the punishment of imprisonment was not called for against the convicts, they should be taught a lesson for their wrongdoing.

Noting that the imposition of monetary penalty shall meet the ends of justice, the judge slapped a fine of Rs 2 lakh on each convict for cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy.

After the fine was paid, around 4.15 pm, Hemchand and Rajkumar were released — not only from the lawful detention but also the excruciating trial that had kept them in knots for over three decades.

Heading: Killer roads of Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Sunday evening's events at the Ambience Mall, one of Asia's longest malls, is a perfect example of the disturbance a hoax bomb call can cause.

The call came at 6.10 pm to the security personnel. The caller said a bomb has been planted in a car inside the parking lot and that there were two men roaming inside the mall who would detonate it soon.

The security guards immediately began their drill for evacuating visitors, shop owners and employees, said Yogender, one of the security personnel.

"We informed the police too and they were quick to arrive. By that time, we had evacuated a considerable portion of the mall," he said.

The entry point was closed. Every person was thoroughly frisked at the exit points and every vehicle leaving the mall was checked to make sure that there was no risk.

"We were asked to vacate the premises around 6.15 pm. There was no time even to lock the cash in the safe. We just had had to walk out," said Gopi, an employee at Cookie Man.

According to the Mohinder Lal, the Commissioner of Police, Gurgaon, the Control Room received the call about the bomb at 6.30 pm. "We immediately deployed teams and started evacuating the area as a precautionary measure. We are carrying out the regular drill," said Lal.

The police cordoned off the entire stretch between the first exit after the toll plaza (from Delhi) till Shankar Chowk.

Namita Pandey, a resident of Delhi, said: "After the recent blasts in Delhi this was the first time that my husband and I had gathered enough courage to step out of the house on a weekend. I was tempted by the discounts offered by many outlets and wanted to try out retail therapy. Just when we thought things were getting back to normal, comes this call. The scar would take time to heal."

Addressing the media inside the Mall, Joint Commissioner of Police Manjeet Singh Ahlawat said: "We have not found any suspicious object. Our team is still searching and we have deployed our bomb squad. As of now, it seems the work of some prankster. But we are not taking it lightly and are investigating the matter to find out the exact details."

The CP said the mall would resume function as soon as the routine drill was over. No arrests have been made. But vigil at other important places in the city has been stepped up.
