Heading: Five witnesses come forward in Soumya murder case; police yet to make headway - Indian Express
Content:
When Ram Kali went to local a doctor last year complaining of abdominal pain, she had little idea the treatment would turn out to be a long-drawn ordeal, damaging both her kidneys in the end.

In March 2006, Ram Kali visited the OP Nursing Home, run by one Dr A K Handa, because of pain in the right side of her abdomen. The doctor suggested surgery and a Ureteroscopy was performed the next day, after which Ram Kali was discharged from the nursing home.

She, however, still complained of severe pain, for which Handa gave her some painkillers and performed another surgery a month later. But her condition continued to deteriorate. She went to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), where tests revealed her kidneys had stopped functioning.

The doctor's decision at OP Nursing Home, however, proved costly for him, as Ram Kali then approached the District Consumer Forum seeking redress. The forum has directed the nursing home and Handa to pay Rs 7 lakh to Ram Kali as compensation, keeping in consideration her "life-long suffering".

The doctor argued that since the X-Ray report at the time showed no abnormality, he had no other alternative to find out the real cause of the pain. He said that after visiting AIIMS, Ram Kali stayed at home for some days without any medical advice, resorting to Ayurvedic medicines that might have led to her present condition. The forum refuted his claims and observed that Ram Kali's condition had deteriorated due to faulty treatment.

"We have no hesitation in holding that Dr Handa at OP Nursing Home resorted to Ureteroscopy in haste and did not bother to find out the cause of pain. Instead, he resorted to administering antibiotics and painkillers, which are known toxic elements for the functioning of kidneys. The evidence as such clearly makes out a case of medical negligence and deficiency in service on his part," the forum stated.

The nursing home and Handa are now liable to pay the compensation within a month of receiving the order. "We received the order this Friday and the district forum has given us a month's time to appeal to a higher body. We will appeal in the State Consumer Forum against the order," Handa told Newsline.

Ganga Ram to pay Rs 25,000 in 1992 case

Slamming Ganga Ram Hospital for "detaining" a patient for hours due to the non-clearance of medical bills, the Delhi Consumer Commission in a recent order has directed the hospital to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation. Commission president, Justice J D Kapoor, held the hospital guilty of deficiency in service for keeping Vandana Gupta "hostage" on account of bill clearance in March 1992. Vandana, admitted there for child delivery, was not discharged as her husband sought to shift her to a different hospital for better treatment.

Heading: 4 injured in clash outside cop’s home - Indian Express
Content:
After the Delhi Police's appeal to eyewitnesses to come forward for helping with the investigations of the murder of TV journalist Soumya Vishwanathan on Nelson Mandela Marg on September 30, five people have stepped forward as witnesses to the incident.

But the police are yet to make headway in the case, with the cops still puzzled over the motive behind the murder.

"All witnesses who have come forward were at the spot of the crime after the murder. There are no accounts of what happened at the time of the murder. We are now asking residents of the Vasant Kunj area to help us with the investigations. A picket has also been set up on the road to stop vehicles passing by and ascertain whether any of them had travelled on that road on the night of the murder," a senior police officer said.

The first witness is an employee of Punjabi by Nature, who was on his way home when he spotted Soumya Vishwanathan's Zen car rammed into a divider on Nelson Mandela Marg. The second witness was a taxi driver who was passing by when the restaurant janitor flagged him down for help.

The third witness claimed that he was travelling on the road when he heard a gunshot, but he did not stop. The other two eyewitnesses have revealed that they saw the car and two men standing near it. Police suspect that these witnesses had seen the janitor and the taxi driver outside the car.

"Another witness, who works as a bouncer at a nearby hotel, has also approached us. He claimed that on the night before the murder, he had witnessed a road rage incident. They may be unrelated, but we are taking no chances," a senior police officer said.

Police said they are reconstructing the chain of events on that fateful night, starting from the CCTV footage obtained from her office parking lot. At present police know that after her shift at 3 am, Soumya left office in her Zen car and was headed home on Nelson Mandela Marg to C-Block, Vasant Kunj. Soumya had last spoken to her father at 3.15 am and her body was discovered at 3.30 am.

Just one bullet had been fired from a country-made weapon, which was found lodged on the right side of her head.

Heading: MCD planning dog centres to control stray numbers - Indian Express
Content:
A group of people in an inebriated state created a ruckus outside the house of a Delhi Police constable in the Alipur area of West Delhi on Saturday evening.

The police said a clash that followed between the constable's relatives and the miscreants left four people injured. Nine people have been arrested in connection with the incident.

Police officers said the incident was reported around 7.30 pm. Seven people in a drunken state were creating a commotion outside Constable Rajender Singh's house in Palla Village in Alipur. "Constable Singh, posted with the PCR division of Northwest Delhi, was not present at home. His son, Pradeep, went outside to enquire and when he saw the miscreants, he asked them to stop the ruckus and go elsewhere. The miscreants then attacked him without warning and started beating him up," a senior police officer said.

The police said Pradeep's brother Sanjeev and other relatives came out to stop the commotion and their neighbours also joined in. Soon, the matter went out of control as the two groups started pelting stones at each other. They also clashed with each other, the police said.

A bystander called the PCR. The police rushed the four injured to the Hari Chand Hospital in Narela. They were discharged after first aid, the police said. "After that we placed seven men under arrest. We also arrested two neighbours of Constable Singh, among them a woman. Other than these two, Vimla and Surender Kumar, the rest are 'history-sheeters' and have been arrested before for similar crimes," a senior officer said.

Heading: Cops search for men who stabbed reporter - Indian Express
Content:
After several unsuccessful attempts towards the sterilisation of stray dogs, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) now plans to set up "Dog Care Centres" across the city.

These centres will function like day care dog hospitals. Apart from sterilisation, these centres will also ensure regular vaccination and will act like adoption centres.

Going by MCD records, 27,199 dogs have been sterilised till May this year. And the corporation is hopeful that after these centres are opened, it will be able to hasten the entire process.

Currently, the MCD outsources the sterilisation programme. "We have been carrying out sterilisation through various NGOs and the department does not have any count of stray dogs. Till date, the counting of strays has not been taken up professionally. But these centres will ensure we have an area-wise dog count," MCD Standing Committee Chairman Vijendar Gupta said.

The MCD approached the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) for the allotment of land but has not received any satisfactory response yet. "We had written to the DDA about a year ago but have not received any positive response from them. They have not taken our file seriously," Gupta said.

He said that if they get enough support from the government they would be able to hasten the process.

"We will initially set up four centres in East, West, North and South Delhi. The East Delhi site has been identified in Karawal Nagar," MCD Commissioner KS Mehra said.

The centre is expected to be operational by the end of this year. It will not only take care of stray dogs but will have a facility for pets as well.

Depending on the need of the area, the MCD will take these centres to the zonal level. "We will have a separate budget and staff for the dog centres from next year. We are hopeful the city will be free of them before the Commonwealth Games," Gupta said.

Heading: City pandals step up security ahead of Puja - Indian Express
Content:
Saurabh Mishra (27), a sports reporter with Zee News, was stabbed in a robbery bid on Saturday night. The police said four assailants, including an autorickshaw driver, attacked him in a bid to snatch his mobile phone.

"I was walking towards my home on the slip road near the Defence Colony flyover, when an autorickshaw stopped in front of me. Three men got out and pretended to be busy talking to each other. When I passed them by they tried to snatch my mobile phone. I resisted and one of them stabbed me," Mishra said.

Police officers said the incident was reported around 9.35 pm. They said Mishra had left office in Film City in Noida's Sector-16A in his office cab. The cab had dropped him near the Andrews Ganj bus stop and he was walking home when the incident took place.

The officers said that while he was being attacked, another autorickshaw driver was passing by and the passenger inside came to Mishra's aid. The assailants then scrambled back into the auto and escaped. The police said nobody took down the registration number of the autorickshaw.

After the attack, Mishra reportedly tried to follow the assailants but they managed to escape. He went to the police station and registered a complaint.

"We rushed him to AIIMS, where he was discharged after first aid. We have registered a case against unknown people and are on the lookout for them," a senior police officer said.

In August earlier this year, an autorickshaw driver, along with two accomplices, snatched Rs 2.58 lakh from a family in the Red Fort area.

Heading: Delhi underground - Indian Express
Content:
The five-day Durga Puja festivities began on Sunday with Maha-shashti. Newsline did a survey of major pandals in the city and found that on the first day of Puja, most pandals in the city saw heavy security arrangements.

C R PARK (Kali Mandir)

The famous Kali Mandir in C R Park is an important centre of convergence during Durga Puja. This year, special arrangements have been made for security with Delhi Police, Civil Defence and Home Guard personnel stationed at the temple. Six CCTV cameras have been installed at various points in the temple. Sniffer dogs are also being used for the first time.

"The temple is elevated, which provides it with a natural boundary. We have also taken care to ensure there are two separate entries for residents and the general public," Anita Haldar, reception committee co-convenor at Kali Mandir, said.

C R PARK (K BLOCK)

The pandal at K block, famous for winning the award for best idol the last three years in a row, has chosen a historical theme from Harappa and Mohenja-Daro to do up its idols. Security arrangements here include personnel from the Delhi Police and private security guards. Four machans have been set up at four points of the pandal. In addition to barricades, there are separate entries for residents and the general public, with a separate exit. Provision has also been made for an emergency exit, along with a special entry for VIPs.

C R PARK (B BLOCK)

Security has been tightened at the B block pandal with more than 125 private security guards and more than 50 personnel of the Delhi Police. "Apart from eight CCTV cameras, four machans have also been set up in the four corners of the pandal," Inspector Sanjay Kumar Singh said. Besides the main entry, there are separate entries for volunteers and vendors.

Significantly, this year the Durga Puja committee of B Block has decided not to call any crowd pulling celebrities. "We have called performers from Kolkata instead to avoid any rush beyond our capacity," Ashim Banerjee, organising committee president, said.

MINTO ROAD PUJA SAMITI

"We have made security arrangements as per the crowd expected and will strengthen the arrangements if more people come in," Duty Officer Bodh Raj said. Security has been reinforced with a machan opposite the main gate, 10 CCTV cameras, four hand-held metal detectors and two doorframe detectors. There are two points for entry and exit, with an emergency exit also in place. "We have invited ex-contestants from the Sare Ga Ma Pa music show and performers from Kolkata," D K Bose, samiti president, said.

Heading: Half of elders in Delhi harassed by children for property: Survey - Indian Express
Content:
Number crunching

Congress leaders might have gathered to present a picture of unity and send across a common message at the rally organised to push the government's initiative for regularising unauthorised colonies in the Capital, but they need to do their math and agree on the number of colonies to be regularised as part of the initiative. Addressing the thin number of spectators who turned up for the rally, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit said 1,300 to 1,400 colonies would be regularised; while Union Urban Development Minister Jaipal Reddy put the number at 1,500. Dashing the hopes of those who came to the rally on a sultry afternoon, UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi's total was a dismal 1,200.

The high road

VIPs in the city, it seems, have finally realised that their "movement" on the Capital's roads can be a problem for the rest of us. Sheila Dikshit had earlier pioneered this cause by inaugurating flyovers electronically (while sitting in the Secretariat building). Now, Sonia Gandhi too has followed suit. On her way to Chhatrasal Stadium, where she addressed a Delhi government rally on Saturday, she flew in an helicopter from Safdarjung Airport and landed at Old Police lines, instead of using the road.

Me and my BMW

Villages neighbouring Gurgaon used to register one of the highest incidents of cattle theft in the district till a few months ago. The figures, however, witnessed a sharp decline recently. Upon investigation, one of the most important reasons the administration discovered was that where earlier there used to be cattle tied in front of every house, there are BMWs parked now! Officials say that an average of 10 luxury cars are registered in the area each month.

Pet-ty issues

The Bunty gang, infamous for the murders it committed, affected animals too. During the Delhi Police's hunt for Bunty in August, an IPS officer posted in the South district and involved in the investigations ended up losing his pet — a dog — as he couldn't pay attention to his well being. "I couldn't take care of my dog even when I was told he was sick and hadn't been keeping well. I was so busy with the Bunty case that I realised it only after he died," the officer said. "I decided to present my daughter with a dog then."

Hard times

After issuing half-page advertisements in national dailies and inviting tenders from private players for the running of super-specialty hospitals in Tahirpur and Janakpuri, the Delhi government has left the deal hanging. The government had already purchased equipment, appointed a medical superintendent and even hired Class IV staff but has not been able to find anyone to run the hospital. Rumour has it that a certain private player had showed willingness, but backed out at the last minute, as it had already suffered huge losses in the share market.

In power

Tariff hikes during election season do not bode well for any government. Recently, the BSES tariff hike case was adjourned by the Appellate Tribunal of Electricity to November 19, right in the middle of the pre-election period. Now, senior officials in the power department indicate that efforts will be made to get another adjournment when the next hearing comes up, as the current state government can ill afford the hike right before the elections. Power hikes are not always good for those in power.

Yes minister

When the witness is someone like Samajwadi Party General Secretary Amar Singh, even the court staff goes out of its way to keep things smooth during the hearing. As Singh sought adjournment from recording his statement against a man who allegedly tried to extort money from him, a police officer assisting the court as the naib court hurriedly asked the judge to give a date in December. Enraged, the defence counsel reminded the judge that the cop had no business to seek dates for the leader, as he was only there to help the prosecution and not the witnesses. Deciding to not escalate matters, the judge told the counsel he had not even heard what the naib court said and deferred the matter to December after making inquiries from the SP leader.

Hostile witness

Used to discussing "hostile witnesses" and their adverse impact on trials, a TV reporter realised what it feels like to be tagged as one. He earned the label after an interesting turn of events. The reporter had covered a case of alleged rape three years ago and received a summon to appear as a prosecution witness. The investigating officer asked him to recount the event and read his statement, which, according to him, was never recorded. When questioned by the prosecutor, he failed to narrate the facts, saying he had covered a number of such stories in his career. The court then declared him as "hostile". Coming out of the court, he said: "Now I realise how it feels when declared a hostile witness."

Booked out

The All India Publishers' Union, Indian Regional Journalists' Association and some other groups have threatened to hold a demonstration outside the National Book Trust office in Vasant Kunj to protest against the failure of the government and the trust to aid private publishers and organisers of book fairs. Rivalry amongst publishers and private organisers of book fairs and the trust has led to filing of complaints and attempts to block the public body from conducting book fairs. The grievance of the private organisers is that most of the funds (crores of rupees) sanctioned by the trust go into the pockets of officials and the public body intentionally organises book fairs in cities where private or non-governmental bodies already hold fairs. This reduces the profit margin for private book fairs. In addition, they complained that funds released by the Ministry of Human Resource Development for the aid of privately organised book fairs are handed out to fictional NGOs and pocketed by the officials of the trust which is authorised to disburse this money.

Hard PILs to swallow

Frivolous public interest litigation (PILs) is an occupational hazard at the Delhi High Court. The latest is a one-page petition demanding the High Court rap the police for "security lapses" that caused the September 13 blasts. Vehemently denying that his intention is to hog the limelight, the counsel made an emotional appeal to the sceptical court: "Your Lordships, this is a fit case to intervene. I can prove it. The blasts are caused by foreign immigrants in disguise. The security situation in Delhi is poor." The Bench's retort: "May be a better thing to do is order the bomb blasts to stop immediately. Case dismissed."

Heading: Reproduction Line - Indian Express
Content:
Almost half of the elderly owning property in their names in the national capital are harassed by their kith and kin, a study claimed in New Delhi.

"Fortynine per cent of elderly with property in their names are being harassed by their own children and also the in-laws of their children," a survey by NGO HelpAge India said.

Rest of the senior citizens were victimised by landlords, neighbours and civic bodies it said, adding that "maximum cases of abuse were from affluent colonies of the city".

However, only 44 per cent of those facing harassment have reported the matter to the police and bulk of those who have not lodged complaints, are afraid of the abusers, said the study based on the sample survey conducted in the national capital.

Other reasons cited by the elderly for not taking the ordeal to the police being their emotional dependence on their children and their wish to "preserve family honour".

"There is also a distinct lack of faith in the police and legal system and physical frailty becomes a constraint," the study observed.

"With urbanisation and industrialisation spreading to all segments of the society, real estate value has shot up.

New issues and problems have cropped up as a result. One such is abuse of older people for property," the study said.

Elders come under intense pressure to either sell off their property or transfer ownership to their sons or daughters and are subjected to various forms of abuse if they refuse.

"The dependency factor emerges very strongly in the cases of property disputes. Most of those being harassed are dependent on their children. Those who are able to support themselves are empowered enough to turn around and quash such demands," the study noted.

Heading: Shall We Dance? - Indian Express
Content:
Can't afford an original canvas? Grab a signed serigraph or a giclee print

It is not often that the first lady of Indian art dons the role of a curator, but when she does, Anjolie Ela Menon never fails to surprise. So as guests gushed over Tyeb Mehta's Woman on Rickshaw and FN Souza's Head at the Taj Mahal Hotel, it took Menon to tell them that the works were not original, but digital reproductions on canvas.

"They are so close to the original that it is difficult to distinguish," says Menon, as she recollects two years of hard work that went into the exhibition "Kalpana: Masterpieces of Figurative Indian Painting". It had reproductions of two figurative works each by 14 Indian artists, including Jamini Roy, Amrita Sher-Gil, Krishen Khanna and Manjit Bawa. "With the reproductions, we intend to reach out to a global audience," says Menon, who has handed over five sets of the 28 reproductions to the Indian Council for Cultural Relations to display at their centres world over. Menon, who had sourced the original canvases from private galleries, the National Gallery of Modern Art and artists' studios, admits that exhibiting them would have cost a lot more money and energy.

This was a one-off project for Menon, but for several others in the Indian art mart, serigraphs that involves silk-screen printing, offset reproductions and computer-aided giclee prints are commonplace stuff.

"They make art affordable. Those who cannot buy the original can opt for high-quality, signed serigraphs," says Parul Vadehra, director, Vadehra Art Gallery. Walk into her bookstore at Defence Colony and suspended on the walls are limited-edition serigraphs of Paramjit Singh and offsets prints of canvases by MF Husain, Ram Kumar and A Ramachandran, all priced at Rs 20,000 onwards. Vagabond, the 1956 oil on board by Ram Kumar, was sold for over $1 million at the Christie's New York auction in March, but Vadehra has its signed, offset print on sale for Rs 30,000. "These are limited-edition and numbered. The prices tend to multiple over the years," notes Vadehra.

Atit Trivedi, manager of Ahmedabad-based Archer Group, agrees. In the mid 1990s, his group arguably introduced India to serigraphs with reproductions of canvases from Husain's Madhuri-Maqbool series priced at Rs 1,000-2,000. His website is now selling serigraphs of Husain's Jaisalmer series for Rs 85,000, but in the Bonhams auction in 2006 it sold for over Rs 1 lakh. "The connoisseurs are a little sceptical about reproductions but the interest is gradually growing," notes Trivedi, who witnessed a sale of above Rs 5 lakh at the recent India Art Summit.

Lavesh Jagasia of The Serigraph Studio, whose portfolio comprises serigraphs of artists like Jogen Chowdhury, SH Raza, Lalu Prasad Shaw and Ganesh Haloi, is now gearing up to add six more serigraphs of Jehangir Sabavala to the set of 18 released last year. Titled The Complete Collection, the set will be priced at about Rs 29 lakh and released at the Seoul International Art Fair this month. "The artists are involved at every stage, from choosing the work to giving the nod of approval before the serigraph is exhibited," says Jagasia who is planning to rope in younger Indian artists for the Dubai chapter of The Serigraph Studio.

Meanwhile, international artists are calling on India with their reproductions. An exhibition by The Fuschia Tree that is currently on at The Attic, Connaught Place, has on display giclee prints of works by UK-based Van Renselar, Peru's Jose De La Barra and Dane Willers from Botswana, among others. If the original 32 x 42 inch Willers canvas Elephant Bull is available for Rs 2.6 lakh, the 16 x 24 inch unsigned print is priced at Rs 7,875. "People may not be familiar with international artists but there is curiosity and the response is encouraging. These are ideal for those looking for reasonably priced art for their homes or offices," says Chanda Chaudhary Barrai from Fuschia.

Tripat Kalra, director of Gallerie Nvya, notes that serious art collectors too have reproductions in their portfolio. Last year, her gallery released 30 sets of six serigraphs by Goan artist Viraj Naik, priced at Rs 20,000.

Though Menon is slightly apprehensive about allowing printers to convert her acrylics into pixels, Husain has given a go-ahead to Trivedi to release a scroll serigraph of his work Horses and Mother. "This will be released next year," says Trivedi. The days when prints meant replicas on fragile sheets of paper are over.

Heading: Kubrick’s Robe - Indian Express
Content:
With a rendition of The Three Musketeers and classical choreographies, the annual Ananya Dance Festival promises to be as entertaining as ever

At the Chennai home of Kuchipudi nattuvanar Jai Kishore Mosalikanti, last-minute rehearsals are in full swing. The artist himself is away on a day-long workshop, but five of his disciples are undergoing rigorous practice sessions with his wife and fellow performer Vani Kishore. "Since it will be our first group appearance in Delhi, we have decided to put up our most recent piece of choreography that is replete with traditional references to literature, drama and classical poetry. It showcases the best of our tradition with as much individualism as possible," says Vani, in between practice sessions.

The Kishores' performance will be part of the seventh annual Ananya Festival, organised by the city-based NGO Seher. With the five-day fest set to take off at the Purana Quila on October 11, a handful of the country's leading classical dancers are headed towards the Capital. There will be Bharatnatyam by Kalakshetra, Chennai's famed troupe and Odissi by Durga Charan Ranbir and his group, besides performances by relative newcomers like Kathak dancer Malti Shyam and Mohiniyattam artist Jayaprabha Menon. "Performing at Ananya is a coveted offer since it's a wonderful platform to connect with fellow artistes and an audience interested in your art. I have formulated my choreography in such a way that even people who are not clued into the technical aspects of dance can relate to the strong emotional content of the performance," says Shyam, whose performance will close the festival. One of the highlights will be the dance-theatre rendition of Alexander Dumas' famous novel The Three Musketeers by Leela Samson and her troupe on the opening day of the festival.

Sanjeev Bhargava, festival director, plans to have an open symposium with the performers at the Alliance Francaise on October 13 and 14. "With each passing year, the audience has become more sensitised to different kinds of performances, but the dynamics of a performance or the semantics of a choreography are still alien to them. So we thought we would keep a forum for people to come and listen to the choreographers," says Bhargava. Entry to the festival is free, like every year.

Heading: Kiwi Flight - Indian Express
Content:
Prashant Verma's new collection is inspired by 2001: A Space Odyssey and his models will walk to JFK's speech on space mission

After his collection "Giant" brought together Hollywood and Mumbai in its billowy dresses and boxy jackets, designer Prashant Verma has gone for a futuristic look with robots, lunar surfaces and clean geometrical patterns. His new collection "Point of Man" for the forthcoming India Fashion Week even owes an acknowledgment to Stanley Kubrick in its unmistakable overtones of the film 2001: A Space Odyssey.

The 23-year-old designer, who surprises as much with his insouciance as with his playful use of colour and form, says, "The focus is not too much on the market or the audience. I have come to a point where I feel I have to do something substantial in my work and for my satisfaction." The nonchalance continues. Though Verma counts Dr David Bowman, the protagonist of Kubrick's epic masterpiece, as his muse, he discounts any inspiration from international designers.

There is more surprise in store. The models will walk down the runway to excerpts of John F Kennedy's speech on the space mission. On the ramp will be unisex trousers, a severe ivory dress with geometrical patterns, yards of chiffon with prints of marbled surfaces of Jupiter and a crushed, black asymmetrical shirt paired with billowy shoulder sleeves. Unlike, his earlier palette of hot and cold colours, Verma's use of hues is controlled this time. "I have used white along with cobalt blue and orange. The palette is muted," he says.

Heading: Back in Business - Indian Express
Content: George Fistonich does not fly out of New Zealand on a whim. The 70-year-old, who is behind the Villa Maria winery that is hailed as one of the 50 greatest wineries of the world by Wine Spectator, travels only to those countries where his wine is sold. Fistonich, therefore, had a reason to visit India: the New Zealand high commissioner was celebrating one year of Villa Maria wines in the country. "I am glad the wines are doing well here," says Fistonich, who set up the Villa Maria wine estate in Marlborough in 1961 and earned recognition with his very first vintage (1962). There are only five wines in India — the Cellar Selection Sauvignon Blanc 2007, Cabernet Sauvignon 2006, Riesling 2007, Seddon Pinot Gris 2006, and Villa Reserve Pinot Noir 2006 — but the Kiwi says he does not believe in flooding the market. "We do not want to create a confusion in the consumer's mind by putting too many wines in the market. First, we want to study the response," he says over a glass of red.

Heading: Pet subject - Indian Express
Content:
Little Toe-Tappers

Sunday witnessed 10 brilliantly gifted kids battling it out at the Grand Finale of Hallmark Kids Idol – Dance Your Way Through, where children between the age group of 7-13 got a chance to display their burgeoning talent. The vigorous competition had started with the free audition round in 11 schools and four dance institutes where 1,150 kids auditioned. After a host of grueling preliminary rounds, eliminations and training programmes, to witness the performance of the finest. Vaishnavi Patil was the winner and Abhinav Jha and Aboli Naik were the runner ups.

Bejewelled

It was an evening of designs and designer wears as Krsala, a jewellery store by Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri was opened in the city. The store was inaugurated by actress Vidya Balan, who sported the best of designs from the store. The models shimmered on the ramp with a range of designs while Balan scintillated the audience in a saree with the unique jewellery piece. The evening saw other guests including MP Suresh Kalmadi and Achla Sachdev admire the collection. Diamonds and gems in amazing designs lit the night to glory.

Gold-en moment

Ushering in the festival of lights in a truly sparkling manner, Ranka Jewellers inaugurated its new diamond department. Apart from their various separate exclusive departments for gold, silver, pearls, american diamonds, precious stones and sunglasses, Ranka Jewellers opened Glitterati today. The posh diamond department at Laxmi Road, will have cut and rose cut diamonds as well as Indo-western designs on display. The diamond jewellery is certified by international standards and has a photo of each ornament on the certificate with the grade and quality of the diamond weight. As part of the celebrations, Ranka Jewellers will present an inaugural offer. No deduction in diamond and gold value will be made while exchanging the ornaments and 90 per cent cash will be paid on the value of the diamond ornaments, excluding labour charges.

Divine dining

The swish set of Pune came out in droves to witness and experience the art of Gastronomy which has been explored, enhanced, and evolved with Impresario Entertainment & Hospitality Private Limited newest vision, Stone Water Grill.

Riyaaz Amlani along with Amit Bhosale mingled and played gracious hosts to a select gathering of Pune's elite crowd. The team of creative minds behind this venture has achieved landmarks in the business of Hospitality with multi-award winning counterparts Salt Water Grill in Mumbai and Smoke House Grill in Delhi. Now, they have brought their new milestone exclusively to Pune.

Inspired by the elements, Stone Water Grill is a landscape which has been carefully coaxed into a Fine dine restaurant and a bar lounge. The 'Place' offers varied table experiences for the guests both in the bar/lounge and fine dine setting. it has a dining area for 70 people, 3 Private Dining areas for groups of 8-20 and a private party area for more than 100 people.

Seen congratulating the duo were Meera and Suresh Kalmadi, Natasha and Adar Poonawala, Michelle and Yohan Poonawala, Timmy Narang and Isha Koppikar, Malini and Dileep Vengsarkar, Kedar Gawde, Prameet Kotak, Hemant Thakker, Rizwan Amlani, Vickrant Chowgule, Neelam and Anil Seolekar, Sejal and Prasanna Firodia, Avinash Bhosale, Sunita and Baba Kalyani, Maushmi and Honaji Sanas,Gauri Naiknaware, Masumeh Makhija, Sumer Kalmadi among many others.

Heading: Passport theft: 2 yrs on, ‘kingpin’ held - Indian Express
Content:
Samwartak Singh took charge as the new Director Public Instructions (Schools) last week after much speculation. Though his name was proposed earlier when S K Setia, the former DPI, was all set to go in July, Singh had to wait for sometime before assuming office.

Singh was, meanwhile, given charge as municipal secretary, Municipal Corporation (MC) UT. "It is all part of the job. If not the Education department, I was working for the MC. I believe in giving my best to whatever I do, no matter what the department or the post is," he says.

Singh has many plans up his sleeves to improve the Education department and his focus areas include infrastructure and mid-day meals.

"Schools based in slum areas are deficient in proper infrastructure, which is essential for providing a conducive environment. Improving the quality of mid-day meals and Sarv Shiksha Abhiyaan too, is on the top priority list," says Singh.

During his tenure, Singh will also focus on instilling moral values in students. "We need to infuse good manners and principles in children so as to make them better human beings. In view of materialism prevalent in the society, it becomes all the more important and I will stress on this," he says.

Asked if he will be as media savvy as his predecessor, a quick reply comes, "Not really. Since I believe more in practical work, my focus will be on my work."

He, however, urges the media fraterinty to support him in his causes. "Since they are capable of generating change in society, I expect journalists to discharge their duties responsibly. I will try to be in touch with them if the situation demands," says the DPI (S).

On his views regarding Setia's unaccomplished plans, Singh says: "It all depends on how suitable the plans are. After consultation, if my seniors say that they are apt, I will definitely work on them."

Regarding his equation with Setia, he says: "We are very good friends. But I would not like to get into personal details," he says.

"Samwartak means the first ray of sun that falls on the earth when a new era starts. It was christened by a local priest at Hashimara, West Bengal, where I was born," concludes the DPI (S) as he explains the meaning of his name.

Heading: ‘My aim will be to instill moral values in children’ - Indian Express
Content:
The alleged kingpin of the 'passport theft' case, Gurjinder Singh alias Lucky (34) was finally arrested by the Crime Branch of Chandigarh Police in Kapurthala on Sunday.

Lucky, a resident of Kapurthala, was absconding since the last seven months, ever since the first suspect was arrested in the case in March 2008. More than a dozen accused, including Lucky's father, relatives, friends and two employees of the Regional Passport Office, Chandigarh, have already been arrested since the theft was discovered in October 2006.

Police say Lucky was first arrested while trying to cross over to Austria from Italy on a fake visa and deported back to India in 2004. A Jalandhar-based travel agent had taken lakhs of rupees from his family to send him abroad.

"After his return, Lucky adopted the same method to earn quick money and started working as a commission agent for travel agents. Later, he became a professional travel agent himself. In connivance with RPO employees, he got 48 passports stolen from the passport office," said a police officer.

Preliminary investigation has found that Lucky and his accomplices charged an average of Rs 9.5 lakh from an aspirant for arranging a passport, visa and other relevant papers. l Lucky's crime file

A notorious criminal, wanted by Delhi and Amritsar Police. Seven criminal cases on charges of cheating, forgery, fraud, criminal conspiracy and human trafficking registered against him at Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi. Three criminal cases on similar charges pending trial at Raja Saansi

International Airport, Amritsar. Cases also registered against him at Kapurthala City police station, Sector-34 police station, Chandigarh.

* Modus operandi

Lucky's cousin Bhupinder Singh, who lived in Belgium, was arrested on September 30. Another cousin Tejinder Singh alias Lovely, who stays in Italy, is also wanted in the racket. Both used to come to India with fake work-permits for the aspirants, whom Lucky had allured. Dummy interviews used to be conducted by the trio, which charged lakhs of rupees for sending the people abroad.

* 32 of 48 stolen passports yet

to be recovered

"Only 16 of the 48 stolen passports have been recovered. During interrogation, Lucky claimed that he had used six of the passports for sending people abroad. In all, Lucky claims to have sent around 45 persons abroad on fake passports or fake work permits in the last three years," said Sub-Inspector Hardit Singh, Incharge of the Cyber Cell, Crime Branch.

Heading: 17-year-old gangrape victim says accused tried to force her into prostitution - Indian Express
Content:
Two youths allege assault by four policemen in custody

The police asked us to urinate on each other, forced us to stand with our slippers in our mouth and brutally assaulted us in custody at the Sector-39 police station" — alleged two persons, arrested for their involvement in a group clash in Dadumajra on October 2.

In a complaint to the UT Administrator, UT Inspector General and Senior Superintendent of Police, their counsel advocate Mohinder Singh stated that four police personnel — identified as Sub-Inspector Pargat Singh (Incharge, Police Post, Maloya), Constables Sher Singh, Ajmer Singh and Sumit Kumar —meted out "inhuman treatment" to his clients.

On October 3, Chandigarh Police arrested four Dadumajra residents — Ravinder alias Tinda, Monu, Salman and Ramesh — on charges of vandalism and setting a motorcycle on fire.

Two of the accused, Monu and Ravinder (the complainants), were released on bail the same day while Salman and Ramesh are still in jail as they could not furnish their bail bonds.

Alleging false implication and demanding legal action against the police personnel, the two accused stated in their complaint:

"We surrendered at the Sector-39 police station around 8 am and the police registered a criminal case — FIR number 550 — under Sections 147, 148, 149, 341, 435, 506 of the IPC against the four of us."

"We were lodged in a room adjoining the bathroom by S-I Pargat Singh. There, he and the constables misbehaved with us. First, they thrashed us mercilessly and then asked us to stand with our slippers in our mouth. We refused but they beat us again and forcibly put the slippers in our mouth. We stood like that for two to three hours. Around 6 pm, S-I Pargat Singh instructed us to urinate in each others' mouth. Again, we refused. Later, he brought his own urine in a glass and made us swallow it. He also threatened to parade us naked in our colony."

Flatly denying all allegations, S-I Pargat Singh said: "Nothing of that sort occurred. They are unnecessarily levelling such allegations against me as I am the Investigating Officer in the case. They were medically examined as well. Why didn't they raise their voice then?"

Heading: ‘Look after your soldiers, they are special’ - Indian Express
Content:
The 17-year-old victim of the recent gangrape in Panchkula told Newsline that the four accused tried to force her into prostitution. "They wanted me to earn for them and even threatened to kill my five-year-old brother if I did not toe their line," she said.

On September 16, the victim was allegedly gangraped and tortured by four persons, including a woman, in a garage at Haryana government office in Sector 4, Panchkula.

"About a year ago, Aman Ahuja (son of the Haryana Additional District Transport Officer and already arrested) along with one Jitesh drugged me and took me to a hotel in Manimajra, where they took pornographic pictures of me. After that, they started exploiting and blackmailing me. The accused said they would send me to Goa if I didn't comply with their demands," said the girl.

According to the victim's family, the girl wanted to end her life and had even written a suicide note. Now, it seems the family is under threat as well.

"We are getting calls from unknown numbers asking us to take Rs 20 lakh and settle the issue. We have also received three or four death threats," said the victim's father.

With several of the accused still at large, the family is tense. The victim added: "I gave a description of the accused to the police and requested them to make sketches but they refused. Initially, the male police officers asked me all sorts of embarrassing questions. It was only after I objected that a woman police officer was called."

Also, the police have not taken the girl to the incident of crime to recreate the sequence of events even once.

Superintendent of Police, Panchkula, Sandeep Khirwar said: "The investigation is on."

Heading: Victim identifies two accused - Indian Express
Content:
'From the time a soldier takes the oath of allegiance to serve his nation, he places his life on trust with those who command him — the officers and his nation. He trains hard, as Abhinav Bindra did, deals with pitfalls and failures with determination and takes failure as a learning curve'

It was on August 11, 2008, at 9.47 am, the Tricolour was smartly raised by Chinese soldiers with the anthem being played faultlessly in the packed indoor shooting range at Beijing Olympic Games. Millions of proud Indians — men, women, children — including military veterans proudly stood in rapt attention in front of their television sets, choking with spontaneous tears and emotion.

The man with the golden Walther PPK gun — bespectacled, gifted, mature-beyond-his-years, unassuming — 25-year-old Abhinav Bindra was in extraordinary control of his emotions as his "poker face" effectively concealed them with a bland, impenetrable "been there, done that" look.

As the moving tunes of the National Anthem reverberated, all that the young man permitted himself was a stringently rationed smile that slowly lighted up his handsome visage. The Buddha (alias the Monk, Constant Comatose, as his shooting buddies called him) had, at last, smiled.

What's with this enigmatic, silent young man that makes him so special? His role models — his brilliantly successful, committed, and perceptive parents — gave a hint during the unending interviews they faced since their Buddha smiled. Dr AS Bindra opined that Abhinav, on his return to India, would dedicate his gold medal to the thousands of men in uniform who had offered supreme sacrifices in preserving the sovereignty of India. In dedicating Abhinav's achievement, the entire family truly displayed a Heart of Gold as such deep respect can only come from a family who are soldiers at heart themselves.

The driving force of the family was not individual glory or the greedy lure of lucre, but rather the deep interest in national pride and national interest. What could be a better medium for Abhinav to express himself than earning for his country its first individual gold medal since the Olympics began 112 years ago.

From the time a soldier takes the oath of allegiance to serve his nation, he places his life on trust with those who command him — the officers and his nation. He trains hard, as Abhinav did, deals with pitfalls and failures stoically with true grit and determination and takes failure not as rejection but as a learning curve.

Abhinav worked through deep despair at Athens, when the Holy Grail slipped out of his hands; breaking the Olympic record but still missing out on a podium finish.

"He's finished", announced those taking sadistic, unrelenting note of his disabilities. The normal response of a young person would have been to throw in the towel.

But Abhinav carried on with his quest for excellence believing that his time under the arc lights would come soon.

"I believe in myself," was his measured, laconic response to media persons asking for his secret of success.

Facing extraordinary challenges at freezing heights, a number of truly extraordinary soldiers cheerfully took a call at Kargil in 1999, with some like young Thapar knowingly walking into the arms of death, some like Vikram Batra unwilling to rest on past laurels, but willing their tortured bodies to make a final effort for their nation. These young men, all of Abhinav's age, lived and died, not for materialistic gains, but because their country needed them. They overcame their internal devils to rise above themselves.

Abhinav climbed his Tiger Hill at Beijing. A grateful nation, though, must never forget the key symbolism behind his achievement. Look after your soldiers in every way you can — they, like Abhinav Bindra, are indeed special.

Heading: ‘Women, be fearless, don’t let problems intimidate you’ - Indian Express
Content:
The German national, who was allegedly kidnapped and molested by five youths last week, today identified two of the accused— Harpreet Singh and Pankaj. The three others arrested in the case — Sompal, Sukhi and Jolly — had refused the identification parade.

In the identification parade at Model Jail in Burail, which went on for around two hours, the victim had to identify two accused, out of nearly a dozen men with matching physical description of Harpreet and Pankaj.

The victim, accompanied by her father and few officials of the German Embassy reached Chandigarh today and was taken to the Model Jail around 9.30 am. The identification parade commenced around 10 am and carried on till noon, in the presence of Sub-Divisional Magistrate (South) Prerna Puri. UT Deputy Commissioner RK Rao had yesterday appointed SDM (South) Prerna Puri to get the identification parade conducted in her presence.

The Chandigarh Police had moved an application in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate on Saturday, seeking permission for the identification parade of the accused, after two then gave their consent to be put through it.

"Obtaining the consent of the accused for the identification parade is required according to the law, which was given by Harpreet and Pankaj. Thus, they both were put through the identification parade, and subsequently identified by the victim. We have even got the two vehicles and places, where she was illegally confined, identified by the victim," said Assistant Superintendent of Police Madhur Verma.

Heading: Proposal to run deluxe buses between city and Panchkula - Indian Express
Content:
"Women should not forget the power that God has endowed on them: the ability to procreate, which makes them all the more powerful," said Chand Asani, winner of this year's Neerja Bhanot Award. Dr A R Kidwai, Governor, Haryana, conferred the award on Chand at St Stephen's School, today.

Speaking on the occasion, Chand, who hails from Mumbai, said: "The award represents the spirit of Neerja Bhanot's determination in the face of overwhelming circumstances. I urge women to be fearless and not be intimidated by problems in life."

Chand, 51, was married at the age of 15, and was later shattered to find that her husband was a habitual infidel. "He refused to provide for me and our two children. Since I did not want to return to my parent's house, I decided to take charge of the situation," she said. She then decided to become self-reliant.

She said: "I completed my Master's degree in English Literature. It was the challenge that I took head-on with life, which kept me going." Since then, the SNDT Women's University Rural Development Centre in Mumbai, has been a part of her life. She now works for Kalyani, a rural women's co-operative in Kulak village near Udwada in Gujarat, where she coordinates with workers, arranges for non-formal education and training programmes and explores employment opportunities. She is also actively involved in women's struggle for livelihood, particularly tribal women.

Trust organises painting competition

Nearly 400 children participated in a painting competition organised by the Neerja Bhanot Pan Am Trust at St Stephen's School on Sunday. The theme of the competition ranged from 'My Pet' for the juniors to 'My Teacher in Class' for the seniors.

Heading: Two-day mega lok adalats in December - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to enhance the public transport system and check the influx of vehicles in the city, the Haryana Roadways has proposed inter-city air-conditioned buses and intra-city as well as inter-city low floor deluxe buses between Chandigarh and Panchkula. These buses will not only run between the two cities but also ply inter-sector within Panchkula, particularly between the Inter State Bus Terminus (ISBT) in Sector 43 to Panchkula sectors.

"The inter-city AC buses have been proposed between Chandigarh and Panchkula and other towns in the state. These would run within different sectors of Panchkula and cater to passengers between ISBT in Sector 43 Chandigarh and Panchkula. The proposal is under consideration and the feasibility is being analysed," said K S Kalson, General Manager, Haryana Roadways.

For the convenience of passengers, the state roadways had also proposed to include more than 60 low-floor buses for inter and intra cities. Sources said the state transport authorities were eager to launch AC buses in public-private participation on inter-city routes.

Hitting the roads first would be the low-floor deluxe buses. "In order to decongest traffic within the city, the department has come up with low-floor deluxe buses. The order for the same has been placed and the design for fabrication is under process. The city residents might see these buses on roads very soon," said M Ramshekhar, Haryana Transport Commissioner.

Competing with the Chandigarh Transport Undertaking (CTU) low floor buses, the new buses would be launched with some improvements in the model and chassis design.

"Providing better quality bus services to the city residents, the Haryana Roadways is making efforts with the motive to offer comfort at minimal costs. These buses would initially run intra-city; within the sectors of Panchkula and later expand to inter-city; between Chandigarh and Panchkula," added Ramshekhar.

With low cost cars hitting the roads soon, the volume of traffic is expected to increase manifold. The Roadways is emphasising on motivating the public to use public transport system to the maximum.

Heading: State govt releases Rs 2 crore for sewer treatment plant - Indian Express
Content:
About 2.5 lakh cases pertaining to disputes like mutation, revenue, criminal and civil matters are likely to be settled and disposed of by way of compromises in December.

The State Legal Services Authorities, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh have decided to organise mega Lok Adalats on two days — December 20 and 21— in Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.

The Mega Lok Adalat project called 'Samadhan 2008' has been launched. In this context, a meeting was held under the chairmanship of Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice T S Thakur in Chandigarh. The meeting was attended by Justice MS Gill, Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel, judges of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chief Secretaries of Punjab and Haryana and Chandigarh Home Secretary, Advocate Generals of Punjab and Haryana and other senior government officers.

The Chief Justice suggested targeting the disposal of about 2.5 lakh cases in the mega Lok Adalats and stressed upon the State Executive of the three states to cooperate for disposal of maximum number of cases by identifying them category wise.

Justice Thakur also stressed upon the Chief Secretaries and other government functionaries to issue instructions to the concerned departments to coordinate with the Legal Services Authorities and to give wide publicity to make the general public aware about the adalats.

The Member Secretary of Haryana State Legal Services Authority, meanwhile, said that rural Lok Adalats were held on Sunday at various villages in Haryana. Around 79 cases were settled pertaining to civil, criminal, mutation and revenue related disputes.

Heading: BJP leader, son arrested on charges of dowry harassment - Indian Express
Content: The state government on Sunday released Rs 2 crore, as the first premium for the construction of a sewer treatment plant (STP) at Singhpura in Zirakpur. The plant will be constructed on two acres of land, owned by the Municipal Council, and will be completed in two years. The sewer line will cover nearly 50 per cent of the Zirakpur MC. The Centre has issued Rs 16.79 crore under the Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme of Small and Medium Towns (UIDSSMT) for this plan.

Heading: Amazon — the new housing project in Panchkula - Indian Express
Content: Dera bassi : BJP district leader Suresh Gupta and his son, Rohit, were arrested on Sunday on charges of dowry harassment. A case has been registered against five members of the family on the complaint of Jyoti, daughter-in-law of Gupta, who reportedly consumed some poisonous substance on Sunday morning. Jyoti alleged in the presence of SDM Sohanlal that she had been harassed mentally and physically by her in-laws for dowry. Rejecting the allegations, Suresh Gupta termed the issue as a "conspiracy being politically motivated". SHO D S Grewal said the police have booked Suresh Gupta, his wife Kaushalya, son Rohit and two married daughters under Sections 498-A, 406, 506 and 34 of the IPC besides the Arms Act. The police have also recovered a .32 bore revolver and started investigations.

Heading: MC decides to enclose open areas - Indian Express
Content:
Joining the league of private players like DLF and Parsavnath, another Mumbai-based company, Bhoomi Greens, is all set to start with a housing project — Amazon — in Sector 30, Panchkula. Nearly 16 acres of land has been purchased by them and they have also received the approval from the government for the same.

"Housing is coming up as one of the major demands of the residents of Panchkula. With several developmental projects like the four-laning of the highways, Kalka-Pinjore urban complex, improvement of the infrastructure, the entire area here is turning into a prime land," said RS Perhar, one of the partners of the project.

He added, "It is for this that nearly 16 acres of land has been purchased by us for the project."

Bhoomi Greens, claims that 650 flats of different types will be constructed. "We plan to have flats of three different categories. While the smallest will be a two-bedroom flat, the other two will be three and four-bedroom flats," added Perhar.

There are also plans afoot to beautify and develop the seasonal rivulet passing from behind the project area.

The company also aims to construct luxury apartments with facilities like a table tennis court, health club, dispensary, banquet hall, guest rooms and swimming pools.

"We plan to have water walls to add to the scenic beauty to the area. The project will be launched in two months' time and will be completed in about 36 months," added Perhar.

Heading: It’s a girl! - Indian Express
Content:
The misuse of open spaces in various sectors across the city will soon be a thing of the past. In a new venture, the Municipal Corporation, has decided to enclose unutilised open spaces and install benches and swings there.

The project will be executed by the Horticulture Wing of the MC and has been started in some places. The open spaces will be enclosed by constructing a toe-line wall, which will have an iron railing.

An MC official said the initiative will prevent parking in open spaces and will ensure that pieces of paper and polythene do not collect there.

The issue was debated in the house meet of the MC a number of times. Some councillors were of the opinion that residents, who park cars on government land should be fined and parking vehicles in such areas be treated as an offence. The MC is also constructing new green belts in Sector 17 and 24.

Heading: Lens Master - Indian Express
Content:
Recently the tricity saw a handful of activities to promote the cause of the girl child

Daughters are a matter of pride, after all she is as much the family's blood as the boy. While often they are refused love, care and acceptance efforts straight from the heart are making sure that the girl child is a celebrated, and not a neglected being. Narvijay Yadav, Founder President, Beti Foundation of India, hopes to change the attitude of society. "We believe in celebrating daughters." So is the discrimination more in rural or urban India? "It's hardly about that. What matters is the mind-set. Female foeticide happens despite the education and monitory capacity, while in villages a lot of forward thinking has happened. The problem is that even though girls are working now, the minds of the people are still blocked. But the youth today is quite progressive, it will change things in the future," he hopes.

It is not just NGOs and the 'biggies' who are out there to make a difference, even the young ones are contributing their bit to the cause, their own way. One may not think them mature enough to realize the gravity of such issues but one look at their efforts at you realize the truth behind their simple approaches. They are far more sensitive towards their surroundings than we perceive. And the students of Dikshant International School, Zirakpur, proved exactly that in a recently held a painting exhibition. Their colours, ideas and expressions paid tribute to the different faces of the Indian women. Mitul Dixit, Director of the school, believes that it's important to inculcate such values in students early on. "We call ourselves citizens of a developed nation of the 21st century trying to live with the illusion that we are at par with the developed giants of the world but with cases of dowry deaths, the decreasing sex ratio of women in India due to female foeticide and infanticide , we as a country cannot call ourselves a developed nation, although, the government of India is taking initiatives to solve the issues faced by women but the only solution is to educate the present generation of children and create awareness amongst them to bring about a total change.The paintings on exhibition are for sale and the proceeds would be donated to an NGO "Asmita" with the objective of "saving the girl child in India."

Not only schools but other institutions are also pitching in. On Daughter's Day, Ivy hospital, Mohali, launched launched Ivy Sukanya Scheme for the benefit of the single girl child. Dr Rajesh Bali, Medical Superintendent shares, "The inspiration for such a noble program came from the Beti Foundation of India. The scheme is focused on the welfare of single girl child. Any family having a single girl child may get her name registered with us at a nominal fee to ensure free OPD facility for her at Ivy Hospital for one year along with 10% discount in the indoor care too. The aim is to promote the love, care and acceptance of girl child in the community." State Bank of India recently adopted 50 girls of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 10 and Government Model Senior School- Sector 12. Ajay Swaroop, Chief General Manager, SBI, Chandigarh, tells, "Last year the bank initiated 'adoption of girl child' scheme sponsoring the their education up to class twelve in an effort to boost the literacy rate among girls. As many as 600 girls have already been sponsored by different branches of the bank in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir," he tells adding that the initiative has been undertaken to make make a difference in the society.

Heading: Back to Sanawar - Indian Express
Content:
Raghu Rai hones the lens language of the tricity shutterbugs

Looking Back

In a slide show at Government Museum and Art Gallery- Sector 10, people of Chandigarh were exposed to some of the finest works of renowned photographer Raghu Rai. As the photographs clicked from his early works, his interactions with the names in the country to the vast cultural diversity of India, Rai spun stories around each frame and enlightened us with his exploration through the viewfinder.

"Art is not beauty, it is expression and exploration. It is meant to take you higher than from where you are at present," says the man best known for his captures of the Bhopal gas tragedy, Mother Teresa and Indira Gandhi. Raghu Rai was in town for a two day photojournalism workshop organised by Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi. The workshop was attended by around 60 amateur and professional photographers from the tricity. He interacted with media photographers and photo enthusiasts of the city also commenting on their photographs.

Rai commented that photography today is facing a lot of repitition. "Landscapes are not bad but nature will give you something beautiful any given hour. Explore the streets around you. For instance, if you are a college student go capture the energy. Good photography cannot happen sitting down at the same spot." Rai sees himself as a street photographer and incidentally it was not photography but music that Rai was interested in. "But after my father's reprimand 'Mirasi banega kya?' it became history!" So the first shot happened with a camera borrowed from his brother. "I chased an innocent looking donkey till it got tired. The shot was good enough to be published in London Times and the payment was enough for two months!" And for those still stepping into the field Rai's advise is "don't always follow the mind, if you don't enjoy the 'ras' of life then it's a waste. Live fully, be passionate about what you do and keep raising the bar" So is he planning to take on the teacher's role? "I'm quite mismanaged, teaching requires discipline. Students do come to me for a month or as long as six months but after the training they lose all that they have learnt. Now I only take up students who have the fire to make a difference."

You heard him!

Heading: Style Wrap - Indian Express
Content:
Got together after a span of 50 years, here's meeting up with the batch of 1958 on its 161st Founder's Day

The sweet smell of fresh pine greets Dr Praveen Kumar as she sets foot in Sanawar after a gap of 50 year. The same smell that beckoned her to stay back when she was in Class V. Now here from England for the 161st Founders Day, "it's these, the hills, the school and my friends that forced me to give an ultimatum at my work place for a weeks off," Kumar, who is working as the President of British Medical Association, tells us and makes us meet her group from school — Lila Kak, who's come all the way from Boston, Asha Nanda from Delhi and Jasbir Singh from Chandigarh. All here after a well-chalked out plan, reliving the childhood days and standing at a spot, where Charlie once was. "Charlie the shop that sold samosas, tea and chips and was close to the boys dormitory," Nanda gives insight about the way the school once was, as the four flaunt sleeveless black jackets and red badges stating the year of passing-out. "These are gift from Jasbir," the trio chorus and tell us that back in school too they lived by dress codes on off days.

Memories and momentos ruling the day, while some wore red scarves, others had umbrellas dedicated to the day. But what really stood out were the name slips with the names of houses written in bold. "Though years might have passed the legacy of our houses still holds true," Brig TPS Chawdhary, who's been a part of project Trishna, emphasizes that Nilgiri House is the tops. The mere mention of the house is enough to have about five from the total of 22 of the batch come to his side, the Vindhiyas too took a step forward.

Years of separation not withstanding, "the time of uninterrupted bonding is what holds us close," says Sarabjit A Singh, a consultant with World Bank, who had tears rolling during the parade. "It's the spirit of the place that gets us on a high," he manages a smile and tells us about Re 1 per week that they all used to get to spend. "And in that we used to think we can buy the world," laughs Dr Kumar. This one's to the good old times.

The True Worth

Made in an hour's time and gifted to the Lawrence School, Sanawar, in 1982 by MF Hussain, the painting now pitched at Rs 2 crore by INTACH found a place worthy of it this month. Put up at the Parker Hall, "The painting got marred over the years and the batch of 1986 restored it and got it back this month," the headmaster Praveen Vasisht tells us.

Gifted during the tenure when his son, Owais, was a student here, Imran Baig, an alumnus, initiated the process of restoration. "The painting depicts the motto of the school 'never give in' ," Ikman Bath, a faculty member tells us.

Heading: Green Grandeur - Indian Express
Content:
Some years back when it came to winter wear, we had to make do with bulky shawls that came with no-fuss trimmings, unless of course you had a pure Pashmina on your hands. All of that changed when the "stole" hit the market. Shorter, smarter and available in a riot of colours, it fast found its way into every wardrobe possible. The young and restless would drape a blood-red silk one over a black evening dress while their Moms would prefer to team it with trousers and a kurti. Since then the stole has arrived every winter season in new avatars and we are still lapping or wrapping it up. Dishing out a collection each year is city's Rashi Setia who is back with her annual collection of stoles. "This time it's a spread of all kinds," tells Rashi who brings in a smart lineup of both casual as well as formal wear. "As far as colours go, expect to see a lot of chocolate tones. While colours like red and black still remain best-sellers," tells Setia who has worked with Swarovski and metal work for her collection this time. "Stoles are becoming dressy too. For instance with the Diwali parties now picking up steam, most ladies opt to wear a simple outfit and play up the elegant factor with a stole," she says. Keeping all that in mind, Setia's put together pieces with pearl and lace work as well. Then there are more "jazzier" ones with applique, net and tissue embellishments. "Velvet is completely out this time. I have used fabrics like silk Pashmina, wool, silk on silk and viscose blends as well," the designer mentions. And all-time favourites like Burberry checks and those with pom-pom trimmings are thrown in too.

The exhibition is on at The Episode, #202, Sector 9, Chandigarh on October 6 & 7.

Heading: We will contest LS polls on the issue of development, says Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
Malachite has graced various design sensibilities across the world

This week, I would first like to talk about Danila, a Russian craftsman who was so consumed by the beauty of Ural mountains that he once decided to carve a 'lively' flower from malachite stone. Working upon the fragile stone with simple hand tools, it took him seven years of time and focus to realize his dream. It's an inspiring tale of perseverance, won't you agree? The name Malachite (pronounced as mala-kite) variates from Greek "malache" meaning "mallow". Nature conjures the most vivacious green patterns and makes it a popular semi-precious stone. This opaque stone is easily recognizable from its unique banded patterns of green, dark green and blackish green. Malachite is a mineral stone and is a green carbonate of copper which extends it its colour. A brittle stone with silky surface, it exhibits a widely variable habit. It is probably the oldest green mineral. Known as the "stone of protection", it has been esteemed over centuries. Malachite was apparently recovered from mines in Suez-Sinai as early as 4000 BC though archaeological evidence traces malachite mining around 3,000 years back at King Solomon's mines. It was used as a mineral pigment in green paints till the 1800s. Egyptians used it to cure convulsions and as a strong anesthetic. Travellers valued it as the "guardian stone" as it was assumed to break into pieces sensing any approaching danger. Ancient Egyptians, Romans and Greeks used malachite for styling jewellery. Malachite is an important mineral specimen and has been used as an ornamental stone that has graced various design sensibilities. Figurines, gorgeous vases and boxes etc are carved from the same. The Tazza, one of the largest pieces of malachite is in North America.

Today, malachite is mainly sourced from Zaire, Russia, Germany, France, Australia and USA. Be careful though as some malachite is treated with oil, epoxy or waxed to enhance colour. It's a polished stone and water usually removes its protective surface. Use soft cloth for cleaning. Being very fragile, the artisan may use inlay setting and semi-bezel to protect the tips.

Malachite is a bold statement stone. You can soften the intense patterns with single hue from the stone or contrast it with black. For subtle hues, Satya Paul is always the best bet for prints. Barbara Streisand teamed malachite danglers dot on a Vogue cover. With winters near take liberty with gloss and high shine. Go metallic. Malachite stands out in the sculpted neckpiece in Missoni's latest collection. Whether you are a designer or a novice, unleash your creative juices and play along the natural lines of malachite to create the jewellery piece or the entire ensemble.

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: End of coal shortage in sight - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda said that Congress party will contest the forthcoming Lok Sabha and Assembly elections on the issue of development work undertaken by the party in the state.

Talking to the media here today, he appreciated the Indo-US nuclear agreement, and said that Haryana will be benefited more as a nuclear energy-based plant would be developed in Fatehabad.

He also attended the bhumi poojan samaroh of an over-bridge, where he said, "Sirsa, which was ignored during the INLD government, is our top priority. We have already sanctioned Rs 3.8 for the augmentation of sewerage system and the upgradation of drainage system, as the city has been facing serious water-logging problem during the rains"

Earlier, at function organised at the Aggarsen Bhawan, he announced that life and works of Aggarsen Maharaj will be included in school curriculum.

Announcing a 1,100-square yard plot, near the old BDO office, for the construction of Aggarsen Bhawan, he also sanctioned Rs 11 lakh for the Aggarwal Sabha.

The local media, however, boycotted the function organised in Aggarsen Bhawan, following alleged misbehaviour by the organisers.

Heading: Gang of dacoits busted, four held - Indian Express
Content:
For long, the thermal power plants in the state have been affected by the poor quality and low supply of coal. This has restricted power generation at a time when there is an urgent need for more power supply to meet the increasing requirements of industry, agriculture and domestic needs.

However, a recent move by the state government may help improve matter in this regard. It has been decided to constitute a joint venture company by the Haryana Power Generation Corporation Limited (HPGCL) and Indra Prastha Generation Corporation Limited (IPGCL) for improving power supply in the state.

Talking to The Indian Express, Sanjiv Kaushal, managing director of HPGCL, said the JVC had been agreed upon in principle. "Haryana's thermal plants in the coming years would have sufficient quantity of coal to generate 4,000 MW of power for 25 year. A coal block, namely Mara-II Mahan in Singrauli district in Madhya Pradesh, has been allocated to HPGCL and Delhi Power Board by the Central government," said Kaushal.

Kaushal informed that the total area of the coal block was about 66 sq kms, having estimated reserves of 950 miliion tonne. The total capacity of the coal block is to provide coal for generating 8000 MW of power for 25 years. "Haryana would get half of that capacity," said Kaushal.

"We are also exploring the possibility of establishing a pithead plant in Madhya Pradesh itself. This would be of immense benefit to Haryana as the entire coal transportation cost would be saved," he said.

The idea behind the formation of the JVC between HPGCL and IPGCL was to find out ways for further development of the coal block. The required documents including the Joint Venture Agreement, Memorandum of Association and Article of Association have already been finalised.

The JV Company will have two Directors from HPGCL and two from IPGCL, with the posts of chairman and CEO resting with Haryana and Delhi for two years at a time on rotation-basis. The Letter of Intent was issued to MECL, Nagpur on February 26 for priority exploration of coal block, covering an area of approximately 10 sq kms in the first phase, at a cost of Rs 4.25 crore.

Applications for obtaining prospective license for mining in the coal block have already been filed with State Mining Department and for the forest clearance for topographical and geographical survey with Forest Department, Madhya Pradesh.

Kaushal said that to expedite the requisite clearances, a joint team of officers from HPGCL and IPGCL has been deputed to Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, Ranchi. The mining would involve both open-cast and underground mining and the apportionment of the coal extracted from the block between both the parties will be decided by the Union Ministry of Coal, after consultation with both the parties.

"There would be substantial improvement in quality as well as quantity of coal in Haryana after completion of the project," assured Kaushal.

Heading: Long-term power plan for Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
The Yamunanagar Police has busted a gang of dacoits and arrested three persons, identified as Muraslin, a resident of Shivpuri B, Sudesh, a resident of Amarpuri Colony and Kamal, resident of Mandewari. Three of them were arrested from a desolate building in sector 18, while they were allegedly planning a dacoity at a kothi in sector 18 part-II. Two persons, however, managed to escape, taking advantage of the dark. They were identified as Baldev, resident of Mahirampur and Sonu alias Kala, resident of Shivpuri B Colony, Jagadhri. Baldev was also arrested later.

Disclosing this today, a spokesman of the police department said cases have been registered against the accused under sections 399 and 402 of the Indian Penal Code sections 25, 54 and 59 of Arms Act at Faraqpur police station.

One 12-bore musket, 10 live cartridges of 12-bore and one khukhri were recovered from Muraslin, one 315-bore pistol, two live cartridges and a khukhri from Sudesh and one khukhri, a rod and three live cartridges of 12 bore from Kamal. A 315-bore pistol and one live cartridge was recovered from Baldev's possession.

The accused have admitted to their involvement in a number of incidents of looting.

Heading: Sonia’s stamp of approval may not be enough for Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
In view of fast growing demand of electricity due to fast pace of development in Gurgaon district, the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) and the Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam (HVPN) have prepared a Rs 6,034-crore long-term plan and a Rs 1565-crore short-term plan to expand and augment power transmission and distribution system. The plan is to cater the load demand for the period up to the year 2021.

A spokesman for the Haryana Power Utilities said here today that rapid growth of Gurgaon had led to tremendous growth of load on the transmission system which is 20 to 25 per cent compared to 8 to 10 per cent in other areas of the state.

Under the long-term power transmission plan, the DHBVN and the HVPN would construct 486 additional substations, which include 11 sub-stations of 400 KV level, 32 of 220 KV, seven of 66 KV and 436 of 33 KV level. As many as 124 substations of 2775 MVA capacity would be constructed by the year 2011-12, while 192 sub-stations of a transformation capacity of 4000 MVA and 170 substations of 4000 MVA capacity would be set up during the period from 2012 to 2016 and 2016 to 2021, respectively, he said.

He said that at present, there were five 220 KV sub-stations of 960 MVA transformation capacity in Gurgaon, feeding 50 power transformers at 24 sub-stations of 66 KV level.

Heading: Hooda promises Tata ‘every possible facility’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress rally at Panipat, in the presence of UPA chairperson and Congress president Sonia Gandhi, may have further raised the status of Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, but this, in no way, means that Hooda can rest on his 'laurels'.

Sonia, in fact, has visited Haryana as many as six times during the regime of Bhupinder Singh Hooda, which, many say, is a her certificate of approval for Hooda's leadership skills. However, given a chance, some leaders would like to pull the rug from below Hooda's feet at the first opportunity.

Kuldeep Bishnoi, now disqualified as member of the Lok Sabha, his father and former Chief Minister Bhajan Lal, and two other MLAs - Rakesh Kamboj and Dharampal Malik, have been taking pot-shots at Hooda and off late, Arvind Sharma, the MP from Karnal too has been threatening to rebel against Hooda's leadership.

Sharma was almost on the verge of quitting Congress and joining BSP before the Trust Vote in Parliament on the UPA government.
