Heading: Cops stand their ground - Indian Express
Content:
A trocious and ridiculous. That's what the legal fraternity says about the police filing a dacoity case against 10 people who manhandled a traffic constable at Kunte chowk on Laxmi Road on Friday evening. The police claim the 10 people had snatched a two-wheeler being towed away from a no-parking zone. They were arrested on Saturday.

It's gross misuse of power, said Harshad Nimbalkar, a leading criminal lawyer. "How can police file a dacoity case when no dacoity has been committed? Dacoity is too serious a charge. The offence in this case is not of that nature. At the most, the police could have filed a case under Section 353 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for preventing a government servant from discharging his duties," said Nimbalkar, who is also a member of the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa.

Asking police higher-ups to intervene, Nimbalkar said if the lower rung had erred, the seniors should see to it that justice is done.

Former president of the Pune Advocates Bar Association Gorakhnath Kale agreed that dacoity charge cannot be slapped on the offenders in this case.

"The owner was trying to claim his vehicle from the police," he said. Kale also feels they should have been charged with obstructing government work instead.

Kale said under the Motor Vehicles Act, traffic police had no right to tow away vehicles parked on roadsides or in no-parking zones without intimating the owners.

Mukund Sarda, principal of the New Law College, Erandwane, said invocation of Section 395 on the 10 citizens defies all logic. "How can obstruction of government work be dacoity? For a dacoity charge, there has to be an intention, motive, use of force and threat to life," he said, adding that in this case, Section 183 of the IPC would have been more appropriate.

Section 183 says that whoever offers resistance while any property is being taken away by the lawful authority of any public servant shall be punished with an imprisonment for six months, or a maximum fine of Rs 1,000, or both."

Sushil Mancharkar, another prominent criminal lawyer, in fact, wants the 10 citizens to file a theft charge against the policemen. He said, "Nobody, including police, has the right to take away any property without the knowledge or consent of the owner."

Heading: Bitten by poll bug, parties select and woo communities - Indian Express
Content:
The police are trying to justify the dacoity case they have slapped. "Legally, a dacoity case can be registered against anyone taking away a vehicle forcibly from the police. Since the case is the subject of a court investigation, I cannot comment," said Rajendra Sonawane, Joint Commissioner of Police.

Referring to several attacks on traffic police in recent weeks, he said the increasing attacks indicated that police were strictly implementing the law. He said people get "sadistic pleasure" by breaking traffic rules. "The violators get away with a small fine. They have no fear, as they know the punishment is mild. The licence of offenders should be suspended for a year and the violation should attract imprisonment. The situation will improve only then," he said. "The problem is compounded as the cases take a long time to come up for hearing. Every day we prosecute around 2,000 violators and register a large number of cases."

Heading: Centuries after Bajirao Peshwa courted Mastani, their lake finds a new spark - Indian Express
Content:
chunk by chunk: Everyone's eye on Warkaris; Christian and Muslim votes too targeted

With Lok Sabha and Assembly elections getting closer, political parties have identified the communities whose votes they will target and set about wooing them.

Everyone has expressed solidarity with the Warkaris, who are in millions, spread across the state and have launched an agitation no one can afford to ignore. The NCP is also wooing Muslims while the Congress has expressed solidarity with oppressed Christians.

The Warkaris are waging a battle against the proposed Dow Chemicals research centre at Shinde village near Chakan. The Shiv Sena was the first to support their demand, with party leader Ramdas Kadam announcing that his party would not allow the Dow unit to come up. The BJP followed it up with party state secretary Vinod Tawade calling on arrested Warkari leader Bandatatya Karadkar in Yerawada jail and conveying his party's support for the agitation.

NCP chief Sharad Pawar had criticised the Warkaris, but then Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar too announced that NCP would not allow the Dow unit to come up. Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil also announced withdrawal of cases filed against the protesting Warkaris.

The NCP's Pune chief Jaideo Gaikwad sees the Shiv Sena and the BJP support as a political gimmick but says the NCP had no political motive in supporting the Warkaris.

But a Congress leader was frank enough to admit: "It's obvious that no political party can go against Warkaris, who are in millions." He added that his party too was trying to calm down the situation with Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh saying there was a misunderstanding among Warkaris about the Dow project.

Parties also hosted a number of iftar parties, with the NCP taking the lead in the city. Pawar attended one such iftar, organised by a local leader in Rasta Peth. City NCP executive president Anil Bhosale too organised an iftar at Sakhar Sankul in Shivajinagar.

Local NCP leaders brushed aside suggestions that the iftars were to woo Muslim voters. Gaikwad said the objective was to reach out to the Muslim community that is feeling alienated in the current atmosphere.

Another NCP leader said: "We are a secular party and have been organising various programmes for all communities. It is not true these are meant to woo voters."

If the NCP is holding iftars, the Congress had taken to the streets recently in support of the Christian community. City Congress chief Abhay Chhajed was the first to extend his party's support for the Catholic Association of Poona that held a dharna recently in protest against attacks on churches and Christians in several other states.

Although the leaders deny their support for any community had anything to do with the elections, political observers see it differently. They say the race to reach out to as many communities as possible will only increase in the coming days. In the current scenario, no party can afford to neglect any community. They have to reach out to all, they said, adding that delimitation had also somewhat changed equations in the constituencies and political parties could no longer be too sure about their previous strongholds.

Heading: Pay hike ensures cracker of a Diwali for college teachers - Indian Express
Content:
The Mastani Lake, believed to have derived its name from Bajirao Peshwa's love for a court dancer named Mastani, is set for a makeover. A plan to transform the 275-year-old lake into a tourist spot has begun, with the estimates committee of the state government, led by local MLA and committee chairman Ashok Tekawade, recently paying a visit to the lake. The move is also aimed at generating employment for the local people.

Tekawade told Newsline: "The lake is strategically located and linked to history. The area has a lot of scenic beauty. Despite this, the reservoir is neglected. We are considering developing it into a tourist place. It will lead to the overall development of the surrounding area."

The lake was known as Wadki Talab, as it is located near Wadki village. Legend has it that it symbolised the love between Bajirao Peshwa and Mastani, a court dancer. Hence it became popular as Mastani Lake.

"The construction of the lake is believed to have started during the reign of Bajirao Peshwa, who died in 1740. As per historical evidence, construction activity was on even during the reign of Nanasaheb Peshwa after Bajirao's death," said Pandurang Balkawade, a city-based historian.

A bird's eye view of the lake can be enjoyed while travelling via Dive Ghat towards Saswad. "When the roads in Dive Ghat were being built, they should have been done in such a way to facilitate easy flow of water to the lake from the surrounding mountains. But this was not done. The lake largely remains dry, sometimes in monsoon. If we have to turn it into a tourist spot, we will have to reserve a lot of water for the lake and if necessary bring additional water from Fursungi canal."

When contacted, an official of the Pune Zilla Parishad, said, "We are exploring possibilities of collecting more water for the lake throughout the year."

District Collector Chandrakant Dalvi, who also visited the site last week, said, "The Revenue and Forest departments own the lake and the surrounding land. Hence, necessary permission needs to be given by these departments first. To implement the project, the District Planning and Development Committee (DPDC) will have to approve the necessary funds."

MLA Tekawade is optimistic that the plan will work out. "It might take time, but it will surely happen. We will put the plan before the Tourism department."

Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
There's some extra cheer for teachers of colleges under the University of Pune this Diwali, with their salaries ready to touch a new high. The G K Chadha Salary Review Committee set up by the University Grants Commission (UGC) has recommended a salary in the range of Rs 32,500 to Rs 65,000 for lecturers, readers and professors. Principals will get more than Rs 70,000 and Vice-Chancellors nearly Rs 80,000.

Teachers' organisations in the city welcomed the hike but wondered whether the incentive would be passed on to the teachers hired on contract.

The Chadha Committee recently submitted its report to UGC Chairman Sukhdeo Thorat. The UGC is expected to discuss the recommendations in its meeting on Tuesday. The recommendations are expected to come into effect after six months as they will require the approval of the central and state governments.

"The rise in salary would surely attract talented people to the profession," said Atul Bagul, president of Pune University Teachers' Association.

Principal of SP College Madhav Pendse said a pre-entrance training for teachers should be introduced. "There is a difference between someone coming to the profession by choice and someone getting attracted by the good money. Teaching is not only a profession but also a responsibility," he said.

Dhananjay Kulkarni, state convener of the Vidyapeeth Vikas Manch, said the benefits should also be applicable to teachers working on contract and those who are paid by the hour. "Over 30 per cent of the teachers in the colleges affiliated with University of Pune are on contract or paid by the hour. Some benefits will have to be passed on to them."

Although principals will benefit more than teachers, the principals' forum points out an ambiguity. The recommendation doesn't clarify what it means by an undergraduate college (UG) and postgraduate college (PG). "Virtually, there is not a single PG college in the state. There are some PG departments in some colleges. If the recommendation suggests that the benefits will pass on to PG colleges, then no principal in the state will benefit," said Nandkumar Nikam, president of the State Principals' Federation. "We will meet the UGC chairman and the Union HRD Minister over this," he added.

Heading: chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
Every dog has its day. And this is certainly true in today's context when television channels are dishing out a large variety of programmes on pets, especially dogs. From sharing your bed to sharing your car, sofa and even your life's agonies and ecstasies, pets are a reason to smile when the chips are down. An integral part of your family, it is only justifiable that they get their share on satellite television too.

After gaining mass popularity the first time around, NDTV Good Times has now brought back its most popular show Heavy Petting. A show on pets and for pet lovers, it brings out the humanitarian side of Indians who own pets. "Audiences are moved by realism and animals provide us real life experiences. They are sensitive, straight-forward creatures, who provide us opportunity to embrace and incorporate these necessary elements into our own lives," says Seema Rahmani, the anchor. While the show talks about the joys and heartaches of owning a pet, it brings to the fore NGOs and quirky owners who have cats, dogs, turtles and even stranded pigeons as pets.

After all, pet shows on television provide you with a dose of edutainment. "A lot of pet issues are behavioral and health-related. These shows provide helpful tips, answers to viewer queries, and useful tools to handle these issues," says Rahmani. Similarly Victoria Stilwell roams around the streets of USA, training mischievous dogs on It's Me or the Dog, Animal Planet. Many Indians took inspiration from her to do the same here. Aparna Khosla, a dog owner says, "It is thanks to the show, I was able to train my little Pomeranian to follow certain commands. After all, well-trained dogs are liked by all."

It isn't just talk shows anymore reality shows for pets are getting popular by the day. Groomer Has It, a show hosted by Jai Rodriguez on Animal Planet, has 12 professional groomers cut and style their pet to achieve the title of Groomer of the Year. "It is a lifestyle show for dog-owners, where dogs are trained to face the camera, helped to overcome shyness and are taught to put their best foot forward. It is for the modern viewer," says Rajiv Bakshi, director, marketing and communications, Discovery Networks Asia Pacific.

In spite of the growing number of channels and pet shows, why is the focal point still on dogs? "Dogs are a favourite pet in India," reasons Bakshi. Nevertheless these shows have opened up people to embracing their pets and also street dogs as their own through various testimonies, stories and facts. Most of all it has developed a need for compassion. Vincent Machado, a veterinarian says, "Television programmes on pets can only help people better their understanding on pets, their ailments, the kind of climate they require and also the various vaccinations they should undergo during their lifetime. Dog Whisperer on National Geographic did a good job of it."

Owning a pet is easy, but it is pampering them the right way is what one needs to learn. And of late, television has been doing a good job of getting this one right.

Heading: Loving the lens - Indian Express

Heading: A Helping Hand - Indian Express
Content:
With Asia's largest collection of cameras, Farid Shaikh and his passion for cameras is a treat for photography lovers

Passion is too incapable a word to explain what camera means to Farid Shaikh. Life minus camera is equal to nothing for this camera lover who over years has gathered over 2000 cameras from across the globe. So much so that his collection is registered as the biggest collection of cameras in Asia.

Off NIBM road, ahead of Kalyan mangal karyalay, a small building named Farid Manzil is a museum every inch of which has a tale of historic evolution of photography and camera. Welcoming the visitors is Farid Shaikh, who takes the guests on a euphoric journey- photography and its development. His eyes glow, eyebrows raise and hands start playing with the cameras as Shaikh starts talking about his most prized possessions- his cameras.

"This is one of the oldest cameras in the world. It is a Kodak box camera. You will be surprised to know that these cameras were made of cardboards. This is the aperture. This is the viewfinder. The first camera had only one viewfinder and the disadvantage of it was that one could take only vertical photographs with this. The next version of cameras came with two view finders so that vertical as well as horizontal pictures were possible," says Shaikh, explaining the oldest of the box cameras from his collection.

An irreplaceable part of Shaikh's collection is the Baby brownie series of cameras that brought about a revolution in the structure of cameras. "One of the baby brownies had an open view finder. But there was a challenge in that as well. The frame and the view would mismatch after clicking, as the shutter was located below the lens. This problem was eliminated in 1945 with 127 Baby Brownie where the shutter button was brought on the upper side of the camera. This was the foundation of the modern age cameras. Today's cameras have a shutter on top and this was the beginning of modern day camera designs. In fact they also came with optical viewfinder," adds he.

Honoured with countless awards, Shaikh's collection boasts revolutionary cameras in the history like the 12 exposure Kodak reflex twin lens, E and F models of Baby brownie and so on. And that is not enough because the collection has a wide variety of makes like Ensign, Zeiss, Gevabox, Agfa and so on.

"Let me tell you an interesting story about how flash came into existence. There was a time when Magnesium powder was used to generate the flash. They used to put Magnesium powder in the place of the flash and at the time of exposure- simply put an ignited cigarette stick in the powder. The flash generated used to provide light for the exposure. What came later were Magnesium silver coils. Today's electronic flash has its roots in the Magnesium powder," smiles he.

Another section in Shaikh's museum is the Folding cameras section. "I have four series of the Agfa Isolette. The cameras in this series boasted of accessories like self-timer, range finder, three shutter speeds and so on. Some time during 1950s, the Zeiss Ikon, one of the best coupled, professional cameras was introduced," says Shaikh playing with the Zeiss Ikon in his collection.

Another fascinating machine that finds its place in the collection is the Kodak waist pocket camera. With an open slot provided by the side of the camera, this marvelous machine allows the user to write the description of the venue where the photograph was clicked. And this was a part of the revolution in as early as 1885. Shaikh has a 15-lens camera manufactured by Warner Brothers. In one go this efficient camera, using 15 lenses used to produce 15 copies of the same view. The First World War had witnessed tiny spy cameras and Shaikh has a collection of spy cameras. For instance a camera in the lighter, camera in a gun, binocular, camera with a radio and so on. Nordetta, made in Germany is one of the first cameras in 3D photography. The Kodak Panorama camera the lens of which covers 180 degrees thus capturing the entire 180 degree view in one go is also an eye catcher.

"I also have the first video camera by JVC. It was created in 1979 and it came with a VCR, battery and a charger. RCA small video camera came with a monitor as well and I have that," adds Shaikh. An entire shelf is dedicated to Polaroid cameras. "These cameras were invented by Polaroid Land in 1960s. This was the introduction of instant photographs. This is where we find the roots of instant passport size photos," explains Shaikh handling the Polaroid 600 professional camera from his collection that he brought from Egypt.

The historic journey in the dreamy world of photography smoothly lands one into the mesmerising world of modern age cameras like Nikon, Minolta and so on. This collection of machines used to preserve memories leaves the visitors creating a valuable imprint, the image of which cannot be erased. And if dreams could be captured, this one is an image perfect. Isn't it?

Heading: No stone unturned - Indian Express
Content:
The Yellow Ribbon pre-Diwali fair is a commendable collective effort to market products made by self-help groups

That aid to the under privileged in India has evolved from mere handouts to building of self-sustainability was amply visible at the Yellow Ribbon Pre-Diwali NGO Fair at the Ishanya Arcade. The fair that started on October 3 and is on till October 6 was organised with the aim of helping self help groups and NGOs display and market their products for which free space was provided to them at the mall by Ishanya Foundation.

With 42 NGOs present at the fair to market goods such as chocolates, flower vases, pickles, studded jewellery, candles, diyas, cloth bags and tribal art, the gathering represents different causes and sections of society, from women empowerment to environmental concerns, HIV/AIDS patients and leprosy patients.

Apart from the few known names such as Concern India, Helpage and Akansha a number of NGOs are providing unique and essential services at the event. For instance, Doorsteps has put on display a wide variety of aprons, clay containers, drawings and diyas made by the children of construction site workers. The proceeds from the sale will be going for the education of kids, many of whom are taught in a well-equipped bus that contains blackboards and books.

Getting into the spirit of things, Navkshitij has on display beautiful lamps, vividly coloured dandiyas and well packaged chocolates, all made by mentally challenged adults that the NGO cares for. Two young girls, Sonia Gandhi and Amruta Kataria are displaying their creations at a quiet corner stall called Kite Creations that comprises eco friendly clocks made of jaggery and paper machie.

Animals in need of help are not forgotten either. The members of Paws Pack add, "Paws Pack with the support of RESQ was formed in January 2007 and we provide a unique 24 hour service to rescue injured animals, complete with an animal rescue help line, fully mobile operation van with built-in mini operating theatre and six kennels for animals undergoing treatment." The colour yellow resplendent at the venue, forms a decorative theme to symbolise hope and joy.

More power to such initiatives that will surely light up the festive season in many under privileged homes in and around the city.

Heading: Clubbing Cadence - Indian Express
Content:
Educational experts come together to provide personalised learning to special children at Cornerstone

They say every child is special but there are some children who have special needs. Their wants go beyond the usual obstinate materialistic demands and insist on sensibility, acceptance and understanding from their educator. These children have learning difficulties like dyslexia, dysgraphia and dyscalculia. Boosting these kids towards realising their potential and giving them inclusive education is of utmost importance. And this time to take up the Herculean task are educational psychologists, special educators, counsellors and experts- Madhvi Kapoor, Reena Bonagiri, Sandy Andrade, Rashmi Kothari and Hema Nair who reach out in the most individual way offering counselling, remedial teaching in English and Marathi, supporting groups, holding therapeutic workshops and more, to children with learning challenges as well as to their parents. This is the motive behind their organisation Cornerstone. Launched in June, Cornerstone now attends to over ten children.

"It is a condition. Giving the child overcoming and coping strategies we alter the way they process particular information. Using his strengths, step by step, consistently and systematically there can be almost up to 90 percent recovery. To imbibe self confidence and addressing them accordingly is very important. There are very bright kids and there is no difficulty at the sensory level. The problem lies at the perception level and is child centric. Hence we attend to the needs amd then make a special programme to follow up with," says Kapoor.

These children come to the centre after their school hours to learn and are in turn studied. "The child comes with a diagnosis. We identify the levels and have remediation and recommendations. Although we follow an international system, it has been implemented in Marathi as well with an intention to cover a larger part. The age group varies from five to 13 years. However, the younger the better since at a later age, the child needs to unlearn before he starts again," adds Bonagiri.

They further plan to give training in remedial work to the teachers and stress on having such centres in all schools given the fact that 10 percent of the population has these learning difficulties. "More than hyping the problem, awareness needs to be created. There are hardly any centres and there's a dearth of trained professionals. There is a system, methodology and more importantly sensitive teachers. For instance a child who has been coming for the last five years has had a lot of processing difficulties in school including writing and bad comprehension. She couldn't read two letter words put together. After observing and assessing her for the last five years she is now able to read one year lower than her grade and very confident. The greatest reward of this lies in seeing the progress in the children," smiles Kothari.

The centre is open from 4 to 8 pm from Monday to Friday at 515, A9 Eden Garden, Vimanagar.

Heading: Project Runway - Indian Express
Content:
This Saturday, Cuban band Nu Havana introduced the city to the driving Afro Cuban beats and scintillating Salsa Moves

If it's just the famous Cuban cigar you associate the country's name with then meet this quintet that is all set to take Cuba beyond its stereotypical image . Unveiling the other side of Cuba, the Cuban music,which, till date remains deprived of its fair share of recognition, the quintet of two-year-old Nu Havana band has been touring across the country, thundering various cities with the vibrant Cuban music. This Saturday it was the city that experienced the blistering raw Afro – Cuban beats with the moves of toe tapping, head bobbing salsa.

Percussionist Janet Trillo, trumpeter Alexey Quesada, animator Sandy Marquetti and dancers Narjara Fuented and Aldeliz Publes make-up the band that has been performing across the globe presenting a mix of salsa, reggae, hip-hop and even jazz, all packaged together in Cuban style.

"In Cuban music there is a rhythmic structure that has tension and release that everyone can feel, and it makes one move. With our music we celebrate life so our music is very lively and energetic. We are all sort of united by the groove," shares Yusmel Gonzalez, the band manager, 'Nu Havana', which is a band that has been put together by the Cuban Ministry of Culture and is currently on a three-week, five-city tour of India to promote Havana Club, a Cuban white rum that is also now available in India.

But the quintet avers they are not only touring the country for the promotion of the rum but to celebrate the communion of sound and movement. " We are here for music and a cultural exchange. What people generally associate our country with is either civil war or the cigar. We want to paint the other picture of our country, which is of a rich culture and when it comes music, of driving beat and vivacious energy," shares Sandy Marquetti, animator and also the vocalist of the band. Elaborating on Cuban music he says, "To us music and movement go hand in hand, one complimenting the very existence of other that is why when we talk of music we talk of dance. It's impossible for us to enjoy one without the other that is why Cuban music is full of life. It's very energetic. Anyone who listens to it will have his or her foot tapping."

With two dancers, one animator, one percussionist and one trumpeter the quintet however prefers to be addressed as a group of music lovers than a full fledged musical band. "For our band to fall in the category of a full fledged professional band we think there is a lot more to add. We have a percussionist, as percussion is the soul of Cuban music and a trumpeter because trumpet is next to percussion when it comes to Cuban music but we don't have a guitarist and a keyboard player," shares Marquetti

However the modest group of five when performed on Chan Chan, a popular Cuban number the audience was left craving for more.

Heading: Protest grows, but PMPML unlikely to reduce fares - Indian Express
Content:
City got glimpses of the haute couture as Neeta Lulla showcased creations from her festive and autumn winter collection.

In silk culottes, pinafores and brocade skirts, she paid a fashionable ode to women at 2007 Lakme India fashion week. And this year the fashion week bathed in the hues and shades of Immortal love. Even with disrepute of 'the international kind' for Aishwaraya's dress at Cannes, Neeta Lulla grows on the fashion scene living up to the expectations of being a perfect connoisseur of blending modern cuts with traditional elements. The reason to this she states, "I admit my mistakes, work on it and move ahead. Once or twice if you experiment and go wrong this does not mean you don't have it in you. Unless you take the risk of going wrong while experimenting you won't be able to satisfy the creative urges in you."

With her Immortal Love gathering rave reviews from fashion critics, her idea of creating an exotic colour palatte and painting shades of love in nude and tan to add the 'the unique' quality to her signature style she silences hearsays about her indo western experimentation.

Lulla was in town at the launch of Vitoria Lagoon where she showcased creations from her festive and autumn winter collection.

Over 300 films, dressing 90 artistes and more than a hundred shows, she has been there and done it all. With her award studded 25 years in fashion, Lulla comes a long way, pushing limits of fashion to an extent that nears the international fashion scene with her every experiment with the indo western theme.

And now her festive garment line is all set to dress her clientele in her signature style. Pairing traditional tunics with slacks and tights the collection keeps her glamour quotient intact and the Bollywood touch evident with the complete Jodhaa Akbar flavour. Thick, rich jackets and resham embroidered sarees harkening back to the Mughal opulence, Lulla paints her collection with a lush colour spectrum. "It's not just the festive collection, fashion this year will see every colour of the world, as people like to adorn themselves with vibrant colours these days," says the national award winner for designining Sridevi's clothes in Lamhe. A brilliant array of jewel reds, vibrant greens, yellows and oranges with heavy gilded embroidery, the dupattas, tunics and lehengas of her festive collection are all set to ornate the wardrobe s of her sizzling clientele of Bollywood stalwarts.

Heading: Developers woo buyers - Indian Express
Content:
Around 250 persons, including senior citizens , on Saturday marched down from Deccan to Swargate to the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) office to continue their protest against the fare hike.

Till now, citizen activist groups have collected over 25,000 signatures protesting against the fare hike. "We are targeting around 1 lakh signatures from the public. We are determined to see that this reaches its logical conclusion and we will be taking this issue up at the public level, state government level and the judiciary level, said Jugal Rathi, president PMP Pravasi Manch.

PMPML chief S B Patil said that these issues would be referred to the PMPML board of directors. " We will put it to the board of directors but it is unlikely that the fare revision will be done," he said.

The petition presented to the PMPML on Saturday demanded that the fare hike be revised. It has said that the company should work towards recovering all dues from the municipal corporations. "Some months ago, the general body had passed a resolution that all pending dues should be recovered from the state government. If they get it from the government, there is no reason, why PMPML should not be in profit," he said.

In the past two months, the company has added an additional 70 buses, it has plans to acquire 250 more buses in the coming months, with route rationalisation, they ought to be able to increase revenue. With auto rickshaw fares also increasing, in the past two months the revenue has increased by 2 per cent.

"We have told them that once they withdraw the hike, we will support them and agitate for them with the state government in getting the dues owed to the company," Rathi said.

Rathi also called the proposed move by PMPML to privatize one of the depots adhoc and hypocritical. Even as they are saying that private buses run by contractors are bad, they want to lease out a depot to the private players, he said. On Wednesday, Patil had said that they would contemplate allowing private operators to run one depot.

Heading: Seniors should not fall prey to easy money, says Umranikar - Indian Express
Content:
With the Pune Builders and Promoters Association (PBAP) reiterating that the demand and supply gap will only increase, and the prices will continue to rise, the developers in tie-up with Housing Financial Institutions (HFI) are taking on burden of lessening interest rates.

The ongoing PBAP exhibition at the SSPMS grounds, which has 90 developers participating, is offering buyers interest rates at 9.55 and 10 percent for two years, in the hope that the interest rates will go down in the coming years. With the interest rates going up by 40 per cent in the last three years, the special schemes are offered at the exhibition on booking at the venue itself.

Announcing the scheme at the exhibition, PBAP president Lalitkumar Jain said that these tie-ups are with the ICICI bank, HDFC and State Bank of India (SBI). "With most banks not lending any money to most developers even for construction purposes, affecting the cash flow, the source remains the customers. Though the construction cost and land cost have not come down the developers will compromise on their profits and are willing to take some burden,''he said at a press meet highlighing the cash crunch faced by developers in Pune.

With the present rate of interest escalating upto 11.75, Jain said that on consultation with economists, it is understood that the rate of interests will go down in future. "After elections the rate of interest will definitely go down,''he said. Jain said Pune has never been an inverstors market and is surely isolated from underwriters. The only investment attributed can be to second home buying by IT professionals or NRIs for rentals.

Heading: Mayawati’s new gift: a Buddha Sthal at Alambagh - Indian Express
Content:
There has been an increase in the crimes against senior citizens in the city and for that to some extent everyone including the citizens themselves are responsible. I would like to take this opportunity to warn all citizens to be aware of people who come into their societies, and not to fall prey to scamsters, godmen and salesmen promising them free things, and easy money," Jayant Umranikar, Additional Director General of Police said at the golden jubilee celebrations of the Institute of Engineers on Saturday. He said, "It's important for senior citizens to be active even in their fading years. They should not start outliving their usefulness and should try and adapt themselves to the surroundings as much as possible. Senior citizens should get themselves registered at the local police stations. Another important thing that they can do is they should make a proper list of their assets and should retain control of their property till they are alive. Their children owing to property issues usually dump their old parents into old age homes. Senior citizens should themselves fit and also change and modify their lifestyle according to their age."

The Indian Institute of Engineers, on the occasion of their golden jubilee celebrations had organised a lecture on "Safety of senior citizens."

Vinay Sathe of SoftSpin Technologies spoke at length about his new software for mobile phones, which would alert people and the police in case of an emergency. "One of the main problems we faced while designing the software was to ensure that it was compatible with all the available handsets in the market. The second most important issue that we faced while designing the software was to ensure that the technology remained simple enough to be used by everyone and also affordable. Hence we designed the software keeping the ease of usage in mind." The lecture also included an A/V presentation by Vinay Sathe explaining the merits of the software developed by him. Umranikar praised the innovation and urged citizens to register themselves and avail the benefit of the system as soon as possible.

Heading: Soon, a virtual classroom hub at Noida, 250 institutes to benefit - Indian Express
Content:
After B R Ambedkar and Kanshiram, the Mayawati government has now decided to construct another monument — dedicated to Lord Buddha, costing Rs 100 crore in Alambagh.

The monument — Buddha Sthal — is going to be developed along the 60-year-old Sharda canal, with a 3.5 km stretch — Kanpur Road to Bangla Bazaar — of the canal being given a facelift at a cost of Rs 90 crore. Spread over 6,000 sq metre, the monument will be coming up across the VIP road from Kanshiram Memorial.

The Uttar Pradesh Rajikya Nirman Nigam (UPRNN) will be handling the project along with the Irrigation Department, which is the nodal agency.

"A Delhi-based firm, Architect Bureau, has designed both the projects and no deadline has been set for their completion as yet," said A K Gautam, UPRNN General Manager.

A big pedestal has already been made in the middle of the Buddha Sthal on which a giant statue of Buddha will be installed.

Four 50-feet high pillars of marble from Rajasthan are being erected around the pedestal to support a canopy that will cover the statue. On the three sides, the park will have 100 stone columns, topped with elephant heads. The Sharda canal is being beautified with stonework and greenery.

Boundary walls made of Mirjapuri Chunar marble will be erected on both sides of the canal, said a UPRNN assistant engineer. This marble was chosen due to its longevity.

Heading: Scolded by father, girl commits suicide jumping into Gomti - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 250 engineering colleges across the state will soon have the opportunity to interact with some of the best teachers. The reason: Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) is setting up a virtual classroom hub at its Noida centre, which will beam quality-teaching programmes to 12 select institutes of the state.

These nodal centres will then offer the facility of virtual classrooms to nearly 25 colleges located in their vicinity.

The twelve nodal centres will be set up at Harcourt Butler Technological Institute (HBTI), Kanpur; Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lucknow among a host of others (see box).

The students at the nodal centres, sitting in their virtual classrooms equipped with plasma screens and computers, will also be able to interact with the teachers using video conferencing.   

The project has been funded by the Union Ministry of Information and Communication Technology, which has sanctioned Rs 3 crore for the project. The university has been asked to start these virtual classrooms within two years.

"For nodal centres, only those colleges have been selected which have good infrastructure and an excellent academic record," said UPTU Vice-Chancellor Professor Prem Vrat. "Initially, students of 250 engineering colleges will enjoy the facility of virtual classrooms. But in future, the university will connect all management and pharmacy colleges too with the virtual hub," said Vrat.

Nodal centres will record the lectures for recasting these to other colleges located in the nearby areas, he added. Fourteen project associates and two project scientists were being recruited to install, run and monitor the functioning of the centres. The Centre has formed a project implementation group to decide the technical specifications of virtual classrooms. It comprises engineering experts from IIT-Roorkee; HBTI, Kanpur, IIT-Kanpur; and Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lucknow.

Professor B S Paswan, an expert in electronics and computers in IIT, Delhi, will be heading the group.

Heading: Train destined for Lucknow heads for Allahabad, leaving passengers harried - Indian Express
Content:
A 16-year-old girl committed suicide by jumping into the river from the Gomti barrage on Sunday afternoon.

Rajni, a Class X student of the Maharishi Grah Vidhya Mandir, took the extreme step after she was scolded by her father.

According to the police, Rajini went to the market along with one of her friends. After an hour when she returned home, her father Shri Ram, a class four employee with the municipal corporation, scolded her for returning late and not informing the family about her visit.

"When her father and mother left for work and market, respectively, Rajini went to Gomti barrage, which is around 500 metres from her home and jumped into the river," said Sub-Inspector Narad Muni Singh of Hazratganj police station.

He added that a passersby who saw the girl jumping, raised an alarm and also informed the police.

Some boatmen who happened to be present nearby jumped into the river and fished her out.

Rajini was rushed to CSMMU's trauma centre where the doctor declared her dead on arrival.

"It is a case of suicide. There was no injury marks on the body," said Inspector Ajeet Singh Chauhan.

Heading: Health helpline to counsel couples - Indian Express
Content:
It was a terrible experience for passengers of a special train —4006 (B) Delhi-Darbhanga Express — on Sunday when they found that the train was heading to Allahabad instead of Lucknow.

Railway officials at the Kanpur station made the mistake by sending the train on a wrong route.

Panic-stricken passengers then pulled the chain of the train which stopped near Sarsol railway station, about 20 kms from Kanpur.

"We went to the Train Ticket Examiner (TTE) and told him that the train was heading towards the wrong direction. He then passed the information to his seniors," said Praveen Kumar Srivastava, a passenger. The harried passengers said that at first the TTE refused to take the train back to Kanpur saying that he has been asked by the authorities to head to Allahabad. "After a drama of over two hours, we were informed that the railway authorities have decided to take the train back to Kanpur," said another passenger Dharmendra.

At Kanpur, angry passengers held demonstrations. A senior railway official in Lucknow said the mistake occurred because the Northern Railway headquarters had failed to give them the route programme.

An official from Kanpur said another train with a similar number, 4006 (Lichvi Express that runs from Delhi to Darbhanga via Kanpur, Allahabad and Varanasi) added to the confusion, leading to the mistake.

Public Relations Officer of North Central Railway Amit Malviya said an inquiry has been set up to look into the cause of the incident.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Barabanki, Allahabad and Varanasi can now avail the benefits of Saathiya family planning helpline — supported by US Agency for International Development.

This will enable them to interact with the counselors and obtain medical support. The project has already been launched in Lucknow. The helpline will now have an extended timing as well as an extensive outreach campaign to reach out to not only married couples but also youngsters of a marriageable age.

"We have a panel of counselors, Saathiya Mitrs, who will give advice relating to reproductive health and family planning on toll-free numbers. We also have a panel of doctors, chemists and pharma companies who provide us services at nominal charges," said Meenakshi Dixit, Training Officer, Saathiya. 

Dr Chandrawati, senior gynecologist and a panelist in the campaign, said there was a lack of awareness about marital issues. "The youth today has so many queries regarding sexual health and family planning and such a helpline is a boon for them," said Chandrawati.

In the second phase, she said, the helpline will try to reach out to youngsters studying in colleges especially girls.

Heading: BSP supporter shot dead - Indian Express
Content:
Babus' lips sealed, courtesy Maya raj

Suspensions and frequent transfers in the Mayawati government, as pointed out recently by the Governor, have affected the morale of the bureaucracy so much that it has sealed their lips. The IAS Association used to bring out a quarterly newsletter in which senior officers wrote on issues ranging from good governance to transfers and suspensions. In Mayawati's regime, the magazine has not seen the light of the day. Office bearers of the association also keep quiet on the issue. An officer explained: "As long as an officer is in the good books of the big boss, the misery others face does not matter to him. It's only when he faces any trouble that he wants others to raise the issue." 

Man-made disaster no cause for concern

There has been a lot of talk about disaster management lately. After a section of the under-construction flyover on Faizabad Road caved in, no one in the government had any clue about the next step. Neither there was any trained manpower nor equipment to move the 30-metre concrete panel. It took hours to assemble cranes just to lift the structure a bit to find out what had been crushed under it. Perhaps that's why officials of the Revenue Department, which runs the disaster management programme, kept away from the scene. Principal Secretary (Revenue) Balvinder Kumar said: "It was not a natural disaster but a manmade one and, therefore, did not fall in the purview of the disaster management plan." In any case, since the flyover was a Central project, the state government had nothing to do with it, he added. Obviously, the babus do not know that a disaster is a disaster, whether natural or man-made.  

Reducing poverty, Maya not happy

The government has scrapped the BPL survey in which it had already invested crores of rupees. A year ago, Chief Minister Mayawati herself had mooted the idea of a fresh survey. A four-page proposal was prepared with over a dozen criteria. A massive exercise was undertaken in each gram sabha, involving hundreds of government employees. The survey results were also being computerised. Though the number of BPL families had increased in some districts, it had drastically gone down in several others. But given our politicians vested interest in poverty, how can anyone accept a decline in the number of the poor? So, the chief minister ordered that the exercise be scrapped. Officials were told to make additions and deletions, but ensure that nowhere was the number of the poor reduced. The officials are at their wits' end.

BSP Muslim leaders fear losing vote bank

Muslim leaders of BSP are nervous over the turn of events in the wake of the serial blasts in Delhi and the police from four states swooping down on Azamgarh. A vocal Muslim MP wants Mayawati to do something for retaining the Muslim votes, as these were drifting to the Samajwadi Party. Open advocacy of the terror accused arrested and demand for a judicial inquiry into the police encounter in Jamia Nagar in Delhi by SP general secretary Amar Singh has added to the discomfiture of BSP's Muslim leaders. They also do not understand why Mayawati is taking a soft line on the Bajrang Dal while Mulayam Singh has been demanding from the rooftops that the organisation be banned.  

'Workless' IPS splits hair

The 1976 batch IPS officer S Balaji is back as Additional Director General of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) and Anti-Corruption Organisation (ACO). In March, Balaji was removed from SIT when he was preparing to file the chargesheet in the much-publicised Uttar Pradesh State Industrial Development Corporation (UPSIDC) scam. Now, in the ACO, he will handle the police recruitment scam. But the investigation has been over in the case and the ACO has sought the government's sanction to prosecute the officers involved. Until the government makes up its mind, there will be little work to do for Balaji. Maybe, he could use the opportunity to finish the investigation of the UPSIDC scam.

Prez, PM visits make varsity hopeful

Last month, the Lucknow University honoured President Pratibha Patil at a special convocation by conferring on her an honorary D Litt degree. Now, the university is planning to invite Prime Minister Manmohan Singh for its Foundation Day on November 25. The President has just visited the university, if the PM also gives his consent, this would add to the profile and status of the university, said an official. After all, how many universities can claim to have hosted the two topmost dignitaries of the country in one year? It may also help the university get the Central status.

Heading: Bose: Singur crisis fuelled by Tatas’ rivals - Indian Express
Content:
A retired principal and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) supporter, Nathu Pal was allegedly shot dead at a religious function in Panchkhal village under Shatti police station in Kanpur Dehat on Saturday night.

The assailant, Pramod Pal who is a Lekphal, has been absconding. While Nathu's relatives have alleged that Pramod intentionally murdered Nathu, the police say it happened accidentally. SP Kanpur Dehat, N Ravinder said: "During the religious function, Pramod took out his licence gun and started firing in the air. One of the bullets accidentally pierced through Nathu's head."

He added that recommendation to cancel the gun licence of Pramod had been given to the district magistrate.

"We are looking for Pramod, and raids have been made at several locations," claimed the police officer. Nathu's son Shashi Bhushan said, " A few years ago my father and Pramod were at loggerheads over an issue, but the dispute was resolved."

Heading: Nano fiasco: Bloc slams Tatas, Dasmunsi blames CPM - Indian Express
Content:
CPM state secretary Biman Bose hinted that the continuing protest of the Trinamool Congress at Singur could have been supported by the rivals of the Tata Motors.

"Who has approached them (the Trinamool Congress)? For whose interests are they working?" Bose said at the book launch function at the stall of the National Book Agency—the publishing house of the CPM— near Park Circus Maidan.

Speculations are rife in political circles that some corporate players helped the Opposition to convert the land acquisition issue in Singur into a major controversy.

Tata Sons chairman Ratan Tata had alleged on Friday that the protest at Singur was funded by the rivals of Tata Motors.

Bose also slammed the Opposition for its role in Singur which forced Tata Motors to shift out of the state. "This is a great loss to the industrialisation drive of the state. An automobile industry could have been a catalyst in the development of the state," said the Left Front chairman.

He also criticised Trinamool legislator Partha Chatterjee for his role in the Tollygunge violence on Saturday night. Bose said it was the duty of the state government to intervene and take action to control law and order. He did not mince words while criticising the role of intellectuals in West Bengal. "A section of intellectuals has become the weapon of reactionary forces in the state. They do not hold any political ideology and take stands only for publicity. They are like weeds and parasites for the society," he said.

Heading: No Puja pause to Singur violence - Indian Express
Content:
The decision of the Tata Motors to pullout of Singur has evoked mixed reaction from various political parties.

The harshest reaction came from the Forward Bloc, a major constituent of the Left Front.

State Secretary of the Bloc, Ashok Ghosh, said: "The Tatas showed immense arrogance in taking the decision. The state government has provided enough facilities to the Tata Motors and gave them land at such a low cost." He added: "The government spent so much money by providing them police protection. But still they left Singur. It tarnished the image of the state all over the world. It is so unfortunate."

Noting that the state government should learn from the issue, Ghosh said: "The state government should take lessons from the incident and agricultural land should not be acquired for setting up factories. There should be a consensus before acquiring land."

On the other hand, Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi blamed the state government for the Singur fiasco.

"The Left Front government is trying to create a vote bank on Singur issue," he said. The state government must take care of the farmers who had parted with their land for the Tata Motors project, added Dasmunsi.

Senior Congress leader Sudip Bandopadhyay said the crisis could have been averted if the Tata Motors would have been more accommodative and offered some more land from the project area. While the Company has been manufacturing 10 different models at its Pune factory, at Singur they acquired 997 acres for the manufacturing of a single model, he added.

Heading: In two days, 10 kids die at Behrampore hospital - Indian Express
Content:
An apparent outcome of the pullout of the Tata's Nano project from Singur— tension prevails in villages of the area. Bharati Koley, a woman CPM supporter, was allegedly beaten up on Saturday night by Trinamool supporters in Khaserbheri village. Sources said nearly 10 Trinamool supporters stormed into Koley's house and beat her up.

While she is a village health worker, her son had undergone apprenticeship training provided by the Tatas. This is the third incident of violence between the Trinamool and the CPM after the Tatas announced its decision to pullout from Singur.

In another incident, police raided the house of Doodh Kumar Dhara, a Trinamool panchayat pradhan of Khaserbheri village, on Saturday and arrested two persons from his house on charges of beating up Umapada Ghosh, a CPM supporter of Haripur village.

Ghosh, was allegedly beaten up by Trinamool supporters on Saturday.

"The arrested persons were produced in court on Sunday," said Singur Sub-Divisional Police Officer Kalyan Mukhopadhaya.

Though no untoward incident was reported on Sunday, the police kept a strict vigil in the entire area to pre-empt violence. A large portion of the force, which was deployed for guarding the Tata factory, is now being kept on standby if law and order condition further deteriorates in the area.

A police officer said they do not want to deploy police in the villages unless situation demands. "While we want to tell the political parties that violence will not be tolerated, we do not want the people to panic," he added.

The road in Beraberi village that was dug up on Friday night was repaired by locals on Sunday.

Akul Ruidas, a resident, said the people who had dug up the road allowed the repair work to be conducted considering the inconvenience caused to locals.

Heading: Kolkata confidential - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 10 children, including newborns, have died since Saturday at the government-run Behrampur Sadar Hospital in Murshidabad. In the last one week, the number of children who died at the hospital is a shocking 25.

The director of Health Services, Sanchita Bakshi, said: "I have not received any information about 25 deaths in the last one week. But I have the confirmation on 10 deaths in the last 24 hours."

Preliminary inquiry revealed that all the children —- aged between one month and three years — died due to diarrhoea, acute pneumonia, septicaemia and malnutrition.

The administration has, meanwhile, expressed its concern over the deaths, blaming the poor healthcare facilities in the district. The services in the hospital are also hit by Puja celebrations as most of the hospital staff have gone on leave.

The paediatrics ward of the hospital too reveals a sorry picture. There are about 20 beds in the ward, but more than 150 children are admitted here. Although the strength of doctors and nurses in the ward has been stretched to its limit, the hospital is also facing a shortage of medicines.

According to authorities, sick children were referred to the hospital from rural and sub-divisional hospitals of the district, as most of them are understaffed.

"We have to accommodate three to four children in a single bed. We are not well-equipped to deal with such a large number of patients," hospital superintendent Bhaskar Samanta said.

"The situation is grave and higher officials are holding round-the-clock meetings to sort out the crisis," Samanta added.

According to the hospital superintendent, the number of death cases in the district is on a rise.

The district administration has expressed its concern over the deaths caused by malnutrition. Most of the malnutrition cases are coming from Lalbagh, Hariharpara, Chunukhali and Neemtala.

On Sunday, a group of locals gathered in front of the hospital and expressed their anger over the poor health care system.

Phulbanu Begum, a resident of Behrampur, whose three-month-old child is admitted at the paediatrics ward of the hospital, alleged that no one had attended to her daughter in the last 24 hours. She said that patients are cramped together in unhygienic conditions.

Meanwhile, at Kulti in Burdwan, two children died of diarrhoea and 500 others were taken seriously ill after drinking contaminated water from a municipality reservoir.

The administration has collected the water samples from the reservoir and sent them for lab tests. The areas most affected by diseases like diarrhoea, acute pneumonia and septicaemia are: Lalbazar, Ranchi village, Mosjedipar and Hossaindanga of Kulti municipality.

Heading: Time for fun, frolic and minting money - Indian Express
Content:
Singur trauma breaks Nirupam

After the Tatas announced their decision to leave Singur, besides the chief minister, one person who was heartbroken was Commerce and Industries minister Nirupam Sen. The man behind Bengal's industrialisation drive is a hapless person now. Sen is not speaking much but people close to him informed that the news had shattered him. His sadness was reflected when this correspondent called him for a quote. "We honestly tried for the project. I did my best. But now it will never happen. I am sad. Please pardon me, I am not in a condition to speak about Singur and industrialisation," said Sen. His associates say he has broken down since Tatas decided to leave. "We are trying to cheer him up. I told him that Singur is not the end of the world. Our industrialisation drive in Bengal will continue," said a senior CPM party leader and a friend of Sen.

Buddha-Pranab friends forever

That Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee were quite pally was evident on Sunday when they attended the foundation-laying ceremony of an IT Special Economic Zone at a five-star hotel on Eastern Bypass. While Bhattacharjee, in his speech, referred to Mukherjee as our 'beloved external affairs minister', the Union minister said he shared the thoughts of the chief minister on industrialisation. And during the whole programme, they were seen engrossed in intense talks.

When cops seek safety

It was a hilarious sight at the Charu Market police station on Saturday night. When violence broke out in Tollygunge neighbourhood, the policemen at the Charu Market police station were the first to scurry for cover. The first to run away was the sentry posted outside the police station. Next to follow were the sergeants, who fled when they saw the mob charging towards them. They even left their motorbikes on the road. Moments later, sub-inspectors and other police officers in the police station fled. Even the lockup constable ran away leaving the lockup unguarded. The driver of a police vehicle, however, could not follow them because he was asleep then. By the time he woke up, it was too late and he was beaten up.

CAB's top secret: team composition

Trust the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) to come up with something funny. Last month, Jagmohan Dalmiya & Co had devised a novel plan to help out the West Bengal cricket team in getting some much needed pre-season practice in the form of a special masala tournament — the Challenger Trophy.

After weeks of anticipation, last week the CAB eventually chalked out the team compositions of the one-day competition to be played from October 12. The three-team tournament will feature top 36 players of the state and is being seen as a platform for selection for the prestigious Ranji Trophy. Laxmi Ratan Shukla, Manoj Tiwary and Ranadeb Bose are the captains of the three sides.

Now, after having finalised the three teams, the CAB has suddenly decided to reshuffle the teams. Why? Because some newspapers have published the composition of the teams!

Here goes CAB joint-secretary Arun Mitra's explanation, baffling as it sounds: "We carefully drafted the three teams. And then I find the team details in newspapers the next day. I am disappointed. We are reshuffling the teams and will announce them at the last moment."

This is perhaps the first time ever that a sports body has decided to reshuffle a cricket team merely because it showed up in newspapers after getting finalised.

Question to the CAB now — the BCCI has finalised the Indian team for the Tests against Australia, and Sourav Ganguly is a part of it. And the team composition has appeared in the newspapers. So, will the CAB now ask the BCCI to scrap the Indian team because it's been published in papers?

Stretch legs at New Town lock-ups

The township in New Town will be comparable with the best cities on Earth. With top class hotels, IT parks and high rises with modern facilities, the state government is expecting businessmen, professionals and celebrities to throng the city. The police department also has plans to set up hi-tech police stations. "The lock ups will be modern ones. We are planning to have a small courtyard attached to the lockups for the arrested persons to stretch their legs," said a senior police officer of the West Bengal Police.

The police stations will also have marble floorings. "The people entering the New Town police stations should not have the feeling which one usually gets when one enters a thana," the police officer said. The state housing board, which looks after the planning of the entire New Town area, is also eager to have state-of- the-art police stations. Housing Minister Goutam Deb wants the police stations to be models for other states.

Heading: Flying squads to keep a vigil on crowd - Indian Express
Content:
No matter what the Kumartuli artisans have to say about the tradition being the dominant flavour of Durga Puja, the puja economics is an entirely different ball game. It is as if faith and economy are inexorably linked together with this annual carnival bringing in a resurgence of economy. MNCs to hawkers, each find their own way to mint money.

Of course, the recent years have witnessed a gradual drifting away of corporate sponsors, but as a whole, it is industry funding instead of subscriptions that decide the budget of the puja pandal giants. It is an entire cycle of awards, publicity and advertisements that encompasses the euphoria that grips the city.

For instance, Ekdalia Evergreen has one of the highest puja budgets in the range of Rs 35 to 40 lakh.

"80 per cent of our puja funding comes from corporate sponsors," said one of the puja committee members. The Park Circus Sarbajanin is almost entirely funded by sponsors. The hi-profile puja, which has Trinamool Congress leader Ajit Panja in the puja committee, will have none other than the Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee gracing the pandal as the chief guest.

That alone, however, cannot be a cause for cheer with organisers complaining that they had to trim their budget after their traditional sponsors "Colgate" parted ways.

"We still have mobile service providers and other companies but Colgate had been an important sponsor," said Abhijeet Bakshi of the Park Circus puja committee. Even after the "trimming", the puja budget stands tall at Rs 17 lakh this year.

The Jodhpur Park Sarbajanin has a budget of Rs 18 lakh with almost two-thirds of it coming from sponsors. The puja committee has struck gold, with ITC alone chipping in with funds to the tune of Rs 2.5 lakh. In addition, there are a whole range of other sponsors as diverse as DISH TV to Metro Dairy to Dominos pizza.

For the Chaltabagan Lohapatty puja, the organisers prefer the subscription route to corporate sponsors. "Almost the entire puja budget of Rs 10 lakh comes from advertisements in souvenirs published during pujas. The organisers know the donors well," said Ashok Jaiswal.

FD Block in Salt Lake has corporate sponsors contributing nearly one-third of the Rs 20 lakh budget. College Square and Baghbazar Sarbajanin are two budget giants in Central and North Kolkata. The former is a great crowd-puller for its locational advantage, as it is located at the hub of the central Kolkata puja circuit. No wonder, with a budget hovering around Rs 20 lakh it has the biggest brands coughing up funds for it.

"It all depends on the location and negotiating skills of the organisers," said Arup Biswas of the Suruchi Sangha committee at New Alipore, which has a budget in the range of Rs 15 to 17 lakh.

"Sponsors do not pay for putting up hoardings which they can do along the main roads. They are, however, willing to cough up if we provide them with stalls close to the pandal premises," say the organisers in unison.

Heading: Age no bar to enjoy the Pujas, old age homes overflow with joy - Indian Express
Content:
Following the recent spate of terrorist attacks across the country, the Kolkata police do not want to take any chance during the Durga Puja celebrations. To keep a check on the city during the four days of revelry, the police officers have introduced flying squads.

Such a step has been taken by the Kolkata police for the first time to execute random security checks in the city.

The flying squads come as an added security measure to keep a tight vigil not only on the crowds and pandals, but also on the streets during the pujas. "Plain-clothed police personnel will roam in the city instead of being stationed at a particular place. These policemen will be on the lookout for any suspicious element in the crowd," said a senior police officer of Lalbazar.

The squad will be divided into several teams, each of which would move from pandal to pandal. Equipped with hand metal detectors, these teams will randomly check anyone in the crowd. "These teams can be moved quickly from one place to another in case of an emergency," the officer added.

In addition, the fire brigade, too, has made special arrangements to minimise the chances of a fire breaking out during the pujas. Eight temporary firefighting stations have been set up in the city. Firefighting engines will be posted at the Shyampukur, Lake Town, Tollygunge, Muchipara, Behala, Tiljala, Metiaburz and Watgunge police stations.

"These places have been selected as there are a number of big pujas in the surrounding areas," said Bibhash Guha, divisional officer of the fire brigade. The number of fire-fighting vehicles has also been increased. "All the defunct firefighting vehicles have been renovated and will be on standby in case of an emergency," Guha said. The fire brigade has also requested the police to keep the roads leading to the water pumping stations clean so that in case of an emergency, fast movement could be possible.

Heading: Mahashasti brings a gleam to the eyes of visually-impaired - Indian Express
Content:
Jamuna Sarkar (70) and Sudhanshu Ranjan Dey (90), both residents of old age homes in Kolkata, are still young at heart, as they refuse to let their age spoil the excitement of celebrating Durga Puja.

"Although I cannot walk properly and have no relatives to celebrate the puja, I am still looking forward to the festival," said Sarkar, who stays in The Refuge, a home for destitute and old women at BB Ganguly Street. Puja is held in the premises of The Refuge every year.

For most of the city residents, Durga Puja is an occasion of festivities, but most of the residents of old age homes do not get the opportunity to share their joy with their relatives as most have been either dumped by them or have no one to take care of them.

It is heartening when the city is caught up in the puja fever, they celebrate the festival in their own ways.

"I know that no one from my family will come here. But we will celebrate pujas at my old age home. I cannot wait to wear new sarees that were provided by welfare organisations," said Nirmala Chakraborty (80), another resident of The Refuge.

With the idols already placed inside the premises, the residents of The Refuge cannot conceal their exhilaration as they plan puja rituals.

"I have been living here for the last 10 years. I know what it feels like when one is considered as a burden on the family. But during pujas I forget everything," said Sundari Das (75) of The Refuge.

At Nabonir, another old age home in the city, one can hear its residents discussing puja pandal hopping sprees. Each day of the festival will be special for them, as they will be taken to pandals by various volunteer groups.

"The sound of dhak and the smell of bhog is what I am looking forward to," said Ela Datta (80), a resident of Tollygunge branch of Nabonir.

Behind all the anticipation and enthusiasm, there is still a streak of disappointment in their eyes when they think about their families.

The spirit of Durga Puja, however, brings the sparkle back in their eyes.

"I was thrown out of my house by my family. There are times when I shiver while recalling my past experiences but then on occasions like Durga Puja I try to forget my pain and embrace the festival," said Rekha Baral (75), another resident of Nabonir.

Heading: Mummies, sphinx come alive at Kalindi pandal - Indian Express
Content:
For seven-year old Madhumita Mahato, the elaborate theme pujas of Kolkata were something she had seen only on television. That too, only till she had her vision intact. So, when the girl was told that she would be taken on a real pandal-hopping spree in Kolkata, she could not contain her glee.

Madhumita had completely lost the vision in her left eye, and was gradually losing the vision in her right eye too, making her parents give up hope that the girl would ever be able to see again. A resident of an interior village in Bankura district, Madhumita's case was taken up by the Susrut Eye Foundation and Research Centre, a non-profit organisation specialising in eye care.

"The doctors back home had given up and they referred us to Kolkata. We have been regularly shuttling to and from Kolkata for her treatment. She has got back her vision, we are very happy today," said her father.

Mahashashthi, the sixth day of the puja fortnight, marked the perfect day-out for Madhumita and six others who had undergone successful cornea transplantation and had regained their vision.

The Susrut Eye Foundation on Sunday organised a trip to the pandals for these patients. The outing started at 10 am with the group assembling near the Susrut facility in Salt Lake. After touring the Salt Lake Pujas, they were taken to the pandals on the VIP Road.

This was followed by a hurricane trip to some of the best puja pandals in south Kolkata. Even though their trip was cut short with the rain gods playing spoilsport, the patients said that they had a wonderful time.

Heading: US warns tourists of ‘unsafe’ days of durga puja - Indian Express
Content:
If you are fascinated by ancient Egypt civilisations, the Kalindi Saradotsav puja pandal is the place to visit. With mummies, pharaohs and ancient Egyptian kings and queens, the exotic pandal theme promises to be a visual delight.

Organised by the Kalindi Housing Estate in north Kolkata's Belgachia area, the puja committee is known to deal with diverse themes. Last year, it had recreated the Bishnupur Ram Lakshman Temple.

Walk inside the pandal and one is greeted by replicas of mummies laid in wooden caskets.

The old world charm is brought alive by paintings and sculptures of pharaohs that dominate the interior decor.

There are models of sphinx and pharaoh kings with detailed descriptions. Since the Durga idol has been kept a traditional one, the main draw is the eight feet replica of the mummy of Egyptian queen Cleopatra.

The matching lighting further adds to the spooky ambience.

Organisers claim that the theme is inspired by the exhibits in the Cairo Museum of Egypt. Puja Committee secretary Arkaprabha Roy said: "Every year we try to explore a different theme for the puja. This year, we drew inspiration from the Egyptian culture."

The organisers hope that the theme will go down well with the pandal hoppers. The pandal was inaugurated by eminent writer Buddhadeb Guha.

Artist of the Puja Committee, Prabir Mondal says, "This is a new concept as we have attempted to recreate the magic of Egypt. We have tried our best to make it different from other theme pujas."

Heading: Pak Govt to resolve issue of banned ICL players - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Kolkata police wrap the city and its suburbs in a security blanket during the ongoing festive season, the US government has alerted all its natives travelling in or to Kolkata and other parts of West Bengal to maintain a high level of "security vigilance". The advisory for American tourists was posted on the US Embassy website on September 29.

Interestingly, apart from asking tourists to be careful, the message also says they are expected to face road diversions, blockades, disruptions in public transport and traffic congestion during the festive season.

To assist the tourists, the Bureau of Consular Affairs and the US Embassy issue consular information sheets, travel warnings, public announcements, and warden messages concerning conditions in countries where Americans may be planning to visit or reside from time to time.

The "warden message" titled "Holiday Security in Eastern India" stated that the US government wants to remind American citizens living in and visiting eastern India that they need to maintain vigilance during the holiday season, from Durga Puja and Eid in October till Christmas and New Year in December-January.

The message also highlights, on the basis of press reports, that over 3 million tourists are expected to be in Kolkata on key festival days.

Warning the travellers of other obstructions which they might face on the roads in Kolkata, the advisory also informs them that the festive days bring with them a rise in crime. It, therefore, advises the tourists to take care of personal items, especially in crowded areas.

The advisory comes at a time when the authorities are leaving no stone unturned to help Kolkata brace up for all-round security during the Pujas. The Kolkata police have issued a list of do's and dont's for the people of Kolkata during the pujas. Even the police chief Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti has asked people to be very alert during the festive season.

Heading: Lacklustre Valencia reclaim top spot in Spain - Indian Express
Content:
In what would be music to the ears of Pakistan's banned ICL players, the government has agreed to consider their case and formulate a policy to resolve the crisis in consultation with the Cricket Board.

Law minister Farooq A Naek told reporters in Lahore that the ICL issue was discussed in a meeting with the former Test players.

The Indian Cricket League has around 18 Pakistani players including Inzamam-ul-Haq on its payroll and are not considered for selection in national and domestic teams.

The Pakistan Cricket Board had banned all the players, who aligned with ICL as it was not an ICC recognised event.

"I have asked them (players) to show me their contracts with ICL so that we can formulate a new policy about them and solve the problems of both sitting and retired cricketers.

"I have spoken to the President (Asif Zardari) over this issue and he is very keen to see the revival of cricket in Pakistan," Naek said.

Inzamam-ul-Haq, who has also attended the meeting, said he had raised the issue of banning the players.

"I did speak to the Minister about ICL players because if an ICL player is needed to fulfil his duties for the national side, then he will come and play as it is mentioned in the contract.

"I don't think that if a player gets a chance to play for ICL, he should go and be banned by the board. This is totally unfair. This is stopping a player from earning through his chosen profession," he said.

The former batsman with experience of 120 Tests is leading the Lahore Badshahs in the second edition of the ICL season.

Heading: Gilchrist comes back to take on Australia in T20 match - Indian Express
Content:
A Manuel Fernandes strike proved enough for a lethargic Valencia to beat Valladolid 1-0 and reclaim top spot in the Spanish first division.

Valencia started slowly with the much publicised threat from Juan Mata, David Villa and Joaquin Sanchez failing to fire and instead it was Valladolid who caused most danger down the wings through Pedro Leon and Jonathan Sesma.

But Fernandes scored the only goal of the game when he fired a powerful shot from the edge of the area after 54 minutes to put Valencia on top of the table on 16 points.

Villarreal also have 16 points after a 2-1 win on Saturday against rock-bottom Real Betis but are in second spot on goal difference.

Earlier Sunday, Sevilla bolstered their Champions League hopes for nest season with a 4-0 mauling of Athletic Bilbao to move into third place on 14 points.

The home side never allowed tiredness from their midweek UEFA Cup efforts effect them as they went ahead after 26 minutes through Frederic Kanoute and then five minutes before the interval Renato Santos doubled their advantage.

The best goal of the game came after 75 minutes in a well-worked counter-attack with Adriano Correia providing the finishing touch. Substitute Ernesto Chevanton wrapped up the game with ten minutes to go.

"It's going well but it's still early days. We maintained a good rhythm and that is what we need to continue doing until the end of the season but it will be long and hard," said Manolo Jimenez, who has set a record by becoming the first Sevilla coach to string together eleven matches without defeat.

Barcelona are in fourth spot on 13 points after their 6-1 thrashing of Atletico Madrid on Saturday.

Sporting Gijon moved off the bottom of the table with a surprise 2-0 victory over Real Mallorca with goals from Carmelo Gonzalez and Roberto Canella.

They were the first points for Sporting against a side unbeaten in four matches, but after surviving some early scares their counter-attacks cut through Mallorca and they could have had more with Mate Bilic hitting the post.

Pierre Webo missed from the penalty spot for Mallorca.

Malaga made easy work of struggling Recreativo Huelva as they beat their Andalusian neighbours 4-0.

Eliseu Pereira dos Santos scored the first of his brace in the first minute of the game and then goals either side of the interval from Nabil Baha and Duda Valente firmly placed Malaga in the driving seat.

They finished off the scoring just after the hour mark with Eliseu's second.

Racing Santander left it late, scoring in the second minute of injury time away to Osasuna to claim an important 1-0 victory after a poor start to the season.

Osasuna's Jaroslav Plasil will consider himself unlucky to have been dismissed in the first half for handball inside the area but Ezequiel Garay failed from the penalty spot.

Racing's Juan Varela grabbed the winner, controlling the ball well before firing past the keeper.

Almeria came from two goals down to claim a point in a 2-2 draw away to Getafe.
